headline: 3M should turn margin gains into cash before expanding shareholder returns.
summary: Modest organic growth and better adjusted margins suggest operational progress, but reported margin and cash generation give a more restrained picture. The priority is making improvement fund actual obligations while maintaining investment in demand.
focusTitle: Make cash-backed improvement the allocation test.
focusText: Direct productivity benefits toward products with stronger recurring demand, then size distributions after operating needs and excluded payments. A better adjusted margin matters most when the business can retain the cash it generates.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make productivity improvements visible in reported results
cards.text: Full-year non-GAAP adjusted operating margin rose 200 basis points to 23.4%, while GAAP margin fell to 18.6%. The gap makes the durability and cash cost of the improvement central allocation questions.
items: Preserve savings in lower-return operating activities
Protect product and customer-facing investment
Monitor reported margin alongside adjusted improvement

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Find growth beyond the PFAS comparison
cards.text: 2025 non-GAAP organic sales grew 0.9%, or 2.1% on the adjusted basis excluding manufactured PFAS products. Excluding manufactured PFAS improves the comparison, but neither basis supports an aggressive expansion assumption.
items: Prioritize end markets showing repeat orders
Separate pricing from underlying shipment demand
Match capacity commitments to recurring demand

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Budget against cash actually available
cards.text: 2025 operating cash flow was $2.3 billion; non-GAAP adjusted free cash flow was $4.4 billion. The adjusted cash figure alone could overstate the flexibility available for investment and distributions.
items: Reserve cash for excluded payment obligations
Improve inventory and receivables conversion
Set spending gates using operating cash

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep distributions subordinate to obligations
cards.text: 3M distributed $4.8 billion through dividends and repurchases in 2025. Returns exceeded reported operating cash flow, making the funding mix important to resilience.
items: Size repurchases after required cash payments
Compare debt funding with retained cash
Preserve liquidity before expanding capital returns

headline: A. O. Smith needs a focused China recovery while protecting its stronger businesses.
summary: China's decline is the clearest operating weakness, and India's expansion has not prevented lower Rest of World sales. North America's profitability provides support, so resource allocation should distinguish recovery work from businesses already performing well.
focusTitle: Recover international demand without diluting returns.
focusText: Focus China resources on products and channels that can restore profitable sales. Preserve North American execution and integrate Pureit around India's organic momentum, using regional contribution rather than aggregate international sales to judge progress.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Rebuild China sales with targeted channel execution
cards.text: China third-party sales declined 12% in 2025. The size of the decline calls for specific product and distribution decisions rather than broad expansion.
items: Identify weak product and channel combinations
Align inventory with local order patterns
Test promotions against profitable unit growth

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep India's growth engine distinct from acquisitions
cards.text: India non-GAAP organic sales rose 13% in local currency; acquired Pureit contributed $54 million. Local-currency organic growth and Pureit's contribution offer separate opportunities with different integration requirements.
items: Expand distribution around successful existing products
Integrate Pureit service and dealer support
Monitor organic growth separately from acquired sales

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect North America's earnings contribution
cards.text: North America sales were $2.984 billion; segment margin reached 24.4%. The region's margin provides a strong base from which to fund selective international initiatives.
items: Preserve commercial equipment pricing discipline
Prioritize service availability and product reliability
Monitor mix shifts before adding capacity

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Allocate international resources by regional economics
cards.text: Rest of World sales declined 4% to $880.4 million. India's strength has not offset weaker markets across the reported Rest of World business.
items: Compare regional contribution after selling costs
Reduce inventory exposure in slower markets
Fund expansion where orders support returns

headline: Abbott should scale diabetes care while broadening the sources of growth.
summary: Medical devices, particularly diabetes care, are growing faster than the wider company, while established pharmaceuticals adds a separate growth source. The task is supporting adoption and access without letting device momentum obscure the testing-related drag.
focusTitle: Expand access while preserving portfolio breadth.
focusText: Prioritize dependable device supply and patient adoption, supported by reimbursement access. Keep pharmaceutical growth and non-COVID demand visible so capital allocation reflects durable opportunities across the portfolio rather than the strongest product category alone.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Translate diabetes momentum into sustained adoption
cards.text: Annual diabetes-care sales reached $7.998 billion, up 16.3% on a non-GAAP organic basis. Faster growth makes patient access and continued use more valuable than shipment expansion alone.
items: Expand sensor availability through care channels
Strengthen patient onboarding and ongoing support
Monitor adoption persistence and reimbursement access

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale devices without concentrating execution risk
cards.text: 2025 medical-device sales were $21.387 billion, with 11.9% non-GAAP organic growth. Strong device growth warrants investment, with category-level returns guiding where capacity and commercial support go.
items: Prioritize capacity behind sustained category demand
Support clinician training for growing devices
Monitor supply reliability and category concentration

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve pharmaceuticals as a second growth engine
cards.text: 2025 established-pharmaceutical sales were $5.536 billion, up 7.4% on a non-GAAP organic basis. Medicines provide growth beyond devices and deserve investment suited to local market economics.
items: Improve availability in growing medicine markets
Allocate promotion by product-level demand
Monitor currency exposure and local profitability

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Separate testing comparisons from underlying demand
cards.text: Annual non-GAAP organic sales increased 5.5%, or 6.7% excluding COVID-19 testing. The exclusion changes the growth picture, so diagnostics decisions need a clearer view of recurring demand.
items: Size testing capacity to current utilization
Develop recurring non-COVID diagnostic demand
Monitor total and underlying sales together

headline: AbbVie should protect its growth franchises while addressing aesthetics weakness.
summary: Immunology and neuroscience are expanding strongly, but oncology is growing slowly and aesthetics is declining. The priority is maintaining access and execution in the leading franchises while making a targeted response to weaker businesses rather than spreading investment evenly.
focusTitle: Fund durable therapy growth and a selective aesthetics response.
focusText: Use product-level uptake and access to guide immunology and neuroscience investment. Give aesthetics a focused demand and profitability plan, while requiring oncology initiatives to demonstrate a credible contribution beyond the faster-growing franchises.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect immunology access as concentration grows
cards.text: 2025 immunology sales rose 14.0% to $30.406 billion; Skyrizi contributed $17.562 billion. Skyrizi's contribution makes reliable access and continued uptake central to the portfolio's resilience.
items: Strengthen payer access for key therapies
Support prescribing and treatment continuity
Monitor concentration across immunology products

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Broaden neuroscience's growth contribution
cards.text: Annual neuroscience sales increased 19.6% to $10.767 billion. Neuroscience offers meaningful diversification, making product-level adoption a useful guide to incremental investment.
items: Allocate commercial support by therapy uptake
Support access for approved indications
Monitor persistence across growing neuroscience products

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore aesthetics demand with selective investment
cards.text: Annual aesthetics sales declined 6.1% to $4.860 billion. Elective-treatment weakness requires a distinct commercial response rather than assumptions drawn from therapeutic growth.
items: Identify weak treatment and geographic demand
Support productive provider relationships and training
Test promotions against treatment profitability

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make oncology spending earn its place
cards.text: 2025 oncology sales increased 1.5% to $6.655 billion. Slower growth increases the need to distinguish promising products from offsets within the oncology portfolio.
items: Prioritize products with improving uptake
Address access barriers in weaker therapies
Monitor competitive pressure and product contribution

headline: Accenture should convert AI commitments into profitable delivery while rebuilding booking momentum.
summary: Managed services is expanding faster than consulting, and AI bookings create an opportunity for future work. With total bookings slightly lower, the priority is conversion and delivery economics rather than treating contract commitments as equivalent to realized growth.
focusTitle: Connect selling capacity to profitable execution.
focusText: Prioritize AI work with clear deployment paths and delivery capabilities, while protecting managed-services economics. Adjust consulting staffing and investment to actual project starts, using contract conversion and client outcomes to judge the strength of demand.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Turn booking coverage into executable work
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 new bookings were $80.62 billion, down 1%, with a 1.2 book-to-bill. A positive book-to-bill provides coverage, but softer bookings make contract quality and start dates consequential.
items: Resolve obstacles to signed project starts
Allocate delivery teams to confirmed commitments
Monitor cancellations and contract conversion

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make AI bookings produce repeatable client value
cards.text: Annual generative-AI bookings were $5.9 billion. The commitment base creates opportunity if deployments can earn attractive delivery economics and follow-on demand.
items: Prioritize AI engagements with deployable use cases
Build reusable delivery capabilities across accounts
Monitor conversion and project-level profitability

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve managed-services delivery economics
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 managed-services revenue increased 9% in non-GAAP local currency to $34.57 billion. Faster local-currency growth supports investment, provided recurring work does not outrun effective delivery capacity.
items: Standardize delivery for repeatable service needs
Align utilization with contracted workload
Monitor renewal quality and service performance

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Match consulting capacity to discretionary demand
cards.text: Annual consulting revenue was $35.11 billion, up 5% in non-GAAP local currency. Slower local-currency growth argues for selective deployment of talent and stronger project-start execution.
items: Focus proposals on funded client priorities
Redeploy skills toward active project demand
Monitor pricing and billable utilization

headline: Adobe should turn subscription expansion into durable customer retention and product adoption.
summary: Recurring commitments and Digital Media growth provide a solid base, while business and consumer subscriptions are expanding faster. Digital Experience is also growing, so the priority is improving monetization and adoption across customer groups without assuming equal expansion everywhere.
focusTitle: Grow through customer value and renewal quality.
focusText: Support the tools and workflows customers use repeatedly, then connect that engagement to renewals and expansion. Allocate enterprise resources according to deployment progress while preserving the faster-growing business and consumer subscription opportunity.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make ARR expansion durable at renewal
cards.text: Year-end total ARR was $25.20 billion, up 11.5%. The larger recurring base increases the value of keeping customers engaged before renewal decisions.
items: Intervene early where product usage weakens
Connect account support to expansion opportunities
Monitor renewals by customer group

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Convert creative adoption into stronger monetization
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 Digital Media revenue increased 11% to $17.65 billion. Digital Media growth supports investment in workflows that encourage sustained use and paid expansion.
items: Improve onboarding across creative workflows
Package upgrades around demonstrated customer needs
Monitor paid adoption and ongoing usage

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Extend business and consumer subscription momentum
cards.text: Business Professionals and Consumers subscription revenue rose 15% to $6.50 billion. The faster-growing group offers a useful route to broader productivity adoption and recurring relationships.
items: Simplify first-use subscription onboarding
Promote relevant upgrades to engaged subscribers
Monitor conversion and subscriber retention

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Improve enterprise deployment and expansion
cards.text: Annual Digital Experience revenue grew 9% to $5.86 billion. Digital Experience trails the other disclosed growth measures, making implementation quality a practical commercial priority.
items: Remove obstacles to enterprise implementation
Link account expansion to deployed workflows
Monitor renewal and implementation completion

headline: AMD should support its growth engines while managing Embedded as a separate recovery.
summary: Data Center, Client and Gaming all expanded strongly, but Embedded remains weaker following customer inventory adjustments cited by management. The priority is matching supply and development spending to distinct demand cycles, rather than assuming portfolio-wide growth continues uniformly.
focusTitle: Scale selectively across different chip demand cycles.
focusText: Protect product execution and customer qualification in Data Center and Client, with Gaming capacity tied to specific demand. Treat Embedded inventory normalization as a separate allocation decision and require evidence of renewed customer orders before expanding commitments.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale Data Center around durable customer demand
cards.text: 2025 Data Center revenue increased 32% to $16.6 billion. Server CPUs and accelerators offer growth opportunities with different product qualification and capacity requirements.
items: Allocate supply by confirmed customer deployments
Support CPU and accelerator software adoption
Monitor demand concentration by product family

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make Client growth withstand PC cycles
cards.text: Annual Client revenue rose 51% to $10.6 billion. Strong growth warrants support, but share expansion and broader market demand should guide capacity differently.
items: Prioritize designs with repeat customer adoption
Align production with channel sell-through
Monitor share gains versus PC demand

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Manage Gaming's two demand streams separately
cards.text: 2025 Gaming revenue increased 51% to $3.9 billion. Console and Radeon opportunities can require different supply commitments even with the same reported growth rate.
items: Plan console supply against customer schedules
Manage Radeon inventory by channel demand
Monitor profitability across gaming product types

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require order evidence before expanding Embedded supply
cards.text: Annual Embedded revenue fell 3% to $3.5 billion; management cited earlier customer inventory adjustments. Management's inventory explanation suggests recovery decisions should depend on customers' actual replenishment behavior.
items: Align shipments with customer inventory needs
Prioritize applications showing renewed orders
Monitor sequential orders and cancellation patterns

headline: AES should secure funding and execution discipline before expanding its renewable pipeline.
summary: Completed capacity and new power agreements show progress, but the contracted backlog creates substantial construction and financing obligations. The key priority is converting signed demand into cash-generating projects without allowing budget commitments to outrun available capital.
focusTitle: Stage growth around funded project returns.
focusText: Prioritize projects with committed financing, workable construction schedules and sound contract economics. Use commercial-operation milestones and cash generation from completed assets to support the next wave of investment, while retaining room for cost and commissioning setbacks.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make the Clean Energy budget financeable
cards.text: AES Clean Energy had a 7.6 GW backlog, with construction and contracted-project budgets exceeding $12 billion. A project budget exceeding $12 billion makes funding structure a central determinant of achievable growth.
items: Secure financing against specific project commitments
Stage construction by funding availability
Monitor cost exposure and tax-credit eligibility

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Convert backlog without stretching execution capacity
cards.text: Year-end contracted backlog was 12.0 GW, including 5.7 GW under construction. The under-construction portion creates nearer execution obligations within the larger contracted pipeline.
items: Sequence procurement around commissioning milestones
Allocate teams to critical construction bottlenecks
Monitor delays and remaining funding needs

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn construction completion into operating cash
cards.text: AES completed construction of 3.2 GW of renewables and energy storage in 2025. Finished capacity contributes economically only when assets operate reliably under their commercial arrangements.
items: Resolve remaining commercial-operation requirements
Build operating support around commissioned assets
Monitor availability and project cash returns

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve contract quality as agreements expand
cards.text: AES signed long-term power agreements for another 4.0 GW of renewable energy in 2025. New long-term agreements support demand visibility, but growth should meet project-return and funding tests.
items: Price contracts for project-specific cost risks
Diversify customer exposure where economically justified
Monitor contracted returns before committing capital

headline: Aflac should turn Japan's new sales into a stronger in-force premium base.
summary: Japan's new premium sales improved, but earned premiums still declined, highlighting the difference between new business and the existing book. US premium growth provides support, although its lower adjusted margin makes profitable retention and product economics important.
focusTitle: Prioritize profitable retention across the insurance book.
focusText: Use Japan's new sales momentum to strengthen long-term premium persistence, with channel support linked to durable policies. In the US, balance premium expansion with claims and servicing economics so growth does not steadily dilute underwriting contribution.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Stabilize Japan's earned-premium base
cards.text: Full-year Japan net earned premiums declined 3.9% in yen. The decline despite stronger new sales makes retention and the runoff of existing business central questions.
items: Target retention support to vulnerable policies
Adapt product offers to durable coverage needs
Monitor lapses and in-force premium trends

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make Japan's sales growth persist
cards.text: Japan annual new premium sales increased 16.0% to ¥74.4 billion. Higher new premium sales create value when policies remain active and distribution costs are recovered.
items: Support agents selling suitable recurring coverage
Improve onboarding and policyholder service
Monitor new-policy persistence by channel

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build US growth around durable coverage
cards.text: US annual net earned premiums increased 2.9% to $6.0 billion. Premium expansion offers room for investment if customer and employer relationships remain productive.
items: Deepen productive employer and agent relationships
Improve enrollment and ongoing policy service
Monitor retention alongside premium growth

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect US profitability as premiums grow
cards.text: US full-year pretax non-GAAP adjusted margin was 20.6%, versus 21.1% previously. The lower adjusted margin calls for focused attention to claims and cost economics.
items: Review pricing against product-level claims experience
Improve servicing efficiency without reducing support
Monitor adjusted margin by product mix

headline: Agilent should broaden growth beyond its stronger laboratory businesses.
summary: Life Sciences and Diagnostics and CrossLab are growing faster than Applied Markets, while reported growth exceeds the company's core comparison. The priority is preserving service-led customer relationships while directing commercial effort toward the slower end markets selectively.
focusTitle: Use the installed base to support balanced growth.
focusText: Maintain reliable laboratory support and cross-selling in stronger businesses, while aligning Applied Markets inventory and selling resources with actual customer investment. Judge expansion on the core comparison and business-level returns rather than the reported growth rate alone.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make CrossLab relationships support repeat business
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 CrossLab revenue was $2.908 billion, up 6%. Service growth can strengthen laboratory relationships and improve the economics of the existing installed base.
items: Improve service availability for active laboratories
Connect support visits to relevant customer needs
Monitor renewals and service attachment

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support Life Sciences and Diagnostics demand selectively
cards.text: Annual Life Sciences and Diagnostics revenue reached $2.726 billion, up 11% on the release’s rounded basis. The faster-growing business merits resources where product demand and customer utilization support investment.
items: Prioritize supply for consistently ordered products
Strengthen application support for laboratory users
Monitor adoption across product categories

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Rebuild Applied Markets through targeted opportunities
cards.text: Applied Markets annual revenue grew 1% to $1.314 billion. Limited growth argues for focused end-market decisions rather than uniform commercial or capacity expansion.
items: Target applications with funded customer projects
Align inventory with instrument order patterns
Monitor end-market orders and conversion

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Allocate capital using the core growth picture
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 revenue grew 4.9% on Agilent’s non-GAAP core basis, versus 6.7% reported growth. The reported comparison is stronger than Agilent's non-GAAP core basis, affecting assumptions behind spending.
items: Base capacity plans on recurring customer demand
Separate portfolio effects in investment cases
Monitor core growth against spending commitments

headline: Air Products should rebuild its project portfolio around returns and dependable gas demand.
summary: Lower volumes reflect disposals, exits and helium demand cited by management, while pricing and energy pass-through support sales comparisons. The priority is improving the economics of the remaining business and selecting projects carefully rather than chasing replacement revenue.
focusTitle: Reinvest selectively after project exits.
focusText: Concentrate capital and operating support on industrial-gas projects with credible customer demand and attractive returns. Match organizational costs to the remaining portfolio, while distinguishing contractual energy recovery and pricing from genuine improvements in gas volumes.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make project selection more demanding
cards.text: Management emphasized high-return industrial-gas projects and organizational right-sizing after fiscal 2025 project exits. Management's emphasis on returns and right-sizing makes disciplined reinvestment the central operational decision after exits.
items: Rank projects by contracted return and funding
Stage capital behind customer-backed demand
Align organizational costs with retained operations

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Rebuild volumes within the retained business
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 volumes declined 4%; management cited the LNG disposal, helium demand and project exits. The disclosed causes combine portfolio changes with demand weakness, requiring different commercial responses.
items: Target merchant-gas customers with recurring needs
Match helium supply to customer demand
Monitor retained-business volumes separately from exits

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Preserve price realization without weakening relationships
cards.text: Annual pricing increased 1%, led by non-helium merchant gases. Modest pricing support helps economics, but sustainable customer demand remains important to volume recovery.
items: Defend pricing where service value supports it
Tailor contracts to customer consumption patterns
Monitor price realization and customer retention

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep energy recovery aligned with costs
cards.text: Higher energy cost pass-through added 2% to the fiscal-year sales comparison. Pass-through supports sales but does not by itself establish stronger underlying gas demand.
items: Maintain cost-recovery terms in gas contracts
Reduce avoidable energy use in operations
Monitor recovery timing against energy payments

headline: Airbnb should convert broader supply and market expansion into productive bookings.
summary: Bookings are growing and expansion markets are outpacing core markets, but listing scale alone does not establish supply productivity. The priority is improving the match between guests and available stays while separating underlying booking growth from currency and booking-value effects.
focusTitle: Grow through better matching and reliable stays.
focusText: Direct market investment toward locations where guest demand and suitable supply reinforce each other. Help hosts deliver consistent stays and use booking conversion, repeat activity and listing utilization to decide whether additional supply improves marketplace economics.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Convert demand into completed booking activity
cards.text: 2025 Nights and Seats Booked totaled 533.0 million, up 8%. The booking increase supports investment in discovery and checkout that makes available supply easier to use.
items: Improve search relevance for available stays
Reduce friction in booking and support
Monitor conversion and repeat guest activity

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make expansion-market momentum economically durable
cards.text: Expansion-market origin-night growth averaged roughly twice the core-market rate during 2025. Faster origin-night growth suggests opportunity, with local supply quality and acquisition economics guiding deployment.
items: Build suitable supply in growing destinations
Adapt guest support to market needs
Monitor repeat bookings and acquisition efficiency

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Improve listing productivity before adding undirected supply
cards.text: Airbnb ended 2025 with more than 9 million active listings. A large active listing base increases the value of availability, relevance and reliable host execution.
items: Help hosts improve calendars and listing quality
Address low-conversion supply in key markets
Monitor booked nights per active listing

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Separate marketplace demand from booking-value changes
cards.text: Annual gross booking value increased 12% to $91.3 billion, or 10% excluding currency. Reported and ex-currency growth differ, while booking value can also reflect mix and pricing.
items: Match offers to guest budget and trip needs
Assess promotion economics by booking cohort
Monitor nights and booking value separately

headline: Akamai should scale security and cloud while managing delivery's decline.
summary: Security and Cloud Infrastructure Services are growing, with particularly rapid expansion in Guardicore Segmentation and API Security. Delivery remains a meaningful declining business, so the priority is funding the growth transition while keeping infrastructure and selling costs aligned with demand.
focusTitle: Build the growth portfolio without carrying excess delivery costs.
focusText: Concentrate commercial and technical investment on demonstrable security and cloud adoption, using customer retention and service economics as allocation tests. Manage delivery for profitable customer relationships and capacity efficiency rather than assuming newer products erase its decline.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve security's broad growth contribution
cards.text: 2025 security revenue rose 10% to $2.243 billion. The larger security business provides a stronger base than relying only on the fastest-growing products.
items: Deepen security adoption within existing accounts
Strengthen implementation and ongoing customer support
Monitor renewals across security product families

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn faster security adoption into lasting deployments
cards.text: Annual Guardicore Segmentation and API Security revenue increased 43% to $293 million. Guardicore and API Security growth warrants investment in implementation capacity and repeatable enterprise selling.
items: Prioritize deployment support for contracted customers
Build cross-selling around demonstrated security needs
Monitor active deployments and customer expansion

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale cloud infrastructure against utilization
cards.text: Cloud Infrastructure Services annual revenue increased 36% to $314 million. Rapid infrastructure growth requires capacity decisions tied to actual workload economics and customer demand.
items: Add capacity where committed workloads support it
Improve customer onboarding and workload migration
Monitor utilization and contribution after infrastructure costs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Resize delivery around profitable customer demand
cards.text: 2025 delivery revenue fell 5% to $1.257 billion. A declining delivery business can constrain the transition if its capacity and cost base remain inflexible.
items: Align network capacity with retained traffic
Prioritize contracts with sustainable delivery economics
Monitor churn and cost per delivered workload

headline: Albemarle should protect liquidity while improving lithium economics.
summary: Higher Energy Storage volumes did not prevent lower adjusted EBITDA, showing that shipment growth alone is insufficient. Specialties and productivity gains provide support, while sharply reduced capital spending makes selective investment and preservation of operating capability the central priorities.
focusTitle: Favor cash-efficient output over volume-led expansion.
focusText: Use product and customer profitability to guide Energy Storage production, preserve the stronger Specialties contribution and retain productivity improvements. Stage capital carefully so near-term cash protection does not undermine the projects or operating assets most likely to earn acceptable returns.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve Energy Storage economics before expanding output
cards.text: 2025 Energy Storage non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA declined 8% to $697 million despite higher sales volumes. Lower adjusted EBITDA despite higher volumes makes contribution per unit more relevant than volume growth alone.
items: Allocate output toward stronger customer economics
Align production with profitable contracted demand
Monitor realized pricing and unit operating costs

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve productivity gains without eroding reliability
cards.text: Albemarle reported approximately $450 million of 2025 cost and productivity improvements. Reported savings support resilience if they can persist without weakening asset performance or customer service.
items: Embed savings in procurement and operating routines
Protect maintenance needed for reliable production
Monitor recurring savings and operating disruptions

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use Specialties as a balanced investment priority
cards.text: Annual Specialties non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA increased 21% to $276 million. Higher adjusted EBITDA provides a counterweight to Energy Storage weakness and a distinct allocation opportunity.
items: Prioritize Specialties products with sustained demand
Protect service levels for profitable customers
Monitor cash contribution by product family

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Stage capital without starving critical assets
cards.text: 2025 capital expenditure declined 65% to $590 million. The spending reduction protects cash but makes project sequencing and essential maintenance decisions more important.
items: Fund safety and sustaining asset requirements first
Gate expansion spending on credible returns
Monitor deferred work and remaining commitments

headline: Alexandria should prioritize occupancy and cash leasing returns over headline rent increases.
summary: Vacancy remains the central operating challenge even as renewal and re-leasing rates rise. Existing tenants account for most leasing activity, while fixed-rate debt limits one financing exposure. The priority is converting tenant relationships and available space into durable rent-paying occupancy.
focusTitle: Lease space on terms that improve cash returns.
focusText: Focus commercial effort on suitable tenants and realistic occupancy gains, evaluating cash rents alongside incentives and tenant spending. Preserve financing flexibility while using the existing tenant base as a foundation for renewals and carefully chosen expansion.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Convert available space into productive occupancy
cards.text: North American operating-property occupancy was 90.9% at year-end 2025. Year-end occupancy leaves a meaningful leasing task that rental-rate increases alone cannot resolve.
items: Prioritize leasing efforts by building competitiveness
Tailor space offers to credible tenant requirements
Monitor occupied space and leasing costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Judge leasing gains on cash economics
cards.text: Annual renewal and re-leasing rental rates increased 7.0%, or 3.5% on a cash basis. The lower cash-basis increase shows why reported rental changes need an investment-return perspective.
items: Negotiate rent and incentives as one package
Stage tenant improvements against lease commitments
Monitor cash rent after leasing expenditure

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Deepen relationships while broadening tenant demand
cards.text: Existing tenants generated 82% of leasing activity over the last twelve months. Existing tenants provide substantial activity, making retention valuable while highlighting the need for additional demand sources.
items: Engage tenants before expansion and renewal decisions
Target complementary tenants for available space
Monitor renewals and new-tenant leasing separately

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve debt stability while managing property commitments
cards.text: Fixed-rate debt represented 97.2% of year-end total debt. Fixed-rate debt reduces immediate rate sensitivity, but does not remove maturity and funding obligations.
items: Sequence property spending against available funding
Preserve liquidity for debt maturities
Monitor refinancing exposure and interest coverage

headline: Align should turn higher case volumes into stronger revenue per case.
summary: Clear Aligner shipments and younger-patient starts are growing, but Clear Aligner revenue is nearly flat. Imaging growth adds support, making the priority better case economics and practice adoption rather than assuming treatment growth automatically produces equivalent revenue growth.
focusTitle: Improve conversion and treatment economics together.
focusText: Focus commercial support on practices that can convert patient interest into completed treatment starts, while evaluating pricing and product mix. Use imaging and CAD/CAM workflows to strengthen practice productivity and preserve profitable growth in younger-patient treatment.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Close the gap between cases and revenue
cards.text: Annual Clear Aligner revenue increased 0.5% to $3.245 billion. Revenue growth trails shipment growth, making realized pricing and case mix important to commercial decisions.
items: Review discounting across Clear Aligner case types
Promote treatment options with sustainable economics
Monitor revenue per case and product mix

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make shipment growth valuable for practices
cards.text: 2025 Clear Aligner shipments rose 4.7% to 2.611 million cases. Growing case volumes are more durable when practices can deliver treatment efficiently and consistently.
items: Improve clinician onboarding and treatment support
Reduce workflow obstacles to patient starts
Monitor practice activity and repeat case submissions

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support younger-patient adoption with practice execution
cards.text: 935,800 teens and children started Invisalign treatment during 2025, up 7.8%. Teen and child starts outpace overall case growth, creating a focused training and treatment-support opportunity.
items: Support clinicians serving younger treatment patients
Improve family-facing treatment education materials
Monitor starts and treatment engagement by offering

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make imaging strengthen the treatment workflow
cards.text: 2025 imaging systems and CAD/CAM services revenue rose 2.7% to $789.6 million. Imaging and CAD/CAM growth can support the aligner business when equipment adoption improves everyday practice use.
items: Link system demonstrations to actual practice workflows
Provide training that supports regular system utilization
Monitor equipment adoption and associated case activity

headline: Allegion should preserve organic momentum while making acquisitions earn their place.
summary: Organic growth, adjusted margin improvement and stronger available cash flow provide a healthy base. Acquisitions also contribute to reported expansion, so the priority is integrating them without obscuring the performance and cash productivity of the existing security business.
focusTitle: Use cash generation to support disciplined integration.
focusText: Protect the product, service and cost execution supporting organic growth. Integrate acquired operations around clear customer and operating benefits, then compare acquisition spending and ongoing investment with cash available after the business's operating needs.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve growth in the existing business
cards.text: 2025 non-GAAP organic revenue increased 4.1%; reported growth was 7.8%. Organic expansion supports further investment, with product-level demand guiding commercial and capacity decisions.
items: Prioritize security offerings showing repeat demand
Protect delivery reliability for existing customers
Monitor organic growth by product and channel

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Integrate acquired growth into sustainable operations
cards.text: Acquisitions contributed 3.1% to the full-year revenue comparison. Acquisition contribution adds scale but does not establish improved economics in the existing portfolio.

Sequence integration work around operating continuity
Monitor acquired retention and integration expenditure

Standardize avoidable operating and procurement costs
Monitor service quality alongside adjusted margin

items: Fund essential product and operating investment
Compare acquisition spending with available funding
Monitor cash conversion after integration needs

headline: Alliant Energy should separate weather recovery from durable utility earnings.
summary: Both utility businesses reported higher earnings, but the temperature comparison also improved materially. focusTitle: Plan investment around recurring load and recoverable costs.
focusText: Use weather-normalized utility performance to establish the sustainable earnings base. Align large-customer infrastructure with the renegotiated service arrangement and maintain reliable service, so stronger reported earnings support disciplined investment rather than assumptions about recurring weather benefits.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build on Interstate Power and Light's improvement
cards.text: Interstate Power and Light earned $457 million in 2025, versus $362 million reported in 2024. Higher earnings support investment, while weather and other drivers should inform the pace of spending.
items: Prioritize reliability work with clear customer benefits
Align spending with recoverable utility investment
Monitor recurring utility earnings and service quality

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Wisconsin Power and Light's contribution
cards.text: Wisconsin Power and Light annual earnings were $401 million, versus $345 million in 2024. The earnings improvement broadens support for the group and warrants business-specific operating discipline.
items: Maintain reliability through targeted asset investment
Manage controllable costs across utility operations
Monitor earnings drivers separately from weather effects

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Avoid capital commitments based on favorable weather
cards.text: 2025 temperature effects added an estimated $11 million to earnings, versus a $51 million reduction in 2024. The large temperature swing affects the comparison without establishing equivalent recurring operating improvement.
items: Use normalized demand in investment planning
Retain flexibility for less favorable temperatures
Monitor weather-adjusted earnings and energy demand

Tie spending gates to customer commitments
Monitor connection costs and load development

headline: Allstate should preserve auto underwriting gains while containing homeowners catastrophe exposure.

focusTitle: Grow policies within disciplined underwriting economics.
focusText: Protect the auto pricing and claims execution supporting profitability, and use it to pursue suitable policy growth. In homeowners, align pricing, geographic exposure and risk transfer with catastrophe experience so faster premiums translate into resilient underwriting returns.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect auto's underwriting improvement
cards.text: 2025 auto recorded combined ratio improved 10.0 points to 85.0. The lower recorded combined ratio provides a strong base, but expansion should preserve claims and pricing discipline.
items: Maintain pricing against evolving claims costs
Improve claims handling without weakening service
Monitor loss trends by policy cohort

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Translate better economics into suitable policy growth
cards.text: Year-end auto policies in force increased 2.3% to 25.504 million. Higher policies in force indicate expansion alongside improved profitability, supporting selective customer acquisition.
items: Target acquisition where underwriting economics support it
Improve retention through effective policy service
Monitor new-business quality and renewal retention

Align risk transfer with catastrophe scenarios
Monitor catastrophe losses against retained exposure

items: Adjust pricing for property-specific risk characteristics
Prioritize retention of appropriately priced policies
Monitor premium growth against noncatastrophe claims costs

headline: Altria should improve nicotine-pouch competitiveness while managing cigarette decline for cash.

cards.text: on! held 15.4% of the nicotine-pouch category in 2025, down 3.4 percentage points. Falling share despite higher shipments suggests volume growth alone is an incomplete test of progress.

Refine adult-customer offers using repeat demand
Monitor category share and promotional economics

Preserve pricing discipline across remaining demand
Monitor volume sensitivity and cash contribution

cards.label: What is working

Support retailer execution and product availability
Monitor repeat purchases and retail sell-through

items: Allocate support by product-level contribution
Reduce inventory exposure in declining oral products
Monitor total oral volume and profitability together

headline: Ameren should turn infrastructure investment into recoverable returns and dependable service.

focusTitle: Sequence investment around customer value and recovery.
focusText: Prioritize infrastructure that improves service and can earn approved returns, with funding matched to the pace of construction. Use territory-level demand and rate outcomes to guide deployment rather than treating the projected rate-base growth as an achieved result.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make investment translate into recurring utility returns
cards.text: Management attributed higher 2025 non-GAAP adjusted earnings partly to infrastructure investment and new Missouri electric rates. Management's attribution supports the importance of rates and infrastructure, with execution determining the durability of benefits.
items: Prioritize projects with clear service benefits

Monitor earned returns and reliability outcomes

items: Identify recurring load behind sales growth
Target reliability work around customer needs
Monitor weather-adjusted consumption by customer class

items: Match distribution upgrades to local load needs
Improve utilization of existing network assets
Monitor volume trends separately from rate effects

items: Stage projects against financing and recovery capacity
Preserve flexibility for construction cost changes
Monitor funding needs and regulatory milestones

items: Allocate credit limits by repayment performance
Evaluate reserve needs against portfolio composition
Monitor provisions alongside credit exposure growth

Monitor loss experience across underwriting cohorts

Improve renewal offers where pricing is adequate
Monitor comparable premiums and retention

Distinguish acquired or exited premiums in allocations
Monitor exposure quality alongside premium growth

focusText: Prioritize production quality and suppliers' readiness so backlog becomes accepted aircraft and cash. Apply the same discipline to defense programs, and base spending decisions on recurring operating cash requirements rather than assuming the Digital Aviation Solutions gain can recur.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep commercial delivery growth grounded in production quality
cards.text: 2025 commercial deliveries rose to 600 aircraft from 348 in 2024, with 1,173 net commercial orders. Higher deliveries and net orders support recovery, with reliable execution determining how much demand can be fulfilled.
items: Prioritize quality controls before production increases
Coordinate suppliers around achievable delivery schedules
Monitor customer acceptance and rework requirements

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Convert backlog without overcommitting production cash
cards.text: Year-end backlog was $682 billion, including more than 6,100 commercial aircraft valued at $567 billion. The large backlog provides visibility but also requires manufacturing capacity, working capital and dependable program execution.
items: Sequence production against executable customer commitments
Align inventory purchases with realistic build schedules
Monitor backlog conversion and delivery cash receipts

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make defense revenue growth earn adequate program returns
cards.text: Defense, Space and Security generated $27.234 billion of annual revenue, versus $23.918 billion in 2024. Higher revenue alone does not establish stronger profitability across complex defense and space programs.
items: Prioritize program milestones with clear customer acceptance
Control engineering and execution cost exposure
Monitor program contribution and cash requirements

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Build the cash recovery on recurring operations
cards.text: 2025 operating cash flow recovered to $1.065 billion from negative $12.080 billion. Earnings included a $9.6 billion Digital Aviation Solutions disposal gain. Positive operating cash flow is progress, while the disposal gain does not establish equivalent recurring earnings.
items: Budget operating commitments against delivery-driven cash
Reserve flexibility for remaining program obligations
Monitor cash conversion excluding disposal effects

headline: Booking Holdings should make travel growth and merchant expansion earn efficient customer acquisition.
summary: Room nights and bookings grew, and merchant revenue increased while agency revenue declined. Marketing spending also expanded, making the priority conversion, retention and merchant operating economics rather than treating higher booking value or a channel mix shift as sufficient evidence of better profitability.
focusTitle: Grow repeat demand while improving transaction contribution.
focusText: Prioritize customer experiences that turn discovery into completed travel and repeat usage, then evaluate marketing by incremental contribution. Support merchant operations with dependable payment and service capabilities so channel expansion improves cash and customer economics rather than adding avoidable complexity.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Convert room-night growth into durable customer relationships
cards.text: Room nights totaled 1.235 billion in 2025, an increase of 8% from 2024. Higher room nights support demand, with repeat use and dependable travel fulfillment governing its longer-term value.
items: Improve booking usability across accommodation choices
Strengthen support for completed guest stays
Monitor repeat bookings and cancellation patterns

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Separate booking-value growth from underlying travel demand
cards.text: Gross bookings reached $186.1 billion in 2025, increasing 12%, or approximately 10% on a constant currency basis. Reported and constant-currency growth differ, while room mix and pricing also inform commercial priorities.
items: Match offers to customer trip requirements
Preserve accommodation availability in active destinations
Monitor nights and constant-currency booking value separately

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make merchant expansion improve transaction economics
cards.text: Annual merchant revenue increased to $17.755 billion from $14.142 billion, while agency revenue declined to $7.968 billion from $8.524 billion. The merchant-agency shift changes operating requirements and should be evaluated through contribution and customer outcomes.
items: Improve payment and settlement reliability
Align support capacity with merchant transaction needs
Monitor contribution after payment and service costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require marketing growth to create incremental value
cards.text: Marketing expense increased to $8.186 billion in 2025 from $7.278 billion in 2024. Higher spending makes acquisition efficiency important alongside the expansion of room nights and bookings.
items: Allocate spend to channels producing profitable bookings
Improve direct repeat booking through useful service
Monitor incremental contribution and acquisition payback

headline: Boston Scientific should support cardiovascular adoption while integrating growth across the portfolio.
summary: Cardiovascular organic growth is particularly strong, with Endoscopy and Neuromodulation also expanding. Urology's reported growth substantially exceeds its organic comparison, making the priority clinical adoption, dependable supply and integration discipline rather than applying the strongest growth rate to the whole device portfolio.
focusTitle: Scale clinical use and supply around durable product economics.
focusText: Prioritize training and availability for fast-growing cardiovascular products while maintaining execution in the other specialties. Evaluate Urology's underlying demand separately from portfolio effects, and allocate capacity according to sustained procedure adoption and product contribution.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make cardiovascular growth dependable for clinical users
cards.text: Cardiovascular sales reached $13.250 billion in 2025, with non-GAAP organic growth of 20.8%. Rapid organic expansion creates opportunity if training, supply and customer support scale alongside procedure adoption.
items: Prioritize supply for sustained cardiovascular procedure demand
Expand clinician training for adopted technologies
Monitor repeat use and product availability

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Endoscopy's steady adoption contribution
cards.text: Annual Endoscopy sales were $2.916 billion, with non-GAAP organic growth of 7.7%. Organic growth supports focused investment in products and clinical support that customers continue to use.
items: Support clinician adoption within approved applications
Maintain dependable supply to active treatment centers
Monitor procedure demand and product contribution

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Distinguish Urology integration from underlying growth
cards.text: Urology annual sales were $2.709 billion, increasing 23.1% as reported and 4.7% on a non-GAAP organic basis. The reported-organic gap makes acquisition and portfolio effects important to the pace of new investment.
items: Integrate customer support across the expanded offering
Allocate capacity using underlying product demand
Monitor organic adoption and integration expenditure

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Extend Neuromodulation through durable treatment use
cards.text: Annual Neuromodulation sales were $1.199 billion, with non-GAAP organic growth of 8.0%. Organic expansion supports commercial resources focused on access, clinician execution and ongoing customer confidence.
items: Strengthen provider training and patient-start support
Address practical access barriers to treatment
Monitor continued use and product-level returns

headline: Bristol Myers should accelerate durable Growth Portfolio adoption while managing legacy erosion.
summary: The Growth Portfolio expanded, with Breyanzi and Camzyos contributing strong growth, while the Legacy Portfolio and Revlimid declined. The priority is scaling access and execution in newer therapies while aligning legacy costs and funding commitments with a smaller revenue base.
focusTitle: Build the transition around treatment adoption and contribution.
focusText: Direct commercial, access and supply resources toward growth therapies with sustainable patient uptake. Preserve valuable legacy relationships without maintaining commitments sized to earlier revenue levels, using portfolio contribution and cash generation to judge how effectively growth offsets erosion.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make Growth Portfolio expansion durable beyond the comparison
cards.text: Growth Portfolio revenue reached $26.4 billion in 2025, increasing 17% on both a reported and foreign-exchange-adjusted basis. Reported and FX-adjusted growth support the transition, with treatment adoption and contribution determining its strength.
items: Allocate resources by therapy-level uptake and returns
Strengthen payer access for growing medicines
Monitor net product contribution across growth therapies

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Align legacy commitments with lower revenue
cards.text: Legacy Portfolio revenue declined 15% as reported in 2025; Revlimid revenue declined 49%. The Legacy and Revlimid declines create a clear funding and resource-allocation task.
items: Resize commercial support around remaining patient demand
Prioritize legacy products with sustainable contribution
Monitor erosion and cash retained for growth investment

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale Breyanzi through treatment delivery capability
cards.text: Breyanzi annual revenue increased 82% as reported, or 80% excluding foreign exchange. Strong growth supports investment where access and treatment-center execution enable actual patient adoption.
items: Support treatment-center readiness for ongoing demand
Coordinate supply with scheduled treatment needs
Monitor patient starts and treatment fulfillment

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support Camzyos access and prescribing continuity
cards.text: Camzyos annual revenue increased 77% as reported, or 76% excluding foreign exchange. Rapid expansion offers a second focused opportunity, with sustained use more valuable than a single growth comparison.
items: Improve provider onboarding and treatment support
Address reimbursement barriers affecting patient access
Monitor continued treatment and net revenue quality

headline: Broadcom should preserve execution and cash conversion across both major businesses.
summary: Semiconductor Solutions and Infrastructure Software both expanded, with stronger adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow supporting the operating model. The priority is maintaining product delivery, customer retention and disciplined capital allocation rather than assuming recent growth automatically warrants uniformly higher spending.
focusTitle: Invest in durable demand while preserving strong cash economics.
focusText: Support semiconductor programs with credible customer commitments and software relationships with sustained adoption. Use recurring operating contribution and cash conversion to rank product investment, financing needs and capital returns, keeping adjusted earnings distinct from the cash available for allocation.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make semiconductor growth durable through customer execution
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 Semiconductor Solutions revenue was $36.858 billion, compared with $30.096 billion in fiscal 2024, an increase of 22%. The annual segment expansion supports investment, with product qualification and supply reliability determining practical returns.
items: Prioritize programs with confirmed customer requirements
Align supply commitments with qualified demand
Monitor product mix and customer concentration

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve software growth through adoption and retention
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 Infrastructure Software revenue reached $27.029 billion versus $21.478 billion, increasing 26%. A larger software base creates opportunity when products remain useful and customer relationships endure.
items: Improve implementation and ongoing technical support
Focus account expansion on demonstrated workflow needs
Monitor renewals and active product adoption

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep operating leverage linked to sustainable investment
cards.text: Annual non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA increased 35% to $43.004 billion from $31.897 billion. Higher adjusted EBITDA provides capacity to invest, with spending choices still requiring product and customer return tests.
items: Protect engineering behind durable customer demand
Control costs that do not improve product value
Monitor incremental expenses and adjusted operating contribution

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use cash strength for deliberate capital allocation
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 non-GAAP free cash flow was $26.914 billion, versus $19.414 billion in fiscal 2024. Higher free cash flow supports flexibility, with competing operating and financing needs guiding its use.
items: Fund essential product and operating commitments first
Rank remaining allocations by achievable returns
Monitor retained cash after investment and distributions

headline: Broadridge should rebuild closed-sales momentum while preserving recurring revenue economics.
summary: Recurring revenue and investor position counts grew, supporting the installed client base. Closed sales declined and event-driven revenue depends on variable communications activity, making the priority winning and implementing durable contracts rather than relying on activity growth or exceptional events to sustain expansion.
focusTitle: Strengthen selling and conversion around recurring client value.
focusText: Preserve reliable processing and communications services, while directing commercial effort toward funded customer requirements. Use implementation progress and recurring contribution to judge new wins, with position growth and event-driven revenue informing capacity rather than substituting for a stronger sales pipeline.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Rebuild closed sales with executable client propositions
cards.text: Closed sales declined 16% to $288 million in fiscal 2025 from $342 million in fiscal 2024. The decline weakens one source of future contracted growth even as recurring revenue expands.
items: Focus selling on funded client modernization needs
Remove obstacles between proposals and signed contracts
Monitor win rates and implementation readiness

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve recurring growth through dependable client service
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 recurring revenue rose 7% to $4.508 billion; growth was also 7% on a constant currency basis. The reported and constant-currency increase supports ongoing investment in reliable relationships and useful service expansion.
items: Improve reliability across recurring service workflows
Expand services around demonstrated client requirements
Monitor retention and incremental recurring contribution

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make position growth productive for the platform
cards.text: Equity position growth was 16% and mutual fund and ETF position growth was 7% during fiscal 2025. More positions increase service activity, with scalable processing and unit economics determining the benefit.
items: Scale processing capacity around confirmed activity
Improve efficiency in high-volume communications workflows
Monitor unit costs and client service outcomes

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Avoid building fixed commitments around event-driven revenue
cards.text: Annual event-driven revenue rose 12% to $319 million; higher mutual fund communications partly offset fewer proxy contests. Event activity contributes earnings, but communications and contest volumes can vary.
items: Flex service resources with event workload
Base fixed investment on recurring client requirements
Monitor event contribution separately from recurring economics

headline: Brown & Brown should turn acquired scale and margin gains into stronger per-share economics.
summary: Organic Revenue grew modestly and the adjusted EBITDAC margin improved, while acquisition-related revenue adds scale. Diluted earnings per share declined despite higher company net income, making the priority integration and capital efficiency rather than assuming a larger business automatically creates stronger shareholder economics.
focusTitle: Make growth improve client value and per-share contribution.
focusText: Preserve organic brokerage relationships and integrate acquired teams around retention and cost discipline. Evaluate acquisitions and financing through their recurring contribution per share, using the gap between company earnings and diluted EPS to focus capital allocation without assuming weak underlying demand.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make earnings growth translate into per-share progress
cards.text: Annual diluted net income per share declined 8.7% to $3.16, while company net income increased 6.1%. Higher company net income and lower diluted EPS make per-share contribution a separate test of expansion.
items: Evaluate acquisitions using recurring per-share contribution
Compare financing choices against expected operating returns
Monitor diluted shares and earnings contribution together

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Strengthen organic client growth alongside acquisitions
cards.text: Full-year non-GAAP Organic Revenue increased 2.8% to $4.672 billion in 2025. Positive but modest Organic Revenue growth makes retention and new-account execution important to the enlarged platform.
items: Support producers in productive existing client relationships
Improve renewal preparation and specialist customer advice
Monitor organic retention and new-account economics

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Integrate acquired scale into durable customer revenue
cards.text: The annual non-GAAP Organic Revenue reconciliation excluded $836 million of acquisition-related core commissions and fees. Management highlighted the Accession acquisition. The acquisition-related exclusion shows why organic performance and acquired contribution need separate operating plans.
items: Protect acquired-client and producer continuity
Sequence integration around customer renewal requirements
Monitor acquired retention and integration spending

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve margin improvement without weakening service
cards.text: Full-year non-GAAP adjusted EBITDAC margin increased to 35.9% from 35.2% in 2024. The higher adjusted EBITDAC margin provides support, with efficient integration and ongoing service quality governing durability.
items: Standardize useful operating and procurement practices
Protect client-facing capabilities during integration
Monitor adjusted margins alongside client outcomes

headline: Brown–Forman should restore developed-market momentum while preserving emerging-market growth.
summary: Emerging markets and Travel Retail grew organically, while the US was flat organically despite a reported decline. Developed international organic sales fell, making focused brand and distribution execution in weaker markets the priority.
focusTitle: Allocate brand investment according to local demand and returns.
focusText: Support emerging-market and Travel Retail opportunities with dependable distribution, while targeting developed-market offers and inventory to actual consumer demand. Separate organic and reported comparisons when setting commitments so portfolio and currency effects do not drive inappropriate spending decisions.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore developed international organic demand
cards.text: Developed international fiscal 2026 net sales were flat as reported and declined 3% on a non-GAAP organic basis. Flat reported sales mask an organic decline, making local commercial execution more important than the headline comparison.
items: Target brands and channels with weakening sell-through
Align distributor inventory with current consumer demand
Monitor organic sales and promotional effectiveness

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Stabilize the US through disciplined brand execution
cards.text: United States fiscal 2026 net sales declined 7% as reported and were flat on a non-GAAP organic basis. Flat organic sales give a more measured demand signal than the reported decline alone.
items: Prioritize brand offers with sustainable retailer economics
Improve availability in productive US channels
Monitor consumer sell-through and organic performance

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve emerging-market momentum with controlled expansion
cards.text: Emerging market fiscal 2026 net sales increased 14% as reported and 12% on a non-GAAP organic basis. Reported and organic growth both support opportunity, with local demand and distribution quality guiding investment.
items: Expand distribution where repeat demand supports it
Protect price realization across growing brand offers
Monitor local contribution and distributor inventory

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make Travel Retail growth repeatable at the outlet level
cards.text: Travel Retail fiscal 2026 net sales increased 6% as reported and 5% on a non-GAAP organic basis. Organic expansion supports targeted commercial investment rather than assuming all travel locations perform alike.
items: Focus assortment on productive traveler purchasing needs
Improve availability in stronger travel outlets
Monitor outlet sell-through and brand contribution

headline: Bunge should turn expanded processing scale into efficient integration and cash contribution.
summary: Reported soybean, softseed and grain volumes increased on comparisons that are neither organic nor pro forma. Significant Viterra integration spending makes reliable execution and asset-level economics the priorities as the business expands.
focusTitle: Integrate operations around profitable throughput and customer continuity.
focusText: Coordinate plants, logistics and commercial coverage across the expanded business, with processing margins and working-capital needs guiding capacity deployment. Evaluate integration spending against practical operating benefits while keeping reported volume expansion separate from evidence of improved returns.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make the larger grain network operationally productive
cards.text: Reported Grain Merchandising and Milling volume rose to 67.166 million metric tons in 2025 from 36.660 million. The reported volume change increases the importance of coordinated logistics and asset economics without proving comparable demand growth.
items: Coordinate storage and transport around customer requirements
Allocate handling capacity by contribution opportunities
Monitor network utilization and working-capital needs

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Prioritize soybean throughput with attractive economics
cards.text: Bunge processed 41.013 million metric tons of soybeans in 2025, compared with 36.824 million in 2024. Higher reported processing volumes support scale, with margins and plant reliability determining the operating benefit.
items: Match soybean purchases to viable processing opportunities
Improve plant scheduling and operating reliability
Monitor processing contribution and inventory exposure

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use softseed capacity according to product demand
cards.text: Annual softseeds processed increased to 10.751 million metric tons from 9.308 million in 2024. More throughput creates opportunity when product sales and operating economics justify the processing commitment.
items: Align processing with customer product requirements
Prioritize plants with dependable operating performance
Monitor crush economics and capacity utilization

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make integration spending earn observable operating benefits
cards.text: Corporate acquisition and integration selling, general and administrative expense for the Viterra combination was $216 million in 2025, versus $227 million in 2024. The Viterra combination requires continued resources, so cost reduction should preserve customer and operating continuity.
items: Prioritize integration work removing duplicated processes
Coordinate commercial systems around customer continuity
Monitor remaining spending and realized operating improvements

headline: BXP should turn signed leases into rent-paying occupancy and stronger recurring property earnings.
summary: Leasing volume and long contract terms provide demand visibility, but closing-quarter leased space exceeds occupancy and annual FFO per share declined. The priority is moving commitments through tenant work and rent commencement while keeping the cost of winning leases within viable property returns.
focusTitle: Make leasing activity produce cash and recurring earnings.
focusText: Prioritize delivery of signed space, preserve tenant relationships and evaluate new leases after incentives and improvement spending. Use occupancy, rent commencement and non-GAAP FFO per share together to judge whether the leasing program is improving the operating portfolio.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Move signed space into rent-paying occupancy
cards.text: The fourth-quarter portfolio was 86.7% occupied and 89.4% leased, including signed space not yet recognizing rent. The leased-occupied gap shows why contract signatures do not immediately translate into recognized rental income.
items: Resolve tenant-delivery and fit-out bottlenecks
Sequence tenant improvements against lease commencement dates
Monitor rent commencements and occupied space

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore recurring property earnings per share
cards.text: Annual non-GAAP FFO per diluted share was $6.85 in 2025, compared with $7.10 in 2024. Lower non-GAAP FFO per share makes cash leasing economics more important than leasing volume alone.
items: Prioritize leases with viable cash contribution
Control property costs without weakening tenant service
Monitor FFO alongside leasing and tenant spending

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve leasing demand with selective commercial effort
cards.text: BXP executed more than 5.5 million square feet of leases during 2025. Substantial signed space provides a foundation for recovery if customer commitments translate into durable occupancy.
items: Focus leasing teams on competitive available buildings
Match space proposals to credible tenant needs
Monitor conversion and cost of new leasing

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make long lease terms earn adequate lifetime returns
cards.text: Leases signed during 2025 had a weighted-average term of 10.1 years. Longer commitments improve visibility, but incentives and tenant improvements determine the value of the contracted rent.
items: Negotiate rent and tenant spending as one package
Match improvement investment to tenant credit quality
Monitor cash returns across committed lease terms

headline: C.H. Robinson should preserve productivity gains while rebuilding profitable freight activity.
summary: Revenue fell more than adjusted gross profit amid market and portfolio effects. Productivity and company-defined adjusted margin improved, making service quality and profitable customer activity the priorities as the workforce becomes smaller.
focusTitle: Use efficiency to strengthen customer and transaction economics.
focusText: Protect reliable freight execution and prioritize profitable shipments. Separate divestiture and surcharge effects from retained-business activity, using gross profit per transaction and cost to serve to turn productivity gains into durable growth.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Build growth around transaction contribution
cards.text: Annual non-GAAP adjusted gross profit fell 1.3% to about $2.7 billion; management said higher LTL, truckload and customs gross profit per transaction offset ocean pressure. The smaller adjusted gross-profit decline suggests transaction economics offer a better decision anchor than revenue alone.
items: Prioritize freight with sustainable transaction contribution
Develop productive LTL and customs relationships
Monitor volume and gross profit by service

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve productivity through reliable shipment execution
cards.text: Management reported double-digit annual productivity improvement in North American Surface Transportation and high-single-digit improvement in Global Forwarding. Productivity creates durable value when customers retain dependable logistics support.
items: Standardize repeatable shipment and customer workflows
Redeploy staff toward complex customer requirements
Monitor shipment reliability and retained customers

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep the smaller workforce capable of supporting growth
cards.text: The company-defined, non-GAAP adjusted operating margin reached 29.1%, up 490 basis points; average employee headcount fell 11.5%. This margin is not measured against revenue. A smaller workforce must sustain customer service alongside adjusted-margin gains.
items: Align staffing with actual transaction workload
Retain expertise in complex freight and customs needs
Monitor service failures and employee capacity

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Rebuild retained-business demand rather than headline revenue
cards.text: Annual revenue fell 8.4% to $16.2 billion; management cited the European surface transportation divestiture, lower ocean pricing and volumes, and lower truckload fuel surcharges. Management's cited divestiture, ocean and surcharge effects require separate commercial and operating responses.
items: Target customer shipments within retained service lines
Match ocean capacity arrangements to viable demand
Monitor retained volumes separately from fuel surcharges

headline: Cadence should convert broad design demand into durable adoption and backlog revenue.
summary: Core EDA, IP and hardware adoption all provide positive signals, with year-end backlog supporting visibility. The priority is sustaining customer implementation and renewals while converting contracted work on schedule, rather than treating prospective revenue recognition or hardware customer additions as completed recurring growth.
focusTitle: Support customer execution across software, IP and hardware.
focusText: Prioritize implementation that deepens design-platform use, repeat IP adoption and productive hardware deployments. Track backlog conversion against contract requirements, keeping hardware timing and customer concentration visible in capacity and commercial decisions.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Core EDA adoption through customer execution
cards.text: Core EDA grew 13% in 2025; management cited hyperscalers, digital full-flow deployments and AI-driven products. Management's cited drivers support demand, with renewals and deployed workflows determining its durability.
items: Improve onboarding across integrated design workflows
Support customers deploying AI-driven design products
Monitor renewals and adoption by customer group

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make IP adoption lead to repeat design relationships
cards.text: IP grew nearly 25% in 2025; management cited HBM, UCIe, PCIe, DDR and SerDes adoption. Faster IP growth supports investment in qualified customer designs and dependable technical integration.
