items: Prioritize support for adopted interface IP families
Improve integration help during customer design cycles
Monitor repeat design wins and customer expansion

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn hardware customer breadth into productive use
cards.text: Hardware added over 30 customers in 2025; seven of the ten largest customers bought both Palladium Z3 and Protium X3. New customers and dual-system adoption support opportunity, while repeat demand depends on successful deployment.
items: Support effective Palladium and Protium implementation
Align supply with confirmed customer installations
Monitor utilization and follow-on hardware orders

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Convert contracted work without overstating realized growth
cards.text: Year-end backlog was $7.8 billion, with $3.8 billion of remaining performance obligations expected to become revenue during the following twelve months. The following-twelve-month recognition expectation is forward-looking, making execution and acceptance milestones central to visibility.
items: Coordinate delivery resources with contract obligations
Resolve customer acceptance and implementation bottlenecks
Monitor backlog conversion and recognition timing

headline: Camden should improve rental growth and cost control before stretching capital commitments.
summary: Same-property revenue grew slowly while expenses rose faster, limiting NOI improvement. Liquidity covers the stated remaining development funding but also supports other obligations, making the priority stronger property economics and selective capital allocation rather than evaluating buybacks or development independently.
focusTitle: Protect property contribution and reserve funding flexibility.
focusText: Improve rent and retention outcomes while targeting controllable expenses, then stage development and repurchases against all cash obligations. Use market-level property returns and lease-up progress to decide where capital can strengthen recurring earnings without weakening financial flexibility.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve property earnings beyond modest revenue growth
cards.text: Same-property expenses increased 1.7% in 2025, while same-property net operating income increased 0.3%. Expenses outpaced same-property revenue, leaving little NOI growth and making local operating execution important.
items: Target controllable maintenance and service costs
Review supplier contracts without weakening resident experience
Monitor expense growth and property-level contribution

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Balance rental pricing with resident retention
cards.text: Same-property revenue increased 0.8% in 2025 compared with 2024. The modest revenue increase calls for pricing and leasing decisions tailored to local demand.
items: Adjust rent offers to market-specific demand
Improve renewal service for valuable resident relationships
Monitor rent realization and resident retention

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Stage development around total funding needs
cards.text: At December 31, 2025, Camden had $635.2 million of liquidity and approximately $213.8 million remaining to fund its wholly-owned development pipeline. Year-end liquidity exceeds remaining development funding, but debt and operating obligations still compete for cash.
items: Prioritize completion of committed development work
Maintain funding capacity for debt and operating needs
Monitor remaining construction costs and lease-up progress

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make repurchases compete with property investment
cards.text: Camden repurchased approximately 2.53 million common shares in 2025 for $270.6 million, at an average price of $106.92. Buybacks return capital while reducing funds available for development, existing properties and financial flexibility.
items: Compare repurchases with property-level return opportunities
Pace buybacks after committed funding requirements
Monitor retained liquidity and recurring per-share contribution

headline: Capital One should integrate Discover while preserving credit quality and funding value.
summary: Reported card activity and deposits expanded on a base including Discover from May 18, 2025. A lower card charge-off rate and stronger auto originations provide support, making the priority comparable customer economics and integration rather than treating acquired scale as equivalent to organic progress.
focusTitle: Make the larger franchise earn durable risk-adjusted returns.
focusText: Preserve customer and deposit relationships through integration, with cohort credit performance guiding lending decisions. Separate acquired balances and activity from existing-business trends, and allocate growth according to contribution after losses and funding costs rather than reported volume alone.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn acquired card scale into lasting customer activity
cards.text: Reported Domestic Card purchase volume rose 27% to $812.221 billion in 2025. The reported purchase increase includes Discover, so comparable spending and retained accounts are the useful commercial tests.
items: Protect cardholder service through integration
Improve engagement across existing and acquired accounts
Monitor comparable purchase activity and account retention

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Validate better card losses at the cohort level
cards.text: The Domestic Card full-year net charge-off rate was 5.12% in 2025, compared with 5.91% in 2024. The improved reported rate needs interpretation alongside acquisition accounting and the changed portfolio mix.
items: Maintain underwriting discipline across card portfolios
Target early support to emerging repayment stress
Monitor delinquencies and losses by acquisition cohort

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep auto growth within sound underwriting economics
cards.text: Annual auto loan originations increased 19% to $40.996 billion from $34.542 billion. Higher originations add future credit and collateral exposure alongside earning assets.
items: Price originations for borrower and collateral risk
Align lending approvals with repayment capacity
Monitor subsequent losses and used-vehicle exposure

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve deposit value through integration
cards.text: Consumer Banking average deposits rose to $379.915 billion from $303.873 billion, while their annual average rate fell to 3.02% from 3.23%. Lower average pricing and larger balances provide support, while acquired-account retention determines the durability of benefits.
items: Maintain effective service for acquired deposit accounts
Align pricing with relationship value and funding needs
Monitor retention and funding cost by account group

headline: Cardinal Health should preserve better distribution economics while funding specialty growth carefully.
summary: Pharmaceutical and Specialty profit improved despite lower revenue, while Medical Products and Distribution and smaller businesses also strengthened. The priority is sustaining contract and service economics, with adjusted cash flow used carefully when ranking acquisition, debt and operating investment needs.
focusTitle: Back profitable customer relationships and disciplined cash deployment.
focusText: Preserve specialty and distribution improvements through reliable execution and contract economics, then assess the smaller businesses separately for growth quality. Allocate capital using recurring cash requirements and acquisition contribution rather than sales totals or adjusted cash flow in isolation.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect pharmaceutical contribution beyond revenue scale
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 Pharmaceutical and Specialty Solutions revenue declined 3% to $204.6 billion, while segment profit increased 12% to approximately $2.3 billion. The divergence between revenue and segment profit shows why mix and contract terms matter to returns.
items: Prioritize specialty relationships with viable contract economics
Preserve reliable fulfillment for existing customers
Monitor product mix and customer contribution

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make medical distribution's improvement sustainable
cards.text: Global Medical Products and Distribution annual revenue rose 2% to $12.6 billion, while segment profit increased 47% to $135 million. The earnings gain comes from a relatively small profit base, making continued execution important.
items: Improve product availability for healthcare customers
Target distribution and sourcing cost efficiency
Monitor recurring segment contribution and service quality

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Allocate smaller-business growth resources individually
cards.text: Annual revenue in Other increased 19% to $5.4 billion, with segment profit rising 22% to $516 million. The Other grouping contains distinct businesses whose investment needs and economics should not be assumed identical.
items: Rank at-Home and Nuclear opportunities by returns
Evaluate OptiFreight growth with service capacity needs
Monitor organic contribution separately from acquired growth

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Use cash capacity after actual funding obligations
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 non-GAAP adjusted free cash flow was $2.5 billion. Adjusted free cash flow supports assessment, while available cash depends on the adjustments and competing commitments.
items: Fund essential distribution and operating investment
Rank acquisitions against debt and funding needs
Monitor operating cash after excluded payments

headline: Carnival should preserve stronger voyage economics while continuing to reduce leverage.
summary: Modest passenger growth accompanied better constant-currency net yield and fuel efficiency. Lower adjusted leverage adds flexibility, making cash generation after vessel investment and further debt reduction the priorities.
focusTitle: Protect yield and efficiency while retaining cash for debt reduction.
focusText: Allocate voyage and fleet decisions according to ticket, onboard and operating contribution, preserving dependable guest experiences. Use available cash after required vessel spending to strengthen financing flexibility, with debt maturities and interest costs visible alongside the adjusted leverage measure.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve yield through pricing and onboard value
cards.text: Annual non-GAAP net yield per available lower berth day was $208.30 on a constant currency basis in 2025, versus $197.33 in 2024. The non-GAAP yield improvement reflects more than ticket prices, so commercial decisions should consider the full voyage economics.
items: Match ticket offers to voyage demand
Improve relevant onboard experiences and purchasing opportunities
Monitor net yield and variable selling costs

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make modest passenger growth commercially productive
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 passengers increased to 13.6 million and passenger cruise days to 101.7 million. Higher passengers and cruise days support activity, while voyage mix and customer value determine the earnings contribution.
items: Align itineraries with sustained guest demand
Improve guest service supporting repeat cruises
Monitor occupancy and contribution by voyage type

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Embed lower fuel intensity in fleet operations
cards.text: Annual fuel consumption per thousand available lower berth days fell to 29.2 metric tons from 30.9. Improved intensity supports efficiency, while total fuel costs still depend on prices and deployed capacity.
items: Preserve efficient vessel operating practices
Prioritize efficiency investments with credible cash returns
Monitor fuel intensity alongside vessel utilization

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn lower leverage into enduring funding flexibility
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 non-GAAP net debt to adjusted EBITDA fell to 3.4 times, nearly one turn below 2024. The improved adjusted ratio is encouraging, with actual debt and cash obligations still guiding capital allocation.
items: Prioritize debt needs after required vessel investment
Align refinancing with scheduled cash generation
Monitor maturities and cash interest requirements

headline: Carrier should turn commercial and service strength into broader sales recovery.
summary: Commercial HVAC and aftermarket are growing strongly, yet organic sales still declined. Carrier therefore needs a more balanced demand engine while protecting service economics. The gap between reported and adjusted margins, alongside substantial shareholder distributions, makes recurring cash profitability the right constraint on expansion.
focusTitle: Build around the installed base while repairing the weaker demand mix.
focusText: Allocate selling and operating resources toward commercial conversion and service attachment, with separate recovery plans for weaker equipment markets. Fund those priorities from repeatable operating earnings before allowing distributions to determine the investment envelope.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Commercial growth needs a stronger consolidated payoff
cards.text: Organic sales fell 1% despite double-digit commercial HVAC and aftermarket growth, excluding NORESCO. Strong pockets are not yet sufficient to carry the whole portfolio.
items: Separate residential order trends from commercial project demand
Prioritize commercial backlog conversion and installation readiness
Measure equipment growth alongside price and product mix

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Manage to repeatable operating profitability
cards.text: The 10.0% operating margin trails the 15.1% adjusted measure. Resource decisions should reflect which costs recur as commercial and service activity expands.
items: Assign recurring costs to equipment and service economics
Tie capacity additions to sustainable operating contribution
Monitor whether reported margin follows adjusted improvement

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make aftermarket growth more durable
cards.text: Double-digit aftermarket growth, excluding NORESCO, offers a useful counterweight to equipment weakness. Deepening customer relationships can extend that benefit beyond the initial equipment purchase.
items: Attach maintenance agreements to commercial equipment installations
Improve parts availability for the active installed base
Monitor service renewals and contribution by customer cohort

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Preserve investment capacity after cash returns
cards.text: Approximately $3.7 billion of dividends and repurchases creates a substantial competing use of funds. Commercial delivery and service expansion still require operating capacity and working capital.
items: Reserve funding for parts, technicians and project execution
Test distributions against operating cash and investment needs
Keep repurchases responsive to equipment demand uncertainty

headline: Carvana should protect per-vehicle economics as retail volume expands.
summary: A 43% increase in retail units is supported by meaningful GAAP operating profitability, making execution at higher throughput the central issue. Adjusted EBITDA also looks strong, but the consolidated noncash earnings benefit should not be treated as funding for capacity or evidence of better vehicle economics.
focusTitle: Scale reconditioning and delivery at the pace of profitable demand.
focusText: Expand throughput where vehicle preparation, inventory turnover and delivery reliability can sustain operating contribution. Use operating cash generation and GAAP operating economics to govern spending, keeping consolidated earnings effects separate from parent-attributable results.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Capacity must keep pace with retail growth
cards.text: Carvana sold 596,641 retail vehicles in 2025, up 43%. That growth raises the value of reliable reconditioning throughput and disciplined vehicle sourcing.
items: Align vehicle purchases with local reconditioning capacity
Remove bottlenecks in inspection and preparation workflows
Monitor delivery delays and reconditioning cost per vehicle

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the operating profit earned on each sale
cards.text: GAAP operating income reached $1.881 billion with a 9.3% margin. Preserving that contribution matters more than adding units that strain fulfillment economics.
items: Compare contribution across vehicle types and sales markets
Allocate capacity toward profitable inventory turnover
Track transport expense and returns alongside unit growth

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Translate adjusted profitability into funding capacity
cards.text: Adjusted EBITDA was $2.237 billion at an 11.0% margin. Expansion decisions need to consider cash absorbed by inventory and the operating infrastructure behind those earnings.
items: Budget inventory growth alongside reconditioning investment
Evaluate facility additions against operating cash generation
Monitor cash conversion as retail throughput rises

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep noncash income out of expansion assumptions
cards.text: Consolidated net income of $1.895 billion included a $621 million net noncash benefit. That benefit does not establish recurring cash available to support more vehicle sales.
items: Base recurring spending on operating earnings and cash
Separate noncash benefits in capacity investment cases
Distinguish consolidated results from parent-attributable earnings

headline: Casey's should convert food and loyalty growth into stronger store productivity.
summary: Prepared food and dispensed beverages are leading comparable inside-sales growth, while fuel profitability benefits from a wider margin as well as modest gallon growth. The enlarged store network and rewards base create opportunities, but food execution and repeat visits must justify the operating complexity of that reach.
focusTitle: Connect the food offer, rewards activity and store economics.
focusText: Use loyalty offers to build repeat food purchases, support kitchens with disciplined labor and waste management, and judge footprint expansion on store contribution. Keep fuel volume and cents-per-gallon profitability separate when allocating resources.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the food growth engine
cards.text: Inside same-store sales rose 4.2%, with prepared food and dispensed beverages up 5.2%. Kitchen execution should preserve the contribution from this stronger category.
items: Match kitchen staffing to food ordering patterns
Improve food availability while controlling preparation waste
Monitor food contribution after labor and ingredients

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Do not build fixed costs around fuel margins
cards.text: Fuel margin rose to 42.6 cents per gallon from 38.7 cents, while same-store gallons increased 1.4%. Profit improvement therefore exceeds the underlying volume increase.
items: Set fuel pricing with local gallon retention in view
Stress-test store budgets against lower fuel margins
Track fuel-to-inside purchase conversion by location

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make rewards membership produce repeat purchases
cards.text: Nearly 10.5 million rewards members provide substantial reach across 2,944 stores. Membership is more valuable when it produces incremental visits and profitable inside purchases.
items: Target food offers around demonstrated purchase occasions
Measure repeat visits among active rewards customers
Evaluate offer contribution after redemption and discount costs

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Require new stores to earn their place
cards.text: The footprint increased to 2,944 stores from 2,904. Growth should improve network economics rather than obscure how existing stores perform.
items: Separate new-location contribution from mature-store sales gains
Standardize food execution across added and existing stores
Allocate expansion capital using store-level cash returns

headline: Caterpillar should recover price and margin discipline while converting higher volume.
summary: Higher volume is producing sales growth, but unfavorable price realization and lower margins show that more activity is not translating proportionately into profit. Strong enterprise cash flow provides room to execute, although repurchases and dividends also compete for those resources. The priority is profitable production and pricing discipline.
focusTitle: Turn incremental equipment volume into better operating contribution.
focusText: Coordinate pricing, manufacturing schedules and dealer demand so volume growth improves earnings quality. Preserve investment in productive capacity and service execution, and let sustainable cash generation determine the room for shareholder returns.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Improve the value captured from additional volume
cards.text: Higher volume added $3.4 billion to annual sales growth, partly offset by $0.8 billion of unfavorable price realization. More units need to carry adequate contribution.
items: Review discount approvals by equipment family and market
Match production schedules to dealer order conversion
Monitor incremental contribution after price concessions

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Address the operating margin deterioration
cards.text: Operating margin fell to 16.5% from 20.2%; adjusted margin also declined to 17.2% from 20.7%. The shared direction points to a substantive profitability priority.
items: Identify plant and product lines diluting contribution
Prioritize productivity work that protects delivery reliability
Track margin recovery alongside volume and price realization

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use cash strength to support better execution
cards.text: Enterprise operating cash flow of $11.7 billion and year-end enterprise cash of $10.0 billion provide operating flexibility. Deployment should strengthen the production and customer-support economics.
items: Fund bottleneck removal with clear operating paybacks
Preserve liquidity for inventory and dealer demand shifts
Measure cash conversion across equipment production cycles

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Balance distributions against the margin repair effort
cards.text: Repurchases of $5.2 billion and dividends of $2.7 billion were meaningful cash uses in 2025. Continued returns should leave room to address weaker operating conversion.
items: Reserve funding for manufacturing and service priorities
Assess payouts against cash after essential investment
Adjust repurchases to changes in order and cash trends

headline: Cboe should protect options competitiveness while preserving richer contract economics.
summary: Full-year net revenue grew strongly, and fourth-quarter options activity benefited from both higher volume and higher revenue per contract. Yet fourth-quarter market share declined. The priority is to preserve the value of the index-options mix while improving customer participation, without assuming favorable market activity will persist.
focusTitle: Grow options participation without giving away contract value.
focusText: Use product, distribution and execution investment to deepen the options franchise. Judge commercial incentives on incremental contribution and retained order flow, distinguishing full-year revenue progress from the fourth-quarter operating indicators.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build on the broader revenue advance
cards.text: Full-year net revenue reached $2.4 billion, up 17%. That provides a stronger base for investment, but the allocation should reinforce durable customer and product relationships.
items: Prioritize investment in products with repeat customer usage
Link technology spending to trading capacity and reliability
Monitor revenue contribution across product and service lines

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Convert higher options activity into repeat participation
cards.text: Fourth-quarter options average daily volume increased 24%. Cboe should use stronger activity to expand recurring engagement rather than size operating commitments solely around the quarter.
items: Improve onboarding and connectivity for options participants
Maintain execution reliability during heavier trading sessions
Track customer activity across changing market conditions

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Defend share through execution and distribution
cards.text: Fourth-quarter options market share declined to 29.2% from 30.4%, despite volume growth. Participation gains need to be assessed relative to the broader options market.
items: Investigate order-flow losses by product and participant group
Target liquidity programs at economically attractive lost flow
Measure retained share after incentives and execution changes

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Preserve the value of the index-options mix
cards.text: Fourth-quarter options revenue per contract rose 13%, partly from greater index-options mix. Mix benefits can support revenue without establishing equivalent pricing improvement across every product.
items: Separate product mix from within-product pricing trends
Support index-options distribution with targeted customer education
Evaluate fee incentives against net contract contribution

headline: CBRE should turn balanced business growth into dependable cash generation.
summary: Resilient and transactional businesses both grew at similar rates, giving CBRE more than one source of momentum. Operating cash flow and a large servicing portfolio support that breadth. The main opportunity is to expand repeatable client relationships while ensuring transaction growth and servicing obligations translate into cash rather than added working-capital strain.
focusTitle: Use recurring client relationships to strengthen the cash base.
focusText: Deepening resilient services and disciplined loan servicing can support investment through changing transaction conditions. Allocate talent and technology to profitable client coverage, and require transaction expansion to demonstrate cash contribution as well as revenue growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen resilient client relationships
cards.text: Revenue in resilient businesses rose 13%. These activities offer a useful platform for broader client engagement and should earn investment where contract economics remain attractive.
items: Expand services within existing property and occupier accounts
Protect contract pricing against staffing and delivery costs
Monitor renewals and cash contribution by client relationship

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make transactional growth economically selective
cards.text: Transactional businesses grew revenue 14% in 2025. Sustaining that progress requires deploying brokers and support resources where completed activity produces attractive contribution.
items: Allocate specialist coverage to productive transaction opportunities
Manage transaction staffing against completed deal economics
Track pipeline conversion and receivables after deal completion

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Translate revenue breadth into spendable cash
cards.text: Operating cash flow was approximately $1.6 billion. Growth across different business models should be assessed through collections and the cash needed to deliver services.
items: Strengthen billing and collection processes on growing accounts
Compare investment proposals with cash after operating needs
Monitor working-capital absorption across services and transactions

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Scale servicing controls with the loan portfolio
cards.text: The loan servicing portfolio ended 2025 at $459 billion. Its scale makes operational quality, borrower responsiveness and servicing capacity important complements to portfolio growth.
items: Match servicing teams and systems to account complexity
Prioritize exception resolution and timely borrower communication
Monitor servicing costs, errors and client retention

headline: CDW should restore profit conversion while backing small business and healthcare demand.
summary: Small Business and healthcare sales grew strongly, while education weakened. At the same time, lower hardware margin rates and administrative costs growing faster than sales reduced the benefit of demand growth. The priority is to direct coverage toward attractive customer opportunities while tightening the cost and product economics of delivery.
focusTitle: Combine targeted sector growth with tighter selling economics.
focusText: Invest in productive Small Business and healthcare relationships, adapt education coverage to its weaker demand, and manage hardware pricing and support costs together. Measure success through gross profit and operating contribution, not sales growth alone.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build profitable small-business relationships
cards.text: Small Business segment sales rose 13.3%. The opportunity is to retain these customers and broaden their technology relationships without allowing support effort to outrun account contribution.
items: Prioritize repeat purchasing and account development opportunities
Bundle appropriate support with profitable hardware transactions
Monitor gross profit after small-account servicing costs

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Give healthcare and education different plans
cards.text: Healthcare customer sales increased 13.3%, while education declined 1.8%. A uniform coverage budget would miss the different demand conditions across these customer groups.
items: Direct specialist coverage toward qualified healthcare demand
Align education inventory and staffing with purchasing activity
Compare sector pipeline conversion and customer contribution

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Recover value in hardware selling
cards.text: Gross margin slipped to 21.7% from 21.9%, with management citing lower rates in certain hardware categories. Product selection and commercial terms should protect gross profit dollars.
items: Review discounting in affected hardware categories
Balance product mix with customer fit and contribution
Monitor category gross profit after vendor and fulfillment terms

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Stop overhead from consuming sales growth
cards.text: Selling and administrative costs rose 9.0%, faster than 6.8% sales growth. Expanding coverage needs to produce sufficient account economics to support the added expense.
items: Link incremental selling spend to qualified gross-profit opportunities
Simplify repetitive ordering and account-support workflows
Track sales productivity and administrative cost per account

headline: Cencora should make distribution investment and acquisition integration earn their operating cost.
summary: RCA-related expense growth and a narrow reported operating margin put execution quality at the center of the investment case. International Healthcare Solutions adds a distinct earnings base, while the announced U.S. distribution plan creates future capacity opportunities. The priority is disciplined integration and capacity economics, including cold-chain service quality.
focusTitle: Build distribution capability with clear contribution and service milestones.
focusText: Coordinate RCA integration, international operations and proposed U.S. capacity around customer demand and dependable fulfillment. Stage future spending to useful capacity and operating cash needs, preserving the distinction between announced investment and money already spent.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make RCA integration improve the delivery model
cards.text: Management linked higher distribution and administrative expenses partly to the January 2025 RCA acquisition. Integration should produce an effective operating network rather than permanent duplication.
items: Map overlapping distribution and administrative workflows
Standardize service processes without disrupting customer fulfillment
Monitor integration expense alongside customer retention and contribution

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Protect thin reported operating economics
cards.text: GAAP operating margin was 0.82%, compared with adjusted margin of 1.31%. Small changes in fulfillment or administrative costs can materially affect reported operating contribution.
items: Prioritize error reduction and productive distribution workflows
Evaluate customer terms against full cost to serve
Monitor reported margin as integration spending evolves

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use international scale selectively
cards.text: International Healthcare Solutions generated $30.4 billion of revenue and $648.3 million of adjusted operating income. Resource allocation should preserve contribution across its own market and service mix.
items: Compare customer and market contribution within international operations
Direct resources toward reliable and profitable healthcare distribution
Monitor working capital alongside adjusted operating income

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Stage the planned distribution build against demand
cards.text: The announced $1 billion U.S. investment plan through 2030 includes cold-chain capacity. It is a forward-looking commitment, whose value depends on useful capacity and execution.
items: Sequence capacity projects around customer fulfillment requirements
Include temperature-controlled handling costs in investment cases
Monitor project spending, utilization and cold-chain service reliability

headline: Centene should improve medical-cost economics before relying on administrative savings.
summary: Higher health benefits ratios, especially in Commercial, are the central earnings pressure. Lower adjusted SG&A helps but does not resolve insured-care costs. The priority is better underwriting and care economics, supported by clear claims development and payment planning.
focusTitle: Prioritize benefit pricing, care management and claims visibility together.
focusText: Focus Commercial product decisions on observed care costs and member needs, while examining medical-cost trends across the wider portfolio. Preserve useful administrative efficiencies, but retain the claims and care-management capability needed to improve underwriting economics.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Medical-cost pressure needs an operating response
cards.text: The annual health benefits ratio rose to 91.9% from 88.3%. More premium is being consumed by benefits, increasing the importance of pricing and effective care management.
items: Analyze utilization and unit-cost trends by covered population
Align provider and care-management efforts with costly care patterns
Monitor medical-cost performance against premium and benefit assumptions

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Give Commercial a focused economics plan
cards.text: Commercial health benefits ratio increased to 87.9% from 77.3%. This deterioration deserves product and market-level action rather than a uniform response across every insurance business.
items: Reassess Commercial pricing and benefit designs by market
Identify care categories driving unfavorable Commercial cost changes
Evaluate product contribution before expanding member acquisition

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve useful administrative efficiency
cards.text: The adjusted SG&A expense ratio fell to 7.4% from 8.5%. These savings help, provided they do not weaken the functions needed to address medical-cost pressure.
items: Protect claims accuracy and care-management operating capacity
Simplify administrative work that does not improve member service
Monitor service performance alongside the adjusted expense ratio

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Connect claims reserves to emerging care costs
cards.text: Medical claims liabilities rose to $20.544 billion from $18.308 billion. The balance needs to be understood with claims timing and cost development, without assuming it proves reserve inadequacy.
items: Examine claims development by care category and service period
Align cash planning with expected benefit payment patterns
Monitor payment timeliness and changes in reserve assumptions

headline: CenterPoint should turn Houston reliability gains into disciplined capacity expansion.
summary: Reported Houston outage improvement is encouraging, while the larger capital plan and earlier load-growth forecast increase execution demands. Non-GAAP earnings growth provides support but does not by itself fund the build. The priority is to prioritize useful grid capacity, preserve reliability and align future investment with funding and customer demand.
focusTitle: Sequence the grid build around reliability and validated load needs.
focusText: Use actual connection requirements and operational performance to rank projects within the announced plan. Coordinate construction, funding and customer commitments so the response to forecast demand strengthens service without outrunning the resources needed to deliver it.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the reliability improvement
cards.text: Management reported over 100 million fewer customer outage minutes in Houston Electric during 2025. Investment choices should preserve that customer benefit as network demands increase.
items: Identify the grid interventions supporting outage improvement
Prioritize maintenance and hardening with clear reliability benefits
Monitor outage frequency and duration as load increases

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Translate earnings progress into financial capacity
cards.text: Non-GAAP EPS rose 9% to $1.76, compared with GAAP EPS of $1.60. Capacity decisions should reflect recurring earnings and cash available after existing system needs.
items: Connect recurring operating earnings to available investment funding
Model cash needs alongside planned capital deployment
Monitor financing requirements as construction spending ramps

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make the larger capital plan executable
cards.text: The announced 2026–2035 capital investment plan increased to $65.5 billion. Its forward-looking scale calls for disciplined project selection and delivery capacity.
items: Rank projects by reliability, connection need and readiness
Secure construction resources around executable project schedules
Monitor project costs and funding against approved scope

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Validate the timing of Houston load additions
cards.text: Management forecasts 50% Greater Houston peak-load growth by 2029, two years earlier than previously forecast. That increases urgency without making every projected connection certain.
items: Confirm customer connection milestones before committing related capacity
Stage network additions around substantiated load requirements
Test project sequencing under slower and faster load scenarios

headline: CF Industries should protect the selling-price benefit against higher gas costs.
summary: Selling prices improved across every segment, while sales volumes were roughly flat and ammonia production increased. Higher natural gas costs therefore deserve close attention before attributing stronger pricing to better underlying volume demand. Project and incident impairments also argue for selective capital deployment rather than assuming all capacity investment earns attractive returns.
focusTitle: Run the ammonia network for contribution and disciplined capital returns.
focusText: Coordinate production, gas procurement and product allocation around achievable netbacks. Protect reliable operations and challenge the economics of impaired projects, so pricing gains support cash contribution after ongoing plant and capital requirements.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve productive ammonia capacity
cards.text: Gross ammonia production rose to approximately 10.1 million tons from 9.8 million. Higher output is useful when it supports reliable customer delivery and profitable product conversion.
items: Prioritize maintenance that protects dependable ammonia output
Align plant utilization with product demand and inventory
Monitor production efficiency and contribution by facility

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Manage the gas-cost exposure within product economics
cards.text: Average natural gas cost, including realized derivatives, rose to $3.31 per MMBtu from $2.40. Higher selling prices need to be evaluated after that input-cost increase.
items: Assess gas procurement against expected plant operating needs
Compare product netbacks after delivered gas costs
Monitor margin sensitivity across gas and selling-price scenarios

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Do not mistake price recovery for volume expansion
cards.text: Average selling prices increased across all segments, but total sales volumes approximated 2024. Commercial decisions should distinguish attractive pricing from incremental customer demand.
items: Allocate output toward stronger realized product netbacks
Match inventory commitments to actual customer orders
Track price, volume and mix contributions separately

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make project decisions respond to impairment evidence
cards.text: Two fourth-quarter impairments totaled $76 million, including the electrolyzer project and the Yazoo City incident. These items call for project-specific operating and capital responses.
items: Reassess remaining project spending against achievable economics
Prioritize incident remediation that restores reliable operations
Track project cash requirements separately from impairment charges

headline: Charles River should align discovery and safety capacity with weaker customer demand.
summary: Weaker Discovery and Safety Assessment revenue and margin outweigh modest Research Models and Services growth. The reported-versus-non-GAAP margin gap adds urgency. The priority is matching laboratory capacity to sustainable customer work while preserving study quality.
focusTitle: Restore discovery and safety utilization without weakening study quality.
focusText: Target customer conversion and resource scheduling in Discovery and Safety Assessment, while preserving the more stable Research Models and Services base. Adjust the operating footprint to support recurring contribution and cash needs rather than relying on adjusted profitability alone.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Rebuild a more dependable organic revenue base
cards.text: Consolidated organic revenue declined 1.6% in 2025. The business needs better conversion of customer research requirements into delivered work before adding broad operating capacity.
items: Prioritize customer opportunities with clear study requirements
Review cancellation and start-date patterns by service line
Match hiring and capacity decisions to executable demand

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Focus the margin response on Discovery and Safety
cards.text: Discovery and Safety Assessment organic revenue fell 2.6%, and non-GAAP operating margin declined to 24.2% from 25.7%. Utilization and commercial execution should be managed together.
items: Align laboratory staffing with confirmed study schedules
Improve study handoffs and scheduling to reduce idle capacity
Monitor service contribution alongside study delivery quality

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the steadier research-models franchise
cards.text: Research Models and Services organic revenue grew 1.2%. Its modest growth offers a useful base, though expansion should remain proportionate to demonstrated customer needs.
items: Preserve reliable research-model availability and customer service
Target appropriate service extensions within existing customer relationships
Monitor repeat orders and contribution before expanding capacity

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make recurring costs visible in footprint decisions
cards.text: GAAP operating margin was 0.6%, versus 19.8% on a non-GAAP basis. That gap matters when assessing which operations can fund investment and support continuing research services.
items: Include continuing costs in facility and staffing decisions
Link restructuring spending to specific capacity improvements
Monitor cash delivery alongside reported and adjusted margins

headline: Charles Schwab should convert strong asset gathering into deeper, durable client relationships.
summary: Asset inflows, new accounts, trading and managed-investing flows all advanced strongly. The priority is lasting client relationships and dependable service at higher scale, with investment focused on retained assets and account engagement rather than assuming trading activity keeps accelerating.
focusTitle: Connect account acquisition, asset retention and appropriate managed investing.
focusText: Invest in client onboarding and advisor support where they improve relationship depth. Preserve dependable trading service and assess growth through retained assets, funded accounts and client outcomes, so higher engagement produces relationships that remain valuable across market conditions.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Retain the assets arriving on the platform
cards.text: Core net new assets were $519.4 billion, up 42%, representing 5.1% organic growth. Retention and useful client engagement can make these flows more valuable over time.
items: Strengthen service for clients transferring substantial asset relationships
Identify avoidable friction in transfers and asset consolidation
Monitor retained assets and relationship depth after onboarding

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make new accounts become active relationships
cards.text: Clients opened 4.7 million new brokerage accounts, up 13%. Account growth creates value when customers fund them and find dependable ongoing service.
items: Simplify account funding and first-use onboarding steps
Tailor support to clients with incomplete account activation
Track funded-account retention and ongoing service needs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Scale trading infrastructure without overcommitting costs
cards.text: Daily average trades reached 7.7 million, up 31%. Strong usage calls for reliable capacity, while activity-sensitive economics require flexibility if market participation changes.
items: Stress-test trading systems for concentrated activity periods
Improve support workflows around trading and execution problems
Match variable service capacity to observed activity patterns

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Deepen managed investing with client fit
cards.text: Managed investing net flows reached $68 billion, up 36%. The next priority is maintaining service quality and suitable solutions as advisory relationships expand.
items: Improve handoffs between brokerage service and advisory teams
Allocate advisor capacity around client complexity and needs
Monitor managed-relationship retention and client service outcomes

headline: Charter should turn network investment into customer adoption and cash returns.
summary: Stronger operating cash flow supports substantial network investment. Internet, mobile and rural reach create monetization opportunities, but the priority is converting availability into retained customers and contribution after the capital needed to serve them.
focusTitle: Link each network build to adoption, service quality and cash contribution.
focusText: Coordinate rural sales, installation capacity and mobile cross-selling around the expanded network. Use consistent customer definitions after reporting-policy changes, and prioritize further construction according to take-up and capital productivity rather than passings alone.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Deepen the Internet and mobile relationship
cards.text: Charter ended 2025 with 29.7 million Internet customers and 11.8 million mobile lines. The combination offers a retention and cross-selling opportunity if service economics remain attractive.
items: Target mobile offers to appropriate existing Internet households
Coordinate support across Internet installation and mobile activation
Measure relationship retention using consistent reporting definitions

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Convert rural availability into paying connections
cards.text: Charter activated 483,000 subsidized rural passings during 2025. Network availability only becomes productive capital when customers connect and receive reliable service.
items: Coordinate local acquisition with completed rural network availability
Ensure installation capacity matches rural customer sign-ups
Monitor rural take-up and contribution after installation costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require line extensions to show capital productivity
cards.text: Annual capital expenditures were $11.7 billion, including $3.9 billion for line extensions. Construction sequencing should reflect achievable customer adoption and the cost of serving additional locations.
items: Rank extensions by demand evidence and construction readiness
Control project scope and installation costs by build area
Monitor capital per connection alongside service reliability

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use stronger cash flow to sustain execution
cards.text: Operating cash flow increased to $16.1 billion from $14.4 billion. That improvement supports the build, though investment needs determine how much financial flexibility remains.
items: Plan network spending against operating cash after recurring needs
Preserve funding for maintenance and customer service
Track cash conversion as new areas begin generating revenue

headline: Chevron should make production growth deliver stronger returns on capital.
summary: Production and reserves advanced, and structural cost reductions provide useful support. Yet return on capital employed declined materially, showing that greater operating scale is not enough by itself. The priority is to protect cash and project economics while directing investment toward the production and reserves with the strongest sustainable contribution.
focusTitle: Optimize the expanded production base before committing further capital.
focusText: Combine operating reliability and structural savings with selective project funding. Judge reserve additions and production growth by development requirements, realized contribution and capital returns, preserving flexibility when commodity economics change.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn higher production into profitable throughput
cards.text: Worldwide oil-equivalent production increased 12%, with U.S. production up 16%. The enlarged operating base needs dependable infrastructure and disciplined production economics.
items: Prioritize reliability in the larger U.S. production footprint
Coordinate production schedules with available processing and transport
Monitor unit operating costs and contribution by asset

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make structural savings durable
cards.text: Chevron reported $1.5 billion of structural cost reductions in 2025. These savings can improve resilience if they remain embedded without undermining safe and reliable asset operations.
items: Standardize operating practices behind repeatable cost reductions
Protect maintenance and workforce capabilities supporting asset reliability
Track recurring savings against production and service performance

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Treat reserve replacement as an investment pipeline
cards.text: Reserve replacement reached 158%, with year-end proved reserves of approximately 10.6 billion BOE. Reserve additions need to translate into attractive production economics before they justify development spending.
items: Rank reserve development by capital intensity and expected contribution
Stage project spending around infrastructure and execution readiness
Monitor development costs and conversion into producing assets

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore capital productivity across the portfolio
cards.text: Return on capital employed fell to 6.6% from 10.1%, despite production growth and cost reductions. The portfolio needs closer discipline around the earnings produced by committed capital.
items: Challenge low-return assets and discretionary expansion proposals
Direct capital toward projects with resilient operating economics
Track capital returns alongside production growth and savings

headline: Chipotle should rebuild restaurant traffic while keeping expansion economically disciplined.
summary: Comparable sales declined because transaction losses outweighed a higher average check. New restaurants and digital ordering add reach, but lower volumes and wage inflation are also pressuring labor economics. The priority is to improve repeat visits and restaurant throughput so expansion strengthens contribution rather than compensating for weaker existing-store demand.
focusTitle: Improve the guest visit before relying on more locations or higher checks.
focusText: Use menu execution, digital convenience and restaurant staffing to support transaction recovery. Continue evaluating new units and Chipotlanes on local demand and contribution, while matching labor deployment to service requirements and order volumes.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Traffic needs a specific recovery plan
cards.text: Comparable restaurant sales fell 1.7%, with transactions down 2.9% and average check up 1.2%. Higher spending per visit did not offset fewer customer transactions.
items: Identify visit occasions with weaker customer repeat activity
Improve food availability and order accuracy during peak periods
Evaluate offers on incremental visits and restaurant contribution

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make expansion earn its operating complexity
cards.text: Chipotle opened 334 company-owned restaurants, including 257 with a Chipotlane. New capacity should complement local demand rather than obscure weaker comparable-store traffic.
items: Assess new-unit demand alongside nearby restaurant performance
Sequence openings with trained managers and crew availability
Monitor new-restaurant contribution and nearby sales displacement

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use digital reach to improve convenience
cards.text: Digital orders represented 36.7% of annual food and beverage revenue. That channel can support repeat purchasing when preparation, pickup and restaurant operations work smoothly together.
items: Improve pickup readiness and digital order accuracy
Coordinate digital capacity with kitchen and front-line demand
Monitor repeat digital purchases and fulfillment-related complaints

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Protect service while improving labor productivity
cards.text: Labor rose to 25.1% of revenue from 24.7%, with management citing lower volumes and wage inflation. Staffing decisions need to address both throughput and guest experience.
items: Match crew schedules to channel-specific order patterns
Train teams to reduce preparation and handoff bottlenecks
Track labor hours per transaction alongside service quality

headline: Chubb should preserve commercial underwriting strength while tightening catastrophe exposure.
summary: North America Commercial P&C improved its combined ratio, and overseas and life premiums expanded. Personal P&C moved in the other direction as catastrophe losses increased. The priority is differentiated underwriting: preserve profitable commercial growth, reassess catastrophe-sensitive personal exposures, and ensure expanding international and life businesses retain sound economics.
focusTitle: Allocate growth capacity according to risk-adjusted underwriting performance.
focusText: Use commercial execution as a base while applying product- and geography-specific controls in Personal P&C. Support overseas and life distribution selectively, with pricing, claims capability and capital requirements evaluated alongside premium growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the commercial underwriting advantage
cards.text: North America Commercial P&C improved its annual combined ratio to 81.4% from 83.9%. Growth should protect the selection and pricing discipline supporting that result.
items: Prioritize commercial renewals with attractive risk-adjusted contribution
Maintain underwriting authority tied to exposure complexity
Monitor claims development as commercial premium opportunities expand

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Reassess personal catastrophe economics
cards.text: North America Personal P&C combined ratio rose to 91.5% from 83.6%, with higher catastrophe losses. Exposure accumulation deserves a focused response even though the ratio remains below 100%.
items: Review catastrophe concentrations by geography and insured property
Align pricing and coverage terms with risk characteristics
Evaluate reinsurance and retention choices against portfolio exposure

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Grow overseas without weakening underwriting standards
cards.text: Overseas General net premiums written rose 7.5%, or 8.0% in constant dollars. Expansion should be evaluated through local underwriting performance rather than currency-translated volume alone.
items: Target distribution in markets with attractive underwriting economics
Match claims resources to growing local policy portfolios
Monitor local-currency premium growth and loss experience together

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Support life growth with appropriate capital and service
cards.text: Life net premiums written increased 15.1% to $7.279 billion. Faster growth increases the importance of product economics, persistency and the resources needed to support policyholders.
items: Assess new life business against product-specific capital needs
Expand policy service capacity alongside distribution activity
Monitor persistency and emerging claims by product cohort

headline: Church & Dwight should rebuild domestic demand while protecting margin quality.
summary: International growth offsets some domestic weakness, while the vitamin exit partly explains modest organic growth. Different reported and adjusted margin trends require attention to recurring costs. The priority is domestic demand execution supported by selective international investment.
focusTitle: Redirect resources toward stronger brand demand and sustainable contribution.
focusText: Use the portfolio transition to focus selling and brand investment on continuing businesses with attractive repeat purchasing. Address domestic shelf and consumer execution, preserve productive international growth, and keep reported costs visible in investment decisions.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Separate portfolio cleanup from continuing demand
cards.text: Organic sales increased 0.7%, including a 130-basis-point drag from the exited vitamin business. The exit affects comparisons, but the remaining portfolio still needs convincing demand progress.
items: Redirect vitamin-related resources toward productive continuing brands
Separate exit effects from ongoing category sales performance
Monitor continuing-business volume and contribution after transition costs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Give domestic brands a focused demand plan
cards.text: Consumer Domestic organic sales declined 0.5%. Improving core U.S. performance requires brand- and category-specific commercial action rather than relying on international growth to offset weakness.
items: Identify domestic categories losing repeat purchases or distribution
Improve shelf availability and product value communication
Evaluate promotions on incremental volume and gross profit

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Back international growth where economics support it
cards.text: International organic sales grew 5.5%, outperforming the domestic business. Investment should reinforce the markets and brands producing sustainable demand and acceptable cost to serve.
items: Prioritize distribution gains in productive international markets
Adapt brand investment to demonstrated local purchase patterns
Monitor market contribution after logistics and selling costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect margin beyond the adjusted presentation
cards.text: Adjusted gross margin held at 45.2%, while reported gross margin declined 100 basis points. The operating plan should account for cash and recurring costs behind that difference.
items: Build brand investment plans around sustainable gross profit
Assign transition costs to specific operational improvements
Monitor reported margin alongside mix and pricing decisions

headline: Ciena should turn optical growth into stronger margin and cash conversion.
summary: Optical growth provides a strong demand engine, but lower margin, customer concentration and working-capital needs complicate its value. The priority is profitable program delivery, broader repeat demand and better conversion of revenue into cash.
focusTitle: Coordinate optical program delivery with commercial and cash discipline.
focusText: Use customer deployment schedules to manage inventory, billing and production capacity. Protect margin in major optical contracts and broaden repeat demand beyond the largest accounts, so higher revenue produces usable cash and a more resilient customer base.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Convert optical momentum into durable deployment relationships
cards.text: Optical networking revenue increased to $3.246 billion from $2.643 billion. Reliable execution can deepen customer relationships, provided investment follows actual deployment requirements.
items: Align engineering and supply capacity with confirmed deployments
Prioritize installation readiness and customer acceptance milestones
Monitor repeat optical orders and program contribution

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Manage concentration without weakening strategic accounts
cards.text: Two customers each exceeded 10% of annual revenue and together represented 28.4%. Their deployment decisions therefore deserve close attention alongside efforts to broaden the customer base.
items: Map major-account commitments to production and engineering capacity
Develop additional optical customers using established deployment capabilities
Test operating plans against delayed large-customer orders

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Release cash from deployment working capital
cards.text: Average days sales outstanding were 88 and product inventory turns were 2.7. Growth planning should account for billing timing and the stock required to fulfill customer projects.
items: Resolve acceptance and billing blockers on completed deployments
Match component purchases to executable customer schedules
Monitor aged receivables and inventory by optical program

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Improve the gross profit earned on optical growth
cards.text: GAAP gross margin declined to 42.0% from 42.8%. Stronger optical sales need careful product, contract and delivery economics to translate into better profitability.
items: Review contract pricing against product and deployment costs
Prioritize engineering work that improves manufacturing economics
Track gross contribution by product and major customer program

headline: Cigna should improve earnings conversion in pharmacy and healthcare services.
summary: Services revenue outpaces adjusted operating income, particularly in Pharmacy Benefit Services, while Healthcare medical costs increased. The HCSC transaction also affects revenue comparisons. The priority is service-level contribution and medical-cost management in the continuing business.
focusTitle: Focus on profitable service delivery and continuing-business healthcare economics.
focusText: Address the cost and contract mix behind weaker pharmacy earnings conversion while protecting Specialty and Care Services growth. Reassess Healthcare pricing and care-management assumptions using the continuing portfolio, keeping transaction effects separate from operating demand.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve specialty growth while improving conversion
cards.text: Specialty and Care Services adjusted revenue grew 14%, while adjusted pre-tax operating income increased 8%. Demand is expanding, but contribution is growing more slowly than activity.
items: Prioritize specialty contracts with attractive cost-to-serve economics
Improve coordination across care delivery and customer support
Monitor adjusted operating contribution alongside service growth

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Repair pharmacy contract and delivery economics
cards.text: Pharmacy Benefit Services adjusted revenue increased 18%, while adjusted pre-tax operating income declined 2%. Revenue growth is not currently producing stronger segment operating earnings.
items: Evaluate contract renewals using full service delivery costs
Identify administrative and fulfillment costs reducing contract contribution
Track client retention alongside adjusted operating margin

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Respond to the higher medical care ratio
cards.text: Cigna Healthcare medical care ratio rose to 84.4% from 83.2%. Pricing and care-management decisions need to reflect emerging medical costs rather than rely on services growth elsewhere.
items: Analyze utilization and unit costs by healthcare product
Align provider engagement with higher-cost care pathways
Monitor medical costs against premium and benefit assumptions

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Plan around the continuing healthcare portfolio
cards.text: Healthcare adjusted revenue declined 11%, but increased 7% excluding the HCSC transaction. Capacity and commercial decisions should reflect that underlying growth and the changed business scope.
items: Reset operating resources for the post-transaction portfolio
Assess continuing-product contribution alongside underlying revenue growth
Separate transaction effects in staffing and investment plans

headline: Cincinnati Financial should make agency expansion produce profitable new business.
summary: Underwriting remains profitable and written premiums increased, but agency-written new business declined despite substantial agency appointments. The priority is to improve the productivity of the distribution network while preserving risk selection. Premium growth should be assessed through new-customer contribution and renewal quality rather than assuming more agencies automatically strengthen organic demand.
focusTitle: Turn distribution reach into disciplined policy growth.
focusText: Help productive agencies convert suitable prospects, strengthen onboarding for newly appointed partners and use underwriting feedback to improve submissions. Preserve the long record of underwriting profitability while separating new-business production from renewal-driven premium growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the underwriting discipline behind profitable growth
cards.text: The annual combined ratio was 94.9%, extending underwriting profit to 14 consecutive years. Distribution expansion should preserve the pricing and selection standards behind that record.
items: Maintain exposure-based pricing and underwriting authority
Review new-business loss experience alongside mature renewals
Monitor combined ratios by line as agency reach expands

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make premium growth earn an adequate return
cards.text: Property and casualty net written premiums increased 9%, exceeding $10 billion. The next test is whether the additional premium carries attractive underwriting contribution.
items: Separate renewal pricing, exposure changes and new policy growth
Prioritize lines with sound risk-adjusted underwriting economics
Monitor premium growth alongside claims development and retention

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Reverse weaker agency new-business production
cards.text: Annual agency-written new business premiums declined 4%. Improving submission quality and conversion offers a clearer operating priority than simply adding more distribution locations.
items: Identify agencies with falling qualified submissions or conversion
Improve underwriting response on suitable new customer opportunities
Track new-business production and early policy performance

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require agency appointments to become productive
cards.text: Cincinnati appointed 420 agencies, including 71 selling only personal lines. New partners need practical support and appropriate product access to justify the added distribution effort.
items: Tailor onboarding to personal-only and broader agency partners
Provide targeted product training and submission support
Monitor activation and profitable production by appointment cohort

headline: Cintas should preserve service productivity while managing transaction-related demands.
summary: Organic revenue and both gross and operating margins improved. The priority is preserving those service economics as customer activity expands, while managing UniFirst transaction expenses so recurring route productivity and customer execution retain adequate resources.
focusTitle: Keep customer growth and service efficiency advancing together.
focusText: Allocate growth resources where route density, reliable delivery and customer retention reinforce each other. Maintain visibility into recurring operating contribution and transaction-related spending, using the margin gains to support productive service capacity rather than assuming every new account is equally valuable.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build on broad organic customer demand
cards.text: Fiscal 2026 organic revenue grew 8.3%. Continued growth should deepen productive customer relationships while maintaining dependable service across the expanded account base.
items: Target additional services within well-served customer relationships
Prioritize new accounts that fit existing service coverage
Monitor retention and contribution across customer cohorts

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve the gross-margin improvement
cards.text: Gross margin reached 50.7%, compared with 50.0%. The operating task is to retain the delivery and service economics supporting that improvement as demand expands.
items: Improve route density and service scheduling where practical
Manage product availability and replacement costs by service line
Monitor account gross profit alongside service reliability

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make incremental growth support operating leverage
cards.text: Operating margin increased to 23.1% from 22.8%. Further investment should strengthen productive service capacity without allowing support costs to outrun profitable customer growth.
items: Link hiring and fleet additions to service demand
Simplify administrative work around recurring customer delivery
Track incremental operating contribution by service geography

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Contain transaction costs and management distraction
cards.text: Fiscal 2026 operating income included $15.1 million of UniFirst transaction expenses. These costs call for bounded workstreams while the underlying customer service operation continues to grow.
items: Assign clear budgets and owners to transaction work
Protect frontline service and customer retention resources
Monitor transaction spending separately from recurring operating performance

headline: Cisco should convert AI demand while restoring the broader Networking business.
summary: AI infrastructure orders and Security growth provide opportunity, while Networking revenue declined and Services grew modestly. The priority is profitable AI delivery alongside a broader networking recovery, supported by durable product adoption and customer service.
focusTitle: Connect emerging infrastructure demand to durable product and service economics.
focusText: Prioritize executable AI deployments without treating orders as realized revenue. Address weaker Networking categories and use services to support adoption and retention, while evaluating Security growth through sustainable customer economics rather than assuming the revenue increase is wholly organic.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn AI infrastructure orders into delivered value
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 AI infrastructure orders from webscale customers exceeded $2 billion. The immediate opportunity is delivery execution and customer adoption, not simply adding more order commitments.
items: Align component supply and engineering with confirmed webscale deployments
Manage acceptance milestones and installation readiness with customers
Monitor order conversion and contribution after delivery costs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Rebuild the broader Networking revenue base
cards.text: Networking revenue declined 3% to $28.304 billion. AI opportunities should complement a product-specific response to weakness in the larger networking business.
items: Identify networking categories with weaker renewal or upgrade demand
Focus sales coverage on justified customer modernization needs
Monitor product demand separately from AI order announcements

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make Security growth deepen customer relationships
cards.text: Security revenue increased 59% to $8.094 billion. The priority is durable adoption and contribution across the portfolio, without inferring an organic growth rate from the total increase.
items: Coordinate security deployment support across customer environments
Prioritize renewals and useful product adoption within accounts
Track customer retention and support costs alongside revenue

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep services aligned with the changing product mix
cards.text: Services revenue grew 3% to $15.046 billion. Product growth is more valuable when customers receive dependable support and the associated service work remains profitable.
items: Attach appropriate support to AI and security deployments
Match technical service capacity to customer implementation needs
Monitor service renewals and contribution across product cohorts

headline: Citigroup should preserve transaction-services growth while containing rising credit risk.
summary: Cross-border and clearing activity expanded, and the efficiency ratio improved, suggesting useful franchise and operating progress. Higher non-accrual loans introduce a different pressure, while shareholder returns make capital discipline important. The priority is to retain the transaction-services momentum without allowing weaker credit performance to consume the benefit of efficiency gains.
focusTitle: Grow fee and transaction relationships within a disciplined credit envelope.
focusText: Back productive cross-border client activity and continue useful operating simplification. At the same time, focus credit resources on deteriorating exposures and evaluate capital distributions against risk needs, earnings capacity and the 13.2% year-end CET1 position.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen the transaction-services franchise
cards.text: Cross-border transaction value increased 10%, and U.S. dollar clearing volume rose 5%. These activities provide opportunities to strengthen operating relationships with existing institutional clients.
items: Expand relevant cash-management services within active client relationships
Protect payment reliability and exception-resolution capacity
Monitor client retention and transaction contribution after service costs

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve efficiency gains that support client service
cards.text: The annual efficiency ratio improved to 64.7% from 66.4%. Further simplification should reduce avoidable expense while preserving the controls and service capabilities behind transaction growth.
items: Simplify duplicate operating processes and manual payment handling
Link technology spending to recurring service cost improvements
Monitor efficiency alongside client service and control performance

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Respond early to deteriorating loan exposures
cards.text: Total non-accrual loans increased 35% to $3.6 billion. Credit remediation and exposure selection deserve specific attention rather than relying on operating efficiency to offset losses.
items: Prioritize borrower reviews in deteriorating credit portfolios
Develop exposure-specific workout and collateral action plans
Monitor non-accrual migration and realized credit losses

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep capital returns responsive to credit conditions
cards.text: Year-end CET1 was 13.2% after approximately $17.6 billion of common shareholder returns. Distribution decisions should preserve room for changing credit requirements and productive client growth.
items: Stress-test capital against adverse credit migration scenarios
Prioritize lending opportunities by risk-adjusted capital contribution
Adjust repurchases to earnings and capital-generation capacity

headline: Citizens should make Private Bank growth durable before stretching capital distributions.
summary: Management describes Private Bank deposit growth, strong year-end equity returns and positive bottom-line accretion. The priority is sustaining those segment economics through retained relationships and reliable service, while preserving capital for growth alongside shareholder distributions.
focusTitle: Deepen Private Bank relationships with disciplined funding and capital use.
focusText: Use deposit relationships to build appropriate client services and recurring contribution. Assess the reported profitability and accretion against the resources needed to sustain the business, and keep shareholder distributions responsive to the bank’s funding and growth requirements.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Retain the Private Bank deposit base
cards.text: The Private Bank ended 2025 with $14.5 billion of deposits. Those balances are most valuable when supported by durable client relationships and appropriate funding economics.
items: Strengthen relationship coverage for significant deposit clients
Offer cash-management services suited to client liquidity needs
Monitor deposit retention, concentration and funding cost

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve the economics behind reported segment returns
cards.text: Management reported a 25% Private Bank return on equity at year-end. Growth decisions should preserve the relationship quality and capital efficiency supporting that disclosed return.
items: Evaluate relationship expansion using full service and capital costs
Allocate banker capacity to productive client coverage
Monitor segment returns as staffing and client balances grow

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Turn accretion into repeatable operating contribution
cards.text: Management described the Private Bank as contributing 7% bottom-line accretion. Sustaining that contribution requires retained clients and scalable service delivery.
items: Separate recurring client contribution from setup-related spending
Improve onboarding and service workflows as relationships expand
Monitor incremental contribution after support and technology costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Leave room to fund the growing franchise
