cards.text: Citizens reported an 80% return of capital to shareholders for the year. That distribution choice should be balanced against funding stability and investment in the Private Bank.
items: Reserve capital for sound relationship growth and credit needs
Assess distributions alongside deposit stability and operating investment
Keep repurchases responsive to changing bank capital requirements

headline: Clorox should normalize demand after ERP shipments while preserving genuine margin gains.
summary: Organic sales and cash flow improved, but advance ERP shipments supplied much of sales growth and part of the margin benefit. The priority is dependable replenishment and sustainable demand and profitability after shipment timing normalizes.
focusTitle: Use sell-through and replenishment to guide the post-ERP operating plan.
focusText: Coordinate production and retailer inventory around actual consumption rather than forward shipments. Preserve the gross-margin improvements beyond the estimated ERP contribution, and use cash strength to support reliable systems and fulfillment execution.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Establish the continuing demand baseline
cards.text: Organic sales increased 5%, while reported sales were essentially flat. The difference makes a clear view of the continuing business important before broadening commercial spending.
items: Separate portfolio and currency effects from continuing sales demand
Evaluate brand investment using consumer and retailer sell-through
Monitor repeat purchasing alongside continuing-business sales trends

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Manage the unwind of advance ERP shipments
cards.text: Advance ERP-related shipments added approximately 3.5–4 percentage points to annual sales. Subsequent replenishment may differ from the shipment pattern that supported the reported year.
items: Align production with retailer inventory and consumption
Coordinate ERP transition plans with major customer replenishment
Monitor service levels and orders as shipment timing normalizes

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the margin improvement beyond shipment timing
cards.text: Gross margin increased 220 basis points to 45.2%, with an estimated 50-basis-point ERP shipment contribution. A meaningful part of the improvement therefore needs separate operational protection.
items: Preserve productive sourcing and manufacturing cost improvements
Assess promotions against gross profit after fulfillment costs
Monitor normalized margin as ERP shipment effects fade

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Turn stronger cash flow into transition resilience
cards.text: Operating cash flow increased to $981 million from $695 million. Deployment should support dependable ERP operations and the working capital required for normal replenishment.
items: Reserve cash for systems stabilization and supply continuity
Match inventory spending to post-transition customer demand
Monitor cash conversion after advance shipments normalize

headline: CME should deepen global participation while preserving reliable interest-rate liquidity.
summary: Average daily volume grew across the overall franchise, with particularly strong metals activity and faster international participation. Interest-rate contracts remain a major source of activity. The priority is to turn this broad engagement into durable customer relationships and dependable execution, while keeping operating commitments proportionate to market-sensitive trading volumes.
focusTitle: Expand access and product depth around trusted execution.
focusText: Preserve the interest-rate liquidity base while allocating targeted distribution and capacity investment to metals and international demand. Judge those investments through retained participation, reliable clearing and contribution across different market activity conditions.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build on broad exchange participation
cards.text: Annual average daily volume reached 28.1 million contracts, up 6%. The operating opportunity is to preserve reliable access and customer engagement as more activity runs through the platform.
items: Maintain trading and clearing capacity for concentrated activity
Improve onboarding and connectivity for productive participants
Monitor customer participation and system performance across products

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect the interest-rate liquidity anchor
cards.text: Interest-rate average daily volume increased 4% to 14.2 million contracts. Its scale makes dependable liquidity and effective customer risk-management access central operating priorities.
items: Support liquidity across relevant interest-rate contract maturities
Coordinate customer education with practical hedging needs
Monitor execution quality and repeat institutional participation

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make metals momentum durable
cards.text: Metals average daily volume increased 34% to 988,000 contracts. Strong activity merits targeted development, while capacity and product commitments should remain grounded in continuing customer usage.
items: Identify recurring commercial and financial metals use cases
Support market access and liquidity in active contracts
Evaluate product investment against retained participation and contribution

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Scale international coverage without diluting service
cards.text: International average daily volume grew 8% to 8.4 million contracts. Broader geographic participation requires accessible distribution and consistent trading and clearing support.
items: Align regional sales coverage with active customer needs
Improve international access to product and clearing education
Monitor regional participation after distribution and support costs

headline: CMS Energy should preserve utility earnings gains while containing operating-cost growth.
summary: Higher electric revenue and gas operating income support investment, but maintenance costs also increased. The priority is productive system spending and reliable service, using recurring earnings and cash rather than revenue growth to guide allocation.
focusTitle: Protect reliable utility service through productive operating spending.
focusText: Use the stronger gas contribution and electric revenue base to support necessary maintenance and customer needs. Rank work by reliability and operating value, and connect adjusted and reported earnings to the cash required to maintain the system.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn electric revenue into sustainable system value
cards.text: Electric utility revenue rose to $5.638 billion from $5.061 billion. Revenue growth should support reliable service and operating contribution, without assuming it directly represents higher customer usage.
items: Separate demand, pricing and other revenue drivers in planning
Prioritize electric operating work with clear reliability benefits
Monitor electric contribution after maintenance and service costs

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve stronger gas operating contribution
cards.text: Gas utility operating income increased to $671 million from $534 million. The focus should be maintaining dependable delivery and the operating practices supporting that contribution.
items: Prioritize gas-system work that protects safe delivery
Maintain staffing and contractor capacity for essential service needs
Monitor gas operating costs alongside service performance

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Control maintenance expense through better work execution
cards.text: Maintenance and other operating expenses rose to $1.727 billion from $1.638 billion. Cost control should improve work productivity while preserving necessary system maintenance.
items: Improve scheduling and coordination of recurring maintenance tasks
Review contractor and material spending by work program
Monitor cost per completed job and reliability outcomes

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep earnings measures tied to funding needs
cards.text: GAAP diluted EPS was $3.53, compared with adjusted EPS of $3.61. Investment and operating commitments should reflect the cash demands of utility service as well as recurring earnings.
items: Align operating budgets with cash after essential system spending
Evaluate adjustments by their effect on continuing funding capacity
Monitor reported earnings and cash conversion together

headline: Coca-Cola should broaden volume momentum beyond pricing and Zero Sugar.
summary: Pricing supported price/mix and Zero Sugar delivered strong volume growth, while other categories were mixed. The priority is broader, repeatable beverage demand, with selective brand investment and cash allocation that preserve growth capacity alongside dividends.
focusTitle: Build affordable, repeatable beverage demand across the portfolio.
focusText: Support Zero Sugar where demand is strong, use category-specific plans for weaker beverages, and evaluate pricing through volume and consumer response. Preserve investment that improves availability and execution while matching distributions to sustainable cash generation.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make pricing support durable consumer demand
cards.text: Full-year price/mix increased 4%, primarily from pricing actions. The commercial priority is to preserve contribution without allowing price realization to mask weaker purchase frequency or category demand.
items: Evaluate pack and price options by market purchase occasion
Coordinate pricing with availability and promotional effectiveness
Monitor volume response and contribution after price changes

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Extend the Zero Sugar growth engine
cards.text: Coca-Cola Zero Sugar volume increased 14% across geographic segments. Strong demand supports targeted availability and brand investment, with execution tailored to local markets.
items: Improve Zero Sugar availability in productive channels
Support sampling and marketing around demonstrated consumer demand
Monitor repeat purchasing and contribution by geographic market

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Give weaker beverage categories a distinct plan
cards.text: Juice, value-added dairy and plant-based volume declined 3%, while water, sports, coffee and tea grew 2%. Portfolio investment should reflect those different demand patterns.
items: Identify weaker category and market combinations requiring action
Refine assortment and execution around profitable consumer occasions
Allocate category support using volume and contribution trends

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Preserve growth investment alongside dividends
cards.text: Capital expenditures were $2.1 billion and dividends were $8.8 billion. Both uses of cash need to fit the operating resources required to support availability and brand growth.
items: Prioritize capital projects with clear distribution or capacity benefits
Assess dividends against cash after operating and investment needs
Monitor investment delivery and continuing cash generation

headline: Cognizant should convert large-deal bookings into profitable delivery.
summary: Bookings and large-deal contract value expanded, while constant-currency revenue and operating margin also improved. The priority is to translate signed demand into delivered work without straining staffing or contract economics. The booking-to-revenue relationship signals opportunity, but it does not establish when revenue will be recognized or how profitable each engagement will be.
focusTitle: Build delivery readiness around the work clients are prepared to start.
focusText: Coordinate client transitions, staffing and account management across the larger deal pipeline. Protect the improved operating margin through disciplined project economics, and distinguish currency translation and signed contract value from underlying delivered growth.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn bookings into executable client work
cards.text: Trailing-twelve-month bookings rose 5% to $28.4 billion, approximately 1.3 times revenue. Converting that demand requires practical scope, staffing and client-start readiness.
items: Prioritize mobilization for contracts with confirmed client milestones
Resolve scope and transition dependencies before adding delivery capacity
Monitor bookings conversion and delayed project starts

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make large deals manageable delivery commitments
cards.text: Cognizant signed 28 large deals, with management reporting nearly 50% growth in large-deal total contract value. Larger engagements increase the importance of transition quality and contract-specific economics.
items: Assign experienced transition leadership to complex large engagements
Stage hiring around contracted work and mobilization progress
Monitor delivery quality and contribution by large-deal cohort

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve underlying revenue momentum
cards.text: Revenue increased 6.4% in constant currency, versus 7.0% as reported. The underlying advance is useful evidence of delivery growth beyond favorable translation effects.
items: Expand relevant services within active client relationships
Allocate sales coverage to qualified funded client demand
Monitor constant-currency growth alongside account retention

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Protect margin as delivery volume scales
cards.text: GAAP operating margin rose to 16.1%, while adjusted operating margin was 15.8%. Investment decisions should preserve productive delivery economics rather than assume adjusted measures are necessarily higher.
items: Match skills deployment and subcontracting to project requirements
Address contract changes that erode planned delivery contribution
Monitor utilization and recurring operating margin together

headline: Coherent should convert Networking growth into durable margins and lower debt.
summary: Networking growth and stronger gross margin improve the operating mix, while Materials remains weaker. Debt repayment adds flexibility. The priority is profitable Networking delivery, demand-led Materials capacity and sustainable cash generation for investment and debt reduction.
focusTitle: Allocate capacity to profitable Networking demand and tighten the weaker portfolio.
focusText: Coordinate production, product investment and customer schedules around the expanding Networking business. Require a distinct demand and cost plan for Materials, and use sustainable operating cash to balance growth investment with further debt reduction.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support the Networking growth engine
cards.text: Networking revenue increased to $3.421 billion from $2.296 billion. The scale of that advance makes supply readiness and customer execution important to preserving growth quality.
items: Align manufacturing capacity with confirmed Networking customer schedules
Prioritize engineering work supporting productive product demand
Monitor delivery performance and contribution by Networking product

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Adapt Materials to its lower demand base
cards.text: Materials revenue declined to $953.8 million from $1.017 billion. Resources should reflect the weaker activity without compromising attractive customer and product positions.
items: Identify Materials applications with weaker orders and utilization
Adjust production and inventory to executable customer demand
Target commercial effort toward profitable repeat Materials business

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve the stronger gross-margin foundation
cards.text: GAAP gross margin improved to 35.2% from 30.9%. Growth investment should retain the product and manufacturing economics behind that progress, rather than pursue revenue without adequate contribution.
items: Evaluate new orders against product-level manufacturing contribution
Preserve quality and productivity improvements in expanding facilities
Monitor gross margin alongside Networking and Materials mix

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep debt reduction compatible with operating needs
cards.text: Coherent repaid approximately $437 million of debt during fiscal 2025. Further repayment should retain funding for delivery capacity and working capital in the growing business.
items: Reserve cash for confirmed production and customer commitments
Prioritize growth projects with clear cash-generation economics
Monitor liquidity after capital spending and debt repayments

headline: Coinbase should make trading gains support a more durable services franchise.
summary: Trading volume and share expanded sharply, supported by growing services and USDC balances. The priority is retained customer relationships and dependable platform service, with investment that broadens contribution while remaining flexible if trading activity changes.
focusTitle: Convert higher participation into retained relationships and resilient contribution.
focusText: Invest in dependable trading, useful subscription services and responsible stablecoin product execution. Evaluate each growth channel through customer retention, operating costs and cash contribution, keeping capacity flexible across different trading and balance conditions.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make higher trading activity operationally dependable
cards.text: Total Coinbase trading volume reached $5.2 trillion, up 156%. That growth increases the importance of reliable execution, customer support and scalable platform capacity.
items: Strengthen platform capacity around concentrated trading demand
Improve resolution of trading and account-service problems
Monitor execution reliability and cost per active relationship

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Retain the customers behind higher market share
cards.text: Crypto trading-volume market share reached 6.4%, approximately twice the prior year. The commercial task is to keep that participation through useful products and dependable service.
items: Identify customer needs driving repeat trading participation
Improve onboarding and continued use of relevant platform features
Track retained activity after acquisition and incentive costs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Deepen recurring service value
cards.text: Subscription and services revenue reached $2.8 billion. Expanding this base can improve relationship breadth if products remain useful and profitable after support and operating costs.
items: Prioritize service features with demonstrated ongoing customer use
Connect trading customers with appropriate subscription offerings
Monitor service retention and contribution by product

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep USDC growth aligned with liquidity and product economics
cards.text: Average USDC balances in Coinbase products reached $17.8 billion. Larger balances merit careful attention to customer access, operational controls and the economics of associated services.
items: Maintain dependable USDC transaction and redemption workflows
Evaluate product spending under changing balance conditions
Monitor balance retention, liquidity needs and service contribution

headline: Colgate-Palmolive should strengthen continuing brand demand while reallocating skin-health capital.
summary: Oral-care leadership and strong cash flow provide foundations, but organic growth was modest and private-label pet volume weakened. The noncash skin-health impairment calls for selective portfolio action. The priority is productive brand investment and continuing-business returns.
focusTitle: Use core franchise strength to fund selective, evidence-based portfolio investment.
focusText: Protect oral-care availability and repeat purchasing, address the economics behind weaker private-label pet activity, and reassess skin-health resources against achievable operating contribution. Keep the noncash impairment separate from the cash available to support those choices.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve growth beyond the private-label volume drag
cards.text: Organic sales increased 1.4%, including a 0.7-percentage-point drag from lower private-label pet volume. The response should distinguish that business from demand in branded categories.
items: Review private-label pet customer and product economics
Align pet production commitments with profitable customer demand
Monitor continuing-category volume and contribution separately

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the oral-care leadership base
cards.text: Reported year-to-date global shares were 41.3% in toothpaste and 32.4% in manual toothbrushes. Strong positions require continuing execution rather than automatic incremental spending everywhere.
items: Maintain distribution and shelf availability in productive markets
Support product communication tied to consumer oral-care needs
Monitor local share, repeat purchasing and brand contribution

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Reassess skin-health spending after the impairment
cards.text: The fourth-quarter $794 million after-tax skin-health impairment was noncash. It calls for a focused portfolio return assessment rather than treating the charge as an operating cash outflow.
items: Reevaluate skin-health product and market investment economics
Prioritize spending with credible continuing demand support
Monitor skin-health cash contribution and remaining capital commitments

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Deploy cash toward durable brand economics
cards.text: Operating cash flow reached $4.198 billion. That capacity can support productive innovation, distribution and portfolio improvement when projects demonstrate a clear operating contribution.
items: Fund core brand and supply projects with measurable benefits
Reserve liquidity for ongoing operations and portfolio needs
Monitor cash conversion after brand and capital investment

headline: Comcast should turn wireless and Peacock growth into stronger operating contribution.
summary: Wireless lines, Peacock subscribers and connectivity revenue all increased, but full-year adjusted EBITDA declined. The business priority is therefore monetization and delivery economics rather than reach alone. Growth investment should favor customer relationships that retain revenue and produce contribution after content, network, acquisition and service costs.
focusTitle: Make subscriber expansion support the economics of the wider customer relationship.
focusText: Coordinate connectivity and wireless offers around retention and contribution, and improve Peacock engagement with disciplined content spending. Allocate resources using customer and product profitability so expanding usage can help reverse weaker consolidated operating conversion.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make wireless strengthen connectivity relationships
cards.text: Domestic wireless added 1.5 million lines, reaching 9.3 million. The opportunity is to deepen customer relationships while controlling acquisition and ongoing service costs.
items: Target wireless offers to appropriate connectivity customer needs
Coordinate mobile activation and account support workflows
Monitor bundled relationship retention and contribution

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Convert Peacock reach into lasting engagement
cards.text: Peacock paid subscribers grew 22% to 44 million. More subscribers provide a larger platform, but retention and content economics determine the operating value of that reach.
items: Prioritize programming that supports sustained subscriber engagement
Improve onboarding and discovery for relevant Peacock content
Monitor churn and contribution after content and acquisition costs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Protect connectivity contribution as revenue grows
cards.text: Connectivity revenue increased 4.2% to $46.0 billion. Pricing, product mix and service efficiency need to support the profitability of that larger revenue base.
items: Focus network and service investment on customer reliability
Evaluate offers using retained contribution after promotional periods
Monitor connectivity retention and customer-service costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Address the gap between audience growth and earnings
cards.text: Adjusted EBITDA declined 1.8% to $37.384 billion despite growth in several customer measures. Capital allocation should identify which activities improve consolidated contribution.
items: Review incremental spending by connectivity, wireless and streaming activity
Prioritize projects with clear continuing operating paybacks
Track consolidated EBITDA alongside subscriber and line additions

headline: Comfort Systems should convert a much larger backlog without sacrificing execution quality.
summary: Backlog expanded sharply while gross margin, overhead leverage and operating cash flow all improved. This is a strong operating position, with the main challenge being delivery capacity rather than a demand turnaround. The priority is to protect project selection, skilled labor availability and cash discipline as the larger book of work moves into execution.
focusTitle: Grow project delivery at the pace of trained crews and dependable cash conversion.
focusText: Sequence backlog according to staffing, procurement and customer readiness. Preserve bid discipline and field productivity, using stronger cash generation to support mobilization and selective capacity investment rather than accepting work beyond reliable execution capability.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make backlog growth executable
cards.text: Year-end backlog was just under $12 billion, roughly twice the beginning-of-year level. The opportunity is substantial, but each project needs realistic staffing and procurement support.
items: Sequence project starts around skilled crew and supervisory capacity
Confirm customer readiness before mobilizing major project resources
Monitor backlog conversion and project schedule adherence

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve stronger project gross margins
cards.text: Gross margin increased to 24.1% from 21.0%. Maintaining that result requires disciplined estimating and field execution as the volume of committed work expands.
items: Retain bid thresholds reflecting labor and procurement risks
Improve field planning and change-order management
Monitor project gross profit against original bid assumptions

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Scale support without losing operating leverage
cards.text: SG&A fell to 9.7% of sales from 10.4%. Further growth should preserve efficient support while providing enough project management and control capacity.
items: Add project support where workload complexity warrants it
Standardize recurring administrative tasks across operating teams
Monitor overhead alongside project quality and completion performance

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Fund mobilization without weakening cash conversion
cards.text: Operating cash flow reached approximately $1.19 billion, versus $849.1 million. Larger project commitments still require careful billing, collections and working-capital planning.
items: Align procurement and mobilization cash with customer billing terms
Resolve unbilled work and collection delays promptly
Reserve liquidity for peak project execution requirements

headline: ConocoPhillips should use drilling efficiency to defend returns against lower realized prices.
summary: Underlying production and Lower 48 efficiency improved, but realized prices fell and reserve replacement remained incomplete. The priority is resilient production contribution and selective resource development, balancing current cash economics with an attractive future reserve base.
focusTitle: Allocate capital to resilient production economics and selective reserve renewal.
focusText: Carry effective drilling and completion practices into suitable assets, match spending to commodity-sensitive cash capacity, and evaluate reserve additions through their development economics. Do not let headline production scale override the effect of lower realized prices.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Evaluate production growth on a comparable operating base
cards.text: Production reached 2.375 million BOE per day, with 2.5% underlying growth after acquisitions and dispositions. Investment choices should distinguish underlying operating progress from portfolio changes.
items: Compare asset production and contribution on consistent portfolio scope
Prioritize reliability in productive existing operations
Monitor underlying output after maintenance and development spending

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect contribution when realized prices weaken
cards.text: Average realized price declined 14% to $47.01 per BOE. Cost and capital discipline become more important when each unit of production earns less revenue.
items: Test asset spending under weaker realized-price conditions
Prioritize production with resilient full-cycle operating economics
Monitor cash contribution per BOE after operating costs

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make Lower 48 efficiency translate into cash value
cards.text: Lower 48 drilling and completion efficiency improved by more than 15%. The opportunity is to retain those execution gains without compromising well quality or dependable production.
items: Standardize effective drilling and completion practices where applicable
Link efficiency projects to actual development cash costs
Monitor production performance alongside faster operating execution

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Renew reserves selectively rather than chasing replacement
cards.text: Organic reserve replacement was 99%, while total replacement was 80%. Future resource development needs attention, but reserve volumes alone should not determine capital allocation.
items: Rank resource additions by development cost and expected contribution
Separate organic resource renewal from portfolio disposition effects
Monitor reserve conversion into economically productive output

headline: Consolidated Edison should make rate-base growth earn more than its financing costs.
summary: Higher electric and gas rate bases supported earnings, while interest costs and share issuance offset benefits. The priority is to coordinate project delivery and financing so useful infrastructure investment produces durable per-share returns.
focusTitle: Connect infrastructure investment, recovery and financing as one operating plan.
focusText: Prioritize projects with clear system benefits and executable cost plans. Match debt and equity funding to the capital program and evaluate results per share as well as in aggregate, preserving the earnings contribution from electric and gas investment.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve productive electric investment economics
cards.text: A higher CECONY electric rate base added an estimated $97 million after tax to annual common-stock earnings. Project execution should sustain that contribution through useful, reliable infrastructure.
items: Prioritize electric projects with clear service and system benefits
Manage project scope and completion against funding plans
Monitor earnings contribution alongside completed electric investment

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Keep gas investment focused on system value
cards.text: Higher CECONY gas rate base contributed an estimated $20 million after tax to annual earnings. Continued spending should remain linked to practical service requirements and operating value.
items: Rank gas work by reliability and service requirements
Coordinate construction with maintenance and customer needs
Monitor delivered project costs and gas earnings contribution

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Reduce the drag from financing the build
cards.text: Higher CECONY interest expense reduced annual earnings by an estimated $38 million after tax. Funding costs therefore need to be incorporated into project and capital sequencing decisions.
items: Match borrowing plans to executable construction spending
Evaluate project economics after financing requirements
Monitor interest burden as invested capital expands

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Protect per-share outcomes when issuing equity
cards.text: Common-share issuance reduced the annual CECONY EPS comparison by $0.18. Funding necessary infrastructure should be assessed through both aggregate earnings and the return earned per share.
items: Sequence equity funding with actual capital requirements
Test investment cases after share dilution and debt costs
Monitor per-share earnings alongside rate-base growth

headline: Constellation Brands should rebuild core beer demand and protect operating contribution.
summary: Beer volumes and margins weakened despite Pacifico and Victoria growth, while Modelo Especial declined. Wine and Spirits faces organic weakness beyond divestitures. The priority is brand-specific demand recovery and cost discipline within the continuing portfolio.
focusTitle: Focus investment on profitable consumer demand in the continuing portfolio.
focusText: Align beer shipments with depletion trends, support promising brands without neglecting Modelo Especial, and manage capacity against weaker volumes. Rebuild Wine and Spirits economics using the post-divestiture business rather than interpreting the reported sales decline as wholly organic.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Align beer supply with weaker consumer takeaway
cards.text: Beer shipments declined 3.8%, while depletions fell 2.1%. Production and distributor inventory decisions should reflect actual consumer movement rather than seek shipment growth alone.
items: Coordinate beer production with distributor inventory and depletion patterns
Improve retail availability where consumer demand remains attractive
Monitor depletion recovery and inventory by beer brand

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use brand-specific growth rather than one beer plan
cards.text: Pacifico and Victoria depletions grew over 15% and 16%, respectively, while Modelo Especial declined approximately 3%. Brand allocation should reflect these different consumer responses.
items: Expand productive distribution for Pacifico and Victoria
Diagnose Modelo Especial purchase and retail execution weakness
Evaluate brand marketing through incremental depletions and contribution

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Protect beer economics at lower volumes
cards.text: Beer operating margin fell 170 basis points to 38.0%, with management citing lower volume, tariffs and fixed-cost absorption. Margin recovery requires both commercial and operating action.
items: Match brewery schedules to realistic brand demand
Address tariff-exposed sourcing and logistics economics where practical
Monitor unit contribution and fixed-cost absorption together

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Reset Wine and Spirits for the continuing business
cards.text: Wine and Spirits organic net sales declined 14%, while reported sales fell 51% after divestitures. The remaining portfolio needs its own demand and cost plan.
items: Align staffing and inventory with the retained portfolio
Prioritize brands with credible repeat-purchase economics
Monitor continuing-brand demand and cash contribution

headline: Constellation Energy should preserve fleet reliability and convert it into dependable earnings.
summary: Fleet operating measures improved and adjusted operating EPS increased despite lower GAAP EPS. The priority is preserving reliable nuclear, dispatchable and renewable performance while assessing the recurring cash and earnings those assets produce.
focusTitle: Protect reliable generation while allocating spending to the strongest operating paybacks.
focusText: Use fleet-specific maintenance and dispatch plans to sustain availability and energy capture. Tie investment to dependable output and recurring cash contribution, retaining a clear distinction between operating earnings progress and the factors affecting GAAP EPS.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the nuclear reliability foundation
cards.text: Nuclear capacity factor, excluding Salem and STP, was 94.7%, versus 94.6% in 2024. Maintaining dependable fleet performance remains more valuable than assuming large incremental gains from an already strong level.
items: Prioritize maintenance and outage planning that preserve availability
Share effective operating practices across applicable nuclear assets
Monitor capacity factor with the same plant exclusions

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Maintain dispatchable fleet execution
cards.text: Gas and pumped-storage hydro dispatch match rate improved to 97.9% from 97.4%. Reliable dispatch performance helps translate available assets into dependable system service.
items: Coordinate dispatch readiness with maintenance and fuel requirements
Investigate dispatch mismatches for actionable operating improvements
Monitor dispatch performance alongside asset operating contribution

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Retain renewable energy-capture gains
cards.text: Energy capture for wind, solar and run-of-river hydro increased to 96.6% from 96.1%. Targeted work should protect these gains where practical operating improvements remain available.
items: Prioritize equipment and control issues reducing captured generation
Coordinate maintenance with expected resource availability
Evaluate improvement spending against incremental captured energy

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep funding decisions anchored in recurring performance
cards.text: GAAP EPS fell to $7.40 from $11.89, while adjusted operating EPS rose to $9.39 from $8.67. Capital decisions need to reflect that differing earnings picture and actual cash generation.
items: Link discretionary spending to recurring operating cash capacity
Evaluate earnings adjustments by their continuing economic effect
Monitor fleet performance alongside reported and operating earnings

headline: Cooper should make vision and surgical growth support reported margin and cash returns.
summary: CooperVision and CooperSurgical grew organically, but reported and non-GAAP margins moved in opposite directions. The priority is sustainable operating conversion, with product and manufacturing investment judged through recurring costs and cash after capital spending.
focusTitle: Back profitable product growth while making recurring costs and capital productive.
focusText: Prioritize vision and surgical opportunities that improve customer relationships and sustainable contribution. Coordinate manufacturing and commercial investment with actual demand, and judge the operating plan through reported profitability and cash after capital spending as well as non-GAAP improvement.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the CooperVision growth engine
cards.text: CooperVision revenue grew 5% organically to $2.744 billion. Maintaining that growth requires dependable product availability and effective support for vision-care customers.
items: Prioritize availability in products with demonstrated customer demand
Strengthen service to productive eye-care customer relationships
Monitor repeat orders and contribution by vision product

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Grow CooperSurgical selectively
cards.text: CooperSurgical revenue increased 3% organically to $1.349 billion. The opportunity is to deepen useful clinical and customer relationships while ensuring product support remains economically productive.
items: Focus commercial coverage on qualified surgical product demand
Coordinate product education with practical customer requirements
Monitor customer retention and contribution across surgical offerings

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Close the gap in operating margin direction
cards.text: GAAP operating margin declined to 17% from 18%, while non-GAAP margin increased to 26% from 25%. Investment choices need to reflect which costs remain necessary to sustain growth.
items: Assign continuing operating costs to product-level economic plans
Prioritize productivity projects with measurable recurring benefits
Monitor reported margin alongside non-GAAP improvement

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require capital investment to improve cash economics
cards.text: Operating cash flow was $796.1 million, with $362.4 million of capital expenditures. Growth capacity should be funded with attention to the cash remaining after that investment.
items: Sequence manufacturing projects around demonstrated product demand
Evaluate capital paybacks through quality, capacity and unit costs
Monitor cash after capital spending and working-capital needs

headline: Copart should use auction scale to improve buyer liquidity and site productivity.
summary: Global membership, substantial throughput and an extensive footprint support Copart’s auction network, while gross profit outpaced revenue growth. The priority is more productive scale through reliable vehicle processing, active bidding and disciplined site investment.
focusTitle: Connect seller throughput, global bidding and efficient physical operations.
focusText: Prioritize investments that move vehicles through locations reliably and improve auction participation. Use site and buyer economics together to judge expansion, preserving the gross-profit conversion already visible in the annual results.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make high vehicle throughput operationally reliable
cards.text: Copart disclosed more than four million units sold in the last year. At that scale, vehicle handling, listing readiness and timely completion directly influence the quality of the auction service.
items: Coordinate vehicle intake, preparation and auction scheduling
Improve listing accuracy and condition information before bidding
Monitor processing time and handling cost per vehicle

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn global membership into active auction liquidity
cards.text: Approximately one million members across more than 185 countries provide broad potential buyer reach. The operating opportunity is to make that reach useful on actual vehicle auctions.
items: Improve vehicle discovery for relevant international buyer needs
Simplify buyer support around payment and vehicle collection
Monitor active bidding and repeat purchases by buyer market

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Invest in locations according to usable capacity
cards.text: More than 250 locations in 11 countries create a substantial physical network. Site allocation should follow throughput and service economics rather than geographic breadth alone.
items: Assess site utilization and vehicle dwell patterns
Prioritize yard improvements that remove processing bottlenecks
Evaluate additional capacity against local seller and buyer demand

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Preserve profitable conversion as the network scales
cards.text: Annual gross profit increased 10.1%, compared with 9.7% revenue growth. That favorable relationship should guide resource allocation as auctions and physical operations expand.
items: Compare gross contribution across services and operating locations
Control incremental handling costs without weakening seller service
Monitor gross profit per vehicle alongside network investment

headline: Corning should prioritize profitable optical growth while adapting the display footprint.
summary: Optical Communications is expanding rapidly and Specialty Materials is also growing, while Display sales declined. The portfolio therefore needs differentiated capacity and commercial plans. The gap between GAAP and core operating margins makes sustainable contribution an important constraint on how quickly the stronger businesses absorb capital and operating resources.
focusTitle: Allocate capacity by segment demand and recurring operating returns.
focusText: Back confirmed Optical Communications opportunities and productive Specialty Materials programs, while adjusting Display activity to its demand base. Preserve margin discipline across the portfolio so revenue mix improvements lead to cash and reported operating progress.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make optical expansion operationally dependable
cards.text: Optical Communications sales rose 35% to $6.274 billion. The opportunity requires supply and customer delivery execution that protects product economics as activity increases.
items: Align optical capacity additions with executable customer demand
Prioritize production quality and on-time customer deliveries
Monitor optical contribution after manufacturing and expansion costs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Adapt Display to weaker sales
cards.text: Display sales fell 5% to $3.697 billion. Production and commercial decisions should protect contribution without allowing capacity or inventory commitments to outrun customer requirements.
items: Match Display production schedules to confirmed customer demand
Review pricing and product mix by display application
Monitor inventory, utilization and segment contribution together

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Support Specialty Materials where programs justify investment
cards.text: Specialty Materials sales increased 10% to $2.211 billion. Selective product and customer development can extend the growth if new programs earn adequate operating returns.
items: Prioritize engineering resources for qualified customer programs
Coordinate material capacity with customer product launch requirements
Monitor program conversion and contribution by materials application

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep core margin strength visible in reported economics
cards.text: GAAP operating margin was 14.6%, compared with 19.3% core operating margin. Portfolio investment needs to reflect continuing costs and the cash required to deliver growth.
items: Include recurring costs in segment capital-allocation cases
Tie productivity spending to measurable operating benefits
Monitor reported margin as optical and specialty sales expand

headline: Corpay should make acquisition-led expansion reinforce organic growth and cash returns.
summary: Organic revenue and adjusted EBITDA both advanced, providing a positive operating base. At the same time, large capital deployment and repurchases create substantial demands on financial resources. The priority is to integrate the cross-border acquisition effectively while protecting existing customer economics and making capital allocation responsive to cash generation.
focusTitle: Prioritize integration quality and profitable customer activity before further expansion.
focusText: Connect acquired cross-border capabilities with useful client services while maintaining dependable payment execution. Evaluate growth investment and shareholder returns together, using recurring contribution and cash needs to determine the pace of additional capital deployment.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the organic customer growth engine
cards.text: Management reported 10% organic revenue growth in 2025. Sustaining that progress requires retaining productive payment relationships while acquisition work occupies management and operating resources.
items: Prioritize retention and service quality in existing customer accounts
Expand appropriate payment capabilities within active relationships
Monitor organic customer activity and contribution by business

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect stronger earnings conversion
cards.text: Adjusted EBITDA increased 13% to approximately $2.6 billion. The operating plan should preserve the cost and customer economics supporting growth beyond the revenue increase.
items: Review cost-to-serve across growing payment activities
Fund automation that improves recurring transaction processing economics
Monitor adjusted earnings alongside operating cash conversion

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make the cross-border acquisition earn its capital
cards.text: Corpay deployed more than $4.3 billion of capital, including its largest cross-border acquisition to date. Integration needs to produce useful capabilities and sustainable contribution.
items: Assign clear ownership for customer and platform integration
Coordinate cross-border service expansion with existing client needs
Monitor integration spending, client retention and acquired contribution

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Balance repurchases with integration funding
cards.text: Share repurchases totaled $782 million. Continued returns should preserve the operating flexibility needed to integrate the acquisition and support organic payment activity.
items: Reserve funding for integration and essential platform investment
Assess repurchases against cash after growth and financing needs
Monitor liquidity as acquired operations join the operating plan

headline: CoStar should turn Homes.com audience and subscriptions into sustainable earnings.
summary: Bookings, Homes.com Network traffic and agent subscriptions provide commercial opportunity, but reported income remains far below adjusted EBITDA. The priority is profitable audience monetization, demonstrating that agent retention and service delivery justify acquisition and platform spending.
focusTitle: Connect consumer engagement to agent value and recurring cash contribution.
focusText: Focus product and sales investment on helping subscribed agents achieve useful outcomes from the audience. Judge acquisition and platform spending through subscriber retention and contribution, while keeping reported earnings and the cash required to sustain growth visible.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Convert bookings into retained customer relationships
cards.text: Annual net new bookings reached $308 million. The operating task is to deliver contracted value and retain customers as booked commitments become ongoing business.
items: Coordinate onboarding with the services customers have purchased
Resolve adoption barriers before renewal conversations
Monitor bookings conversion and customer retention by product

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make network traffic valuable to property participants
cards.text: The Homes.com Network averaged 108 million monthly unique visitors. Audience scale should translate into relevant engagement and useful outcomes rather than become a standalone spending objective.
items: Improve property discovery and the relevance of consumer engagement
Connect agent product features to useful audience interactions
Evaluate traffic spending against engagement and subscriber contribution

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the annual agent subscription base
cards.text: Homes.com had over 31,000 agent subscribers, with 76% on annual contracts. That base offers an opportunity to demonstrate continuing value and improve renewal quality.
items: Provide onboarding that helps agents use subscribed features
Prioritize support for agent adoption and renewal obstacles
Monitor annual-contract renewals and contribution by subscriber cohort

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep growth investment accountable to reported economics
cards.text: GAAP net income was approximately $7 million, versus $442 million adjusted EBITDA. Investment decisions need to include continuing costs and cash demands beyond the adjusted measure.
items: Review marketing and platform spending by incremental contribution
Stage expansion spending around demonstrated subscriber economics
Monitor reported profitability and cash after growth investment

headline: Costco should preserve member value as digital and international demand expand.
summary: Comparable sales, e-commerce and membership fee revenue all grew, with broad underlying geographic strength. The priority is preserving member value and dependable service while ensuring digital fulfillment and expansion strengthen retained relationships and operating contribution.
focusTitle: Protect the member proposition while scaling convenient shopping.
focusText: Use buying discipline, inventory availability and efficient fulfillment to reinforce repeat shopping. Allocate digital and geographic investment where it improves member service and contribution, and judge fee revenue growth alongside renewal behavior rather than assuming it proves stronger retention.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve broad comparable-sales momentum
cards.text: Comparable sales increased 5.9%, or 7.6% excluding gasoline prices and foreign exchange. The stronger underlying comparison supports continued attention to assortment value and reliable merchandise availability.
items: Maintain price and assortment discipline in core categories
Improve availability on products driving repeat member visits
Monitor shopping frequency and contribution alongside comparable sales

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Scale e-commerce with dependable fulfillment economics
cards.text: E-commerce comparable sales increased 15.6%, or 16.1% excluding gasoline and currency effects. Digital growth should retain the service quality and value members expect.
items: Coordinate digital inventory with achievable fulfillment capacity
Reduce delivery and return friction on online purchases
Monitor online contribution after fulfillment and return costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make fee growth reflect lasting membership value
cards.text: Membership fee revenue increased to $5.323 billion from $4.828 billion. Continued success depends on keeping the shopping proposition compelling as the member base and fee revenue expand.
items: Use member feedback to address recurring shopping frustrations
Support renewal through reliable value and service execution
Monitor renewal behavior and engagement across member cohorts

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Carry successful execution across geographic markets
cards.text: Comparable sales excluding gasoline and currency grew 7.3% in the U.S., 8.3% in Canada and 8.2% internationally. Broad strength permits selective sharing of effective operating practices.
items: Adapt successful assortment practices to local member demand
Prioritize market investment using capacity and member-service needs
Monitor geographic contribution after local operating and expansion costs

headline: CRH should convert acquisition and project spending into lasting cash returns.
summary: Higher adjusted margin and operating cash flow support substantial acquisition and project spending. The priority is disciplined integration and capital productivity, ensuring each addition strengthens local operations and cash generation while preserving the improved underlying economics.
focusTitle: Integrate acquired operations and sequence projects around demonstrable operating paybacks.
focusText: Use local market fit, asset productivity and customer service to determine where capital earns the best contribution. Keep funding aligned with cash after operating needs, and require practical delivery milestones for both acquisitions and growth projects.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make acquisition volume manageable and productive
cards.text: CRH invested $4.1 billion in 38 acquisitions. The breadth of activity calls for disciplined integration and clear ownership of the operating benefits expected from each addition.
items: Prioritize integration of procurement, logistics and local customer coverage
Assign accountable operating leaders to acquired businesses
Monitor acquired contribution and cash against integration spending

cards.label: Risk to watch

headline: CrowdStrike should turn recurring-revenue growth into stronger operating economics.

Address adoption barriers before customer renewal decisions
Monitor retained ARR and service costs by customer cohort

headline: Crown Castle should convert underlying site growth into steadier per-share cash earnings.

items: Prioritize amendments and leasing with executable tenant requirements
Coordinate site readiness with customer deployment schedules
Monitor organic billings and contribution by tenant relationship

Adjust spending where cancelled demand removes capacity needs
Monitor cancellation effects separately from continuing tenant growth

Match spending to signed and executable customer commitments
Monitor per-share AFFO alongside capital and financing needs

Protect critical leasing and deployment support capabilities
Monitor cost savings alongside tenant service and delivery performance

headline: CSX should restore arrival reliability while protecting freight revenue quality.
summary: Intermodal growth earned less revenue per unit, while coal and merchandise weakened. Faster train velocity did not improve arrivals. The priority is reliable end-to-end service and disciplined yield management that strengthen customer retention and freight contribution.
focusTitle: Improve customer delivery consistency before relying on volume recovery.
focusText: Coordinate schedules, terminals and customer handoffs to address arrival performance, while pricing and capacity plans reflect the different intermodal, coal and merchandise trends. Use the company-estimated operating measures consistently to judge whether service changes improve delivered freight economics.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make intermodal growth contribute more revenue value
cards.text: Intermodal units increased 4% to 2.995 million, while revenue per unit declined 2%. More activity should be evaluated after lane pricing and the cost of handling added traffic.
items: Review intermodal lane contribution after terminal and transport costs
Target capacity toward attractive customer and corridor demand
Monitor intermodal yield alongside units and service reliability

cards.label: Risk to watch

cards.text: Coal revenue declined 15%, with units down 2% and revenue per unit down 13%. The larger yield decline makes commercial terms and resource allocation important.

Align equipment and crew commitments with expected coal demand
Monitor coal contribution after operating and repositioning costs

Monitor customer retention and contribution by merchandise category

Monitor on-time arrivals alongside velocity and terminal performance

headline: Diamondback should preserve low-cost production while turning asset-sale cash into durable returns.
summary: Lower lease costs, production scale and modest reserve growth support the operating base. Asset sales add cash without establishing recurring funding. The priority is disciplined development and portfolio allocation that preserve unit economics and sustainable financial flexibility.
focusTitle: Allocate capital according to asset contribution and sustainable operating cash.
focusText: Protect cost gains across the producing base and rank reserve development by practical economics. Use asset-sale proceeds deliberately for balance-sheet or high-value operating needs, while keeping continuing production and recurring funding capacity visible.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make production scale economically productive
cards.text: Production averaged 921,000 BOE per day, including 497,200 barrels of oil per day. Operating choices should focus on dependable asset contribution rather than total output alone.
items: Prioritize reliability in high-contribution producing assets
Coordinate field activity with available infrastructure and service capacity
Monitor product mix and cash contribution by asset

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve lower lease operating costs
cards.text: Lease operating expense declined to $5.55 per BOE from $5.87. Sustaining that progress requires repeatable field execution without deferring work needed for reliable production.
items: Standardize effective field operating and maintenance practices
Target recurring service costs with clear productivity opportunities
Monitor lease expense alongside downtime and production reliability

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Convert reserve growth into attractive production economics
cards.text: Proved reserves reached 3.618 billion BOE, up 2%, with oil representing 49%. Resource scale should guide selective development rather than automatically justify a larger capital program.
items: Rank reserve projects by development cost and expected contribution
Stage drilling around infrastructure and operating readiness
Monitor reserve conversion and well performance after spending

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Do not make recurring commitments depend on disposals
cards.text: Non-core asset sales generated approximately $1.7 billion of cash proceeds. Those funds create flexibility but do not establish an equivalent recurring source of operating cash.
items: Assign sale proceeds to explicit financing or investment priorities
Reset operating plans for the retained asset portfolio
Monitor liquidity using continuing operations without further sale assumptions

headline: Digital Realty should convert signed leasing into timely cash-generating occupancy.
summary: Signed leases and fourth-quarter bookings provide a substantial future rent opportunity, while renewal pricing improved. The average commencement lag means that opportunity still requires delivery and customer readiness before rent begins. The priority is disciplined project execution and funding, using company-share economics consistently rather than treating gross leasing commitments as immediately available revenue.
focusTitle: Coordinate lease delivery and capital spending around contractual commencements.
focusText: Prioritize the projects and customer handoffs needed to activate signed rent. Preserve renewal economics, and evaluate new leasing against the capital, ownership share and time required before it contributes to operating cash.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn signed backlog into operating rent
cards.text: Year-end signed-but-not-commenced backlog was $817 million of annualized GAAP base rent at Digital Realty’s share. Execution should focus on activating that contracted economic interest.
items: Rank backlog by customer readiness and delivery dependencies
Assign clear ownership for construction and customer handoffs
Monitor commenced rent against company-share backlog

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the value of new leasing
cards.text: Fourth-quarter bookings represented $400 million of annualized GAAP rental revenue at 100% share, or $175 million at company share. New commitments should earn adequate capital returns.
items: Assess lease economics using the relevant ownership share
Coordinate capacity commitments with executable customer demand
Monitor expected contribution after project and operating costs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Keep renewal gains aligned with retention

Evaluate pricing with retention and account expansion opportunities
Monitor cash renewal spreads and associated customer churn

items: Sequence project spending around contractual delivery milestones
Coordinate commissioning readiness with customer move-in requirements
Monitor commencement delays and cash needs before occupancy

headline: Dollar General should preserve traffic and inventory gains while proving remodel returns.
summary: Traffic, transaction amount and gross margin improved, alongside lower per-store inventory. The priority is preserving availability and shrink gains while making extensive remodeling produce durable customer visits and store contribution after project costs.
focusTitle: Connect better store conditions with profitable repeat visits.
focusText: Preserve shrink and damage improvements without reducing merchandise availability. Use customer response and store contribution to guide renovation priorities, and coordinate replenishment and labor around the demand evident in comparable sales.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build on returning store traffic
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 same-store sales increased 3.0%, with traffic up 1.6% and average transaction amount up 1.4%. Broader transaction growth provides a useful foundation for store improvement.
items: Protect availability in categories supporting repeat customer visits
Improve checkout and shopping execution at busy locations
Monitor traffic and contribution after promotional spending

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve the shrink and damage margin benefit
cards.text: Gross margin increased 107 basis points to 30.7%, with management citing lower shrink and inventory damage. Sustaining those gains requires practical execution inside stores and distribution.
items: Standardize handling and inventory controls behind lower damage
Target shrink interventions to affected stores and merchandise
Monitor loss rates alongside availability and store labor needs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep lower inventory compatible with customer demand
cards.text: Average per-store merchandise inventory declined 7.0% at year-end. Leaner stock is valuable when it reduces cash tied up without creating avoidable lost sales.
items: Align replenishment with local selling and stockout patterns
Reduce slow-moving inventory while protecting essential products
Monitor stockouts and inventory turns alongside per-store balances

cards.title: Make remodeling produce measurable operating returns

items: Compare remodel cohorts on customer visits and store contribution
Coordinate projects to limit shopping and staffing disruption
Rank future work using sustained results after project spending

headline: Dollar Tree should make multi-price and store expansion improve operating contribution.

focusText: Use multi-price assortment to support customer value and repeat visits, while controlling complexity in replenishment and staffing. Allocate new-store and conversion capital according to mature contribution and cash returns within the continuing Dollar Tree business.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build more balanced comparable-sales growth
cards.text: Same-store sales increased 5.3%, including 4.3% higher average ticket and 1.0% higher traffic. The next opportunity is to deepen repeat visits while preserving attractive basket economics.
items: Improve availability in products supporting repeat shopping occasions
Evaluate assortment value through customer purchase response
Monitor traffic and gross contribution alongside ticket growth

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make multi-price assortment operationally productive

items: Refine multi-price assortment using local sell-through and contribution
Simplify replenishment and merchandising for expanded product ranges
Monitor converted-store contribution after inventory and labor costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require new stores to earn adequate returns
cards.text: Dollar Tree opened 402 new stores. Continued footprint growth should reflect achievable customer demand and the operating capacity required to support each location.

Coordinate openings with trained teams and reliable supply
Monitor new-store cash contribution and nearby sales displacement

Monitor contribution after SG&A within comparable store cohorts

headline: Dominion should protect utility earnings growth through stronger project cost discipline.

Monitor recurring operating contribution alongside service reliability

Test financing plans under different market-benefit outcomes
Monitor reported earnings separately from continuing operating contribution

headline: Domino’s should make global store growth reinforce profitable local demand.
summary: U.S. and international same-store sales both increased, while new locations expanded the system’s reach. Monitor currency-excluded comparable sales and franchisee contribution

Monitor retail-sales growth alongside franchisee retention and contribution
