cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve core per-share progress
cards.text: Non-GAAP core EPS increased to $6.55 from $4.93. Continuing investment should support lasting per-share economics after funding costs rather than aggregate earnings growth alone.
items: Assess capital plans after debt and equity financing needs
Prioritize projects with clear utility and shareholder returns
Monitor core per-share contribution as spending advances

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make authorized recovery benefits translate into cash capacity
cards.text: Management attributed higher SCE core EPS mainly to the 2025 general rate case and interest benefits from authorized cost recoveries. Execution should protect the economics of those decisions.
items: Align project costs with authorized operating and investment assumptions
Coordinate recovery timing with utility funding requirements
Monitor recoveries, project delivery and utility cash contribution

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Contain the parent-level financing burden
cards.text: Management reported a larger Parent and Other core loss per share, citing higher interest expense and preferred-stock redemption issuance costs. Parent funding should be evaluated with the utility capital plan.
items: Match financing activity to practical cash and maturity needs
Evaluate refinancing choices after transaction and interest costs
Monitor parent cash requirements and core loss contribution

headline: Edwards should preserve valve growth while containing continuing legal and operating costs.
summary: TAVR and Surgical growth support the continuing business, while higher legal costs pressured margin. Discontinued income explains a separate earnings comparison. The priority is clinical adoption and product execution with disciplined legal spending and continuing cash economics.
focusTitle: Protect clinical adoption and product execution while restoring operating conversion.
focusText: Support TAVR and Surgical demand with targeted clinical and supply resources. Manage litigation exposure and spending explicitly, and evaluate investment through continuing operating economics and cash needs rather than prior discontinued-business income.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the TAVR growth engine
cards.text: TAVR sales reached $4.5 billion, with 8.6% non-GAAP constant-currency growth. Commercial and operating resources should sustain appropriate adoption and dependable product availability.
items: Support clinician education around appropriate TAVR use
Align product supply with demonstrated procedure demand
Monitor continuing TAVR demand and contribution after support costs

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Build productive Surgical relationships
cards.text: Surgical sales exceeded $1 billion, growing 5% as reported and 4% at non-GAAP constant currency. Continued progress requires effective customer support and suitable product execution.
items: Prioritize clinical and customer support for active Surgical programs
Maintain product availability across demonstrated customer needs
Monitor repeat demand and contribution by Surgical offering

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Control legal costs while protecting the product franchise
cards.text: GAAP operating margin fell to 20.8% from 25.3%, while intellectual-property and litigation expenses rose to $325.4 million from $40.4 million. These costs deserve explicit operating accountability.
items: Assign budgets and decision ownership to material legal matters
Evaluate legal strategy alongside product and portfolio economics
Monitor continuing operating margin and legal cash requirements

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep discontinued income out of ongoing spending assumptions
cards.text: Discontinued-operations income was $13.4 million, versus $2.7737 billion in 2024. That comparison should not determine the demand plan or recurring spending capacity of the continuing valve business.
items: Fund ongoing programs using continuing operating and cash economics
Separate remaining discontinued-business obligations from product budgets
Monitor continuing contribution after legal and capital spending

headline: Elevance should improve medical-cost and Carelon contribution before pursuing more scale.
summary: Higher benefit costs and weaker Carelon margin outweigh some benefit from administrative efficiency, while Medicaid attrition reduced membership. The priority is sustainable insurance and care-service contribution, combining medical-cost management with selective retention and productive operating spending.
focusTitle: Coordinate insurance pricing, care delivery and profitable member retention.
focusText: Focus medical-cost responses on the products and care patterns driving pressure. Improve Carelon contract and delivery economics, preserve useful administrative efficiency, and evaluate Medicaid-related enrollment changes through both member service and contribution.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Address the higher share of premium consumed by benefits
cards.text: The benefit expense ratio rose to 90.0% from 88.5%, up 150 basis points. Pricing and care-management decisions should respond to the medical costs underlying that pressure.
items: Analyze utilization and unit-cost changes by insurance product
Coordinate provider and care-management actions around costly care pathways
Monitor benefit costs against premium and member assumptions

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make Carelon growth produce stronger contribution
cards.text: Carelon operating revenue rose to $71.7 billion from $53.9 billion, while margin fell to 4.7% from 5.4%. Segment growth, including intersegment activity, needs better operating conversion.
items: Evaluate contracts using full service delivery and support costs
Prioritize productivity improvements in growing care-service operations
Monitor Carelon margin and cash conversion by service line

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Manage Medicaid attrition without sacrificing product economics
cards.text: Medical membership ended at approximately 45.2 million, down 0.5 million, with management citing Medicaid attrition. Retention efforts should distinguish eligibility changes from avoidable service-related losses.
items: Support appropriate renewal and eligibility-navigation processes
Align operating resources with the changing covered population
Monitor retained membership and contribution by insurance product

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve useful administrative efficiency
cards.text: GAAP operating expense ratio fell to 10.6% from 11.4%. Efficiency gains are useful when they preserve the capacity to manage medical costs and deliver dependable member service.
items: Simplify administrative work without weakening claims accuracy
Protect resources needed for member support and care coordination
Monitor service quality alongside the operating expense ratio

headline: EMCOR should match its growing project pipeline with delivery capacity and overhead discipline.
summary: Strong construction growth and a larger contracted pipeline give EMCOR substantial opportunity. The priority is converting that workload at attractive margins while preventing staffing constraints and higher overhead from absorbing the benefit. Acquisition effects make the quality of growth particularly important.
focusTitle: Allocate capacity to profitable backlog conversion.
focusText: Use project economics and available skilled labor to sequence work. Pair acquisition integration with tighter overhead ownership so expanding construction revenue produces durable cash and operating profit, rather than simply a larger workload.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Contracted growth needs a credible delivery plan
cards.text: Remaining performance obligations rose 31.2% to $13.25 billion. That improves workload visibility, but projects still require scheduling, labor and execution before becoming recognized revenue.
items: Map contracted work to crew availability and procurement needs
Prioritize projects with clear mobilization and payment milestones
Monitor schedule slippage and changes in cancellation exposure

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Explain and contain the higher overhead burden
cards.text: SG&A rose to 10.1% of revenue from 9.7%, despite construction growth. Integration costs and recurring overhead need different responses when allocating management attention.
items: Assign owners to acquired and recurring overhead categories
Consolidate overlapping support functions where delivery permits
Measure overhead absorption as acquired operations mature

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve construction margins as workload expands
cards.text: Electrical and mechanical construction generated a combined 12.5% operating margin. New volume should be selected and staffed to protect those project economics.
items: Carry successful estimating practices into new contract bids
Review labor productivity at major project milestones
Escalate cost overruns before remaining contract margin erodes

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Distinguish acquired scale from repeatable demand
cards.text: Combined construction revenue increased 24.4%. Acquisitions can affect that comparison, so capacity commitments should follow organic opportunities and acquired project quality.
items: Separate acquired workload from growth in existing operations
Check acquired project pricing and customer concentration
Match permanent hiring to sustainable construction demand

headline: Emerson should turn stronger underlying orders and integration savings into durable cash growth.
summary: Orders modestly outpaced sales, adjusted margins expanded and operating cash improved in continuing operations. The task is to preserve that combination as Test & Measurement integration matures, proving that reported run-rate synergies support customer delivery and realized economics.
focusTitle: Connect order conversion, integration and cash allocation.
focusText: Direct integration savings toward reliable delivery and the most attractive order opportunities. Judge progress through realized operating benefits, customer retention and cash available after working-capital and acquisition needs, while retaining the company-defined basis of adjusted measures.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Convert the order advantage into delivered sales
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 underlying orders grew 4% versus 3% underlying sales. The small gap supports demand visibility but makes execution on existing orders more useful than assuming acceleration.
items: Prioritize delivery bottlenecks in businesses with order growth
Align production and service capacity with order schedules
Monitor conversion delays and customer order changes

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make Test & Measurement savings operationally durable
cards.text: Management reported $200 million of run-rate integration cost synergies. This is an integration measure, so sustaining service and realizing savings matter more than treating it as incremental annual profit.
items: Assign operating owners to the remaining integration benefits
Protect technical support and customer-facing integration resources
Compare realized cost reductions with retention and delivery performance

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the sources of adjusted margin expansion
cards.text: Adjusted segment EBITA margin reached 27.6%, up 160 basis points. Better economics should guide resource allocation without letting exclusions obscure the cost of serving demand.
items: Identify segment practices behind the adjusted margin improvement
Preserve pricing and productivity discipline in new orders
Evaluate investment returns including recurring integration cash costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep cash growth ahead of competing capital demands
cards.text: Operating cash flow rose 11% to $3.676 billion. Stronger cash gives flexibility, provided inventory, receivables and acquisition requirements do not consume the operating improvement.
items: Tie inventory purchasing to confirmed delivery requirements
Target collection delays in growing order cohorts
Rank capital uses against cash remaining after integration needs

headline: Entergy should deliver approved infrastructure while keeping regulated returns ahead of rising costs.
summary: Regulatory actions, sales volume and construction-work returns supported utility earnings, with weather also helping. Approved generation and transmission projects create an execution opportunity. The central issue is translating that investment into dependable service and recoverable returns as financing and operating costs rise.
focusTitle: Link construction decisions to customer demand and cost recovery.
focusText: Sequence approved work around credible load requirements, construction readiness and regulatory recovery. Base funding decisions on weather-normalized earnings so a favorable weather comparison does not overstate the recurring capacity to support infrastructure investment.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn project approvals into controlled construction
cards.text: Approvals for Jefferson Power Station and the West Bank and Cypress-to-Legend 500 kV projects advance the investment program. Approval alone does not resolve construction or recovery execution.
items: Assign accountable budget and schedule owners to each project
Coordinate generation and transmission milestones with service requirements
Escalate cost changes alongside their recovery implications

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Separate sustainable load from favorable weather
cards.text: Estimated after-tax weather benefit increased to $91 million from $66 million. That helps reported performance but should not become the baseline for permanent operating or funding commitments.
items: Use weather-normalized sales when evaluating customer load growth
Stress operating budgets against less favorable weather contributions
Monitor recurring earnings after removing weather variability

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the regulated earnings mechanisms supporting investment
cards.text: Management cited regulatory actions and returns on construction work in progress among utility earnings drivers. Maintaining those mechanisms helps align customer infrastructure needs with financial capacity.
items: Keep regulatory submissions aligned with construction progress
Document customer benefits supporting requested infrastructure recovery
Track earned returns against approved recovery mechanisms

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Prevent funding and asset costs from diluting returns
cards.text: Higher interest, depreciation, other operating costs and non-income taxes offset utility earnings growth. Investment economics therefore require attention beyond headline spending or project approvals.
items: Phase funding around construction cash requirements
Include depreciation and operating burdens in project economics
Compare incremental regulated earnings with financing and asset costs

headline: EOG should preserve well-cost gains while integrating Encino and funding disciplined shareholder returns.
summary: Lower well costs and larger reserves strengthen EOG’s resource position. The Encino acquisition also makes portfolio integration central to capital allocation. Returning an amount equal to company-defined free cash flow demonstrates substantial distributions, but future spending and returns should remain tied to project economics.
focusTitle: Make the enlarged portfolio compete for capital on comparable economics.
focusText: Apply the same well-cost and return discipline across existing assets and Encino. Distinguish acquired reserves from organic additions, and fund shareholder distributions from cash remaining after the development required to sustain the portfolio.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Replicate lower well costs without weakening productivity
cards.text: Average well costs declined 7% across the multi-basin portfolio in 2025. The benefit is most valuable when procurement and drilling efficiencies preserve the productive quality of new wells.
items: Transfer successful drilling practices across comparable basins
Use supplier negotiations to reinforce repeatable cost savings
Evaluate completed well economics alongside development spending

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Give Encino a clear integration and capital framework
cards.text: The release highlights Encino as a major portfolio transaction. Its value depends on operating integration and investment choices, rather than the acquisition’s contribution to reported scale alone.
items: Integrate operating plans and procurement with accountable owners
Rank Encino projects against competing basin opportunities
Monitor integration spending and operational handoff issues

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve cash-backed distribution discipline
cards.text: EOG generated $4.7 billion of company-defined free cash flow and returned that amount through dividends and repurchases. Cash generation provides a useful anchor for allocation decisions.
items: Fund essential development before sizing discretionary repurchases
Keep dividend decisions connected to through-cycle cash capacity
Compare distributions with cash after acquisition and development needs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Turn reserve scale into economic development options
cards.text: Proved reserves increased 16% to 5.5 billion barrels of oil equivalent. Reserve additions improve resource depth but are not equivalent to organic production growth or immediately available cash.
items: Separate acquired reserves from organic resource additions
Prioritize reserve development using comparable well economics
Monitor capital intensity as reserves move into production

headline: EQT should lock in lower unit costs while keeping spending resilient to realized gas prices.
summary: Higher sales volume and realized prices combined with lower per-unit operating costs to expand company-defined free cash flow sharply. The strongest operating achievement is the cost improvement; capital commitments should preserve that benefit without assuming the favorable price comparison will persist.
focusTitle: Build allocation decisions around resilient unit economics.
focusText: Maintain cost savings as volumes grow and test development choices against a range of realized prices. Use the stronger cash result to improve financial flexibility, with ownership-recast comparisons kept consistent when judging the underlying operating progress.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect cost efficiency as sales volumes expand
cards.text: Per-unit operating costs fell to $1.05 per Mcfe from $1.23. Preserving that efficiency helps EQT retain more of each realized-price dollar as activity changes.
items: Identify operating practices responsible for lower unit costs
Extend efficient maintenance and field scheduling across assets
Monitor total operating spending alongside per-unit performance

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make higher volumes earn their capital requirements
cards.text: Sales increased to 2,382 Bcfe from 2,228 Bcfe. Additional volume is useful when production and delivery economics remain attractive after the spending needed to support it.
items: Sequence development by delivered gas economics
Align field activity with available delivery capacity
Compare incremental volume with associated capital and operating needs

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use stronger cash to increase allocation flexibility
cards.text: Company-defined free cash flow attributable to EQT reached $2.503 billion versus $684 million. The improvement supports disciplined capital choices, with ownership-recast comparisons relevant to interpretation.
items: Prioritize cash uses after committed development needs
Retain flexibility before increasing recurring distribution commitments
Assess cash conversion on consistent ownership comparisons

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Avoid turning a price benefit into permanent spending
cards.text: Average realized price rose to $3.19 per Mcfe from $2.74. Pricing contributed to the improvement, making cash resilience under weaker realizations an essential capital-allocation test.
items: Stress development economics under lower realized prices
Match discretionary spending to cash generation rather than volume
Monitor realized-price changes against the unit-cost base

headline: Equifax should convert mortgage outperformance and product innovation into stronger operating leverage.
summary: Mortgage revenue outgrew its underlying market in the fourth quarter, and the Vitality Index suggests meaningful new-product contribution. Stronger annual free cash flow is encouraging, but the lower full-year adjusted EBITDA margin makes profitable scaling the priority rather than growth alone.
focusTitle: Scale the offers that improve customer economics and margins.
focusText: Direct investment toward mortgage and new-product propositions with repeatable adoption and attractive servicing costs. Preserve cash generation while testing whether these growth sources can expand profitability, keeping fourth-quarter demand signals distinct from full-year results.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Translate mortgage outperformance into durable customer value
cards.text: Fourth-quarter U.S. mortgage revenue rose 20% despite a declining underlying market. That performance warrants investment in the products and customer relationships supporting revenue beyond market volume.
items: Identify mortgage offers driving customer adoption and revenue
Extend effective sales practices across comparable mortgage accounts
Monitor retention and revenue as underlying application volumes change

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make revenue growth restore adjusted margin leverage
cards.text: Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 31.9% from 32.3%. Expansion initiatives should be judged on their incremental delivery and selling costs as well as revenue contribution.
items: Examine servicing costs in growing product lines
Prioritize scalable delivery and reusable product capabilities
Monitor incremental profitability as new revenue cohorts mature

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the stronger cash conversion
cards.text: 2025 free cash flow reached $1.13 billion, up almost 40%, on the company-defined basis. That creates capacity to invest without letting cash discipline fade during product expansion.
items: Fund product investment against clear commercial milestones
Maintain collection discipline across expanding customer accounts
Compare cash generation with investment and operating commitments

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require innovation to become repeatable commercial adoption
cards.text: The fourth-quarter Vitality Index reached 17%, above the company’s 10% long-term goal. New-product contribution is promising, but sustained customer use and profitable renewal determine its lasting value.
items: Support sales teams with product-specific customer use cases
Prioritize innovations with repeat usage and renewal potential
Monitor adoption, retention and servicing cost by product cohort

headline: Equinix should convert record-scale bookings into recurring revenue without straining delivery economics.
summary: Bookings growth substantially exceeded monthly recurring revenue growth, while the interconnection base and AFFO per share both advanced. The opportunity is strong, but execution now depends on converting booked demand into available capacity, active services and durable cash earnings per share.
focusTitle: Coordinate customer activation with capacity and capital allocation.
focusText: Prioritize deployment against contracted customer requirements and interconnection opportunities. Manage booking conversion, service reliability and cash returns together so demand growth strengthens recurring economics rather than creating a gap between commitments and delivered services.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Give stronger bookings a clear activation path
cards.text: Annualized gross bookings rose 27% to $1.6 billion. Bookings measure demand rather than recognized sales, so installation and service commencement determine how much becomes recurring revenue.
items: Map booked commitments to capacity and activation milestones
Resolve customer installation and provisioning bottlenecks
Monitor time from booking to revenue-generating service

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Broaden recurring growth through existing customer relationships
cards.text: Monthly recurring revenue grew 7% reported and 8% normalized constant currency. Converting demand and expanding active relationships should reinforce this recurring base without conflating the two growth measures.
items: Target expansion opportunities in active customer deployments
Coordinate account teams around recurring-service adoption
Monitor recurring revenue, churn and customer expansion together

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the interconnection ecosystem as it scales
cards.text: More than 500,000 interconnections at year end provide a substantial connectivity base. Reliable cross-connect delivery and useful partner access help preserve the value of that network.
items: Prioritize reliable provisioning in highly connected locations
Support customers adding useful network and partner connections
Monitor connection adoption and service quality by location

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep per-share cash economics central to expansion
cards.text: Company-defined AFFO per share rose 9% to $38.33. Capacity investment should support that per-share trajectory after the resources needed to activate new customer demand.
items: Rank capacity investments against committed customer requirements
Include deployment spending in site-level cash return decisions
Monitor AFFO per share alongside expansion funding needs

headline: Erie Indemnity should preserve management-fee growth while controlling agent and technology cost absorption.
summary: Policy issuance and renewal fees expanded, but commissions and technology expenses also increased. A large charitable contribution affected net income separately. The operational priority is making the growing fee base support efficient agency service and technology spending, rather than treating the contribution as evidence of weak demand.
focusTitle: Improve the operating return on fee and service growth.
focusText: Connect agent incentives and technology investments to policy servicing, retention and efficient renewals. Evaluate recurring fee economics separately from the charitable contribution so operating decisions address the costs management can improve through execution.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Use fee growth to strengthen policy-service economics
cards.text: Annual policy issuance and renewal management-fee revenue increased 8.2%, or $237.7 million. That expanding revenue base creates room to improve service efficiency and agency support.
items: Identify issuance and renewal workflows with scaling potential
Allocate service capacity to growing agency workloads
Monitor servicing expense relative to management-fee revenue

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make agent incentives earn their recurring cost
cards.text: Commissions increased $175.6 million, partly reflecting premium growth and agent incentives. Incentive design should support durable policy relationships while preserving the economics of management fees.
items: Tie incentive evaluation to renewal and service outcomes
Review commission growth against the associated fee growth
Target agency support where retention benefits justify spending

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn technology spending into lower servicing friction
cards.text: Information technology costs rose $24.3 million across personnel, hardware and software. That spending can support scale if it improves the work agents and service teams perform.
items: Prioritize systems that simplify policy issuance and renewals
Assign business owners to major technology spending categories
Measure adoption and processing effort after system changes

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep the contribution distinct from recurring performance
cards.text: A $100 million charitable contribution reduced net income by $80.6 million after tax. Its effect should inform capital allocation without obscuring the fee and expense trends driving ongoing operations.
items: Separate the contribution when setting recurring operating budgets
Assess discretionary commitments against ongoing cash requirements
Monitor recurring fee profitability before changing service investment

headline: Essex should make portfolio recycling improve rental economics while preserving funding flexibility.
summary: Same-property revenue and NOI grew at similar rates, while Core FFO per share increased more modestly. Acquisitions exceeded dispositions, making investment selection and funding important. Available liquidity provides flexibility, but its inclusion of undrawn facilities means it should not be treated entirely as cash.
focusTitle: Connect property operations and portfolio investment to per-share returns.
focusText: Preserve same-property operating discipline while demanding clear rental and funding economics from acquired communities. Use liquidity selectively, considering borrowing requirements and the relationship between property-level gains and Core FFO per share.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect the rental growth reaching property income
cards.text: Same-property revenue increased 3.3% and NOI increased 3.2%. The close relationship suggests property expense discipline should remain central as leasing conditions and operating costs change.
items: Align leasing decisions with property-level net income
Target controllable expenses without weakening resident service
Monitor revenue growth against expense growth by community

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make acquisitions improve the portfolio beyond added scale
cards.text: Essex acquired seven communities for $829.4 million and sold five for a pro rata $563.8 million. Integration and reinvestment economics matter as much as transaction volume.
items: Set operating plans for each acquired community
Compare acquisition funding costs with expected property economics
Recycle disposition proceeds toward the strongest portfolio opportunities

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep per-share cash earnings in investment decisions
cards.text: Company-defined Core FFO per diluted share rose 2.2% to $15.94. Growth is positive, but new investment should strengthen shareholders’ recurring economics rather than only expanding property NOI.
items: Evaluate investment choices through per-share cash earnings
Examine costs separating NOI growth from Core FFO growth
Monitor acquired-property contribution after associated financing costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Preserve usable liquidity through the investment cycle
cards.text: Immediately available liquidity exceeded $1.7 billion at year end and includes undrawn facilities. That supports flexibility, with borrowing capacity carrying different funding implications from cash already on hand.
items: Distinguish cash balances from available facility capacity
Reserve funding for property commitments and operating needs
Stress new acquisitions against higher drawn funding requirements

headline: Estée Lauder should rebuild skin-care and makeup demand while protecting its gross-margin recovery.
summary: Gross margin improved, but weaker organic skin-care and makeup sales accompanied a lower adjusted operating margin. The combination points toward demand conversion and operating leverage as the priority. Better product margin alone is insufficient if travel retail, Chinese conversion and M·A·C retail remain weak.
focusTitle: Concentrate recovery spending on sell-through and productive brand investment.
focusText: Use the gross-margin improvement to support targeted consumer conversion and retailer inventory normalization. Judge brand spending by sustained sell-through and contribution after selling costs, rather than shipment growth that might merely replenish distributor inventory.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Give skin-care recovery a focused conversion plan
cards.text: Organic skin-care sales fell 12%; management cited Asia travel retail weakness and Chinese consumer conversion. Recovery resources should address those specific selling environments and product propositions.
items: Refine skin-care assortments for the cited retail channels
Test product education and conversion activity with retail partners
Monitor sell-through and inventory alongside reported shipments

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore makeup sell-through before rebuilding retailer inventory
cards.text: Organic makeup sales declined 5%, with management citing M·A·C retail softness and retailer destocking. Stronger replenishment requires better consumer demand and a healthier stock position.
items: Align M·A·C retail launches with observed consumer demand
Coordinate retailer replenishment with actual product sell-through
Monitor aged inventory and promotion dependence by makeup line

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve gross-margin gains during the sales recovery
cards.text: Gross margin increased to 74.0% from 71.7%. That improvement provides support, but recovery promotions and product mix should be managed to retain its economic value.
items: Retain sourcing and product economics supporting improved margin
Favor targeted offers over broad discount dependence
Monitor gross margin as channel and category mix changes

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require selling investment to restore operating leverage
cards.text: Non-GAAP adjusted operating margin fell to 8.0% from 10.2% despite better gross margin. Sales recovery needs to cover the operating resources required to generate it.
items: Prioritize brand programs with measurable conversion contribution
Redirect spending from weak campaigns to effective customer touchpoints
Monitor operating expense absorption as organic sales stabilize

headline: Everest should improve current underwriting economics while reducing reserve uncertainty.
summary: The group combined ratio improved, supported by a smaller unfavorable reserve adjustment, but the attritional ratio worsened and written premiums contracted. The priority is disciplined risk selection and pricing, rather than interpreting the headline combined-ratio improvement as broad-based underwriting progress.
focusTitle: Rebuild underwriting quality before pursuing premium expansion.
focusText: Use current accident-year economics and reserve experience together to guide renewals and capacity. Preserve profitable relationships while addressing weaker risk cohorts, and judge improvement separately from changes in catastrophe losses and prior-year development.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Look beneath the better headline combined ratio
cards.text: The group combined ratio improved to 98.6% from 102.3%. This is encouraging, but the worsening attritional measure means the overall result does not establish stronger underlying underwriting everywhere.
items: Compare renewal decisions with current underwriting economics
Allocate capacity toward lines with sustainable risk-adjusted returns
Monitor combined-ratio changes alongside catastrophe and reserve effects

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Reverse deterioration in attritional profitability
cards.text: The non-GAAP attritional combined ratio rose to 89.6% from 88.1%, excluding catastrophe losses and prior-year development. Pricing and risk selection need attention even as the group ratio improves.
items: Target weaker underwriting cohorts for pricing and terms changes
Strengthen risk selection before expanding exposure
Monitor current loss costs against earned pricing improvements

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build on the smaller reserve-development burden
cards.text: Unfavorable prior-year reserve development fell to $657 million from $1.337 billion. The reduced burden helps, while the remaining adjustment still makes claims feedback important to underwriting decisions.
items: Feed adverse claims experience into renewal assumptions
Prioritize claims reviews in cohorts driving reserve adjustments
Track development by underwriting year and affected business

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Avoid replacing lost premium with weaker business
cards.text: Gross written premiums declined 2.9% to $17.706 billion. Growth should come from adequately priced risks rather than relaxing terms to restore the top line.
items: Distinguish deliberate exposure reduction from customer attrition
Retain customers whose pricing meets underwriting requirements
Measure new-business quality alongside premium volume

headline: Evergy should align its capital plan with enforceable large-load demand and customer cost recovery.
summary: Approved large-load tariffs and signed service agreements improve the framework for serving new demand. They accompany a substantial forward-looking investment plan, while weather and demand weighed on 2025 results. Construction sequencing should therefore follow customer commitments and funding economics, not announced load alone.
focusTitle: Make committed load determine the pace of infrastructure spending.
focusText: Connect each major customer project with service terms, required infrastructure and recovery protections. Preserve flexibility in the investment program so delays in customer ramp-up do not leave existing customers or the balance sheet carrying avoidable costs.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn tariff approvals into workable project protections
cards.text: Kansas and Missouri approved new large-load power-service tariffs in late 2025. Those frameworks are useful when applied to actual service commitments and the infrastructure costs customers require.
items: Apply approved tariff provisions consistently to large-load agreements
Match service pricing with project-specific infrastructure requirements
Monitor recovery protection as customer requirements change

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Schedule capacity around signed customer requirements
cards.text: The release announced service agreements for two new large customer projects and expansions of two existing projects. These commitments need practical ramp-up and construction coordination.
items: Coordinate customer milestones with utility construction readiness
Link capacity reservations to documented service requirements
Monitor agreement changes and delays before accelerating spending

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use the capital plan as a prioritized investment framework
cards.text: Management introduced a $21.6 billion 2026–2030 capital investment plan. It provides direction, but remains forward-looking and should be deployed according to readiness and customer value.
items: Rank projects by reliability need and committed load
Stage spending around permitting, procurement and recovery milestones
Evaluate funding requirements before advancing discretionary projects

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Do not overstate recurring demand from weather-sensitive results
cards.text: Management said weather and demand headwinds affected 2025 despite mitigation efforts. Planning needs to distinguish temporary weather variation from durable customer usage and load commitments.
items: Use weather-normalized demand when setting operating assumptions
Prioritize efficiency measures that preserve service reliability
Stress funding capacity against slower customer load realization

headline: Everpure should turn subscription commitments into durable cash earnings while narrowing the profitability gap.
summary: Subscription services grew and remaining obligations expanded considerably faster, providing a useful demand signal for the former Pure Storage. Strong operating cash generation supports investment, but the large difference between GAAP and non-GAAP margins makes the economic cost of growth important.
focusTitle: Scale recurring services with clear delivery and cash economics.
focusText: Coordinate subscription activation and renewal resources with the contracted workload. Protect cash generation while assessing investments on their full economic cost, so a growing recurring base strengthens reported profitability as well as company-adjusted results.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Convert growing obligations into active subscription value
cards.text: Remaining performance obligations rose 40% to $3.7 billion at fiscal year end. Contracted commitments provide visibility, but fulfillment and revenue timing determine their operating contribution.
items: Map subscription commitments to activation and delivery requirements
Prioritize onboarding resources where contracted demand is strongest
Monitor obligation conversion and changes in customer commitments

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make the profitability gap inform spending choices
cards.text: Fiscal 2026 operating margin was 3.1% GAAP versus 17.3% non-GAAP. Investment decisions should consider the costs excluded from the adjusted measure, not assume the higher margin is fully distributable.
items: Evaluate growth projects using full economic resource costs
Identify recurring costs limiting GAAP operating leverage
Monitor whether subscription growth improves both margin measures

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen the recurring customer base
cards.text: Subscription services revenue reached $1.7 billion, up 15%. Sustaining that growth depends on useful service delivery, renewal execution and expansion within existing customer deployments.
items: Focus account plans on adoption and renewal readiness
Prioritize service capabilities customers use repeatedly
Monitor subscription retention and expansion by customer cohort

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep contracted growth affordable to deliver
cards.text: Operating cash flow was $880 million and company-defined free cash flow was $616 million. Their difference makes investment requirements relevant when deciding how quickly to support additional demand.
items: Sequence infrastructure investment against committed service needs
Preserve collection discipline as subscription commitments expand
Compare available free cash with delivery and investment obligations

headline: Eversource should sustain regulated-network returns while containing remaining offshore-wind exit obligations.
summary: Transmission and electric distribution earnings both improved, supporting higher recurring EPS. The offshore-wind payment loss affected reported earnings separately. The priority is preserving regulated investment execution while ensuring residual exit costs do not undermine the funding available for core network needs.
focusTitle: Keep network investment and legacy obligations on separate capital tracks.
focusText: Prioritize transmission and distribution projects by service need and recoverable returns. Manage expected offshore-wind payments explicitly in liquidity planning, allowing recurring utility progress to guide operations without treating the exit-related loss as a demand problem.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make transmission investment keep earning its return
cards.text: Transmission earnings rose to $776.7 million from $724.6 million; management cited continued system investment. Further spending should retain that connection between useful network assets and earnings contribution.
items: Prioritize transmission projects with clear system benefits
Coordinate commissioning with regulatory recovery requirements
Monitor project cost and earned-return performance together

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Control the remaining wind-exit cash exposure
cards.text: Results included a $75 million after-tax loss tied to expected payments following offshore-wind project sales. The business task is containing residual obligations while protecting funding for the utility.
items: Assign ownership of remaining sale-related payment obligations
Include expected payments in utility funding scenarios
Monitor changes in estimated exposure before allocating discretionary cash

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve distribution earnings through reliable asset execution
cards.text: Electric distribution earnings increased to $667.1 million from $631.7 million. Continued improvement should be supported by disciplined service investment and attention to the costs of operating the network.
items: Rank distribution work by reliability and customer need
Maintain operating-cost discipline alongside asset investment
Monitor distribution project completion and earnings contribution

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Use recurring EPS without losing sight of real obligations
cards.text: Non-GAAP recurring EPS rose to $4.76 from $4.57, while reported EPS was $4.56. Both operating progress and the effects excluded from recurring earnings matter to capital capacity.
items: Base operating priorities on recurring utility performance
Assess distributions after expected legacy cash requirements
Monitor reported earnings and cash alongside recurring EPS

headline: Exelon should fund reliable network investment while preserving customer affordability and per-share value.
summary: Strong outage-duration performance supports the value of utility investment, and rates helped earnings. Favorable PECO weather also contributed. The updated equity funding plan makes project prioritization and customer affordability central: capital needs should translate into dependable service and sustainable returns, not spending alone.
focusTitle: Tie financing to demonstrable network and customer benefits.
focusText: Sequence capital expenditures around reliability priorities, recoverable returns and funding capacity. Keep customer relief targeted and evaluate performance on a weather-normalized basis so equity financing and rate-supported earnings are matched by durable operating improvements.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve reliability as the investment program expands
cards.text: All Exelon utilities achieved first-quartile SAIDI performance, with ComEd in the top decile. These outage-duration results provide a concrete service outcome to protect during capital allocation.
items: Replicate effective outage-reduction practices across utility operations
Prioritize projects addressing recurring interruption causes
Monitor outage duration alongside maintenance and capital spending

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make equity funding earn its place in the plan
cards.text: The updated four-year financing plan includes $3.4 billion of equity for capital expenditures. That forward-looking funding requirement raises the importance of selecting productive, recoverable network investments.
items: Stage financing around committed project cash requirements
Rank capital projects by service benefit and earned returns
Monitor funding needs and per-share earnings contribution together

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Connect customer assistance with sustainable service access
cards.text: Exelon reported $60 million of direct assistance through its Customer Relief Fund. Relief can support customer access while network investment continues, provided program execution stays focused on need.
items: Coordinate relief delivery with customer assistance channels
Target outreach toward customers eligible for available support
Monitor assistance uptake and unresolved affordability needs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Separate rate progress from the weather contribution
cards.text: Management cited distribution and transmission rates and favorable PECO weather among earnings drivers. Durable financial capacity depends more on recoverable operations than repeating favorable weather.
items: Use weather-normalized earnings when sizing recurring commitments
Align rate recovery with completed network investment
Monitor operating costs against recurring rate-supported revenue

headline: Expand Energy should balance natural-gas cash generation, debt reduction and shareholder distributions.
summary: Substantial operating cash flow supported both debt reduction and capital returns in 2025. With production overwhelmingly natural gas, the priority is preserving allocation flexibility across gas-market conditions rather than maximizing volume or distributions independently. Earlier-period comparisons also require the merger-adjusted context.
focusTitle: Allocate cash after sustaining the operating base and balance sheet.
focusText: Make development, debt repayment and distributions compete within a single cash framework. Preserve the ability to respond to changing gas economics while keeping merger-adjusted operating comparisons consistent and avoiding permanent commitments based only on one year’s cash generation.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make gas concentration shape production decisions
cards.text: Average 2025 production was approximately 7.18 Bcfe per day, 92% natural gas. This scale makes disciplined development economics more useful than volume targets considered in isolation.
items: Rank development activity by delivered natural-gas economics
Coordinate production plans with available sales and transport options
Stress cash requirements against changing gas realizations

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Keep capital returns flexible around operating needs
cards.text: The company returned $865 million through dividends and repurchases. Further distributions should follow the cash left after development and financing commitments, rather than becoming an inflexible claim on cash.
items: Separate recurring dividend commitments from discretionary repurchases
Size repurchases after committed development and debt requirements
Monitor distributions against cash available across gas scenarios

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the cash engine supporting allocation choices
cards.text: Full-year operating cash flow was $4.575 billion. That provides capacity, but operating cash precedes development spending and should not be treated as entirely available for distributions.
items: Tie operating budgets to field-level cash economics
Maintain collection and cost discipline across production operations
Assess cash remaining after the investment needed to sustain assets

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Continue reducing financing constraints without starving operations
cards.text: Gross debt fell approximately $660 million during 2025. Further balance-sheet improvement can strengthen flexibility when matched with the operating investment required to protect cash generation.
items: Prioritize debt decisions using financing cost and liquidity needs
Reserve capacity for committed field and operating expenditures
Monitor gross debt alongside investment-adjusted cash generation

headline: Expedia should preserve booking growth while sustaining profit and cash gains from its travel platform.
summary: Room nights and gross bookings both grew 8%, while adjusted EBITDA and operating cash grew faster. That combination suggests favorable operating leverage. The priority is keeping travel acquisition, servicing and investment disciplined so booking expansion continues to strengthen economics rather than merely increasing transaction volume.
focusTitle: Scale the travel relationships that produce profitable repeat usage.
focusText: Preserve booking momentum while allocating commercial and product spending toward repeat travelers and reliable fulfillment. Judge expansion through adjusted profitability and cash conversion together, recognizing that gross bookings measure travel transaction value rather than Expedia revenue.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Build on room-night volume with reliable travel execution
cards.text: Booked room nights increased 8% to 415.4 million. Sustained volume requires useful inventory, a smooth booking experience and effective service when travel plans change.
items: Prioritize inventory availability in proven traveler use cases
Reduce friction in booking and post-booking service journeys
Monitor completed stays, repeat bookings and service issues

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make booking acquisition improve platform economics
cards.text: Gross bookings increased 8% to $119.59 billion. Because this is transaction value, customer-acquisition decisions need to be based on retained economics rather than gross booking volume alone.
items: Allocate marketing using contribution after traveler acquisition costs
Develop repeat-booking journeys for existing customers
Monitor conversion and retained economics across booking channels

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect operating leverage as transaction volume scales
cards.text: Adjusted EBITDA rose 19% to $3.501 billion, ahead of booking growth. Preserve the practices supporting that relationship while maintaining the service quality required for repeat business.
items: Extend efficient servicing practices across growing travel categories
Prioritize platform investments with measurable commercial contribution
Monitor adjusted profit growth against booking and expense growth

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep cash growth grounded in sustainable conversion
cards.text: Operating cash flow increased 26% to $3.88 billion. Stronger cash supports investment, but allocation should consider the timing of travel receipts and associated service obligations.
items: Plan liquidity around booking and travel-service timing
Fund product improvements against clear customer-use milestones
Monitor operating cash conversion alongside booking growth

headline: Expeditors should make its larger staffing base earn stronger logistics productivity.
summary: Salaries and other operating expenses grew faster than direct transportation costs, while year-end headcount increased. That does not establish weak demand, but it makes workforce deployment and shipment economics the operational priority. Capital returns should remain compatible with the resources needed to serve customers efficiently.
focusTitle: Align staffing and operating spending with profitable customer workload.
focusText: Use lane, branch and account economics to deploy the expanded workforce. Preserve logistics service quality while improving capacity utilization, and size distributions only after the cash and investment required to support reliable customer operations.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Require workforce growth to improve shipment execution
cards.text: Year-end full-time-equivalent headcount rose to 20,359 from 18,917. The larger team should reduce processing friction or support profitable workload, rather than simply raise the permanent cost base.
items: Deploy staffing against branch and shipment workload patterns
Standardize effective shipment-handling practices across offices
Monitor workload, service quality and productivity per employee

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Slow expense growth through better operating design
cards.text: Salaries and other operating expenses rose 10% to $2.614 billion. Management should distinguish capacity needed for growth from processes that add cost without improving customer service.
items: Target duplicated manual work in shipment administration
Adjust staffing schedules to recurring customer demand
Compare branch expense growth with retained logistics contribution

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep transport procurement disciplined as costs rise
cards.text: Direct transportation and related costs increased 3% to $7.402 billion. Purchase cost trends need to be matched with lane economics and customer pricing before judging profitability.

Review lane pricing when transport purchase costs change
Monitor gross contribution after direct transportation expenses

cards.text: Expeditors returned $875 million through dividends and repurchases in 2025. That allocation should preserve liquidity for shipment operations and productive investment in a larger organization.
items: Reserve cash for logistics working-capital and service needs
Prioritize efficiency investments with clear operating benefits
Size discretionary repurchases after operating funding requirements

headline: Extra Space should restore same-store income while scaling management and acquisitions selectively.
summary: Nearly flat same-store revenue, lower occupancy and declining same-store NOI indicate pressure in the existing portfolio. focusTitle: Put existing-store profitability at the center of growth decisions.
focusText: Coordinate local pricing, customer retention and operating costs to improve property income. Apply those lessons to acquired stores and expand third-party management where the service platform can support owners without diluting attention from the existing portfolio.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Convert stable revenue into healthier property income
cards.text: Same-store revenue grew 0.1%, while company-defined same-store NOI fell 1.7%. With little revenue cushion, controllable property expenses and the profitability of customer acquisition deserve attention.
items: Target property expenses that do not improve occupancy
Evaluate marketing using income after customer-acquisition spending
Monitor store-level revenue against controllable operating costs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve occupancy without relying on uneconomic concessions
cards.text: Ending same-store occupancy declined to 92.6% from 93.3%. Local leasing and retention actions should fill useful capacity while preserving rental economics.

Improve inquiry follow-up and move-in conversion
Monitor occupancy, achieved rents and customer retention together

cards.text: A net 281 stores joined third-party management in 2025. This expands the operating platform, making onboarding quality and repeatable store management important to retaining owners.
items: Standardize onboarding and operating support for added stores
Apply proven leasing practices across managed locations
Monitor owner retention and service workload as stores increase

items: Set property-specific leasing and cost plans after acquisition
Sequence integration resources around operational readiness
Compare acquired-store income with investment and financing requirements

headline: F5 should convert systems momentum into durable software and service relationships while protecting trust.

Monitor follow-on software and service attachment by systems cohort

Monitor renewal retention and service adoption after installations

Monitor deal progression and renewals for emerging friction

headline: FactSet should convert subscription momentum into profitable client expansion while disciplining technology spending.

cards.text: Organic annual subscription value reached $2.3709 billion, up 5.7%, at August 31. ASV is a run-rate measure, so activation and retention remain important before treating it as earned revenue.

Monitor ASV conversion, renewals and client usage together

Assign commercial owners to major platform investments
Monitor recurring technology costs against incremental subscription economics

cards.label: What is working

Scale reusable capabilities across existing client workflows
Monitor GAAP margin as development and compensation costs evolve

Extend effective cross-selling within established client relationships
Monitor retention and expansion across the cited client groups

headline: Fair Isaac should accelerate platform adoption while stabilizing non-platform software relationships.
summary: Platform recurring revenue and retention outperform the non-platform base materially, but total software growth remains modest. Retain support for non-platform customers and structure transitions around their requirements, so stronger platform expansion improves total software retention rather than merely offsetting erosion elsewhere.

cards.text: Platform software ARR rose 16%, while non-platform ARR declined 2%. The divergence supports prioritizing platform opportunities, with investment tied to specific customer use cases and implementation readiness.

Equip sales teams with practical adoption and migration plans
Monitor platform growth after implementation and support costs

cards.label: What could improve

cards.text: Platform net retention was 112% versus 97% for non-platform software. The weaker cohort requires customer-level attention to product needs, renewal friction and feasible transition options.

Offer migration paths matched to customer operating requirements
Monitor non-platform contraction and completed customer transitions

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use platform expansion as a repeatable commercial model

Coordinate customer success resources with larger platform deployments
Monitor expansion durability across successive platform customer cohorts

Prioritize cross-selling that adds useful recurring customer value
Monitor overall ARR growth alongside mix and retention shifts

headline: Fastenal should preserve sales-driven operating leverage while making incremental investment productive.

Extend effective account-development practices across comparable customers
Monitor daily sales growth alongside account retention and usage

Stage asset deployment around demonstrable local demand
Monitor utilization and fulfillment productivity after investment

Match staffing additions to profitable sales workload
Monitor service quality alongside SG&A as a sales share

Preserve purchasing discipline in faster-growing product requirements
Monitor gross profit by customer and product mix

headline: Federal Realty should convert signed leases into occupied, rent-producing space while preserving strong lease economics.

cards.title: Turn leasing activity into dependable rental income
cards.text: Federal Realty signed 454 leases covering approximately 2.5 million square feet of retail space. The scale of signed activity makes execution after signing central to its income contribution.

Coordinate landlord work with tenant build-out requirements
Monitor lease commencement and opening delays by property

cards.label: What could improve

Prioritize capital and property support for near-ready openings
Monitor occupied space and rent commencement together

Assess tenant affordability and operating fit before signing
Compare lease spreads with concessions and landlord commitments

Prioritize tenant retention where economics remain attractive
Monitor comparable income using the same exclusion basis

headline: FedEx should make transformation savings restore operating margin while maintaining network investment discipline.

cards.title: Make transformation savings durable in daily operations
cards.text: FedEx reported more than $1 billion of transformation-related cost savings in fiscal 2026. The operational task is embedding those benefits in routes, facilities and workflows while protecting customer service.

Standardize network processes behind successful cost reductions
Monitor service reliability alongside realized operating cost changes

cards.label: What could improve

Align capacity and operating schedules with shipment requirements
Monitor margin using comparable continuing business scope

Monitor asset utilization and maintenance needs after spending reductions

Reserve funding for essential network and transition requirements
Evaluate repurchases after service and investment commitments

headline: FedEx Freight should restore freight operating leverage while separating spin-off costs from recurring pressure.

Monitor adjusted operating income alongside service performance

Monitor revenue quality and customer mix alongside volume

Protect frontline service capacity during organizational handoffs
Monitor separation cash needs separately from recurring freight costs

Monitor gross profit after delivery and service requirements

Monitor operating expense absorption on both reported bases
