cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Capital Market Solutions’ operating discipline
cards.text: Capital Market Solutions adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 86 basis points to 51.8%. Retain the commercial and delivery practices supporting those economics while funding customer needs selectively.
items: Extend efficient delivery practices across comparable customer engagements
Protect service quality while controlling implementation effort
Monitor segment profitability as revenue mix and investment change

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep the deferred-tax charge in its proper allocation context
cards.text: GAAP continuing earnings included $539 million of noncash deferred-tax expense related to the planned Worldpay stake sale. This affects reported earnings without establishing deterioration in customer operations.
items: Base operating interventions on recurring business performance
Plan transaction-related capital uses around actual cash implications
Monitor continuing operating cash alongside reported earnings effects

headline: First Solar should translate manufacturing expansion into reliable module delivery and disciplined cash deployment.
summary: Higher third-party module volume and the Louisiana commissioning demonstrate expanding production activity. A decision to establish another facility raises the importance of execution and capital prioritization. Year-end net cash provides capacity, but manufacturing tax-credit monetization contributed to its increase and should inform cash planning.
focusTitle: Sequence factory expansion around productive capacity and customer delivery.
focusText: Stabilize the commissioned plant before committing resources that dilute operating focus. Evaluate South Carolina alongside existing capacity needs, and distinguish cash generated by module operations from tax-credit monetization when sizing investment and liquidity reserves.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make higher module volume support dependable fulfillment
cards.text: Third-party module volume increased 24% in 2025. Sustaining that activity requires coordinated production, quality control and customer delivery rather than judging factory success by volume alone.
items: Align manufacturing schedules with customer delivery requirements
Protect module quality as production activity increases
Monitor shipment execution and production efficiency together

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Turn Louisiana commissioning into stable operating performance
cards.text: Management reported commissioning the Louisiana factory during 2025. Commissioning advances capacity, while dependable output and operating economics require continued ramp-up attention.
items: Assign clear ownership of factory ramp-up issues
Prioritize production training and process stability
Monitor usable output, quality and operating costs during ramp-up

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use the net-cash position to preserve execution flexibility
cards.text: Year-end company-defined net cash was $2.4 billion. That supports manufacturing investment, provided allocations also recognize operating needs and the timing of tax-credit cash receipts.
items: Reserve liquidity for committed factory and customer obligations
Rank investments by readiness and manufacturing benefit
Monitor operating cash separately from tax-credit monetization proceeds

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Stage South Carolina spending around a credible capacity case
cards.text: The company decided to establish a South Carolina facility. The next allocation decisions should reflect customer requirements, execution capacity and the resources already committed to the manufacturing network.
items: Sequence new-facility commitments around construction readiness
Compare expansion needs with existing factory utilization
Monitor combined funding and management demands across factory projects

headline: FirstEnergy should convert rate-base expansion into durable earned returns while containing regulatory charges.
summary: Transmission investment and distribution Core Earnings improved, supporting regulated growth. Regulatory charges excluded from Core EPS remain economically relevant. The priority is aligning construction, recovery and compliance so the growing asset base strengthens reported and adjusted results.
focusTitle: Match each investment commitment with recovery and regulatory discipline.
focusText: Prioritize transmission and distribution projects with clear customer value and achievable recovery. Preserve the operating gains while addressing the business decisions behind regulatory charges, rather than allowing Core EPS to become the sole measure of funding capacity.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make transmission asset growth earn reliable returns
cards.text: Total transmission rate base grew nearly 11%. Continued investment should be selected and delivered around useful network capacity, cost control and the mechanisms that convert assets into earnings.
items: Rank transmission work by system need and recoverability
Coordinate project completion with applicable rate mechanisms
Monitor project costs and earned returns as assets enter service

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Address regulatory charges alongside operating improvement
cards.text: The annual bridge included $0.58 per share of regulatory charges excluded from Core EPS. Their exclusion does not remove the need to improve decisions and controls affecting regulatory outcomes.
items: Assign remediation ownership to issues behind regulatory charges
Strengthen review of spending with uncertain customer recovery
Monitor recurrence and cash implications of regulatory adjustments

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect distribution earnings from rates and stronger sales
cards.text: Distribution Core Earnings rose $0.23 per share; management cited Pennsylvania base rates and stronger sales. Operating resources should preserve customer service and the economics of that regulated growth.
items: Align distribution budgets with new rate-supported requirements
Prioritize reliability work benefiting the served customer base
Monitor recurring sales and costs against rate-supported earnings

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep faster Integrated transmission expansion operationally controlled
cards.text: The Integrated segment’s transmission rate base increased 14%. Faster asset growth raises execution and recovery demands even when the overall regulated investment direction is attractive.
items: Stage segment projects around construction and funding readiness
Track recovery milestones alongside Integrated transmission spending
Monitor earnings contribution after financing and operating requirements

headline: Fiserv should turn merchant growth into renewed margin and free-cash-flow improvement.
summary: Merchant Solutions organic growth outpaced Financial Solutions, but GAAP operating margin and company-defined free cash flow both declined. The priority is improving the cost and cash economics of serving these businesses, rather than treating growth in the faster segment as sufficient evidence of stronger overall performance.
focusTitle: Prioritize customer growth that improves contribution and cash conversion.
focusText: Preserve merchant momentum while addressing slower financial-services expansion and operating cost absorption. Allocate product and implementation resources using recurring customer economics, then assess whether those decisions improve both reported margin and cash available after investment.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve merchant momentum with disciplined delivery economics
cards.text: Merchant Solutions organic revenue increased 6%. Commercial investment should deepen useful merchant relationships while retaining the contribution left after onboarding, servicing and product costs.
items: Target merchant offers with repeatable adoption and retention
Reduce friction in merchant implementation and ongoing service
Monitor account contribution alongside organic revenue growth

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Give Financial Solutions a focused expansion agenda
cards.text: Financial Solutions organic revenue increased 2%, trailing Merchant Solutions. The priority is identifying customer needs that support useful product expansion rather than spreading investment evenly across opportunities.
items: Focus account plans on adopted customer workflows
Prioritize product improvements addressing renewal and expansion barriers
Monitor retention and incremental revenue from targeted customer cohorts

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use the remaining cash base selectively
cards.text: Company-defined free cash flow was $4.44 billion, down from $5.23 billion. The business still generates substantial cash, but declining conversion warrants tighter prioritization of competing commitments.
items: Rank investment proposals by cash contribution after delivery costs
Maintain collection discipline in expanding customer relationships
Monitor cash remaining after committed product and operating investment

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make operating leverage a condition of further expansion
cards.text: GAAP operating margin fell to 27.5% from 28.7%. Growth should support stronger reported economics through scalable implementation and cost discipline, not simply add operating complexity.
items: Identify cost categories growing faster than associated revenue
Standardize service processes across comparable customer deployments
Monitor GAAP margin as segment growth and spending mix change

headline: Flex should preserve manufacturing cash generation while controlling portfolio-change costs.
summary: Operating cash generation was substantial, but company-defined free cash flow edged lower and adjusted margin exceeded GAAP margin. Portfolio-optimization costs make disciplined resource allocation important. The priority is protecting customer manufacturing execution and investment economics while preparing organizational changes without assuming the subsequent separation announcement was completed in-year.
focusTitle: Keep operating delivery and portfolio work financially accountable.
focusText: Evaluate manufacturing investments on cash requirements and full operating costs. Give portfolio-change spending separate ownership, while preserving the people and equipment needed for customers, so organizational decisions do not weaken the cash engine funding the transition.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect the manufacturing operations generating cash
cards.text: Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow was $1.685 billion. Preserve customer delivery and working-capital discipline so that cash generation remains dependable through portfolio changes.
items: Align purchasing and production schedules with customer requirements
Prioritize collections and inventory control in manufacturing programs
Monitor operating cash alongside program delivery and working capital

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve cash retained after investment requirements
cards.text: Company-defined free cash flow was $1.060 billion versus $1.082 billion in fiscal 2025. The modest decline favors selective capital allocation rather than a broad reduction in productive manufacturing capacity.
items: Rank equipment spending by committed customer demand
Challenge investments with weak utilization or unclear cash returns
Monitor free cash after essential manufacturing investment

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve adjusted profitability with full-cost visibility
cards.text: GAAP operating margin was 4.9% versus 6.3% adjusted. Use the stronger adjusted economics as an operating reference while including excluded costs in decisions about sustainable investment capacity.
items: Replicate efficient production practices across comparable programs
Price new work for its complete operating requirements
Monitor reported margin alongside adjusted program economics

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Contain portfolio spending without disrupting customers
cards.text: Fiscal 2026 included approximately $53 million of spin-off and other portfolio-optimization costs. These expenditures need clear control, and the subsequent separation strategy should not be treated as a completed fiscal-year transaction.
items: Assign owners and budgets to portfolio-change workstreams
Coordinate organizational handoffs around manufacturing service requirements
Monitor change-related spending and customer delivery interruptions

headline: Ford should scale profitable software and credit strengths while tightening Model e and Blue economics.
summary: Pro subscriptions and Credit earnings grew strongly, while Model e remained loss-making and Blue wholesales declined. Capital allocation should reflect each business’s economics. Segment EBIT and Credit pre-tax earnings inform operating analysis but differ from consolidated GAAP net income.
focusTitle: Make each business earn resources on its own customer economics.
focusText: Support useful Pro software adoption and prudent credit growth, while requiring Model e spending and Blue production decisions to reflect demand and contribution. Avoid using progress in one segment to postpone operational choices in another.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Deepen the software value delivered to Pro customers
cards.text: Ford Pro paid software subscriptions increased 30%. Sustaining that growth requires active use and customer value rather than subscription additions alone.
items: Prioritize software features supporting customers’ vehicle operations
Coordinate adoption support with fleet customer account plans
Monitor subscription usage, renewals and contribution after support costs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Keep Model e investment tied to improving unit economics
cards.text: Model e’s segment EBIT loss narrowed to $4.806 billion from $5.105 billion, but remains substantial. Investment should follow credible product economics and customer demand rather than scale alone.
items: Rank product and capacity decisions by contribution potential
Target manufacturing and product costs with the clearest payoff
Monitor loss improvement alongside volume and capital requirements

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Credit earnings through disciplined underwriting
cards.text: Ford Credit delivered $2.6 billion of earnings before taxes, up 55%. Protecting credit quality and funding economics is central to retaining that support as vehicle-market conditions change.
items: Keep credit decisions aligned with borrower repayment capacity
Balance financing offers with funding and risk costs
Monitor credit performance and funding needs alongside pre-tax earnings

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Align Blue production with the weaker wholesale base
cards.text: Ford Blue wholesales fell 5% to 2.728 million vehicles. Production, inventory and commercial actions should preserve customer value and vehicle contribution without assuming volume recovery.
items: Adjust production mix to observed vehicle demand
Coordinate dealer inventory with practical sell-through requirements
Monitor incentives and contribution alongside wholesale volumes

headline: Fortinet should turn broad security demand into retained customer value and durable cash generation.
summary: Product revenue and billings both grew strongly, with faster growth in Unified SASE and Security Operations billings. Substantial free cash flow supports investment. The priority is converting that demand into deployed, renewed services while preserving implementation quality and the economics of the expanding security platform.
focusTitle: Link platform selling to successful deployment and retention.
focusText: Allocate technical and commercial resources to customer security use cases with clear adoption paths. Maintain product delivery and recurring service quality, and use cash generation to fund the capabilities needed to convert billings into durable customer relationships.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Scale the faster-growing platform use cases
cards.text: Unified SASE and Security Operations billings grew 24%. That demand supports targeted investment, provided customers can implement the capabilities and realize useful security outcomes.
items: Prioritize deployment support for SASE and Security Operations
Coordinate cross-selling around customer security requirements
Monitor adoption and renewals after initial platform purchases

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make billings growth translate into customer delivery
cards.text: Annual company-defined billings increased 16% to $7.55 billion. Billings are not GAAP revenue, making fulfillment, service activation and renewal quality important to the demand signal.
items: Map billed commitments to implementation and service obligations
Resolve deployment bottlenecks affecting customer activation
Monitor conversion and recurring retention alongside billings growth

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the product engine behind customer expansion
cards.text: Product revenue rose 16% to $2.22 billion. Hardware and product adoption can support broader security relationships when the installed base receives effective implementation and lifecycle support.
items: Align product availability with confirmed customer deployment needs
Offer relevant platform capabilities to active product customers
Monitor product deployment quality and follow-on service adoption

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep cash investment focused on sustainable platform economics
cards.text: Fortinet generated $2.21 billion of company-defined free cash flow. That provides capacity, while disciplined allocation is needed to sustain support and product investment as customer commitments grow.
items: Prioritize engineering and support investments tied to adoption
Reserve cash for committed product and service requirements
Evaluate expansion spending using retained customer contribution

headline: Fortive should improve healthcare execution and cash growth before leaning further on repurchases.
summary: Continuing operations showed modest core growth, with weaker growth and slightly lower margin in Advanced Healthcare Solutions. Free cash flow also declined while repurchases were substantial. The priority is strengthening operating contribution and cash conversion across the post-Ralliant portfolio rather than relying mainly on capital returns.
focusTitle: Direct resources toward operating improvements in the retained businesses.
focusText: Prioritize healthcare productivity and useful growth in Intelligent Operating Solutions. Keep repurchases flexible around the investment required to improve those operations, and evaluate progress on a continuing-operations basis after the June 2025 Ralliant separation.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Build on Intelligent Operating Solutions’ core growth
cards.text: Intelligent Operating Solutions core revenue increased 2.1%. The modest growth supports selective customer and product investment, with attention to delivery economics rather than broad expansion spending.
items: Prioritize offerings with demonstrated recurring customer demand
Extend effective customer-development practices across comparable accounts
Monitor incremental contribution from core revenue growth

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve healthcare growth and cost absorption together
cards.text: Advanced Healthcare Solutions core revenue grew 0.8%, while GAAP operating margin slipped to 10.6% from 10.8%. Commercial actions and operating productivity need to reinforce one another.
items: Target customer workflows with clear product adoption opportunities
Address delivery and service processes limiting operating efficiency
Monitor healthcare margin as core revenue and costs change

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the substantial remaining cash base
cards.text: Company-defined free cash flow was $931 million, down 1.3%. The retained businesses still generate cash, but sustaining that base should precede permanent increases in competing commitments.
items: Prioritize working-capital actions within continuing operations
Fund product and service improvements with clear commercial benefits
Monitor free cash after essential operating investment

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Balance repurchases with the retained portfolio’s needs
cards.text: Fortive deployed approximately $1.6 billion toward repurchases in 2025. Allocation should remain responsive to operating investment and funding requirements following the Ralliant separation.
items: Rank repurchases against healthcare and operating-improvement investments
Maintain liquidity for continuing-business commitments
Monitor capital returns against internally generated free cash

headline: Fox should retain recurring distribution strength while managing event-sensitive advertising and content costs.
summary: Advertising and sublicensing benefited from major sports and political activity, while affiliate fees provided recurring support. The priority is preserving monetization while keeping rights, production and digital-content commitments justified beyond favorable event comparisons.
focusTitle: Allocate content spending using repeatable audience and cash economics.
focusText: Build on affiliate relationships and effective Tubi and news monetization, while evaluating sports and digital commitments against their full costs. Separate recurring commercial improvement from event-driven revenue when setting the next cycle of operating and investment commitments.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Carry advertising strengths beyond major event comparisons
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 advertising revenue rose 26%; management cited Super Bowl LIX, political advertising, Tubi and news pricing and ratings. These drivers have different repeatability and should inform distinct sales plans.
items: Extend effective Tubi and news advertiser relationships
Package audience opportunities around actual programming availability
Monitor recurring advertising demand separately from event-driven contributions

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make content commitments earn their full operating cost
cards.text: Management reported higher sports-rights amortization, production costs and digital-content costs. Strong revenue growth should not obscure the cost required to deliver and monetize that programming.
items: Evaluate rights and production decisions using full contribution
Prioritize digital content with demonstrable audience monetization
Monitor content cost growth against associated advertising and fees

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the recurring affiliate-fee foundation
cards.text: Affiliate fees grew 5%, including 7% in Television and 3% in Cable Network Programming. These relationships support the business across advertising cycles when programming value and distribution execution remain strong.
items: Prepare renewals around demonstrated programming and audience value
Coordinate distribution strategy with content investment priorities
Monitor affiliate retention and economics by programming business

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Do not budget sublicensing growth as automatically recurring
cards.text: Other revenue increased 47%, primarily from higher sports sublicensing. That monetization is useful, but future spending should reflect the availability and economics of sublicensing opportunities.
items: Assess sublicensing proceeds alongside underlying rights commitments
Align future programming budgets with contracted revenue visibility
Monitor contribution after the costs attached to sublicensed content

headline: Franklin Resources should stabilize Western Asset while scaling the franchises attracting client capital.
summary: Preliminary results show large outflows concentrated at Western Asset, alongside inflows elsewhere and alternatives fundraising. Market and other AUM movements also helped. The priority is targeted client retention and investment, rather than interpreting asset growth alone as organic recovery.
focusTitle: Separate franchise repair from expansion in proven fundraising channels.
focusText: Give Western Asset a focused client-retention agenda while preserving the teams and products attracting inflows elsewhere. Integrate Apera around client and operating needs, and base resource decisions on organic flows and retained economics rather than market-supported AUM.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make Western Asset client retention the central repair task
cards.text: Long-term net outflows totaled $97.4 billion, including $141.9 billion at Western Asset. The concentration calls for specific relationship and product actions rather than uniform cuts across the organization.
items: Prioritize outreach to Western Asset clients facing allocation decisions
Address client concerns through relevant investment and service teams
Monitor gross redemptions and retained mandates by strategy

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Scale the businesses already winning client allocations
cards.text: Excluding Western Asset, long-term net inflows were $44.5 billion. Resource allocation should preserve those fundraising and retention strengths while the concentrated outflow problem is addressed.
items: Identify strategies and channels driving the positive net flows
Allocate distribution support to demonstrated client demand
Monitor flow durability and contribution after servicing costs

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build alternatives growth on disciplined integration
cards.text: Alternative AUM reached $270 billion after the Apera acquisition and $26.2 billion of fundraising. Preserve fundraising capability while integrating the acquisition around useful client and operating synergies.
items: Coordinate Apera client coverage with existing alternatives teams
Preserve investment capabilities supporting successful fundraising
Monitor retained fundraising and integration resource requirements

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Distinguish asset-market support from client recovery
cards.text: AUM benefited from $67.6 billion of net market change, distributions and other movements. Those movements should not substitute for evidence that client redemptions are improving.
items: Base distribution staffing decisions on organic flow opportunities
Stress fee capacity against less supportive asset movements
Monitor client flows separately from market and other AUM changes

headline: Freeport should protect copper cash economics while executing capital-intensive mining and processing work.
summary: Copper output, prices and unit costs provide the operating foundation, while mining and Indonesian processing projects require substantial capital. Prioritize production reliability and project economics. Sales exceeding production should not be mistaken for expanding mine output.
focusTitle: Link project spending to reliable production and full cash returns.
focusText: Prioritize mining and processing work that supports dependable operating capacity. Evaluate returns across commodity-price conditions and include capital requirements alongside unit cash costs, without presenting future restart plans as completed 2025 operating achievements.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Align copper delivery commitments with actual output
cards.text: Copper production totaled 3.4 billion pounds, while sales were 3.6 billion pounds. The distinction makes production reliability and the source of shipment availability important to operating planning.
items: Coordinate mine output plans with customer delivery requirements
Identify operational constraints affecting dependable copper production
Monitor production and sales separately when allocating capacity

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Give major capital projects clear operating milestones
cards.text: Capital expenditures totaled $4.494 billion, including mining and Indonesian processing projects. Their value depends on productive assets and operating readiness, not merely completing spending.
items: Prioritize project work by operational readiness and critical dependencies
Coordinate processing needs with mining and delivery plans
Monitor project costs, commissioning progress and expected operating contribution

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the unit-cost foundation without underinvesting
cards.text: Company-defined unit net cash costs averaged $1.65 per pound of copper. This helps assess operating economics, but capital and other funding requirements still matter to full cash returns.
items: Protect maintenance and operating practices supporting efficient output
Target controllable mining and processing cost pressures
Evaluate project returns after both unit costs and capital needs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep commodity prices separate from execution progress
cards.text: Realized copper price was $4.75 per pound and gold price was $3,423 per ounce. Favorable realizations can support cash, but should not become the sole basis for permanent project commitments.
items: Stress project economics across lower metal-price realizations
Stage discretionary spending around operating and funding readiness
Monitor cash generation against commodity and production changes

headline: Garmin should sustain Fitness-led growth while protecting product quality across its broader portfolio.
summary: Fitness led growth, while Outdoor, Aviation and Marine also advanced and unit shipments reached a record. The evidence supports disciplined expansion rather than a recovery program. The priority is maintaining differentiated products, reliable fulfillment and effective support as both volume and the breadth of growth increase.
focusTitle: Scale the strongest product opportunities without weakening execution.
focusText: Give Fitness the resources needed to sustain adoption, while retaining segment-specific product and service capabilities elsewhere. Match production and support capacity to actual demand, and assess growth quality through customer usage, product reliability and commercial economics.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Support Fitness momentum with repeatable product adoption
cards.text: Fitness revenue increased 33% to $2.357 billion. Strong growth warrants focused investment in the product experience and commercial execution that can sustain customer demand beyond initial purchases.
items: Prioritize product improvements tied to active customer use
Coordinate inventory and launches with demonstrated Fitness demand
Monitor repeat usage, product returns and sales mix

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Develop Outdoor growth without copying Fitness allocation mechanically
cards.text: Outdoor revenue increased 5% to $2.054 billion. Its different growth pace calls for product-specific prioritization rather than assuming the fastest-growing segment’s spending model applies everywhere.
items: Identify Outdoor products with the strongest customer response
Target development and distribution support to those opportunities
Monitor product contribution and inventory alongside Outdoor revenue

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve broad-based Aviation and Marine execution
cards.text: Aviation revenue grew 13% and Marine revenue grew 10%. Sustaining this breadth requires attention to each segment’s customer requirements and deployment or support needs.
items: Maintain segment-specific product and technical-support expertise
Allocate development resources to demonstrated Aviation and Marine demand
Monitor delivery reliability and customer adoption within each segment

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep record shipments from straining operating quality
cards.text: Garmin shipped more than 20 million units, a company record. Larger volume raises the importance of supply planning, product consistency and service capacity even when reported growth is positive.
items: Align production commitments with channel sell-through requirements
Preserve quality controls as shipment volumes scale
Monitor inventory, warranty issues and support workload together

headline: Gartner should restore contract growth and cash conversion before extending aggressive capital returns.
summary: Nearly flat FX-neutral contract value and lower cash generation make recurring client economics the priority. Substantial repurchases and a Digital Markets impairment reinforce the need for disciplined allocation, with operating improvement supplying the basis for future capital returns.
focusTitle: Reallocate toward client value and internally funded growth.
focusText: Focus commercial and product resources on contract renewal and expansion, reassess Digital Markets investment against credible economics, and preserve cash flexibility. Judge the next phase by recurring contract progress and cash conversion before increasing discretionary repurchase commitments.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make client value translate into stronger contract growth
cards.text: Year-end contract value was approximately $5.2 billion, up 1% FX-neutral. The modest growth makes client retention and useful expansion more important than broad commercial spending without adoption evidence.
items: Target renewal support to client usage and decision needs
Prioritize expansion within engaged client relationships
Monitor renewal retention and new contract contribution separately

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve the cash economics of serving clients
cards.text: Operating cash flow declined 13%, and company-defined free cash flow fell 15%. Operating spending and investment should be tied more closely to sustained client contribution and collections.
items: Prioritize collection issues affecting recurring contract cash
Rank growth investments by retained client contribution
Monitor cash conversion alongside contract value and operating costs

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use repurchase flexibility to protect operating investment
cards.text: Gartner repurchased 7.0 million shares for $2.0 billion. The discretionary element of capital returns can help preserve resources for client-facing improvements when internal cash generation weakens.
items: Compare repurchases with high-value client and product investments
Reserve funding for committed operating and investment needs
Monitor repurchase spending against internally generated free cash

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Reset Digital Markets allocation around demonstrable economics
cards.text: Annual adjustments included a $150 million Digital Markets goodwill impairment. The charge warrants reassessing capital allocation and business assumptions, without treating it as an equivalent current cash outflow.
items: Review Digital Markets investment against its customer proposition
Prioritize initiatives with credible contribution and cash potential
Monitor operating progress against the assumptions supporting continued investment

headline: GE Aerospace should convert exceptional demand into reliable engine and service delivery.
summary: Orders, service revenue and engine deliveries all grew strongly, supported by greater material input from priority suppliers. The priority is execution across the supply and service network. Demand is attractive, but orders should not be mistaken for completed deliveries or earnings before engines and services reach customers.
focusTitle: Coordinate suppliers, production and services around customer commitments.
focusText: Keep production increases tied to available components, quality and customer readiness. Protect service capacity alongside new engine output, using supplier progress to relieve genuine delivery constraints while avoiding commitments that outrun the operating system.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Give the larger order book a dependable fulfillment path
cards.text: Total orders increased 32% to $66.2 billion. Converting demand into customer value requires disciplined scheduling and realistic delivery commitments across the production and service network.
items: Map major order commitments to production and service capacity
Prioritize bottlenecks affecting committed customer delivery dates
Monitor order conversion and changes in delivery requirements

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Turn supplier material gains into balanced production
cards.text: Material input from priority suppliers increased more than 40%. More input helps, but assembly output depends on the right components arriving with suitable quality and timing.
items: Coordinate supplier schedules around critical assembly requirements
Target shortages that still constrain completed engine output
Monitor component quality and usable input alongside delivery volume

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the expanding service relationship with customers
cards.text: Commercial Engines & Services service revenue increased 26%. Sustaining that growth requires dependable service execution while new engine production also competes for technical and material resources.
items: Allocate technical capacity to committed service requirements
Coordinate parts availability with customer service schedules
Monitor service completion and customer operational disruption

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Maintain delivery quality through the engine ramp-up
cards.text: Engine deliveries rose 25%, including 28% growth in LEAP deliveries. Further expansion should preserve product quality and handover performance rather than maximizing shipment counts alone.
items: Match engine ramp-up plans with qualified production capacity
Retain quality controls through higher assembly throughput
Monitor LEAP delivery reliability and post-delivery support demands

headline: GE HealthCare should convert order strength into profitable growth despite tariff pressure.
summary: Orders outpaced organic revenue growth, but adjusted EBIT margin declined with tariffs among management’s cited factors. Higher capital spending raises the stakes: delivery and cost execution must make demand growth support stronger investment returns.
focusTitle: Tie capacity and commercial decisions to net order economics.
focusText: Prioritize conversion in the highlighted growth businesses and respond to tariffs through practical sourcing, pricing and product choices. Stage capital deployment around real delivery needs so demand growth improves profitability rather than simply expanding working and fixed capital requirements.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Translate stronger orders into reliable customer installations
cards.text: Organic orders increased 5.2% and book-to-bill was 1.07 times. Demand visibility improves when manufacturing, installation and customer readiness are coordinated through to revenue recognition.
items: Map committed orders to production and installation milestones
Resolve bottlenecks delaying customer acceptance and service readiness
Monitor order conversion and customer delivery changes

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Address tariff pressure without weakening the customer proposition
cards.text: Adjusted EBIT margin declined 100 basis points to 15.3%; management identified tariff costs as a negative factor. Cost and commercial responses should protect competitiveness and product reliability.
items: Prioritize sourcing alternatives that preserve quality and delivery
Review pricing where tariff exposure changes product economics
Monitor net margin after tariff and mitigation effects

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Focus commercial resources on demonstrated growth businesses
cards.text: Organic revenue rose 3.5%, with management highlighting Imaging, Pharmaceutical Diagnostics and Advanced Visualization Solutions. These businesses offer specific places to deepen adoption and customer relationships.
items: Prioritize customer needs within the highlighted growth businesses
Coordinate product selling with installation and support capabilities
Monitor retention and incremental contribution by growth business

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make higher capital spending remove real delivery constraints
cards.text: Capital expenditures increased to $482 million from $401 million. Added investment should be sequenced against committed demand and practical operating benefits, particularly while margins are under pressure.
items: Rank projects by delivery need and expected operating benefit
Stage capacity investment around order and installation readiness
Monitor utilization and cash returns after assets enter service

headline: GE Vernova should convert a larger, better-priced backlog into delivered operating profit.
summary: Orders and backlog expanded strongly, with improved equipment margin embedded in the backlog. That creates an execution opportunity rather than recognized profit today. A major tax benefit also lifted annual net income, making delivery performance and realized contract economics more useful indicators of ongoing business progress.
focusTitle: Prioritize profitable backlog conversion over order scale alone.
focusText: Coordinate manufacturing capacity, supplier commitments and project execution around the expanded workload. Preserve the economics of new orders through cost and change control, and assess recurring profitability separately from the valuation-allowance tax benefit.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Build a delivery system for the expanded backlog
cards.text: Total backlog increased $31.2 billion to approximately $150 billion. This provides substantial future workload, but conversion requires capacity planning and reliable fulfillment across contract commitments.
items: Map backlog delivery milestones to factory and supplier capacity
Prioritize constraints affecting high-value customer commitments
Monitor conversion schedules and changes in contracted scope

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Protect equipment economics until revenue is earned
cards.text: Equipment margin in backlog improved six percentage points. The improvement is prospective: procurement, manufacturing and project execution determine whether those contract economics reach recognized profit.
items: Embed cost and scope controls in equipment delivery plans
Escalate changes that dilute contracted equipment contribution
Monitor realized margin as improved-backlog orders are delivered

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep order growth disciplined around delivery economics
cards.text: Orders reached $59.3 billion, up 34% organically. Strong demand supports selectivity, making credible delivery and acceptable contract returns more important than maximizing new order intake.
items: Prioritize orders suited to available technical and production capacity
Preserve commercial terms supporting cost and execution risks
Monitor order quality alongside organic demand growth

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Do not allocate capital as though the tax benefit recurs
cards.text: Annual net income included a $2.9 billion benefit from releasing a U.S. valuation allowance. That accounting benefit should be separated from the operating earnings supporting ongoing commitments.
items: Base recurring commitments on operating cash and delivery economics
Preserve liquidity for backlog fulfillment and factory requirements
Monitor operating profit separately from large tax-accounting effects

headline: Gen Digital should turn Trust-Based Solutions expansion into durable platform engagement and recurring value.
summary: Trust-Based Solutions expanded much faster than Cyber Safety, while paid customers and bookings increased. The priority is integrating customer engagement and commercial execution across the broader platform. Customer totals include active transaction users as well as subscribers, so customer growth should not be read as subscription growth alone.
focusTitle: Measure expansion by useful customer relationships and retained economics.
focusText: Develop cross-platform propositions around actual customer needs and engagement patterns. Distinguish subscription renewal from transaction activity, and connect bookings to delivered revenue and service obligations so the larger customer base produces durable commercial value.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Give Trust-Based Solutions growth a durable customer model
cards.text: Trust-Based Solutions revenue reached $1.661 billion from $759 million. The larger business needs clear product adoption, customer support and commercial accountability rather than evaluation through scale alone.
items: Identify offerings supporting repeat customer engagement
Coordinate service resources with the expanded business footprint
Monitor revenue durability and contribution across customer cohorts

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Use customer growth without overstating recurring subscriptions
cards.text: Paid customers increased to 79 million from 68 million. This company-defined count includes active transaction users and subscribers, which require different retention and monetization approaches.
items: Segment engagement plans for subscribers and transaction users
Tailor cross-selling to observed customer use and need
Monitor subscriber renewals separately from repeat transaction activity

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the Cyber Safety revenue foundation
cards.text: Cyber Safety Platform revenue increased to $3.339 billion from $3.176 billion. Protecting this established base requires useful protection capabilities, consistent customer support and disciplined renewal execution.
items: Prioritize capabilities that sustain Cyber Safety customer usage
Coordinate support and renewal outreach around customer requirements
Monitor Cyber Safety retention and expansion after service costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Translate bookings into delivered platform economics
cards.text: Company-defined annual bookings increased to $5.107 billion from $3.988 billion. Bookings should guide fulfillment and commercial planning without being treated as identical to recognized revenue.
items: Map booked commitments to delivery and service requirements
Maintain activation and collection discipline as commitments grow
Monitor booking conversion alongside customer retention and contribution

headline: Generac should restore residential economics and cash conversion while scaling commercial opportunities selectively.
summary: Residential weakness outweighed the positive commercial and industrial sales signal, while adjusted margin and operating cash declined. The priority is aligning residential production and spending with demand, then supporting commercial growth on its own economics. Forward-looking data-center expectations should not substitute for demonstrated 2025 results.
focusTitle: Rebalance resources toward demand-backed, cash-generating activity.
focusText: Improve residential sell-through, inventory alignment and operating costs while preserving productive commercial capabilities. Stage expansion around confirmed customer requirements, with margin and cash conversion used together to judge whether the business is recovering operationally.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Align the residential operation with weaker sales
cards.text: Annual residential product sales fell 7% to $2.27 billion. Production, channel inventory and selling resources should follow actual consumer demand rather than assuming a near-term rebound.
items: Coordinate production and replenishment with dealer sell-through
Target residential offers to demonstrated customer requirements
Monitor channel inventory and discount dependence alongside sales

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make lower volume costs less burdensome
cards.text: Company-defined adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 17.0% from 18.4%. Cost actions should improve operating leverage while preserving installation and support capabilities needed to sustain demand.
items: Match factory and support spending to confirmed workload
Target duplicated operating effort before reducing essential service
Monitor contribution as residential and commercial mix changes

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale commercial and industrial growth on delivered economics
cards.text: Commercial and industrial product sales increased 5% to $1.46 billion. Preserve that progress through customer-focused execution, with expansion based on real orders rather than future market expectations alone.
items: Prioritize commercial projects with clear delivery requirements
Coordinate installation and support capacity with customer commitments
Monitor project contribution and order conversion

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Restore cash conversion before enlarging commitments
cards.text: Operating cash flow fell to $438 million from $741 million. That reduces flexibility and makes inventory, collections and spending discipline central to funding the operating response.
items: Align inventory purchasing with demand-backed production plans
Prioritize collection issues in customer and dealer balances
Stage discretionary investment around improving operating cash generation

headline: General Dynamics should convert broad order strength into reliable program and aircraft deliveries.
summary: Book-to-bill exceeded one in every segment and backlog expanded substantially, while Gulfstream deliveries increased. The evidence supports healthy demand across the group. Higher capital spending makes the next priority disciplined fulfillment: capacity and program execution must convert commitments into revenue and attractive operating returns.
focusTitle: Allocate capacity to executable backlog and dependable delivery.
focusText: Use program requirements and customer milestones to prioritize people, suppliers and capital projects. Preserve Gulfstream’s delivery momentum while protecting execution across all segments, judging investment by the workload it enables and the economics achieved as backlog converts.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn broad order intake into balanced operating plans
cards.text: Full-year book-to-bill was 1.5 times and exceeded one in all four segments. Broad demand makes segment-specific capacity planning more useful than assuming one operating response fits every program.
items: Translate segment orders into staffing and supplier requirements
Prioritize constraints affecting contracted customer milestones
Monitor order conversion and changes in program requirements

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Give the larger backlog a realistic delivery schedule
cards.text: Year-end backlog reached approximately $118 billion, up 30%. This improves workload visibility, but the timing and complexity of execution determine its cash and earnings contribution.
items: Map major backlog commitments to executable program schedules
Escalate cost and scope changes before delivery milestones slip
Monitor backlog aging and milestone completion by program

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Gulfstream’s stronger delivery execution
cards.text: Gulfstream deliveries increased to 158 aircraft from 136. Sustaining that progress requires coordinated production, customer handover and supplier performance rather than shipment growth alone.
items: Align aircraft completion plans with customer acceptance readiness
Protect quality controls as delivery activity increases
Monitor delivery reliability and post-handover support needs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make higher capital spending relieve genuine constraints
cards.text: Capital expenditures were approximately $1.2 billion, up 27%. Investments should support committed workloads and efficient execution, with attention to utilization after assets become available.
items: Rank projects by backlog relevance and operating benefit
Stage spending around construction and production readiness
Monitor capacity utilization and program returns after investment

headline: General Mills should rebuild North American organic demand while preserving share and international momentum.
summary: Retail and Pet organic sales weakened, International grew, and Foodservice included a pricing-index headwind. Retail share resilience suggests the challenge extends beyond competitive position. Prioritize underlying demand, separating Pet acquisitions and the extra week from organic performance.
focusTitle: Direct brand and product investment toward repeatable organic consumption.
focusText: Use category and channel evidence to improve North American sell-through, protect household value and strengthen Pet adoption. Preserve International’s growth, while distinguishing price-index effects and acquisition contributions from changes in underlying customer demand.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Convert retail share resilience into organic sales improvement
cards.text: North America Retail organic sales fell 3%, although pound share held or improved in 65% of the ten largest U.S. categories. Share defense alone is not restoring sales.
items: Prioritize category propositions with clear household value
Coordinate retailer activity around actual consumer sell-through
Monitor category demand and repeat purchases alongside share

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore Pet demand beneath reported growth
cards.text: North America Pet sales rose 6%, including six points from acquisitions and two from the extra week, while organic sales fell 3%. Commercial priorities should address the organic business directly.
items: Target Pet product and channel adoption barriers
Coordinate acquired and existing assortments around customer demand
Monitor organic sell-through and repeat purchase separately from acquisitions

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve International’s organic growth practices
cards.text: International organic sales increased 3%. Identify the product and commercial practices supporting that demand and fund further expansion selectively rather than assuming North American actions apply unchanged.
items: Prioritize International products with demonstrated consumer response
Retain effective local distribution and retail execution
Monitor organic growth after associated brand and delivery spending

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Distinguish Foodservice pricing effects from customer weakness
cards.text: Foodservice organic sales fell 1%, including a two-point bakery-flour index-pricing headwind. An appropriate response separates price mechanics from changes in customer usage and mix.
items: Evaluate Foodservice demand independently of flour index pricing
Focus account development on useful product and service needs
Monitor volume and contribution as indexed prices change

headline: GM should restore North American vehicle contribution and automotive cash conversion.
summary: Lower wholesales accompanied weaker North American adjusted margin and automotive operating cash. China losses narrowed substantially, but the core vehicle business still needs stronger contribution. Prioritize demand-led production, pricing and spending over shipment volume alone.
focusTitle: Make demand-led vehicle decisions strengthen contribution and cash.
focusText: Align North American product mix and production with actual demand while containing avoidable costs and inventory commitments. Preserve progress in China, but evaluate its remaining losses separately so capital stays focused on attractive economics across the automotive portfolio.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Restore the economics of North American sales
cards.text: GM North America adjusted EBIT margin declined to 6.8% from 9.2%. Improving product contribution and operating cost absorption is central to the recovery of automotive earnings.
items: Prioritize vehicle mix with attractive contribution after incentives
Target manufacturing costs without weakening quality and service
Monitor regional margin alongside pricing and production changes

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Align production with a smaller wholesale base
cards.text: Automotive wholesales declined to 3.799 million vehicles from 4.010 million. Capacity and dealer inventory decisions should follow customer sell-through rather than trying to rebuild shipments independently.
items: Coordinate production schedules with dealer demand signals
Reduce inventory commitments in slower-selling vehicle configurations
Monitor dealer stock, incentives and sell-through together

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve China’s progress while addressing remaining losses
cards.text: China equity losses narrowed to $316 million from $4.407 billion. The improvement is material, but continuing losses still call for selective investment and disciplined local operating choices.
items: Preserve operating actions supporting the narrower loss
Rank China product spending by credible local demand
Monitor equity losses and funding requirements after restructuring effects

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect cash flexibility through the operating response
cards.text: Automotive operating cash flow fell to $18.733 billion from $23.939 billion. Production, inventory and investment actions should help restore cash capacity rather than rely solely on earnings adjustments.
items: Tie inventory purchasing to demand-backed production plans
Prioritize capital commitments with clear vehicle economics
Monitor automotive cash after operating and investment requirements

headline: Genuine Parts should reduce vendor-credit exposure while preserving cash for productive distribution investment.
summary: Vendor-credit losses create a specific commercial and cash issue, distinct from the noncash pension settlement. Operating cash supports meaningful investment. Prioritize supplier economics and funding flexibility, without interpreting every year-end charge as weaker customer demand.
focusTitle: Make supplier risk and investment compete within a clear cash plan.
focusText: Reduce dependence on unrecovered vendor balances and protect product availability while allocating capital to productive distribution needs. Separate the pension accounting charge from recurring operations, and evaluate acquisition spending alongside the cash required to sustain the existing network.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Contain the vendor-credit problem at its commercial source
cards.text: Year-end charges primarily reflected expected losses on rebates and other amounts owed by a vendor entering Chapter 11. Recovery and future trading terms require specific attention.
items: Assign recovery ownership to outstanding vendor balances
Review rebate exposure and settlement terms across key suppliers
Protect product availability while evaluating alternative supply options

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Keep investment commitments within available cash capacity
cards.text: GPC spent $470 million on capital expenditures and $318 million on acquisitions. Those demands should be assessed together with supplier exposure and the operating needs of the distribution business.
items: Rank capital projects by service and productivity benefits
Stage acquisition commitments around integration and funding capacity
Monitor combined investment needs against internally generated cash

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the operating cash engine
cards.text: Annual operating cash flow was $891 million and company-defined free cash flow was $421 million. Protecting collections and inventory discipline supports the resources available for network investment.
items: Align inventory purchases with customer demand and supplier reliability
Prioritize collection issues affecting cash conversion
Monitor free cash after required distribution investment

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep the pension settlement separate from operating decisions
cards.text: Results included a one-time noncash pension settlement from terminating the U.S. qualified defined-benefit plan. It affects reported earnings but does not establish deterioration in demand or current cash generation.
items: Base operating budgets on recurring distribution economics
Assess remaining benefit obligations within funding decisions
Monitor recurring cash performance separately from the settlement charge

headline: Gilead should preserve HIV and liver growth while improving Cell Therapy’s competitive execution.
summary: HIV and Liver Disease sales grew, providing a stronger ongoing base as Veklury declined with lower COVID-19 hospitalizations. Cell Therapy weakness presents a separate competitive challenge. The priority is selective commercial and operating investment, rather than attempting to replace every declining Veklury dollar through broad spending.
focusTitle: Allocate resources by franchise opportunity and demand quality.
focusText: Protect access and execution in growing HIV and liver franchises while addressing Cell Therapy’s specific competitive barriers. Plan Veklury resources around its changing demand context so episodic COVID-related sales do not dictate the recurring cost base.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect the HIV franchise supporting the revenue base
cards.text: HIV sales grew 6% to $20.8 billion and Biktarvy rose 7% to $14.3 billion. Sustaining access, supply and commercial execution is central to preserving this large franchise.
items: Prioritize dependable supply and patient-access execution
Focus commercial resources on established customer and provider needs
Monitor franchise demand and access barriers alongside Biktarvy growth

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Address Cell Therapy’s competitive barriers directly
cards.text: Cell Therapy sales declined 7% to $1.8 billion amid competitive headwinds identified by management. The response should focus on delivery, access and account execution rather than untargeted promotion.
items: Identify account-level barriers to Cell Therapy adoption
Coordinate operational support with treatment-center requirements
Monitor demand, access and delivery performance by product

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support the liver portfolio’s demonstrated demand
cards.text: Liver Disease sales increased 6% to $3.2 billion; management cited Livdelzi and HBV/HDV demand. Invest selectively in the access and operating capabilities needed to sustain those franchises.
items: Prioritize access support for the cited growth products
Coordinate supply planning with observed liver-portfolio demand
Monitor product contribution and adoption after commercial investment

items: Align Veklury supply and spending with observed demand
Keep flexibility for changing hospitalization-related requirements
Monitor inventory and demand without assuming prior sales return

headline: Global Payments should make Genius adoption deliver profitable growth within a clearly defined operating scope.

focusText: Focus Genius execution on useful merchant capabilities, reliable onboarding and ongoing service. cards.title: Turn the Genius launch into active merchant usage
cards.text: Global Payments launched Genius in the second quarter of 2025. The launch creates a commercial opportunity, but adoption, reliable service and customer economics determine the platform’s value.

Target capabilities addressing demonstrated merchant operating needs
Monitor active usage, retention and support requirements after adoption

cards.label: What could improve

items: Base market plans on consistently scoped customer activity
Separate disposition effects when allocating commercial resources
Monitor merchant contribution alongside comparable revenue growth

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the operating discipline behind adjusted margin gains

items: Scale repeatable onboarding and merchant-support processes
Prioritize platform spending with demonstrable commercial benefit
Monitor incremental contribution after implementation and service costs

Allocate shared resources using the intended continuing scope
Monitor retained-business costs and revenue on consistent definitions

headline: Globe Life should preserve underwriting growth while improving the balance between financing costs and capital returns.

Keep repurchases responsive to financing capacity, using company-defined underwriting and excess investment measures as operating inputs rather than substitutes for all reported earnings and cash needs.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect the underwriting economics driving operating progress
cards.text: Company-defined insurance underwriting income rose 12% to approximately $1.553 billion. Sustaining that improvement requires policy pricing, risk selection and servicing that preserve attractive insurance contribution.

Feed claims experience into pricing and risk selection
Monitor policy retention and underwriting contribution by business

cards.label: What could improve

items: Align asset allocation with insurance cash-flow requirements
Evaluate reinvestment choices after liquidity and risk needs
Monitor excess investment contribution alongside asset and liability changes

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use repurchase discretion as a financial flexibility tool

Reserve capital for operating and policyholder requirements
Monitor distributions against cash and capital available after commitments

Include interest needs when sizing discretionary capital returns
Monitor financing expense alongside recurring operating contribution

headline: GoDaddy should turn commerce growth into deeper customer adoption while preserving the Core Platform base.

cards.text: Applications and Commerce revenue rose 14% to approximately $1.9 billion. Sustaining that growth depends on customers using capabilities productively and renewing rather than simply purchasing additional tools.

Bundle relevant capabilities around observed customer needs
Monitor active usage, renewals and contribution by adoption cohort

cards.label: What could improve

cards.text: Gross payments volume increased 31% to $3.4 billion. Transaction value indicates activity, but retained economics after payment and support costs should guide investment.

Focus product development on repeat transaction use cases
Monitor payment contribution and merchant retention alongside volume

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the larger Core Platform foundation

Target relevant commerce offers to engaged core customers
Monitor Core Platform renewals and expansion after support costs

cards.text: Net income included a $34.6 million noncash tax benefit versus $267.4 million in 2024. The smaller benefit affects earnings comparisons without demonstrating weaker commercial demand.
items: Set product budgets using recurring operating economics
Evaluate capital uses against actual cash requirements
Monitor business contribution separately from noncash tax effects

Monitor completed-deal contribution alongside advisory pipeline changes

Coordinate financing commitments with funding and risk capacity
Monitor exposures and liquidity alongside equities revenue

Protect investment capacity in strategies attracting client allocations
Monitor retained flows and contribution after servicing costs

cards.text: Apple Card markdowns reduced revenue $2.26 billion while a related credit-reserve reduction was $2.48 billion. These different effects require distinct operational and risk oversight rather than a simplistic revenue conclusion.

Monitor recurring institutional earnings separately from exit-related adjustments

Monitor equipment utilization and regional operating contribution

Monitor recurring cash performance separately from charge-driven earnings effects

Monitor cash available after operating and financing requirements

Monitor reported profitability alongside adjusted margin and cash

cards.text: Same-facility equivalent admissions increased 2.4% and admissions grew 2.3%. Sustaining that activity requires coordinated staffing, facilities and patient-flow execution.

Monitor access, throughput and service quality alongside admissions

cards.text: Salaries and benefits fell to 43.5% of revenue from 44.1%. Maintain the operating benefit through effective scheduling and retention while monitoring the staffing needed for reliable care.
items: Align staffing schedules with actual care requirements
Support retention in roles critical to service capacity
Monitor labor productivity alongside quality and workforce stability

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Balance repurchases with facility and funding requirements
cards.text: Operating cash flow was $12.636 billion, property purchases were $4.944 billion and repurchases were $10.067 billion. These concurrent uses make integrated funding decisions important.
items: Prioritize essential facility investment and operating liquidity
Size discretionary repurchases after committed funding requirements
Monitor total cash uses against internal cash and financing capacity

headline: Healthpeak should preserve outpatient and Life Plan momentum while improving Lab leasing conversion.
summary: Merger-combined same-store cash adjusted NOI grew, led by Life Plan, while Lab growth and retention were more modest. Outpatient Medical provides a sizable renewal foundation. The priority is converting leasing activity into occupied income and retaining tenants, with resources tailored to each property business rather than treating the portfolio uniformly.
focusTitle: Allocate property capital around tenant retention and cash-income conversion.
focusText: Preserve renewal discipline in Outpatient Medical and support Lab occupancy through practical leasing and tenant-readiness execution. Sustain Life Plan operating performance while considering the timing of entry-fee cash separately from recurring property income.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect the outpatient renewal engine
cards.text: Outpatient Medical renewed 3.9 million square feet, retained 79% of tenants and achieved 5.0% cash renewal spreads. Strong retention and rent economics should guide property-level investment.
items: Prioritize renewal outreach around tenant operating requirements
Target property work that improves attractive tenant retention
Monitor renewal spreads after concessions and landlord spending

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make Lab leasing improve occupied cash income
cards.text: Lab signed 562,000 square feet of new leases and 889,000 of renewals, with 72% retention and 5.0% cash renewal spreads. Occupancy conversion and retention need focused execution.
items: Coordinate tenant handovers and build-out readiness after signing
Address renewal barriers in viable Lab tenant relationships
Monitor lease commencement, retention and property contribution

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Life Plan’s operating and cash momentum
cards.text: Life Plan merger-combined same-store cash adjusted NOI grew 12.6%, and nonrefundable entry-fee cash collections reached $153 million. Sustain operating execution while distinguishing entry-fee timing from recurring income.
items: Maintain service capacity supporting Life Plan community demand
Coordinate entry-fee collection processes with resident transitions
Monitor recurring property income separately from entry-fee cash

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Do not allocate capital solely by headline portfolio growth
cards.text: Merger-combined same-store cash adjusted NOI increased 4.0%, including 3.9% Outpatient Medical and 1.5% Lab growth. Different operating trajectories warrant distinct investment and leasing priorities.
items: Rank property spending by retention and income contribution
Direct leasing resources toward specific portfolio bottlenecks
Monitor returns using consistent merger-combined property definitions

headline: Henry Schein should scale technology and core distribution growth while improving underlying earnings contribution.
summary: Technology outgrew the broader business, while Medical and Dental advanced. Sales included acquisition and currency benefits, and non-GAAP EPS rose despite flat non-GAAP net income. Prioritize profitable organic expansion and total contribution alongside per-share progress.
focusTitle: Make product and service growth strengthen underlying business economics.
focusText: Prioritize technology adoption and distribution opportunities that improve customer workflows and contribution. Evaluate acquisitions and operating spending against internal growth and total earnings, keeping the company-attributable and consolidated income scopes distinct when assessing results.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Scale technology through useful customer adoption
cards.text: Global Technology sales rose 7.1% to $675 million, with 6.7% local internal growth. This offers a specific growth platform when onboarding and support help customers use the products effectively.
items: Target technology offers to practical customer workflow needs
Coordinate implementation support with distribution account relationships
Monitor adoption, retention and contribution after customer support costs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make internal growth the center of expansion decisions
cards.text: Sales grew 4.0%, including 2.6% internal growth, 0.9% acquisitions and 0.5% currency. Commercial resource allocation should distinguish organic customer demand from portfolio and translation effects.
items: Prioritize account development with demonstrated internal demand
Integrate acquired customer relationships with clear service ownership
Monitor internal growth alongside acquisition contribution and costs

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Medical and Dental growth with reliable fulfillment
cards.text: Medical sales increased 4.6%; Dental grew 2.8%, including 4.4% equipment growth. These different product needs require dependable distribution and effective equipment implementation support.
items: Align inventory with Medical and Dental customer requirements
Coordinate Dental equipment delivery and customer readiness
Monitor product contribution and fulfillment quality by business

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require per-share growth to accompany total earnings progress
cards.text: GAAP diluted EPS rose to $3.27 and non-GAAP EPS to $4.97, while non-GAAP net income stayed at $605 million. Capital allocation should consider total profit as well as per-share measures.
items: Rank investments by incremental operating and cash contribution
Avoid using EPS alone to justify broader spending
Monitor total recurring earnings alongside share-based performance measures

headline: Hershey should rebuild confectionery profitability without sacrificing demand while scaling Salty Snacks.
summary: Price supported organic growth, but volume/mix was negative and confectionery margins fell sharply. Salty Snacks provides a stronger volume-led signal. Commodity derivative movements complicate reported comparisons, yet lower adjusted EPS confirms that the priority extends beyond accounting volatility to pricing, cost and demand economics.
focusTitle: Balance confectionery price realization with consumer demand and cost resilience.
focusText: Prioritize product and pack choices that protect customer value while addressing confectionery costs. Preserve Salty Snacks’ volume momentum, and assess commodity exposure through operating and cash economics rather than interpreting mark-to-market changes as the full measure of underlying performance.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect demand behind the price-led sales increase
cards.text: Organic constant-currency sales rose 4.2%, with rounded contributions of approximately 6% price and negative 1% volume/mix. Further pricing should account for sell-through and consumer response.
items: Test price and pack choices against consumer value needs
Coordinate retail activity around actual product sell-through
Monitor volume/mix and repeat purchasing alongside price realization

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore North American confectionery contribution
cards.text: Confectionery segment income fell 15.3% and margin declined to 26.3% from 32.3%. Cost and commercial execution need to improve together rather than relying solely on additional pricing.
items: Prioritize cost actions preserving product quality and availability
Focus confectionery assortment on attractive full-cost contribution
Monitor margin alongside volume and promotional requirements

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Salty Snacks’ stronger volume-led growth
cards.text: Salty Snacks sales grew 11.9%, with 9.5% organic constant-currency growth including approximately 8% volume/mix. This supports targeted product, distribution and capacity investment.
items: Prioritize snack products with demonstrated repeat demand
Align supply and distribution with expanding sell-through
Monitor incremental contribution as snack volumes scale

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Manage commodity exposure without confusing valuation and operations
cards.text: Commodity derivative mark-to-market losses were $423.2 million versus $460.4 million of gains, while adjusted EPS fell 32.7%. Both exposure management and underlying operating improvement matter.
items: Align commodity purchasing with practical production requirements
Evaluate pricing and sourcing using full exposure economics
Monitor cash input costs separately from derivative valuation changes

headline: HPE should restore Server margins and cash conversion while integrating Juniper-led networking scale.
summary: Juniper primarily drove Networking growth, while Server revenue increased with lower margin. Hybrid Cloud services offer another positive signal, but cash declined. Prioritize integration and delivery economics that turn the broader portfolio into stronger cash generation.
focusTitle: Allocate resources around customer contribution and integration readiness.
focusText: Protect Server economics through disciplined input costs and mix, integrate Networking around customer continuity, and preserve useful private-cloud service growth. Use cash conversion as a common allocation test while keeping acquired scale distinct from organic demand.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make the larger Networking business operate as a coherent platform
cards.text: Networking revenue increased 51.1%, with management identifying Juniper as the primary contributor. The opportunity is effective integration and customer value, rather than assuming this rate represents organic acceleration.
items: Coordinate customer coverage and support across Networking operations
Prioritize integration steps preserving deployment and renewal continuity
Monitor retained customer contribution after integration requirements

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Repair Server economics beneath revenue growth
cards.text: Server revenue rose 10.2%, but margin fell to 7.6% from 11.2%; management cited input costs and lower-margin mix. Product selection and pricing need to reflect complete delivery economics.
items: Price Server configurations for current input and service costs
Prioritize orders with attractive contribution and feasible delivery
Monitor product mix and margin after customer fulfillment costs

cards.label: What is working
