cards.title: Deepen the service relationships supporting Hybrid Cloud
cards.text: Hybrid Cloud revenue grew 4.9% and services rose 11.7%; management cited higher private-cloud service contribution. Sustain adoption and service execution where customers demonstrate continuing need.
items: Target private-cloud services to active customer operating requirements
Coordinate service delivery with account expansion plans
Monitor service retention and contribution after delivery costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Restore cash flexibility before enlarging commitments
cards.text: Operating cash flow fell to $2.919 billion from $4.341 billion, and non-GAAP free cash flow fell to $986 million from $2.297 billion. Cash conversion needs explicit operational ownership.
items: Align purchasing and inventory with confirmed customer orders
Prioritize collections and integration cash requirements
Stage discretionary investment around improving free cash generation

headline: Hilton should sustain unit-led fee growth while strengthening the economics of existing hotels.
summary: Unit additions and fee revenue grew strongly, while comparable RevPAR was nearly flat and supported by rates. The development pipeline offers substantial opportunity. The priority is high-quality openings and owner economics, so network expansion continues producing dependable fees without masking muted comparable-property demand.
focusTitle: Balance new-room conversion with healthy existing-property relationships.
focusText: Support owners in opening committed rooms and improving guest demand at existing hotels. Prioritize development that can operate successfully, and evaluate fee growth alongside comparable hotel performance rather than assuming new units alone establish stronger demand across the system.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve strong openings through dependable owner support
cards.text: Hilton opened 97,000 rooms and achieved 6.7% net unit growth. Sustaining expansion requires practical opening support, brand readiness and reliable hotel operations after launch.
items: Coordinate owner opening milestones with brand and service requirements
Prioritize support for newly opened hotels reaching operating readiness
Monitor net unit growth alongside closures and owner retention

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve demand quality beneath modest RevPAR growth
cards.text: Comparable currency-neutral RevPAR increased 0.4%, attributed to higher average daily rates. Existing hotels need demand and guest-value attention rather than relying on rate alone.
items: Target guest acquisition and repeat stays around property needs
Support owners balancing room rates with occupancy economics
Monitor occupancy and rate contribution alongside guest retention

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep fee growth supported by healthy operating relationships
cards.text: Management and franchise fees rose 6.4%, while adjusted EBITDA increased to $3.725 billion from $3.429 billion. Preserve efficient platform support and owner value as the system grows.
items: Scale repeatable brand and owner-support processes
Prioritize services that strengthen hotel operating performance
Monitor fee contribution after platform and support costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Convert the pipeline selectively rather than chasing room counts
cards.text: The pipeline reached 520,500 rooms, up 4%, with almost half under construction. Project readiness and owner funding still determine the pace and quality of conversion.
items: Focus development resources on projects with credible opening readiness
Coordinate construction-stage support with owner requirements
Monitor pipeline delays and opening quality by project cohort

headline: Home Depot should rebuild customer transactions while restoring operating leverage.
summary: Higher tickets offset fewer comparable transactions, while both margin measures declined. Customer activity and productivity are the priority. The shorter fiscal year also affects annual sales, so the lost extra week must be separated from underlying demand.
focusTitle: Make customer trips and project value improve contribution.
focusText: Target practical product availability, service and project needs that can increase customer activity without uneconomic discounting. Align operating resources with demand, using the comparable transaction metrics only within their stated scope, which excludes HD Supply and SRS including GMS.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Address fewer transactions beneath ticket-led sales support
cards.text: Comparable customer transactions fell 1.0%, while comparable average ticket rose 1.4%. These measures exclude HD Supply and SRS including GMS, and point to a need for stronger customer activity.
items: Improve availability and service around frequent customer project needs
Target relevant offers that encourage useful additional trips
Monitor transaction recovery alongside ticket and promotional economics

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore cost absorption as comparable demand remains modest
cards.text: GAAP operating margin fell to 12.7% from 13.5%, and adjusted margin to 13.1% from 13.8%. Operational productivity needs to support stronger contribution without undermining customer service.
items: Match store and fulfillment resources to actual customer workload
Target duplicated handling and administrative effort
Monitor margin alongside service quality and comparable activity

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build on modest comparable growth where demand is present
cards.text: Comparable sales rose 0.3%, including 0.5% in the U.S. The positive result supports selective investment in customer and category opportunities rather than a uniform expansion response.
items: Identify categories and locations with durable customer demand
Prioritize inventory and service for attractive project opportunities
Monitor incremental gross profit after associated operating costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep the extra-week comparison out of demand decisions
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 had 52 weeks versus 53, with the extra 2024 week adding approximately $2.5 billion in sales. Calendar effects should not dictate permanent staffing or capacity decisions.
items: Plan recurring resources using comparable trading periods
Separate calendar-driven sales changes from customer activity
Monitor comparable growth before changing permanent operating capacity

headline: Honeywell should make organic growth improve underlying margins while preserving cash and portfolio discipline.
summary: Organic sales and cash grew, but the Bombardier comparison changes the margin interpretation. Subsequent impairments revised continuing earnings. Prioritize underlying operating leverage and realistic asset economics, using final reporting scopes in allocation decisions.
focusTitle: Allocate cash using recurring operating economics and revised asset values.
focusText: Preserve commercial momentum and cash generation while improving costs in the comparable business. Evaluate portfolio spending against the impairment-adjusted asset case, and keep discontinued Advanced Materials and revised continuing earnings distinct when judging the funding available for ongoing operations.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Build on organic growth with a consistent commercial baseline
cards.text: Organic sales increased 7%, or 6% excluding the Bombardier agreement comparison. Both show demand progress, while the distinction matters when sizing resources for recurring customer activity.
items: Prioritize customer opportunities supported by comparable organic demand
Align delivery resources with the strongest executable orders
Monitor growth excluding unusual agreement comparisons

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve the margin trend beneath the comparison benefit
cards.text: Adjusted segment margin reached 22.5%, up 40 basis points, but contracted 40 basis points excluding the Bombardier comparison. Underlying productivity remains a priority despite the headline improvement.
items: Target operating costs limiting comparable margin expansion
Price and select work using full delivery economics
Monitor margin on a consistent agreement-comparison basis

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the stronger cash engine
cards.text: Operating cash flow rose 19% to $6.1 billion and non-GAAP free cash flow was $5.1 billion. Protecting cash conversion supports investment and portfolio flexibility.
items: Maintain inventory and collection discipline in growing operations
Prioritize investments with clear operating cash contribution
Monitor free cash after essential portfolio and operating commitments

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Use revised asset economics in portfolio decisions
cards.text: The February correction added $436 million of goodwill and $35 million of held-for-sale asset impairment, revising annual continuing EPS to $6.94. Allocation assumptions should reflect those revised values.
items: Reassess capital committed to the affected assets
Rank portfolio actions using credible future operating contribution
Monitor recurring returns separately from revised impairment effects

headline: Hormel should restore margins and inventory cash conversion while preserving Foodservice growth.
summary: Foodservice outgrew Retail, but both margin measures declined. Higher inventories and lower cash add allocation pressure alongside investment and dividends. Prioritize profitable production and working-capital discipline rather than sales growth alone.
focusTitle: Connect production and cash allocation to profitable demand.
focusText: Preserve the strongest Foodservice relationships while adjusting assortment, inventory and operating costs to actual customer requirements. Size discretionary commitments around cash remaining after productive investment, using consistent organic definitions that exclude the Hormel Health Labs disposition.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect Foodservice momentum with disciplined customer economics
cards.text: Foodservice organic net sales grew 5.5% versus 1.1% in Retail. Selective commercial resources should follow demand and contribution, without assuming the faster-growing channel is automatically more profitable.
items: Prioritize Foodservice offers meeting demonstrated customer requirements
Coordinate channel plans with manufacturing and delivery capacity
Monitor contribution after channel-specific selling and service costs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Repair recurring margin performance
cards.text: Operating margin fell to 5.9% from 9.0%, while adjusted margin declined to 8.4% from 9.6%. Improvement is needed in recurring operating economics as well as reported results.
items: Target manufacturing and product costs with practical efficiency opportunities
Review assortment and pricing using full contribution economics
Monitor both margin measures after cost and commercial actions

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve operating cash through disciplined production planning
cards.text: Annual operating cash flow was $845 million. It remains a funding source, but should support the production and investment needed for durable earnings before broader cash commitments expand.
items: Link production schedules to demand-backed replenishment needs
Prioritize collections and avoidable working-capital requirements
Monitor operating cash alongside inventory and contribution changes

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Release inventory cash and reassess competing cash uses
cards.text: Inventories increased $171 million to $1.7 billion while cash fell $71 million to $671 million. Capital spending of $311 million and dividends of $633 million reinforce the need for allocation discipline.
items: Reduce excess inventory without weakening customer availability
Sequence capital projects by operational need and cash return
Monitor liquidity after investment and dividend requirements

headline: Host should convert hotel revenue gains into recurring margin while coordinating renovations with demand.
summary: Hotel revenue improved, while margin declined with lower insurance gains and labor costs among the cited factors. Renovations affected group nights and required capital. Prioritize profitable guest demand and project execution, separating insurance effects from recurring hotel economics.
focusTitle: Make property investment and guest mix support durable cash returns.
focusText: Sequence renovations around demand opportunities, preserve service quality and manage staffing productivity. Evaluate revenue gains through contribution after labor and project costs, rather than assuming higher RevPAR or insurance-related accounting establishes stronger recurring profitability.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make stronger hotel revenue produce attractive contribution
cards.text: Comparable Total RevPAR increased 4.2%; room-only RevPAR rose 3.8% to $229.24. Revenue management should preserve that demand while considering the operating cost of each guest and service mix.
items: Coordinate room and ancillary offers around profitable guest demand
Target property revenue opportunities with manageable service costs
Monitor Total RevPAR alongside hotel operating contribution

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Address recurring labor costs separately from insurance comparisons
cards.text: GAAP operating margin fell 140 basis points to 14.0%; Host cited lower insurance settlement gains and higher wages and benefits. These require different operating and allocation responses.
items: Align staffing schedules with actual hotel service requirements
Prioritize retention and productivity in essential operating roles
Monitor recurring property margins excluding insurance gain variability

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve a balanced customer base during renovation work
cards.text: Transient, group and contract customers represented approximately 61%, 34% and 5% of room sales. Group room nights declined amid planned renovations, making sales and construction coordination important.
items: Coordinate group booking availability with renovation schedules
Protect transient and contract service during property work
Monitor group recovery and total contribution as rooms reopen

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep capital projects accountable for operating readiness
cards.text: Annual capital spending was $644 million, including $282 million on return-oriented projects and $75 million on damage reconstruction. Each category needs its own delivery and operating-benefit assessment.
items: Stage project work around guest and property readiness
Control reconstruction budgets separately from return-oriented investment
Monitor reopening milestones and contribution after completed projects

headline: Howmet should sustain aerospace and turbine growth while preserving exceptional margin and cash execution.
summary: Commercial and defense aerospace expanded, gas turbines grew faster still, and margins improved substantially. Strong free cash flow accompanied record capital spending. The priority is selective capacity and operating execution across these growth markets, with a proportionate response to weaker commercial transportation demand.
focusTitle: Deploy capital where committed workload supports attractive returns.
focusText: Preserve the production and commercial discipline behind margin expansion, while allocating resources according to aerospace and turbine requirements. Keep transportation capacity responsive to its weaker demand and balance shareholder returns with the investment needed for reliable customer delivery.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Support aerospace growth with dependable production capacity
cards.text: Commercial aerospace revenue rose 12% and defense aerospace grew 21%. Both opportunities need execution tailored to customer programs, not a uniform capacity increase across the business.
items: Map program demand to qualified production and supplier capacity
Prioritize bottlenecks affecting committed aerospace customer deliveries
Monitor delivery reliability and contribution by aerospace market

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Reallocate carefully between turbines and transportation
cards.text: Gas turbine revenue increased 25%, while commercial transportation declined 5%. Different trajectories favor targeted resource deployment rather than expanding or cutting the whole manufacturing footprint together.
items: Prioritize turbine capacity supported by customer requirements
Align transportation production and staffing with actual workload
Monitor utilization and margins across the contrasting end markets

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the operating practices behind stronger margins
cards.text: GAAP operating margin reached 24.8%, up approximately 280 basis points, and adjusted margin was 25.8%. Continued growth should retain cost, quality and commercial discipline.
items: Replicate effective manufacturing processes across comparable facilities
Protect quality controls as production activity increases
Monitor reported and adjusted margins alongside delivery performance

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep capital returns compatible with productive expansion
cards.text: Non-GAAP free cash flow was $1.431 billion after record $453 million capital spending; common-share repurchases were $700 million. Preserve flexibility for capacity needs as customer demand grows.
items: Rank capital projects by committed workload and operating benefit
Evaluate repurchases after essential production investment requirements
Monitor cash generation and asset utilization after expansion

headline: HP should make Personal Systems growth improve margins while adapting Printing to lower demand.
summary: Commercial-led Personal Systems growth accompanied weaker Printing revenue, and both segment margins declined. Prioritize contribution across these different demand situations, using cash to support selective investment rather than treating computing revenue growth as sufficient operating recovery.
focusTitle: Apply separate operating plans to computing growth and printing contraction.
focusText: Price and source Personal Systems for attractive full-cost economics while aligning Printing inventory and spending with demand. Preserve customer support and productive investment, and assess allocation using group cash as well as segment margins that exclude corporate and unallocated costs.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn commercial computing growth into attractive contribution
cards.text: Personal Systems revenue increased 6%, with Commercial up 8% and Consumer up 4%. Support the strongest customer requirements while preserving product economics and delivery reliability.
items: Prioritize commercial offers with durable customer demand
Align product availability with confirmed customer requirements
Monitor growth after product, fulfillment and service costs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore margins in both product businesses
cards.text: Personal Systems margin fell to 5.3% from 6.2%, and Printing to 18.7% from 19.0%. Different demand trends still require common discipline on product costs and contribution.
items: Review pricing and configurations against current full product costs
Target operating inefficiencies without weakening customer support
Monitor both segment margins alongside relevant product mix

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve cash capacity for selective operating investment
cards.text: Operating cash flow was $3.7 billion and non-GAAP free cash flow was $2.9 billion. That supports flexibility, with $1.9 billion returned through dividends and repurchases.
items: Prioritize investments addressing margin and customer retention opportunities
Reserve cash for essential operating and product commitments
Monitor capital returns against cash after required investment

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Adapt Printing commitments to its smaller revenue base
cards.text: Printing revenue fell 4%, including a 3% supplies decline and 4% declines in commercial and consumer printing. Inventory and product resources should follow actual demand rather than assumed recovery.
items: Align printing supply and hardware inventories with sell-through
Protect service and replenishment for active customer needs
Monitor product contribution and inventory aging as demand changes

headline: Hubbell should preserve operating gains while making higher debt support productive business growth.
summary: Organic growth, margins and operating cash all improved, with Electrical Solutions growing faster than Utility Solutions. Higher year-end debt makes capital allocation the main execution risk rather than evidence of an operating crisis. The priority is preserving contribution and cash discipline as funding commitments increase.
focusTitle: Match operating investment and financing to segment-level returns.
focusText: Sustain the practices behind margin expansion while allocating commercial and production resources according to each segment’s demand. Evaluate additional commitments against cash generation and financing needs so a stronger operating business produces durable financial flexibility.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make Electrical Solutions momentum improve group contribution
cards.text: Electrical Solutions sales increased 7% to $2.1723 billion, versus 2% to $3.6723 billion in Utility Solutions. Segment-specific resource allocation should reflect customer demand and operating economics.
items: Prioritize capacity and commercial support for executable segment demand
Preserve service reliability across the larger Utility Solutions base
Monitor incremental contribution in both segments as growth differs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Keep organic demand central to growth commitments
cards.text: Organic net sales increased 3.3% versus 3.8% reported growth. Planning should use sustainable customer activity rather than assuming every reported growth component repeats.
items: Align production and inventory with organic customer requirements
Prioritize product opportunities with demonstrated adoption
Monitor comparable customer demand alongside reported sales

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve stronger operating margins as activity scales
cards.text: GAAP operating margin rose to 20.7% from 19.4%, and adjusted margin to 22.7% from 21.9%. Both measures support a positive operating assessment and disciplined expansion.
items: Extend effective pricing and production practices across comparable operations
Protect delivery quality while retaining productivity gains
Monitor both margins after incremental growth investment

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep debt growth connected to cash-generating uses
cards.text: Operating cash flow rose to $1.0298 billion from $991.2 million, while debt increased to $2.3254 billion from $1.5681 billion. Funding commitments now warrant closer allocation discipline.
items: Rank debt-funded uses by credible operating cash contribution
Reserve liquidity for committed production and investment needs
Monitor financing requirements against recurring operating cash generation

headline: Humana should improve current medical-cost economics while managing membership shifts and CenterWell costs.
summary: Medicare Advantage membership declined as state-based membership expanded. The consolidated benefit ratio rose despite greater favorable reserve development, while CenterWell’s cost ratio increased. Prioritize current care-cost and service economics over reserve-supported earnings or segment revenue scale.
focusTitle: Align membership, care resources and pricing with sustainable economics.
focusText: Plan operating capacity around the changing membership mix and strengthen claims and care-cost management. Require CenterWell growth to improve contribution, keeping intersegment revenue distinct from consolidated sales and reserve development separate from current-period medical performance.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Adapt service capacity to the changing membership base
cards.text: Individual Medicare Advantage membership fell to 5.2493 million from 5.6618 million, while state-based membership rose to 1.6156 million from 1.4599 million. Different populations require distinct operating plans.
items: Align member service resources with each business’s enrollment
Prioritize continuity and access during membership changes
Monitor retention and operating contribution by membership business

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve medical-cost performance beneath reserve effects
cards.text: The consolidated GAAP benefit ratio rose to 90.2% from 89.8%, while Insurance remained at 90.4%. Current pricing and care-cost execution need close attention despite the stable segment ratio.
items: Analyze current claims patterns by relevant membership cohort
Coordinate care-management resources with observed member needs
Monitor current medical-cost trends alongside benefit ratios

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make CenterWell’s revenue growth produce better contribution
cards.text: CenterWell revenue rose to $22.473 billion from $19.936 billion, including intersegment amounts, but its operating cost ratio increased to 93.1% from 92.2%. Growth requires more efficient service delivery.
items: Target service processes with avoidable cost or duplication
Match operating capacity to patient and member requirements
Monitor segment contribution without adding intersegment revenue to consolidated sales

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Do not rely on greater prior-year reserve support
cards.text: Favorable prior-year medical reserve development increased to $1.029 billion from $701 million, reducing the annual benefit ratio by 80 basis points. That benefit does not establish stronger current claims economics.
items: Base pricing and care budgets on current-period experience
Use claims feedback to improve reserve and operating assumptions
Monitor earnings sensitivity to reduced favorable development

headline: Huntington should sustain profitable loan growth while keeping deposit funding and credit discipline aligned.
summary: Net interest income, margin and fee businesses improved. Lower charge-offs are encouraging, while a higher provision and loan growth ahead of deposits warrant attention. Prioritize relationship growth aligned with dependable funding and credit discipline.
focusTitle: Make each relationship earn its funding and risk capacity.
focusText: Preserve lending spreads and deepen wealth, payments and cash-management relationships where they add customer value. Coordinate loan commitments with stable deposits and expected credit needs, while preserving returns after funding costs and credit provisions.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve the stronger economics of net interest income
cards.text: GAAP net interest income rose 12% to $5.991 billion, while FTE net interest margin increased to 3.13% from 3.00%. Pricing and funding discipline should sustain the improvement.
items: Price new lending for funding costs and credit requirements
Prioritize relationships with durable deposit and borrowing needs
Monitor loan yields and deposit costs alongside margin

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Keep funding capacity in step with loan growth
cards.text: Average loans and leases grew 10% to $136.687 billion, versus 7% deposit growth to $165.778 billion. The mismatch in growth pace makes deposit quality and liquidity planning important.
items: Coordinate loan pipeline commitments with dependable funding capacity
Develop transaction-deposit relationships around customer operating needs
Monitor deposit retention and funding mix as lending expands

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen fee relationships supporting diversified revenue
cards.text: Wealth and asset-management revenue rose 12% to $409 million; payments and cash management increased 7% to $664 million. These services can strengthen useful, ongoing customer relationships.
items: Target relevant services to established customer needs
Coordinate banking and wealth coverage around client requirements
Monitor fee retention and contribution after servicing costs

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Maintain credit vigilance despite lower realized losses
cards.text: Net charge-offs fell to 0.23% from 0.30%, while provision expense increased to $463 million from $420 million. Lower current losses should not weaken underwriting during loan expansion.
items: Maintain risk selection standards in growing loan categories
Escalate emerging borrower stress before losses materialize
Monitor criticized exposures and expected losses alongside charge-offs

headline: HII should turn stronger shipbuilding throughput into repeatable program economics and cash.
summary: Higher throughput and completed ship deliveries support operational progress, while cash generation improved substantially. Segment margins show different dynamics: Ingalls held steady and Newport News improved with contract adjustments among management’s cited factors. The priority is durable productivity and program execution rather than extrapolating every margin gain mechanically.
focusTitle: Embed production gains in program schedules and cost control.
focusText: Prioritize workforce, suppliers and capital additions that improve dependable ship completion. Preserve cash conversion and distinguish contract adjustments from repeatable operating productivity when judging how much capacity and margin improvement can support future commitments.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make throughput gains repeatable across ship programs
cards.text: HII achieved approximately 14% shipbuilding throughput growth and delivered Massachusetts and Ted Stevens. The next task is sustaining productive workflow and dependable program milestones.
items: Transfer effective production sequencing across comparable shipbuilding work
Align skilled labor and materials with critical program tasks
Monitor milestone completion and rework alongside throughput

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Turn Ingalls growth into stronger operating leverage
cards.text: Ingalls revenue increased 11.2%, while segment operating margin remained 7.6%. More work should support productivity improvements without compromising quality or contractual delivery requirements.
items: Target workflow constraints limiting labor and facility productivity
Coordinate supplier arrivals with executable production schedules
Monitor cost performance and margin as Ingalls workload increases

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Newport News progress with realistic attribution
cards.text: Newport News revenue grew 9.0% and margin improved to 5.1% from 4.1%; management cited Virginia-class contract adjustments. Preserve operational gains while recognizing the contract-related contribution.
items: Prioritize production practices that improve recurring program economics
Embed revised contract assumptions in program cost ownership
Monitor execution margins separately from adjustment-driven comparison benefits

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Invest stronger cash in genuine delivery constraints
cards.text: Operating cash flow rose to $1.196 billion from $393 million; non-GAAP free cash flow was $800 million after $402 million of capital additions. Cash improvement provides capacity for selective investment.
items: Rank capital additions by program delivery and productivity benefits
Preserve liquidity for contracted shipbuilding requirements
Monitor cash conversion and asset utilization after investment

headline: IBM should turn Software and Infrastructure momentum into broader client growth and dependable cash.
summary: Software and Infrastructure grew strongly, while Consulting was flat constant currency. Operating cash and IBM-defined free cash flow moved differently. Prioritize client adoption and services contribution, allocating investment against clearly defined cash capacity.
focusTitle: Connect product demand with useful consulting and recurring client value.
focusText: Prioritize software and infrastructure opportunities that solve established client needs and can support effective implementation services. Preserve investment discipline, using the distinct cash definitions appropriately and separating tax-audit and prior-year pension effects from judgments about recurring demand.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Sustain Software growth through deployed customer value
cards.text: Software revenue rose 11%, or 9% constant currency. Commercial and development resources should deepen usage and renewal economics rather than simply maximize initial license or product selling.
items: Prioritize capabilities supporting active client operating requirements
Coordinate adoption support with account expansion plans
Monitor retention and contribution after implementation and support costs

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make Consulting more effective at converting client needs
cards.text: Consulting revenue grew 2% reported and was flat constant currency. The priority is useful engagement design and efficient delivery, particularly where clients need help adopting the broader portfolio.
items: Focus proposals on clearly defined customer implementation outcomes
Coordinate consulting coverage with relevant product demand
Monitor engagement conversion and contribution after delivery effort

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Infrastructure execution as demand expands
cards.text: Infrastructure revenue rose 12%, or 10% constant currency. Match capacity and technical resources with committed customer requirements while protecting product and service quality.
items: Align production and technical support with executable customer demand
Prioritize reliable deployment and customer readiness
Monitor infrastructure contribution and follow-on client adoption

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Allocate using cash measures that reflect the commitment
cards.text: Operating cash flow was $13.193 billion versus $13.445 billion, while IBM-defined free cash flow rose to $14.7 billion from $12.7 billion. The measures support different cash interpretations.
items: Prioritize investments with credible operating cash contribution
Size commitments after the relevant operating and funding requirements
Monitor both cash measures using their consistent company definitions

headline: IDEX should convert stronger organic orders into sales while integrating acquired scale profitably.
summary: Organic orders outgrew organic sales, creating a conversion opportunity. Mott and pricing supported reported growth, while adjusted gross margin was stable. Prioritize delivery, contribution and cash rather than equating acquired scale with volume strength.
focusTitle: Coordinate backlog delivery and acquisition integration around full contribution.
focusText: Focus operations on the constraints separating orders from revenue, with attention to customer timing and acquisition integration. Preserve gross-profit economics and cash discipline while testing whether higher activity improves total earnings as well as reported sales.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn stronger organic order intake into fulfilled demand
cards.text: Orders rose 12% to $3.5612 billion, including 6% organic growth. The demand signal is useful, but production readiness and customer schedules determine how efficiently it becomes sales.
items: Map new orders to available production and supplier capacity
Prioritize bottlenecks delaying confirmed customer deliveries
Monitor order conversion and changes in customer timing

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve organic sales beyond acquisition and pricing support
cards.text: Sales grew 6% reported but 1% organically; management cited Mott acquisition benefits and price across all segments. Resource allocation should distinguish underlying customer activity from added portfolio scale.
items: Integrate Mott customer and operating plans with clear ownership
Target sales support where organic order demand is executable
Monitor acquired contribution separately from existing-business sales growth

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve gross-profit discipline during conversion
cards.text: GAAP gross margin rose to 44.5% from 44.2%, while adjusted gross margin remained 44.5%. Pricing, product selection and production execution should protect that base as deliveries increase.
items: Price new work for current production and delivery requirements
Extend effective procurement practices across comparable operations
Monitor gross contribution as order and acquisition mix changes

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make stronger cash translate into total earnings progress
cards.text: GAAP diluted EPS fell to $6.41 from $6.64, while operating cash flow rose to $680.4 million from $668.1 million. Allocation should preserve cash while addressing the economics behind earnings pressure.
items: Rank investment proposals by full operating contribution
Preserve collection and inventory discipline through order conversion
Monitor earnings and cash together after integration requirements

headline: IDEXX should convert instrument placements into recurring diagnostics demand while preserving underlying margin gains.
summary: Recurring diagnostics and instrument revenue grew strongly, led by VetLab consumables. Reference laboratories also advanced, while rapid assays declined. Reported margin expansion included litigation and currency effects. The priority is sustained clinical workflow adoption and recurring economics, rather than judging success solely through equipment sales or reported margin changes.
focusTitle: Support instrument use that strengthens recurring customer relationships.
focusText: Coordinate installations, training and consumable availability around veterinary customer needs. Preserve reference-laboratory service quality and address rapid-assay weakness selectively, measuring operating improvement on a comparable basis as well as through reported results.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make instrument growth support active diagnostic workflows
cards.text: Diagnostic capital-instrument revenue grew 51.8% reported and 49.3% organically. Equipment demand creates a recurring opportunity only when installations lead to useful, continuing customer adoption.
items: Coordinate instrument installation with customer training and readiness
Prioritize support for routine diagnostic workflow adoption
Monitor instrument utilization and subsequent consumable demand

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Address the weaker rapid-assay business specifically
cards.text: VetLab consumables grew 13.7% organically and reference laboratories 5.9%, while rapid assays declined 3.3%. Different product trajectories call for targeted account and product actions.
items: Identify customer needs behind lower rapid-assay purchasing
Tailor product support to relevant veterinary workflows
Monitor rapid-assay retention and contribution separately from VetLab growth

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the expanding recurring diagnostics base
cards.text: CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue increased 8.9% reported and 8.1% organically to $3.4072 billion. Reliable supply and service can help sustain those customer relationships.
items: Protect consumable availability for active instrument customers
Maintain reference-laboratory reliability and customer support
Monitor recurring revenue retention and service quality together

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep margin expectations grounded in comparable performance
cards.text: Reported operating margin expanded 270 basis points, versus 90 basis points on the comparable non-GAAP basis after litigation and currency adjustments. Underlying efficiency remains positive but smaller.
items: Preserve operating practices supporting comparable margin improvement
Evaluate growth spending using recurring delivery economics
Monitor comparable and reported margins as adjustment effects change

headline: Illinois Tool Works should turn innovation and margin discipline into organic growth while preserving cash flexibility.
summary: Organic revenue was flat despite innovation contributions, while enterprise initiatives improved margins. End-market trends diverged. Prioritize converting product differentiation into customer demand, balancing capital returns with the investment needed for growth and cash generation.
focusTitle: Put selective commercial growth alongside the strong productivity engine.
focusText: Preserve enterprise cost discipline while directing customer-led innovation and sales resources toward end-market needs. Adjust Construction Products to its weaker workload, and evaluate distributions against free cash and investment rather than treating margin expansion as sufficient progress.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Convert customer-led innovation into broader organic demand
cards.text: Organic revenue was flat, while management reported a 2.4% growth contribution from Customer-Back Innovation. The innovation signal is useful, but overall demand still needs a stronger commercial response.
items: Prioritize innovations addressing demonstrated customer operating problems
Equip sales teams with practical product adoption use cases
Monitor incremental customer revenue and contribution from innovation

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Apply different resource plans across the end markets
cards.text: Automotive OEM and Welding organic revenue each grew 2.0%, while Construction Products declined 5.1%. Capacity and commercial investment should reflect these different customer requirements.
items: Support executable growth opportunities in Automotive OEM and Welding
Align Construction Products spending and inventory with demand
Monitor segment contribution as end-market workload changes

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the enterprise productivity supporting margins
cards.text: Segment operating margin increased 70 basis points to 27.2%, while enterprise initiatives contributed 130 basis points to company margin. Retain successful operating practices without confusing segment margin with company GAAP margin.
items: Extend effective enterprise productivity practices across comparable businesses
Protect customer service while simplifying routine operating work
Monitor margin improvement alongside quality and growth investment

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep distributions responsive to internally generated cash
cards.text: Operating cash flow was $3.126 billion and non-GAAP free cash flow $2.707 billion, while dividends and repurchases returned approximately $3.3 billion. Allocation needs to include funding and investment requirements.
items: Prioritize productive operating investment and liquidity needs
Size discretionary repurchases after committed cash requirements
Monitor total distributions against recurring free cash generation

headline: Illumina should strengthen customer demand and service contribution while restoring cash conversion.
summary: Core revenue was flat but grew outside Greater China, while product and service trends diverged. Adjusted Core margin improved despite a lower GAAP margin, and cash declined. Prioritize adoption and cash economics using consistent Core and consolidated scopes.
focusTitle: Connect product adoption with durable service and operating cash.
focusText: Prioritize customer workflows that support repeat usage and appropriate service demand. Preserve underlying cost discipline while evaluating investment against cash requirements, keeping the 2024 GRAIL scope difference from distorting conclusions about Core Illumina’s business.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Broaden demand beyond the modest ex-China growth
cards.text: Core Illumina revenue was flat; excluding Greater China it increased 2% to $4.10 billion on reported and constant-currency bases. Growth initiatives should respond to specific customer adoption needs.
items: Prioritize product support where customers show executable demand
Address account-level adoption and purchasing barriers
Monitor Core demand by region using consistent business scope

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Strengthen service economics alongside product revenue
cards.text: Consolidated product revenue rose to $3.709 billion from $3.656 billion, while service and other revenue fell to $634 million from $716 million. These trends warrant targeted customer and service execution.
items: Align service offers with active customer operating requirements
Coordinate product onboarding with useful ongoing support
Monitor service retention and contribution within comparable operating scope

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve adjusted operating progress with full-cost accountability
cards.text: Core non-GAAP operating margin rose to 23.1% from 21.3%, while GAAP margin fell to 18.6% from 34.0%. Preserve recurring efficiencies while evaluating the full economic cost of investment.
items: Retain cost improvements supporting recurring operating performance
Prioritize investments with clear customer and contribution benefits
Monitor both Core margin measures without mixing consolidated comparisons

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Restore cash flexibility as investment decisions are made
cards.text: Core non-GAAP free cash flow fell to $931 million from $1.070 billion, and operating cash flow declined to $1.079 billion from $1.207 billion. Cash conversion needs operating ownership.
items: Align inventory and collections with actual customer demand
Stage discretionary investment around operating cash requirements
Monitor Core cash after essential product and service commitments

headline: Incyte should fund a broader product portfolio while protecting Jakafi demand and underlying R&D discipline.
summary: Jakafi and Opzelura grew as newer products broadened revenue. Jakafi remains important, while reported R&D declined despite higher expense on management’s adjusted basis. Prioritize selective commercial and research investment rather than assuming a lower recurring cost base.
focusTitle: Balance established-franchise support with selective product and research investment.
focusText: Preserve access and supply in Jakafi while supporting useful adoption across the expanding portfolio. Allocate research and launch resources through clinical and commercial evidence, distinguishing recurring product demand from milestone revenue and acquisition-related expense comparisons.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect Jakafi’s demand-led contribution
cards.text: Jakafi net product revenue increased 11% to $3.0925 billion, primarily driven by 9% paid-demand growth according to management. This remains an important operating foundation for the broader portfolio.
items: Prioritize reliable supply and patient-access execution
Support provider and account needs relevant to existing demand
Monitor paid demand separately from pricing and other revenue effects

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make broader product revenue economically durable
cards.text: Niktimvo generated $151.6 million and Zynyz $66.4 million versus $3.2 million previously for Zynyz. Investment should support appropriate access, account readiness and operational delivery rather than scale alone.
items: Coordinate product support with relevant treatment-center requirements
Prioritize access and supply readiness for growing products
Monitor product demand and contribution after launch support costs

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Sustain Opzelura growth through repeatable commercial execution
cards.text: Opzelura net product revenue grew 33% to $678.5 million, or 32% constant currency. Preserve the access, availability and customer support required for continued franchise adoption.
items: Target access support to identified customer and provider needs
Align supply planning with observed product demand
Monitor adoption and contribution after commercial investment

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Budget research from underlying costs rather than the headline decline
cards.text: GAAP R&D decreased 21%, but management reported an 8% increase excluding Escient acquisition-related payments and other milestones. Ongoing research capacity therefore needs active prioritization despite the lower reported expense.
items: Rank research programs by evidence and development requirements
Stage spending around meaningful program decision points
Monitor recurring R&D commitments separately from acquisition and milestone effects

headline: Ingersoll Rand should turn stronger bookings into organic, cash-generating growth.
summary: Orders grew faster than revenue, but underlying bookings expanded only modestly in both operating segments. The priority is to convert the larger order intake while distinguishing acquisition contributions from repeatable industrial and precision demand.
focusTitle: Use cash strength to deepen order quality.
focusText: Prioritize delivery reliability and service relationships in the existing businesses, then judge acquisition spending against the cash those businesses generate. A larger order book is most valuable when it produces timely shipments, durable customer demand and disciplined working capital.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Convert the order lead into shipments
cards.text: Orders increased 9% to $7.716 billion against revenue growth of 6%. That creates an execution opportunity, with delivery timing determining how quickly bookings support sales.
items: Assign delivery owners to the largest outstanding orders
Align production slots with confirmed customer delivery dates
Monitor cancellations and working capital during order conversion

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Strengthen underlying industrial demand
cards.text: Industrial Technologies and Services organic orders increased 1%. Aggregate growth therefore deserves a separate assessment from the demand generated by existing industrial operations.
items: Target service opportunities within the installed industrial base
Prioritize sales resources toward repeat equipment and service demand
Measure organic bookings separately from acquired order contributions

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make precision growth repeatable
cards.text: Precision and Science Technologies organic orders increased 2%. Focus on the applications producing repeat orders before adding capacity solely on the strength of consolidated growth.
items: Identify precision applications generating repeat customer orders
Match specialized capacity commitments to confirmed project schedules
Monitor order conversion across precision and science customers

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep acquisition capacity tied to cash
cards.text: Operating cash flow of $1.356 billion and company-defined free cash flow of $1.220 billion provide a useful funding base, subject to competing investment needs.
items: Reserve funding for service capability and production reliability
Set acquisition priorities using expected cash conversion
Monitor integration spending alongside cash generated by existing businesses

headline: Insulet should support Omnipod adoption with reliable recurring supply.
summary: U.S. and international Omnipod growth, a larger active user base and higher gross margin reinforce one another. The next priority is to maintain the supply, training and customer support needed to turn broader access into sustained use.
focusTitle: Scale around active users and retention.
focusText: Allocate manufacturing and support resources according to the needs of existing users and the maturity of new Omnipod 5 markets. Preserve the margin improvement while checking that growth reflects durable use, especially where currency translation increases reported revenue.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the U.S. adoption engine
cards.text: U.S. Omnipod revenue rose 27.2% to about $1.9 billion. Continued growth depends on making onboarding and ongoing access dependable as the domestic user base expands.
items: Strengthen onboarding support for new Omnipod users
Resolve recurring supply and customer service issues promptly
Monitor new starts alongside continued use and retention

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Scale international launches selectively
cards.text: International Omnipod revenue grew 44.1%, or 39.3% at constant currency, to $754.3 million. Strong underlying growth supports expansion, with currency kept separate from launch execution.
items: Allocate local support according to launch adoption
Coordinate distribution and training before broadening market reach
Compare market growth using constant currency and retention

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make user growth operationally sustainable
cards.text: Insulet estimated more than 600,000 active global users after adding Omnipod 5 in nine markets. Recurring supply requirements should guide capacity and service planning.
items: Plan consumables capacity around the active user base
Build launch readiness reviews around training and supply
Monitor service levels as newly launched markets mature

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Reinvest margin gains in dependable scale
cards.text: Annual gross margin increased 180 basis points to 71.6%. Preserve that improvement through efficient manufacturing while protecting product availability and the support required for adoption.
items: Prioritize manufacturing improvements that preserve product quality
Evaluate launch spending against sustained user adoption
Monitor unit costs and geographic mix as volume expands

headline: Intel should pair client recovery with disciplined server and manufacturing execution.
summary: Data Center and AI growth and better gross margin provide support, while Client Computing revenue declined. Lower spending helps the cost base, but sustainable improvement requires product delivery and manufacturing efficiency; consolidated comparisons also reflect Altera's deconsolidation.
focusTitle: Protect product execution while rebuilding profitability.
focusText: Allocate resources to competitive client products, server availability and manufacturing improvements that support both. Judge spending reductions by delivery milestones and customer demand, keeping the September 2025 Altera deconsolidation in mind when interpreting consolidated year-over-year changes.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Rebuild the client revenue base
cards.text: Client Computing Group revenue decreased 3% to $32.2 billion. Diagnose whether shipment volumes or selling prices are constraining the business before choosing broad pricing or spending responses.
items: Segment client performance by shipment volume and pricing
Prioritize product and channel work where demand is weakest
Monitor client product availability and customer order conversion

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Convert server demand into durable growth
cards.text: Data Center and AI revenue grew 5% to $16.9 billion. Support that momentum with reliable supply and product mix decisions that also contribute to profitability.
items: Align server supply with confirmed customer requirements
Prioritize engineering support for commercially important server deployments
Monitor server mix and margin alongside revenue growth

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep cost reductions compatible with delivery
cards.text: GAAP R&D and marketing, general and administrative expense fell 17% to $18.4 billion. Savings become more durable when product execution remains adequately funded.
items: Protect engineering resources tied to critical product milestones
Remove duplicated support work before cutting customer execution capacity
Monitor development milestones and service quality after spending reductions

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make the margin recovery operational
cards.text: GAAP gross margin rose 2.1 percentage points to 34.8%. Continued progress should be linked to utilization, manufacturing efficiency and product economics rather than assumed from expense reductions.
items: Prioritize manufacturing improvements with clear product cost benefits
Match production commitments to credible client and server demand
Monitor utilization and cost per wafer alongside gross margin

headline: Interactive Brokers should scale customer growth without concentrating financing risk.
summary: Accounts and customer equity expanded strongly, accompanied by even faster margin loan growth and larger credit balances. The priority is to preserve the platform's appeal while ensuring lending controls, funding management and service capacity keep pace with the larger customer base.
focusTitle: Build operating capacity around the larger balance sheet.
focusText: Use customer growth to deepen durable relationships while maintaining disciplined collateral and liquidity management. Evaluate account activity, asset retention and financing exposure together; year-end balances alone do not establish how much recurring revenue each new relationship will generate.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn new accounts into lasting relationships
cards.text: Customer accounts reached 4.40 million, up 32%. Onboarding, platform reliability and support capacity should keep pace so account acquisition can translate into sustained customer activity.
items: Simplify onboarding friction for newly opened accounts
Allocate support capacity to recurring customer service issues
Monitor account activation and retention by acquisition cohort

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve the larger customer asset base
cards.text: Year-end customer equity increased 37% to $779.9 billion. Protecting those relationships requires distinguishing retained customer assets from changes driven by market valuations.
items: Improve asset transfer and portfolio servicing workflows
Tailor platform support to customers with complex portfolios
Monitor net asset transfers separately from market-driven equity changes

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep margin lending growth controlled
cards.text: Customer margin loans increased 40% to $90.2 billion. Faster lending growth makes collateral quality and concentrated exposures more important as the customer base expands.
items: Review concentrated collateral and correlated borrower exposures
Stress margin requirements against adverse market movements
Monitor collateral shortfalls and credit utilization by customer segment

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Manage credit balances as customer obligations
cards.text: Customer credit balances rose 34% to $160.1 billion. Funding and interest rate decisions should preserve liquidity and customer confidence as these balances change.
items: Align liquid resources with customer withdrawal scenarios
Evaluate customer cash pricing alongside funding economics
Monitor credit balance movements and interest rate sensitivity

headline: ICE should improve Mortgage Technology returns while preserving exchange strength.
summary: Recurring and transaction revenues both grew, supported by a highly profitable Exchanges business. Mortgage Technology's narrow GAAP margin alongside a much higher adjusted margin makes it the clearest area for improving reported returns and capital allocation.
focusTitle: Make mortgage economics a capital allocation priority.
focusText: Protect the exchange platform and recurring customer relationships while directing mortgage investment toward demonstrable workflow value and sustainable profitability. Assess the costs excluded from adjusted results when deciding how much additional capital the mortgage business should receive.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen the recurring revenue base
cards.text: Recurring revenue increased 5% to $5.056 billion. Maintaining customer renewal and product usefulness can provide continuity alongside the more activity-sensitive transaction businesses.
items: Prioritize product improvements that support customer renewals
Expand relevant services within existing recurring customer relationships
Monitor retention and recurring revenue growth by product

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Capture activity without overbuilding fixed costs
cards.text: Net transaction revenue grew 10% to $4.875 billion. Use the stronger activity base to improve execution and capacity while keeping investment resilient to changing trading volumes.
items: Maintain trading capacity and execution reliability during activity peaks
Prioritize transaction products with durable customer participation
Monitor transaction volumes and revenue yields separately

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect exchange economics and reliability
cards.text: Exchanges generated $5.411 billion of net revenue with a 74% operating margin. Preserve that strength by funding system resilience and customer access alongside expense discipline.
items: Protect investment in exchange uptime and operational resilience
Evaluate new exchange products against customer demand
Monitor operating margin alongside reliability and market participation

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Require mortgage investment to improve reported returns
cards.text: Mortgage Technology generated $2.101 billion of net revenue, with a 1% GAAP operating margin and 41% adjusted margin. The distinction matters when judging sustainable business economics.
items: Prioritize mortgage workflows with clear customer adoption
Link mortgage spending decisions to incremental operating contribution
Monitor excluded costs and GAAP profitability alongside adjusted performance

headline: IFF should repair Food Ingredients mix while sustaining stronger businesses.
summary: Taste, Health & Biosciences and Scent recorded comparable currency neutral growth, while Food Ingredients declined amid Protein Solutions softness and low-margin exits. The priority is selective portfolio improvement, with growth evaluated alongside the profitability of the business retained.
focusTitle: Allocate effort to profitable, repeatable customer demand.
focusText: Support successful flavor, bioscience and fragrance applications while addressing Protein Solutions at the customer and product level. Keep divestiture exclusions and non-GAAP measurement consistent when assessing progress, so portfolio exits do not obscure whether the remaining businesses are improving.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve broad-based Taste growth
cards.text: Taste comparable currency neutral sales increased 4%, with growth across all regions. Reinforce customer application work that supports repeat demand rather than assuming every geography requires the same investment.
items: Prioritize flavor development tied to repeat customer applications
Allocate technical support according to regional project conversion
Monitor regional growth and profitability using comparable definitions

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build on Food Biosciences momentum
cards.text: Health & Biosciences comparable currency neutral sales rose 3%, led by Food Biosciences. Direct technical and commercial resources toward applications that can sustain this contribution.
items: Expand customer trials in successful Food Biosciences applications
Coordinate technical support with commercial project priorities
Monitor trial conversion and repeat orders within biosciences

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Separate Protein Solutions weakness from deliberate exits
cards.text: Food Ingredients comparable currency neutral sales fell 3%. Management cited Protein Solutions softness and low-margin business exits, which call for different commercial and portfolio responses.
items: Diagnose Protein Solutions demand by customer and application
Retain business only where pricing supports acceptable economics
Monitor remaining portfolio volumes and margins after exits

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Turn fragrance growth into stronger earnings
cards.text: Scent comparable currency neutral sales increased 3%, including double-digit Fine Fragrance growth, while adjusted EBITDA grew 2% on the same basis. Protect the economics of this expansion.
items: Prioritize Fine Fragrance projects with attractive production economics
Review pricing and resource requirements across the Scent mix
Monitor adjusted EBITDA conversion using the same comparable basis

headline: International Paper should make asset restructuring deliver positive cash generation.
summary: The preliminary continuing-operations results contain substantial impairment, accelerated depreciation and restructuring charges. These do not establish a demand collapse, but negative company-defined free cash flow makes cash delivery from asset rationalization the central business priority.
focusTitle: Judge the restructuring by operating continuity and cash returns.
focusText: Separate noncash accounting effects from restructuring payments and capital needs, then prioritize the projects that improve the remaining production network. Keep conclusions within the preliminary continuing-operations scope and assess whether cash benefits materialize after the associated spending.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Use the impairment to challenge asset allocation
cards.text: Continuing results included a $2.47 billion noncash goodwill impairment. It signals a reassessment of recorded value and strengthens the case for disciplined returns on future investment.
items: Reassess investment priorities across the remaining operating assets
Set cash return expectations for major capital commitments
Monitor operating performance without treating impairment as cash spending

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make rationalization improve the production network
cards.text: Noncash accelerated depreciation of $0.96 billion was linked to asset rationalization. The operating task is to transfer production and preserve customer service while reshaping capacity.
items: Coordinate production transfers before affected assets leave service
Prioritize capacity changes that preserve dependable customer supply
Monitor remaining plant utilization and delivery performance

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Control the cash cost of restructuring
cards.text: Restructuring charges totaled $0.63 billion. Management should connect those charges to specific operating changes and distinguish recognized expense from the associated cash payments.
items: Assign accountable owners to each major restructuring initiative
Sequence restructuring payments against available operating cash
Monitor realized savings and service disruption against implementation spending

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore cash after investment needs
cards.text: Operating cash flow was $1.70 billion, but company-defined free cash flow was negative $0.16 billion. Capital and restructuring demands therefore deserve close prioritization.
items: Rank capital projects by necessity and cash contribution
Improve receivables and inventory management during network changes
Monitor free cash flow after restructuring and capital spending

headline: Intuit should translate rapid product growth into durable customer economics.
summary: Online Ecosystem, TurboTax Live and Credit Karma all expanded strongly, while Global Business Solutions Group also grew. The main allocation question is where growth produces lasting customer relationships, particularly given the slower Online Ecosystem rate when Mailchimp is included.
focusTitle: Scale the strongest workflows with measured customer value.
focusText: Prioritize resources that make tax assistance and business workflows more useful across repeat customer cycles. Evaluate Mailchimp separately within the ecosystem, and avoid treating overlapping Online Ecosystem and Global Business Solutions Group figures as independent sources of incremental growth.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Address the gap inside Online Ecosystem
cards.text: Online Ecosystem revenue grew 20% to $8.3 billion, compared with 25% excluding Mailchimp. Investigate Mailchimp's customer economics while protecting the stronger ecosystem workflows.
items: Identify Mailchimp adoption and retention friction by customer use
Improve connections between marketing and core business workflows
Monitor ecosystem retention with Mailchimp performance shown separately

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make live tax growth repeatable
cards.text: TurboTax Live revenue increased 47% to $2.0 billion. Sustaining that expansion requires effective expert capacity, useful assistance and customer trust across repeat filing cycles.
items: Match expert capacity to demand for tax assistance
Improve handoffs between automated tools and live experts
Monitor repeat use and service quality alongside acquisition costs

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Credit Karma's commercial momentum
cards.text: Credit Karma annual revenue rose 32% to $2.3 billion. Growth should be supported by relevant product matching and durable partner economics rather than acquisition volume alone.
items: Improve product matching around customer financial needs
Prioritize partner relationships with dependable conversion and service
Monitor customer engagement and revenue per successful referral

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep business growth grounded in retention
cards.text: Global Business Solutions Group revenue increased 16% to $11.1 billion. Product expansion should deepen useful workflows while preserving the customer economics of the existing base.
items: Prioritize business features that remove recurring workflow friction
Link cross-selling efforts to demonstrated customer usage
Monitor retention and service costs across business customer cohorts

headline: Intuitive Surgical should scale system support around growing procedure demand.
summary: Da Vinci procedures grew faster than the installed system base, while Ion expanded more rapidly from its own base. This supports an execution focus: ensure training, service and consumables capacity keep pace while preserving the economics of a larger surgical platform.
focusTitle: Fund the capabilities that keep systems productively used.
focusText: Prioritize hospital readiness, dependable service and procedure support alongside new system placements. Evaluate da Vinci and Ion independently because installed base growth alone does not prove comparable utilization, and use the reported non-GAAP gross margin consistently when assessing expansion economics.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support sustained da Vinci procedure growth
cards.text: Worldwide da Vinci procedures increased about 18%. Continued adoption depends on hospital workflows and support capacity that help teams use available systems effectively and reliably.
items: Target training resources to expanding hospital procedure programs
Coordinate consumables supply with expected procedure schedules
Monitor procedure growth and service needs across hospital cohorts

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make placements translate into productive capacity

headline: Invesco should turn its larger asset base into durable revenue and funding flexibility.

Monitor assets by market movement, net flows and fee yield

headline: Invitation Homes should improve new leasing without weakening renewal economics.
