cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make operating leverage repeatable
cards.text: Annual adjusted operating leverage was about 1,200 basis points. The scale of that improvement warrants separating durable revenue and cost execution from changes that may not recur.
items: Identify revenue and expense drivers behind adjusted operating leverage
Protect customer service capacity while removing inefficient spending
Monitor recurring operating trends using a consistent adjusted basis

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use fee services to deepen commercial relationships
cards.text: Adjusted fee-based operating leverage was about 280 basis points. Sustain that contribution through useful client services and disciplined delivery costs rather than indiscriminate cross-selling.
items: Prioritize fee services relevant to existing commercial customers
Improve delivery efficiency in growing fee-based businesses
Monitor fee retention and contribution alongside relationship profitability

headline: Keysight should convert improving orders into cash-generating customer delivery.
summary: A return to full-year growth and accelerating order momentum were accompanied by stronger operating and company-defined free cash flow. The priority is to support executable demand while preserving cash discipline, with available liquidity allocated according to customer requirements and investment returns.
focusTitle: Use cash strength to support the order recovery.
focusText: Prioritize product delivery and capabilities tied to confirmed customer demand, keeping working capital and capital spending proportional to execution needs. Assess returns using consistent earnings figures because the preliminary release and input SEC net income totals differ.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the operating cash improvement
cards.text: Operating cash flow increased to $1.41 billion from $1.05 billion. Keep collections and order-related working capital disciplined as the business supports stronger customer demand.
items: Align procurement with confirmed customer delivery schedules
Resolve receivable delays as orders move through fulfillment
Monitor operating cash alongside inventory and customer collections

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make free cash flow fund productive capabilities
cards.text: Company-defined free cash flow rose to $1.28 billion from $0.91 billion. Use that flexibility to fund necessary product and operating capabilities with clear commercial value.
items: Rank investment proposals by customer need and cash contribution
Protect maintenance and development work needed for order execution
Monitor free cash flow after prioritized capital commitments

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Allocate liquidity without overcommitting to a recovery
cards.text: Cash and equivalents totaled $1.87 billion at October 31, 2025. Preserve flexibility while evaluating capacity, development and other capital uses against the durability of demand.
items: Reserve liquidity for operating and customer delivery requirements
Stage discretionary spending according to confirmed order conversion
Monitor cash headroom after investment and other planned uses

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn accelerating orders into repeatable revenue
cards.text: Management reported a return to full-year growth with order momentum accelerating through FY2025. Delivery and customer acceptance now matter more than treating bookings as completed sales.
items: Prioritize fulfillment resources for executable customer orders
Address product availability and acceptance bottlenecks with customers
Monitor order aging, cancellations and conversion into collected revenue

headline: Kimberly-Clark should protect volume gains while improving profit and cash conversion.
summary: Organic growth was supported by higher volume despite negative pricing, but International Personal Care profit declined and operating cash fell as capital spending increased. The priority is to keep demand gains commercially attractive while tightening investment and cost decisions.
focusTitle: Make each source of volume growth earn its funding.
focusText: Evaluate pricing, manufacturing economics and investment needs at the business level rather than treating higher volume as sufficient progress. Keep the release's discontinued-operations exclusions consistent, and prioritize capital projects that improve the cash and profit contribution of the remaining operations.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve volume without eroding product economics
cards.text: Organic sales increased 1.7%, including 2.5% higher volume and 0.9% negative pricing. Growth should be supported by products whose net contribution remains attractive after commercial spending.
items: Assess product contribution after pricing and promotional effects
Target commercial investment to durable consumer demand
Monitor organic volume and net pricing together

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make North American demand operationally efficient
cards.text: North America organic sales increased 1.8%, with volume up 2.6%. Support that demand through reliable supply and cost-efficient production rather than broad spending expansion.
items: Align production and replenishment with growing product demand
Prioritize productivity work that preserves product availability
Monitor regional product contribution alongside organic volume growth

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Repair international profit conversion
cards.text: International Personal Care organic sales increased 1.7%, but operating profit declined 3.6%. Identify where pricing, mix or operating costs are preventing demand from producing earnings.
items: Review market and product profitability within International Personal Care
Target cost and pricing actions to specific profit pressures
Monitor regional operating profit against comparable sales growth

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Prioritize investment as cash demands increase
cards.text: Operating cash flow fell to $2.8 billion from $3.2 billion, while capital spending rose to $1.1 billion from $721 million. Investment choices deserve stronger cash-return discipline.
items: Rank capital projects by necessity and expected operating contribution
Improve inventory and receivables management across continuing operations
Monitor operating cash after capital spending and funding commitments

headline: Kimco should convert signed leases into occupied, rent-paying space.
summary: Leasing activity and occupancy were strong, while a meaningful leased-to-economic occupancy gap represents rent not yet recognized. The priority is tenant opening execution and dependable collections, converting the leasing pipeline into operating income without weakening property-level returns.
focusTitle: Put tenant openings at the center of growth execution.
focusText: Coordinate landlord work, tenant readiness and commencement requirements to unlock the signed rent pipeline. Preserve small shop leasing progress and evaluate spending by the rent and NOI it can support, distinguishing the annual base rent opportunity from current recognized revenue.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make leasing volume economically productive
cards.text: Kimco leased 12.1 million square feet, up 8.9%. Lease approvals should balance occupancy gains with tenant quality, required property spending and sustainable rental contribution.
items: Prioritize prospective tenants with credible opening and operating plans
Evaluate lease economics after tenant improvement commitments
Monitor signed leasing volume alongside expected net rental contribution

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve high occupancy through tenant retention
cards.text: Pro-rata leased occupancy was 96.4%, with small shop occupancy at 92.7%. Retention and space readiness can protect this position while targeted leasing addresses remaining vacancies.
items: Engage existing tenants before important lease renewal decisions
Prepare vacant small shop spaces for suitable prospects
Monitor retention and occupancy separately by space category

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Turn the signed pipeline into economic occupancy
cards.text: The 390-basis-point occupancy gap represented $73 million of annual base rent. This is a pipeline measure, making tenant opening and rent commencement the practical priority.
items: Assign owners to landlord work delaying tenant openings
Coordinate tenant readiness and outstanding commencement requirements
Monitor opening milestones and rent commencement against signed leases

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the path from property growth to FFO
cards.text: Same-property NOI increased 3.0%, while FFO per diluted share grew 6.7%. Assess whether property execution and funding decisions sustain per-share operating results.
items: Prioritize property spending that supports durable rental income
Evaluate funding choices alongside tenant opening commitments
Monitor FFO per share and same-property NOI with consistent definitions

headline: Kinder Morgan should deliver its gas-led project backlog with disciplined funding.
summary: Natural gas transport volumes increased on the stated pro forma basis, and the backlog is concentrated in gas and power-generation demand. The priority is reliable project execution and capital allocation, with the EagleHawk gain separated from judgments about recurring operating performance.
focusTitle: Translate the backlog into contracted operating contribution.
focusText: Sequence investment around project readiness and customer commitments while protecting existing network reliability. Evaluate natural gas and power-related exposure across the portfolio, and compare recurring cash capacity with construction needs instead of treating a divestiture gain as repeatable operating support.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support higher transport activity with network reliability
cards.text: Natural gas transport averaged 46,603 billion Btu per day versus 44,252 on the release's pro forma basis. Preserve dependable service while assessing incremental capacity needs.
items: Prioritize maintenance supporting reliable natural gas transportation
Identify network constraints affecting contracted customer delivery
Monitor transport volumes using consistent pro forma asset coverage

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make the project backlog executable
cards.text: Year-end project backlog was $10 billion. Capital commitments should follow customer readiness, delivery requirements and credible construction plans rather than backlog size alone.
items: Sequence project spending around confirmed customer commitments
Assign accountability for construction cost and schedule changes
Monitor project completion milestones and remaining capital requirements

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Manage concentrated exposure to gas and power demand
cards.text: About 90% of backlog related to natural gas and nearly 60% supported power generation. Evaluate shared customer and execution risks across that concentrated investment program.
items: Review customer commitments across gas and power-related projects
Coordinate construction resources where projects compete for capacity
Monitor concentration and contracted utilization as projects enter service

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep disposal gains separate from ongoing capacity
cards.text: Annual results included a $123 million EagleHawk divestiture gain. Treat the transaction as a capital allocation event when judging the operating business's funding strength.
items: Allocate disposal resources against prioritized capital and funding needs
Assess recurring operating contribution without the divestiture gain
Monitor construction funding against ongoing cash generation

headline: KKR should convert record fundraising into disciplined deployment and fee growth.
summary: Record capital raising, a larger fee-paying asset base and increased fee-related earnings show strong platform demand. With substantial capital invested, the priority is to maintain underwriting quality and operating capacity while turning commitments into durable fee contribution and investor relationships.
focusTitle: Let investment quality set the pace of expansion.
focusText: Allocate deployment and platform resources according to attractive opportunities and client obligations rather than fundraising momentum alone. Evaluate fee growth separately from investment outcomes, preserving the service and execution standards needed to retain investors as the asset base expands.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make record fundraising deepen investor relationships
cards.text: KKR raised $129 billion of new capital, its annual record. Sustain that momentum through investment execution and communication that reinforce investor confidence beyond the fundraising cycle.
items: Match investor servicing resources to new capital commitments
Provide clear reporting on deployment and portfolio development
Monitor investor retention and repeat commitments by strategy

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn fee-paying scale into durable contribution
cards.text: Fee-paying assets under management rose 18% to $604 billion. Growth should support recurring economics without allowing platform expense to expand ahead of the assets serviced.
items: Allocate platform capacity according to fee-paying strategy needs
Review product economics alongside client servicing requirements
Monitor fee yields and retention across the expanded asset base

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep deployment disciplined as capital availability grows
cards.text: KKR invested $95 billion during 2025. Investment selection and follow-through should guide the deployment pace, rather than assuming available capital must be invested quickly.
items: Apply consistent underwriting standards across new investment commitments
Reserve resources for portfolio support after initial deployment
Monitor concentration and investment performance by deployment cohort

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve fee earnings conversion during expansion
cards.text: Annual fee-related earnings increased 14% to $3.7 billion. Assess that non-GAAP growth alongside platform staffing and the requirements of the larger fee-paying base.
items: Prioritize hiring where it supports measurable client or investment needs
Evaluate strategy expansion against incremental fee contribution
Monitor fee-related earnings and operating capacity using consistent definitions

headline: KLA should sustain inspection growth while managing customer and revenue concentration.
summary: Process Control and advanced-packaging-related businesses expanded, supported by inspection demand and a larger service base. The priority is to maintain product and service execution while distinguishing repeatable customer demand from a settlement contribution and concentration in a major customer.
focusTitle: Build recurring support around the expanding inspection footprint.
focusText: Allocate engineering and service resources to customer applications with sustained demand, while staging capacity commitments against confirmed orders. Evaluate advanced packaging opportunities on their individual economics and keep the cancellation settlement separate when assessing recurring growth in PCB and Component Inspection.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the process control and service engine
cards.text: Semiconductor Process Control revenue increased 25% to about $10.95 billion. Management cited inspection demand and a larger installed service base, making product delivery and service reliability complementary priorities.
items: Align inspection delivery resources with confirmed customer requirements
Expand service capability around the larger installed base
Monitor equipment contribution and recurring service retention separately

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Scale advanced packaging with customer readiness
cards.text: Specialty Semiconductor Process revenue grew 11% to $587.1 million, primarily from advanced packaging. Invest where customer adoption and support requirements justify additional capacity.
items: Prioritize engineering support for adopted advanced packaging applications
Stage capacity additions around customer qualification and delivery needs
Monitor repeat orders and product contribution within specialty processes

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Separate repeatable inspection demand from settlement income
cards.text: PCB and Component Inspection revenue rose 13% to $621.7 million, including AI packaging demand and a project-cancellation settlement. Resource decisions should reflect the recurring customer opportunity.
items: Support AI packaging applications with confirmed customer demand
Base staffing and capacity plans on recurring project economics
Monitor underlying order conversion excluding settlement contributions

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Manage dependence on a major customer
cards.text: TSMC represented more than 10% of FY2025 total revenue. Preserve that relationship while testing how shifts in a major customer's requirements would affect production and support.
items: Coordinate delivery and service planning with major customer needs
Develop commercially viable applications across other customer relationships
Monitor customer concentration and capacity exposure under order changes

headline: Kraft Heinz should rebuild North American demand with disciplined product economics.
summary: Organic sales declined as negative volume/mix outweighed pricing, with North America the clearest weak area. Emerging Markets grew largely through pricing. The priority is commercially attractive demand recovery, while the large impairment warrants stricter investment discipline without establishing the cause of the sales decline.
focusTitle: Direct resources toward products that can regain repeat demand.
focusText: Target assortment, availability and pricing work to the North American products with the weakest customer response. Preserve healthy international contribution, and use realistic product-level cash expectations to decide where brand support and capital investment can improve the retained portfolio.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Address volume and mix before relying on price
cards.text: Organic net sales fell 3.4%, with a 4.1-point volume/mix decline partly offset by 0.7 points of pricing. Product demand and mix require more attention than additional broad pricing.
items: Identify product and channel sources of volume/mix weakness
Test assortment and pricing changes against product contribution
Monitor repeat purchasing and organic volume after commercial actions

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Focus recovery resources on North America
cards.text: North America organic sales declined 4.7%, including a 5.0-point volume/mix decrease. Concentrate customer and brand execution work where the regional demand gap is most pronounced.
items: Prioritize North American products with fixable demand barriers
Coordinate retail availability with targeted brand and promotion plans
Monitor regional product contribution alongside volume/mix recovery

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve international growth without overrelying on pricing
cards.text: Emerging Markets organic sales rose 4.6%, including 4.0 points of pricing and 0.6 points of volume/mix. Support volume development while protecting existing price realization.
items: Allocate distribution support to sustainable local demand opportunities
Tailor pricing decisions to product-level customer response
Monitor organic volume/mix and contribution across emerging markets

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Use the impairment to tighten future allocation
cards.text: Impairment losses totaled $9.306 billion. The accounting charge strengthens the need for realistic returns on portfolio investment, but does not by itself diagnose why sales weakened.
items: Reassess growth assumptions behind major portfolio investments
Rank brand and capital commitments by expected cash contribution
Monitor realized product economics against investment approval assumptions

headline: Kroger should make digital scale earn its fulfillment costs.
summary: Identical sales growth and substantial eCommerce sales demonstrate customer demand, while the automated fulfillment impairment makes delivery economics a clear priority. Alternative Profit Businesses provide another earnings source, but should complement a grocery and digital model that stands on sound operating economics.
focusTitle: Choose fulfillment investments by customer value and contribution.
focusText: Prioritize service reliability and economical order fulfillment over digital sales growth alone. Evaluate automated capacity and other fulfillment options against local demand, while protecting core grocery relationships and the profitability of complementary businesses rather than using their earnings to mask weak delivery returns.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep grocery growth tied to loyal customers
cards.text: Identical sales excluding fuel and adjustment items increased 2.9%. Preserve that demand through dependable availability, relevant assortments and commercial spending that supports repeat visits.
items: Prioritize availability in frequently purchased grocery categories
Evaluate promotions using repeat customer demand and contribution
Monitor identical sales alongside basket economics and customer retention

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make digital scale commercially productive
cards.text: Kroger generated more than $16 billion of eCommerce sales. That scale supports investment only where fulfillment and customer service costs allow orders to contribute economically.
items: Improve picking and delivery workflows for existing digital demand
Match fulfillment options to local customer order patterns
Monitor contribution per order and repeat digital purchasing

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Reset automated fulfillment capital discipline
cards.text: FY2025 included $2.5 billion of impairment and related charges for the automated fulfillment network. Future network choices should be grounded in usable capacity and order economics.
items: Review automated site utilization against current customer demand
Prioritize fulfillment changes with clear service and cost benefits
Monitor remaining capital commitments and operating contribution by facility

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve complementary earnings quality
cards.text: Alternative Profit Businesses generated $1.5 billion of operating profit. Sustain that contribution while assessing the investment and customer relationships required by each activity.
items: Allocate resources to alternative businesses with durable customer value
Evaluate expansion spending against incremental operating contribution
Monitor business-level returns alongside the core grocery economics

headline: Labcorp should integrate laboratory deals while preserving organic testing growth.
summary: Organic growth was meaningful, acquisitions contributed further expansion and new test introductions broadened the offering. The priority is to translate signed and closed transactions into reliable laboratory operations while using stronger free cash flow to fund selective integration and test adoption.
focusTitle: Make integration reinforce the existing laboratory network.
focusText: Prioritize patient and customer service continuity, useful test launches and operational improvements across acquired and existing laboratories. Distinguish completed transactions from signed deals, and assess the cash contribution of expansion rather than equating transaction counts or test introductions with realized business returns.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the organic growth engine
cards.text: Organic growth contributed 4.4% to annual revenue growth, with acquisitions net of divestitures adding 2.5%. Retain separate views of existing laboratory demand and purchased growth.
items: Prioritize service improvements supporting repeat laboratory customer demand
Allocate commercial resources using organic test growth opportunities
Monitor organic growth and acquisition contributions separately

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make laboratory transactions operationally useful
cards.text: Labcorp signed or closed 13 health-system and regional laboratory transactions. Integration planning should reflect each deal's status and protect customer service as operating responsibilities change.
items: Sequence integration work around actual transaction closing readiness
Coordinate test routing and customer communication during transitions
Monitor service continuity and integration spending by completed deal

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Turn new tests into adopted services
cards.text: More than 130 new tests launched during 2025. Commercial value depends on appropriate customer adoption and dependable laboratory execution rather than the introduction count alone.
items: Prioritize customer education for tests addressing clear clinical needs
Match laboratory capacity and turnaround standards to adoption
Monitor test utilization and operating contribution after launch

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use improved cash generation to fund selective growth
cards.text: Company-defined free cash flow rose to $1.21 billion from $1.10 billion. Preserve that funding capacity while meeting integration and laboratory investment requirements.
items: Rank laboratory investments by service need and cash contribution
Stage discretionary deal spending against integration capacity
Monitor free cash flow after acquisition and operating investment needs

headline: Lam Research should restore cash conversion while protecting product investment.
summary: Higher GAAP gross margin and increased R&D support the earnings profile, but working capital absorbed substantially more cash and operating cash flow declined despite higher earnings. The priority is to release cash from operating balances without weakening customer delivery or product development.
focusTitle: Bring working capital back into the earnings improvement.
focusText: Align inventory, procurement and collection decisions with executable customer requirements. Preserve research spending that advances commercially important products, while evaluating margin and cash together so better accounting earnings translate into stronger funding capacity for the equipment business.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the economics behind higher gross margin
cards.text: FY2026 GAAP gross margin increased to 50.5% from 48.7%. Maintain product and manufacturing discipline while checking whether the improvement survives changes in customer demand and mix.
items: Prioritize manufacturing improvements that preserve equipment performance
Evaluate customer orders using product-level contribution
Monitor gross margin alongside product mix and delivery costs

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make higher R&D spending earn customer adoption
cards.text: Annual R&D expense increased to $2.376 billion from $2.096 billion. Focus resources on development milestones and customer needs that justify the larger investment base.
items: Rank development programs by customer need and technical readiness
Protect engineering work linked to important customer qualifications
Monitor milestone delivery and subsequent product adoption

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Address the working capital cash absorption
cards.text: Operating asset and liability changes consumed $1.914 billion, versus a $441.8 million source previously. Identify the specific balances requiring action before applying broad cash restrictions.
items: Review inventory commitments against confirmed customer delivery schedules
Resolve receivables and payment timing exceptions with accountable owners
Monitor cash tied up in each operating balance category

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require earnings growth to translate into cash
cards.text: Operating cash flow declined to $5.858 billion from $6.173 billion despite higher earnings. Funding decisions should reflect actual cash conversion rather than earnings momentum alone.
items: Stage discretionary capital commitments against operating cash availability
Link delivery milestones and customer collections in execution reviews
Monitor operating cash relative to earnings and investment needs

headline: Las Vegas Sands should improve Macao profit conversion while sustaining Singapore strength.
summary: Marina Bay Sands grew revenue and adjusted property EBITDA margin, while Macao's adjusted property EBITDA edged lower despite higher revenue. The Londoner expanded strongly, making property-level operating leverage in Macao the priority alongside preserving the successful Singapore economics.
focusTitle: Direct Macao spending toward profitable guest demand.
focusText: Evaluate staffing, customer acquisition and property costs against the contribution of incremental revenue, with The Londoner assessed within the broader Macao portfolio. Preserve the service and capacity supporting Marina Bay Sands, using annual adjusted property measures consistently rather than extrapolating quarterly hotel or gaming statistics.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Marina Bay Sands revenue momentum
cards.text: Annual Marina Bay Sands revenue increased to $5.590 billion from $4.230 billion. Reinforce the guest experience and commercial execution that can sustain demand without assuming every revenue source grows evenly.
items: Allocate property capacity around demonstrated guest demand
Prioritize guest service improvements supporting repeat visits
Monitor revenue contribution across the property's operating activities

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep Singapore growth profitable
cards.text: Marina Bay Sands adjusted property EBITDA margin rose to 52.3% from 48.5%. Protect that conversion through disciplined operating deployment rather than reducing service capacity indiscriminately.
items: Align staffing and operating schedules with guest activity
Evaluate commercial spending against incremental property contribution
Monitor adjusted property margin alongside service quality and repeat demand

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make Macao revenue growth improve earnings
cards.text: Macao adjusted property EBITDA was $2.310 billion versus $2.327 billion despite higher revenue. Diagnose property mix and operating costs before increasing broad customer acquisition spending.
items: Review incremental revenue contribution across the Macao properties
Target cost and commercial changes to specific margin pressures
Monitor property-level adjusted EBITDA conversion alongside revenue growth

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn Londoner expansion into durable contribution
cards.text: The Londoner Macao revenue rose to $2.556 billion from $1.984 billion. Evaluate the operating resources required by the larger business and its contribution to Macao profitability.
items: Prioritize Londoner guest offerings with attractive operating contribution
Coordinate staffing and commercial activity with actual demand
Monitor Londoner earnings contribution within the broader Macao portfolio

headline: Leidos should prioritize funded backlog conversion while preserving segment margin gains.
summary: A large backlog and book-to-bill of 1.0 times support an established delivery base, with margin improvement in Defense Systems and Commercial & International. The priority is to align resources with funded work and maintain contract economics rather than treating all backlog as immediately executable.
focusTitle: Make funding readiness guide project delivery.
focusText: Allocate staff and supplier commitments to contracts with clear authorization and delivery requirements. Preserve the segment margin improvements through scope and cost control, and keep consolidated versus attributable net income definitions consistent when evaluating overall profitability rather than letting that reporting distinction drive operating decisions.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Improve booking quality alongside replenishment
cards.text: Annual net bookings were $17.5 billion with a 1.0-times book-to-bill ratio. Maintain the work pipeline through bids that fit delivery capabilities and acceptable contract economics.
items: Prioritize bids aligned with existing technical delivery strengths
Price contract complexity and resource requirements explicitly
Monitor bookings and contract contribution rather than volume alone

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Distinguish funded work from total backlog
cards.text: Year-end backlog was $49.0 billion, including $9.7 billion funded. Staffing and procurement decisions should follow funding readiness and customer authorization rather than total contracted opportunity.
items: Sequence delivery teams around funded contract requirements
Stage supplier commitments against authorization and project readiness
Monitor funded backlog conversion and changes in unfunded work

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect improved Defense Systems execution
cards.text: Defense Systems GAAP operating margin increased to 7.2% from 4.6%. Preserve that improvement through contract delivery and disciplined handling of scope or cost changes.
items: Retain project controls supporting efficient defense contract execution
Address cost overruns and scope changes with clear ownership
Monitor segment margin alongside delivery milestones and customer acceptance

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Carry Commercial & International gains into new work
cards.text: Commercial & International GAAP operating margin increased to 7.2% from 4.6%. Apply consistent commercial and delivery standards as the segment takes on additional projects.
items: Use demonstrated project economics when selecting new opportunities
Match staffing and partners to customer delivery commitments
Monitor segment contribution and contract risk as work progresses

headline: Lennar should protect home profitability while converting stronger orders into deliveries.
summary: New orders grew faster than deliveries, but the average delivered price declined. The priority is to align home starts, pricing and construction spending with realizable customer demand so higher unit activity supports earnings rather than merely expanding the number of homes delivered.
focusTitle: Use community-level economics to guide volume decisions.
focusText: Match construction pace to executable orders and evaluate pricing or incentives after their effect on home contribution. Preserve delivery reliability, control land and build commitments, and monitor cancellation risk so the larger order intake becomes profitable closings with manageable cash requirements.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn higher orders into dependable closings
cards.text: New orders increased 9% to 83,978 homes. Sales execution should emphasize buyer readiness and achievable delivery schedules rather than treating every order as a completed transaction.
items: Confirm buyer readiness as homes approach construction milestones
Coordinate sales commitments with community construction capacity
Monitor order cancellations and conversion into completed closings

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Keep delivery growth aligned with build capacity
cards.text: Deliveries increased 3% to 82,583 homes. Match trade scheduling and materials procurement to realistic closing dates to avoid unnecessary inventory or customer delays.
items: Prioritize construction resources for homes nearing committed closings
Resolve trade and material bottlenecks at the community level
Monitor construction cycle time and completed unsold inventory

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Protect contribution as delivered prices decline
cards.text: Average delivered home price fell to $391,000 from $423,000. Assess community mix and commercial decisions before assuming more volume will offset lower revenue per home.
items: Review community pricing and incentives against home contribution
Adjust product and build spending to local buyer demand
Monitor net selling price and cost per delivered home

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make margin discipline govern growth commitments
cards.text: Gross margin on home sales was 17.7%, with a 9.3% net margin. Use those economics to test new starts and land commitments against demand and funding needs.
items: Set new start decisions using expected home contribution
Prioritize land and construction spending within available cash capacity
Monitor home gross margin and net margin alongside unit growth

headline: Lennox should clear transition inventory while preserving commercial climate growth.
summary: Home Comfort Solutions declined, while Building Climate Solutions improved revenue and profit. Pricing and mix supported segment earnings against weaker volume, but excess refrigerant-transition inventory and channel destocking weighed on cash. The priority is demand-aligned production and inventory reduction with disciplined pricing.
focusTitle: Reconnect production, channel inventory and cash generation.
focusText: Use current channel demand to guide Home Comfort output while protecting service and product availability. Sustain the healthier Building Climate contribution, and compare annual results consistently with the FIFO accounting basis rather than confusing the accounting change with the underlying inventory correction.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Adjust Home Comfort execution to weaker demand
cards.text: Home Comfort Solutions revenue declined 7% to $3.3 billion and segment profit fell 4%. Align production and commercial support with actual channel needs during the demand adjustment.
items: Coordinate Home Comfort production with distributor replenishment needs
Target commercial support to products with credible end demand
Monitor channel inventory and segment contribution alongside shipments

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Building Climate's stronger contribution
cards.text: Building Climate Solutions revenue increased 5% to $1.9 billion and segment profit grew 8%. Support delivery and customer relationships where growth is producing better earnings conversion.
items: Allocate delivery resources to confirmed Building Climate requirements
Prioritize product and service work supporting repeat customer demand
Monitor segment profit conversion and delivery performance

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep pricing support compatible with volume recovery
cards.text: Segment profit included $356 million of mix/price benefits against a $255 million volume-related decrease. Protect contribution while testing whether pricing and assortment support sustainable demand.
items: Review product pricing against customer and channel response
Prioritize favorable mix without creating excess slow-moving stock
Monitor price/mix benefits and volume contribution separately

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Release cash from transition inventory
cards.text: Operating cash flow fell to $757 million from $946 million; management cited excess refrigerant-transition inventory and channel destocking. Inventory actions should address specific products and channel positions.
items: Map transition inventory to expected channel replenishment demand
Reduce production commitments for products with excess stock
Monitor inventory aging and cash released without disrupting availability

headline: Lilly should make fast-growing medicine demand operationally sustainable.
summary: Mounjaro and Zepbound expanded rapidly, while Verzenio added growth and manufacturing capacity increased. The priority is dependable supply and disciplined international execution, so product momentum translates into sustained access and commercial contribution without concentrating every resource on the fastest-growing medicines.
focusTitle: Coordinate capacity and market expansion around product demand.
focusText: Allocate manufacturing, distribution and launch support according to each medicine's operating requirements and observed demand. Preserve the broader portfolio while expanding internationally, judging success through reliable supply, appropriate customer access and product contribution rather than revenue growth alone.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Support Mounjaro scale with reliable supply
cards.text: Mounjaro sales increased 99% to $22.965 billion. That larger commercial base makes manufacturing availability and distribution execution important to sustaining product demand.
items: Align manufacturing allocation with demonstrated market demand
Coordinate distribution planning with available finished product supply
Monitor product availability and recurring demand across established markets

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make Zepbound growth repeatable
cards.text: Zepbound sales increased 175% to $13.542 billion. Preserve commercial execution while ensuring operational resources keep pace with rapid expansion rather than relying on the growth rate alone.
items: Prioritize supply and support for established Zepbound demand
Address access and fulfillment friction affecting product availability
Monitor sustained demand and product contribution as volume expands

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Maintain investment in the broader portfolio
cards.text: Verzenio sales rose 8% to $5.723 billion. Protect commercially useful support and operating resources so the focus on faster-growing products does not weaken other established contributions.
items: Retain commercial resources supporting appropriate Verzenio adoption
Prioritize operational improvements that preserve dependable product supply
Monitor Verzenio demand and contribution alongside portfolio resource allocation

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Coordinate capacity additions with international launches

headline: Linde should turn its project backlog into profitable volume and cash growth.
summary: Underlying sales growth came from pricing with stable volumes, while adjusted operating margin improved and operating cash supported substantial capital expenditure. The priority is disciplined project execution that adds durable customer activity without weakening existing operating economics or funding flexibility.
focusTitle: Use project returns to guide capacity investment.
focusText: Protect price realization and plant reliability in the existing business while allocating capital to ready, economically attractive projects. Connect construction progress to customer commitments and cash requirements so the backlog adds productive capacity rather than simply expanding the investment base.

cards.title: Build volume without sacrificing price realization

Maintain pricing discipline where operating costs require support
Monitor underlying volume and price contributions separately
