Prioritize capacity supporting dependable contracts with clear customer obligations.
Monitor deployment delays and contract concentration before accelerating construction.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve cloud growth through dependable service delivery
cards.text: FY2026 cloud revenue increased 39% to $34.0 billion. Growth must be supported by reliable infrastructure and application retention to sustain attractive customer economics.
items: Allocate operating capacity to customer workloads with clear service requirements.
Coordinate infrastructure scaling with application onboarding and support readiness.
Monitor utilization, renewals and customer contribution as cloud capacity expands.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Manage software migration without losing customer value
cards.text: FY2026 software revenue declined 1% to $24.5 billion. Migration can change revenue mix, but lost relationships would require a different commercial response.
items: Provide migration paths that preserve existing customer functionality and economics.
Direct account support toward renewals at risk during product transitions.
Monitor retained customer value separately from the shift into cloud revenue.

headline: Otis should scale service and modernization while containing new-equipment weakness.
summary: Service growth and better service margin provide a durable counterweight to declining new-equipment sales, particularly in China. Modernization offers another route to growth within the installed base. The priority is deploying technicians and commercial resources around recurring relationships while keeping equipment bids and capacity disciplined.
focusTitle: Prioritize installed-base returns and disciplined equipment exposure.
focusText: Expand maintenance retention and modernization conversion where technician capacity can deliver quality service. Keep new-equipment commitments aligned with regional demand and acceptable pricing, preserving the recurring service economics rather than using aggressive construction-market bids to replace lost sales.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Reset equipment exposure to construction demand
cards.text: New Equipment organic sales fell 7%, with China down more than 20%. Regional weakness should guide bidding and operating capacity rather than broad volume replacement.
items: Concentrate equipment bids on projects with acceptable pricing and payment terms.
Align regional installation resources with firm orders and construction progress.
Monitor China order quality and cancellations before adding delivery capacity.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen the recurring maintenance relationship
cards.text: Service organic sales increased 5%, including 4% maintenance and repair growth. The installed base provides repeat demand when contracts are retained and service remains reliable.
items: Prioritize maintenance renewals and repair responsiveness within existing customer relationships.
Align technician coverage with installed equipment density and service requirements.
Monitor contract retention and pricing alongside equipment uptime and response times.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Convert modernization demand without overloading technicians
cards.text: Organic modernization sales increased 9%. Upgrades can deepen installed-base value, but execution capacity must support project delivery and ongoing maintenance obligations.
items: Coordinate modernization installations with maintenance staffing and customer access windows.
Target aging installed equipment where upgrade value supports customer decisions.
Monitor order conversion, project contribution and technician workload as demand expands.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep service margin gains compatible with quality
cards.text: Annual Service operating margin rose 50 basis points to 25.1%. Sustaining the gain depends on productivity keeping pace with labor costs without weakening service.
items: Expand scheduling and routing improvements that reduce unproductive technician time.
Use contract pricing to reflect service intensity and labor requirements.
Monitor service margins together with callbacks, retention and labor inflation.

headline: PACCAR should restore Parts profitability while aligning truck production with demand.
summary: Parts revenue grew but pretax income declined, so aftermarket expansion did not translate into better segment earnings. Financial Services provided stronger profits and truck deliveries sustain the installed-base opportunity. The priority is improving parts contribution while keeping vehicle production and financing exposure aligned with customer economics.
focusTitle: Improve lifetime truck economics across sales, parts and finance.
focusText: Use the installed fleet to deepen profitable aftermarket service rather than maximizing parts revenue alone. Coordinate factory plans with regional orders, and preserve financing discipline so earnings diversification does not create avoidable credit or used-truck value exposure.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make Parts growth produce more profit
cards.text: Parts pretax income declined to $1.67 billion from $1.71 billion despite revenue growth. Product mix, pricing and distribution costs deserve a focused operating response.
items: Identify parts categories where contribution failed to keep pace with sales.
Improve distribution costs and availability without relying on broad price increases.
Monitor category contribution after fulfillment costs as aftermarket volumes change.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build on the installed-base parts opportunity
cards.text: Annual Parts revenue increased 3% to $6.87 billion. Aftermarket demand diversifies revenue beyond new vehicles when product availability and dealer execution support recurring purchases.
items: Prioritize availability for parts that support customer vehicle uptime.
Coordinate dealers and distribution centers around recurring fleet service needs.
Monitor customer retention and distribution productivity alongside parts revenue growth.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Align truck output with regional order quality
cards.text: PACCAR delivered 144,200 vehicles worldwide. Delivery volume matters for factory utilization and future parts demand, while production decisions require current regional order signals.
items: Sequence factory production against firm orders and customer delivery readiness.
Balance model and regional mix with available manufacturing capacity.
Monitor cancellations and dealer inventory before expanding vehicle production schedules.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve financing profit through credit discipline
cards.text: Financial Services pretax profit increased 11% to $485.4 million. Financing diversifies earnings but links returns to borrower payments and used-truck values.
items: Price new financing around borrower quality and residual-value assumptions.
Coordinate customer support and collections when fleet cash conditions weaken.
Monitor delinquencies and used-truck values before loosening underwriting standards.

headline: Packaging Corporation should convert restructuring costs into stronger mill and packaging returns.
summary: Packaging and Paper operating income held broadly steady, while EBITDA excluding special items improved more strongly. Larger special-item expenses make the business priority execution rather than merely presenting adjusted growth: integration and restructuring should produce recurring efficiency without disrupting product availability or customer service.
focusTitle: Tie portfolio changes to repeatable operating improvements.
focusText: Prioritize mill utilization, customer contribution and cash benefits when allocating restructuring resources. Preserve the stable earnings base, while judging acquisition and efficiency initiatives by the operating results they deliver after implementation costs rather than adjusted EBITDA growth alone.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Demand operating benefits from larger special charges
cards.text: Diluted EPS included $1.26 of special-item expenses versus $0.11 previously. Restructuring and acquisition actions need measurable business benefits to justify that burden.
items: Assign integration initiatives specific capacity, service or recurring cost outcomes.
Sequence restructuring to protect customer supply and critical mill maintenance.
Monitor cash charges against realized efficiency benefits before extending initiatives.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect packaging contribution through mill discipline
cards.text: Packaging operating income was $1.125 billion versus $1.102 billion. The core business held up, with volume, pricing and mill utilization requiring separate operating choices.
items: Align mill production with packaging orders and inventory requirements.
Prioritize customer contracts by contribution after converting and delivery costs.
Monitor mill utilization and realized pricing as order mix changes.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Preserve Paper earnings without unnecessary expansion
cards.text: Paper operating income was $129.6 million versus $129.7 million. Stable earnings provide support, while capital choices should reflect product demand and mill economics.
items: Sequence paper output around confirmed demand and available mill capacity.
Prioritize reliability projects that protect contribution from existing production.
Monitor paper pricing and unit costs before committing incremental capacity.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make adjusted profit gains visible in cash returns
cards.text: Non-GAAP EBITDA excluding special items increased to $1.862 billion from $1.637 billion. The improvement should translate into resources after integration and restructuring spending.
items: Use recurring operating contribution to prioritize reinvestment across mills.
Link integration milestones to cash benefits available for capital allocation.
Monitor cash conversion after excluded costs and necessary capital spending.

headline: Palantir should turn rapid contract growth into durable customer usage and delivery.
summary: U.S. commercial and government revenue both expanded rapidly, supported by a much larger contract value pipeline. Strong adjusted cash generation gives room to invest. The priority is disciplined scaling: customer adoption, funded government delivery and contract conversion must remain credible as the business grows beyond signed deal headlines.
focusTitle: Scale implementation around repeatable customer value.
focusText: Direct delivery and product resources toward sustained production use, rather than contract signing alone. Preserve cash productivity as customer complexity expands, and size hiring around executable commercial deployments and funded government work with clear renewal and delivery economics.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make commercial adoption repeatable after the initial win
cards.text: U.S. commercial revenue increased 109% to $1.47 billion. Rapid expansion creates opportunity, but durable economics require customers to keep using and expanding deployed applications.
items: Prioritize implementation support for use cases approaching production deployment.
Reuse successful deployment methods to reduce incremental customer delivery effort.
Monitor retained usage and expansion within existing commercial customer cohorts.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect government delivery and renewal economics
cards.text: U.S. government revenue grew 55% to $1.85 billion. Government remains substantial, making funding, contract renewals and reliable delivery important alongside commercial expansion.
items: Align delivery staffing with funded government milestones and acceptance requirements.
Build renewal plans around demonstrated operational value for existing agencies.
Monitor award concentration and funding changes before adding program commitments.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Convert contract value into achievable implementation schedules
cards.text: Annual total contract value reached $10.8 billion, up 128%. That supports demand visibility but differs from recognized revenue and can include varied contract terms.
items: Sequence customer onboarding around contract duration and delivery obligations.
Distinguish committed deployments from options when planning operating capacity.
Monitor contract conversion and cancellations against the resources assigned.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use cash strength to fund productive scaling
cards.text: Non-GAAP adjusted free cash flow was $2.27 billion at a 51% margin. Cash supports growth, while excluded items matter when evaluating its economic cost.
items: Allocate growth spending toward deployments with repeatable implementation economics.
Balance employee incentives with dilution and long-term customer delivery needs.
Monitor cash generation after adjustments alongside the cost of acquiring customers.

headline: Palo Alto Networks should deepen platform adoption while protecting recurring service profitability.
summary: Next-Generation Security ARR, contracted obligations and subscription revenue all expanded, while GAAP operating income improved substantially. The priority is maintaining that combination as customers adopt more of the platform. Contract growth should become successful deployments and renewals without allowing support or acquisition spending to erode operating progress.
focusTitle: Make recurring security growth operationally durable.
focusText: Coordinate sales, implementation and support around customer adoption rather than contract value alone. Prioritize renewals and platform utilization, and use recurring contribution and service quality to determine where additional selling or delivery resources can earn an attractive return.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn platform contracts into embedded customer use
cards.text: Next-Generation Security ARR reached $5.6 billion, up 32%. Annualized contract value indicates scale, while sustained adoption determines whether renewals can preserve it.
items: Prioritize onboarding that activates purchased security capabilities across customer environments.
Align account plans with adoption gaps and credible expansion needs.
Monitor renewals and product utilization separately from annualized contract additions.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep contracted delivery aligned with operating capacity
cards.text: Remaining performance obligations rose 24% to $15.8 billion. Contracted work supports visibility, but recognition timing and delivery requirements affect staffing and revenue conversion.
items: Sequence implementation resources around contractual deployment and service dates.
Prioritize delivery bottlenecks that could delay customer adoption or acceptance.
Monitor obligation conversion by contract duration before accelerating hiring.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect recurring revenue through dependable support
cards.text: Subscription and support revenue increased to $7.420 billion from $6.424 billion. The recurring base depends on customer security outcomes and sustainable service costs.
items: Improve support workflows for recurring customer issues and complex deployments.
Allocate technical resources to accounts with adoption or renewal obstacles.
Monitor retention and support cost per customer as the base expands.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve operating leverage as investment grows
cards.text: GAAP operating income increased to $1.243 billion from $683.9 million. That operating progress provides a clearer business signal than tax-driven net income movements.
items: Direct incremental spending toward products and sales motions with demonstrated contribution.
Keep delivery investment sufficient to support the expanding subscription base.
Monitor recurring revenue growth against operating expense and service performance.

headline: Parker Hannifin should pair stronger margins with broader organic demand and aerospace delivery.
summary: Profitability and cash generation improved faster than modest organic sales growth, showing useful operating discipline. Aerospace backlog supports future work, but converting it requires delivery execution. The priority is preserving efficiency while directing commercial and capacity resources toward genuine demand across aerospace and industrial markets.
focusTitle: Use cash gains to support profitable organic growth.
focusText: Preserve the practices behind margin improvement and invest selectively in customer-facing engineering and delivery constraints. Balance aerospace backlog execution with industrial demand development, using order conversion and returns to guide capacity rather than treating record profitability as proof of broad volume strength.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Broaden growth beyond efficiency gains
cards.text: Organic sales increased only 1%. That limits the evidence of broad demand strength, even though profitability improved and aerospace provides a visible pipeline.
items: Prioritize industrial accounts where application support can convert identified orders.
Compare aerospace and industrial demand before allocating incremental commercial resources.
Monitor organic order breadth and conversion across product lines.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect margin gains while supporting customer development
cards.text: Segment operating margin increased 150 basis points to 23.0%. Price, mix and productivity can preserve profitability, but should not displace necessary engineering and sales support.
items: Extend proven productivity practices across operations with comparable manufacturing requirements.
Keep pricing aligned with product value and customer retention economics.
Monitor segment margins alongside organic volumes and customer service outcomes.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Convert aerospace backlog without creating delivery bottlenecks
cards.text: Aerospace backlog reached $7.4 billion. That supports visibility, while supplier readiness and delivery schedules determine how much value can be realized.
items: Prioritize supplier constraints affecting contracted aerospace delivery milestones.
Align skilled labor and capacity additions with executable customer schedules.
Monitor backlog conversion, delivery reliability and program contribution together.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deploy cash where it removes profitable growth constraints
cards.text: Operating cash increased 12% to $3.8 billion, or 19.0% of sales. Strong conversion offers flexibility after working capital and essential capital needs.
items: Rank capacity and engineering projects by demand visibility and expected returns.
Preserve maintenance investment required for dependable aerospace and industrial delivery.
Monitor cash conversion after working-capital changes and growth capital spending.

headline: Paychex should integrate Paycor while protecting client economics and funding flexibility.
summary: Management Solutions expanded sharply on an acquisition-influenced base, while PEO and Insurance Solutions also grew. GAAP and adjusted margins moved differently, and borrowings create additional cash obligations. The priority is turning acquisition scale into retained customers and recurring operating benefits while funding integration and debt responsibly.
focusTitle: Make acquired scale produce durable client and cash returns.
focusText: Coordinate Paycor integration around customer continuity, product adoption and realizable operating efficiencies. Preserve the existing payroll and worksite employee franchise, and set distribution capacity after debt service and integration needs rather than interpreting adjusted margin expansion as cash already available.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Separate acquisition scale from existing-client progress
cards.text: FY2026 Management Solutions revenue increased 20% to $4.868 billion, with Paycor changing comparability. Client retention and adoption determine the quality of the enlarged base.
items: Protect customer service continuity as acquired platforms and workflows integrate.
Offer complementary capabilities where existing clients have a demonstrated payroll need.
Monitor retained customers and organic expansion separately from acquired revenue.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require integration to improve recurring economics
cards.text: GAAP operating margin fell to 38.6% from 39.6%, while adjusted margin rose to 43.2%. Integration cash costs and recurring benefits matter to resource decisions.
items: Sequence platform changes to avoid payroll delivery and support disruption.
Assign integration initiatives measurable operating benefits after implementation costs.
Monitor recurring expense efficiency and customer service through the transition.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Grow PEO relationships without diluting insurance economics
cards.text: PEO and Insurance Solutions revenue increased 7% to $1.433 billion. Worksite employee activity supports demand, while retention and insurance costs determine the resulting contribution.
items: Prioritize service quality and renewal support for existing PEO clients.
Align insurance offerings and pricing with client needs and underlying costs.
Monitor worksite employee activity and retained contribution alongside revenue growth.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Preserve cash for debt and integration obligations
cards.text: Year-end borrowings were $4.6 billion and annual operating cash was $2.6 billion. Cash must cover several demands beyond shareholder distributions.
items: Budget integration investment and debt service before discretionary capital returns.
Stage optional spending around cash generated by retained customer relationships.
Monitor liquidity after financing costs, integration payments and distributions.

headline: PayPal should improve branded checkout engagement and transaction contribution, not just volume.
summary: Payment volume grew, and transaction margin dollars excluding customer interest improved, supporting core economics. Aggregate transaction declines conceal a different trend outside unbranded processing, while active account growth remained modest. The priority is profitable engagement and merchant value rather than maximizing volume with weak monetization.
focusTitle: Allocate investment around retained transaction contribution.
focusText: Prioritize branded checkout usage and merchant experiences that increase repeat activity at sustainable economics. Evaluate processing growth separately, and use contribution after losses and servicing costs to guide incentives, product spending and merchant pricing across the payment mix.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make payment volume produce adequate merchant economics
cards.text: Total payment volume increased 7% to $1.79 trillion, or 6% currency neutral. Volume outpaced revenue, making mix and merchant pricing important to returns.
items: Price merchant relationships using contribution after processing and servicing costs.
Prioritize acceptance improvements that increase profitable checkout completion.
Monitor revenue yield and contribution by branded and unbranded payment mix.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Judge engagement within the changing transaction mix
cards.text: Transactions fell 4% to 25.4 billion, but grew 6% excluding unbranded processing. Aggregate declines should not drive the same response across both businesses.
items: Separate branded checkout adoption from processing volume in product planning.
Improve payment experiences where retained users encounter checkout friction.
Monitor transaction frequency and contribution within each payment business.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Deepen activity within the existing account base
cards.text: Active accounts increased 1.1% to 439 million. Slow account expansion makes retained usage and economically justified reactivation important alongside acquiring additional users.
items: Focus engagement offers on existing users with repeat purchase opportunities.
Remove onboarding and checkout obstacles that prevent useful account activity.
Monitor active-user frequency and retention after promotional incentives end.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the improvement in underlying transaction earnings
cards.text: Non-GAAP transaction margin dollars excluding customer interest increased 6% to $14.2 billion. That supports operating progress beyond the benefit of customer interest income.
items: Expand payment products that improve contribution after credit and fraud losses.
Align merchant support spending with transaction value and service requirements.
Monitor transaction margin growth alongside loss rates and processing costs.

headline: Pentair should repair Water Solutions demand while preserving Pool-led profitability.
summary: Pool delivered the clearest growth, while Flow improved profitability on modest sales expansion. Water Solutions declined, showing that demand is uneven across the portfolio. Strong continuing-operations cash generation provides room to respond, provided investment targets specific customer opportunities rather than broad expansion across every segment.
focusTitle: Use cash strength to fund targeted portfolio improvement.
focusText: Protect Pool channel health and extend Flow productivity without starving customer support. Direct incremental commercial effort toward the weak Water Solutions applications, and require capacity and inventory decisions to follow end demand so reported growth becomes sustainable contribution.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Focus the Water Solutions response on weak applications
cards.text: Water Solutions core sales declined 3%. A targeted channel and application response is more useful than applying the stronger Pool demand pattern to the whole portfolio.
items: Identify customer applications and channels responsible for the sales decline.
Redirect sales and product support toward recoverable demand opportunities.
Monitor order conversion and customer retention in the affected businesses.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect Pool growth from channel inventory distortions
cards.text: Pool core sales increased 7% with a 33.8% segment return on sales. Strong segment performance should be sustained through healthy distributor and end-customer demand.
items: Coordinate distributor replenishment with observed sales and seasonal customer needs.
Preserve availability for products supporting attractive Pool contribution.
Monitor channel inventory and sell-through before increasing production commitments.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Extend Flow productivity while rebuilding demand
cards.text: Flow core sales grew 1%, while segment return on sales increased to 23.3%. Profitability improved faster than demand, making repeatable operating benefits valuable.
items: Apply transformation savings to repeatable operating costs across Flow businesses.
Keep customer-facing resources focused on qualified equipment and service opportunities.
Monitor pricing and mix alongside organic order growth and margins.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deploy cash toward the clearest portfolio returns
cards.text: Continuing operations generated $815 million of operating cash and $748 million of non-GAAP free cash flow. Cash supports growth and returns after essential requirements.
items: Prioritize investment that improves customer conversion or removes profitable capacity constraints.
Keep inventory and maintenance spending aligned with segment demand.
Monitor cash conversion after working-capital movements and necessary capital investment.

headline: PepsiCo should rebuild North American volume through better affordability and product value.
summary: North American foods and beverages both lost volume, while EMEA delivered stronger organic revenue growth. Flat core constant-currency EPS despite positive organic revenue suggests growth is not yet producing better underlying earnings. The priority is restoring consumer demand while making productivity savings support economically effective product and pricing choices.
focusTitle: Rebalance value, product mix and cost productivity.
focusText: Test targeted pack, pricing and promotional changes against volume and contribution in North America. Preserve productive regional growth, but distinguish pricing from demand, and allocate savings to offers that improve repeat purchasing rather than assuming revenue growth alone confirms consumer recovery.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Rebuild the value proposition in North American foods
cards.text: PepsiCo Foods North America volume declined 2% excluding acquisitions and divestitures. Affordability and product demand need attention before additional pricing can support durable growth.
items: Test pack sizes and price points against consumer purchase conversion.
Prioritize products and channels where targeted promotions improve repeat demand.
Monitor volume and contribution after promotions rather than revenue alone.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve beverage demand by channel and occasion
cards.text: PepsiCo Beverages North America volume declined 3%. Portfolio and channel choices should reflect where customers see value rather than relying on headline revenue comparisons.
items: Adjust beverage assortment and pack mix to channel-specific purchase needs.
Compare promotional offers using incremental volume and retained contribution.
Monitor repeat purchase and distribution performance across the weaker channels.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve EMEA growth with demand discipline
cards.text: EMEA non-GAAP organic revenue increased 6%. Stronger regional revenue can support the portfolio, although local pricing and unit demand should guide investment decisions.
items: Prioritize regional products with sustained local customer acceptance.
Apply successful route and assortment practices where market conditions are comparable.
Monitor unit trends and contribution separately from local pricing effects.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make productivity fund profitable demand recovery
cards.text: Organic revenue increased 1.7% while core constant-currency EPS was flat. Underlying sales growth did not translate into better earnings, increasing the need for effective reinvestment.
items: Direct savings toward product and affordability initiatives with measurable customer response.
Protect operating improvements that offset input costs without reducing product quality.
Monitor contribution gains after marketing, promotions and productivity investment.

headline: Pfizer should convert non-COVID growth and R&D into a more durable medicine portfolio.
summary: Operational growth outside COVID products indicates underlying demand, while Eliquis remains a significant revenue source. Manufacturing savings create reinvestment room, but research spending still needs clinical and commercial conversion. The priority is broadening durable product contribution while protecting supply quality and disciplined development decisions.
focusTitle: Use savings and R&D to strengthen future product contribution.
focusText: Prioritize programs and launches with credible clinical value and commercial adoption. Manage major-product concentration through portfolio development, while preserving manufacturing quality so cost savings support new medicines rather than jeopardizing the existing earnings and supply base.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn non-COVID growth into repeatable product demand
cards.text: Revenue excluding COVID products increased 6% operationally. That signals underlying product progress, while new uptake and maturing products should guide commercial resource allocation.
items: Prioritize launch support where prescribing adoption and patient access are progressing.
Allocate sales resources across products using sustained demand and contribution.
Monitor product growth separately from currency and COVID-related changes.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Reduce dependence on a major medicine over time
cards.text: Eliquis revenue was $7.961 billion, or 13% of total revenue. Its portfolio weight makes partnership economics and exclusivity exposure relevant to future investment choices.
items: Plan portfolio reinvestment around the contribution at risk from major products.
Preserve appropriate commercial support while preparing alternative sources of growth.
Monitor product concentration and partnership economics alongside exclusivity developments.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make research spending clear clinical and commercial choices
cards.text: Internal R&D investment was $10.4 billion. The business return depends on selecting programs that progress through clinical development and ultimately achieve useful patient adoption.
items: Prioritize development resources using trial evidence and differentiation from available treatments.
Coordinate launch readiness with pivotal milestones and patient access requirements.
Monitor clinical progression and launch uptake before expanding program commitments.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve supply quality while extending manufacturing savings
cards.text: Manufacturing optimization delivered approximately $600 million in net savings by year end. Benefits should remain recurring without weakening quality or medicine availability.
items: Extend process improvements that remove waste while preserving validated manufacturing standards.
Reinvest selectively where capacity or reliability constrains important products.
Monitor supply service levels and quality alongside realized recurring savings.

headline: PG&E should make safety investment deliver durable reliability and affordable new connections.
summary: Undergrounding and other infrastructure work coincided with management-reported reliability improvement, while non-fuel O&M declined. New electric customers and charging ports add demand. The priority is preserving those service gains while targeting construction and operating resources where risk reduction and connection needs justify the cost.
focusTitle: Allocate network investment around risk, service and customer cost.
focusText: Prioritize projects that reduce high-risk exposure or remove real connection bottlenecks. Preserve maintenance while extending sustainable cost improvements, and assess completed infrastructure through measured operating outcomes so construction volume alone does not define the value of the program.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Direct hardening spending toward measurable risk reduction
cards.text: PG&E undergrounded 334 miles and strengthened or covered another 207 miles in high-risk areas. Different interventions should be judged on risk reduction and construction economics.
items: Prioritize routes using exposure reduction and feasible construction alternatives.
Apply project lessons to procurement and cost control across remaining work.
Monitor risk outcomes and construction cost per mile by intervention type.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the reported reliability improvement through operations
cards.text: Management reported 19% improvement in systemwide electric reliability versus 2024. Service outcomes help judge infrastructure value when supported by dependable maintenance and outage response.
items: Identify operating practices and assets associated with fewer customer interruptions.
Protect maintenance and response capability in areas with persistent reliability gaps.
Monitor outage frequency and duration alongside completed network investment.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Extend cost savings without weakening network upkeep
cards.text: Non-fuel O&M declined 2.5%. Lower operating cost can support affordability, provided reductions reflect efficiency rather than deferred maintenance or reduced service capability.
items: Scale work planning practices that reduce repeat visits and avoidable rework.
Retain maintenance resources required for safe and reliable network operation.
Monitor recurring savings together with equipment condition and service outcomes.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Connect new load without creating capacity bottlenecks
cards.text: PG&E connected over 12,730 electric customers and 18,750 EV charging ports. Connections expand service needs and can require localized infrastructure capacity.
items: Coordinate customer connection schedules with feeder and substation capacity planning.
Prioritize upgrades where confirmed demand would otherwise delay new service.
Monitor connection times and local utilization as charging demand develops.

headline: Philip Morris should sustain smoke-free adoption while controlling channel and regulatory exposure.
summary: Smoke-free products are taking a larger revenue share, with oral products growing especially quickly. That gives the portfolio a clear direction, but shipment growth alone cannot establish lasting consumer demand. The priority is disciplined capacity and distribution expansion supported by in-market sales, retention and product-level economics.
focusTitle: Build smoke-free scale around retained demand.
focusText: Allocate commercial and supply resources where repeat purchasing supports continued growth. Preserve category profitability as the mix changes, and manage regulatory and competitive exposure through product and market decisions rather than assuming faster shipments always justify additional capacity.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make the revenue mix shift economically durable
cards.text: Smoke-free products generated 41.5% of net revenue, up 2.8 percentage points. The transition is progressing, making category contribution and regulatory resilience increasingly important.
items: Prioritize smoke-free investments using category contribution and market access conditions.
Align product availability with regulatory requirements in each served market.
Monitor category margins as smoke-free products become a larger revenue share.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Validate shipment growth against consumer sell-through
cards.text: Smoke-free shipment volume increased 12.8%. Growth supports scale, but inventory movements can differ from ongoing consumer demand and should guide replenishment decisions.
items: Coordinate production with distributor inventory and observed in-market purchases.
Improve product availability where recurring demand exceeds dependable supply.
Monitor sell-through and repeat purchasing before increasing channel inventories.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale oral products without weakening unit economics
cards.text: Oral smoke-free shipment volume increased 18.5%, faster than the broader smoke-free portfolio. Capacity and pricing decisions should preserve the economics behind that expansion.
items: Prioritize supply investment where sustained oral demand supports additional capacity.
Test competitive offers against contribution and retained product demand.
Monitor pricing and capacity utilization as oral product shipments expand.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep ZYN distribution aligned with repeat demand
cards.text: Full-year ZYN shipments reached 794 million cans. The sizable operating base increases the value of reliable availability and disciplined inventory across distribution channels.
items: Allocate ZYN supply to channels showing sustained consumer sell-through.
Coordinate distribution expansion with service capability and compliant market access.
Monitor retention and distributor inventory before widening shipment commitments.

headline: Phillips 66 should turn expanded NGL infrastructure into comparable cash returns.
summary: NGL transportation and fractionation reached company records, while acquisitions and dispositions changed the portfolio. Operating cash was lower than the figure excluding working capital, showing a separate cash constraint. The priority is proving that the enlarged asset base earns attractive returns and converts throughput into cash after funding needs.
focusTitle: Evaluate volume growth through utilization and cash contribution.
focusText: Allocate infrastructure spending around contracted demand and integration readiness. Judge acquired assets against the earnings and cash relinquished through dispositions, and preserve working-capital discipline so stronger NGL activity produces resources available for debt reduction and productive reinvestment.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make transportation growth profitable on a comparable basis
cards.text: Annual NGL transportation volumes increased 22% to a company record. Acquisition contribution should be separated from organic flows when deciding where capacity needs expansion.
items: Align transportation capacity with contracted producer and downstream requirements.
Prioritize bottleneck projects using incremental contribution and existing asset utilization.
Monitor comparable throughput and asset contribution after acquisition effects.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Coordinate fractionation growth with dependable feed and demand
cards.text: NGL fractionation volumes rose 23% to a company record. Processing returns depend on sustained supply, customer commitments and effective utilization rather than volume alone.
items: Coordinate fractionation schedules with transportation flows and customer delivery commitments.
Preserve maintenance capability required to sustain dependable processing availability.
Monitor utilization and fractionation economics before committing further capacity.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require portfolio changes to improve underlying returns
cards.text: Asset acquisitions and dispositions each totaled $3.5 billion. Equal transaction totals do not demonstrate equivalent cash generation or a stronger continuing asset portfolio.
items: Integrate acquired operations around identifiable cash and operating benefits.
Compare acquired contribution with earnings and obligations removed through dispositions.
Monitor realized asset returns before using transaction proceeds for further expansion.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Release cash tied up in working capital
cards.text: Operating cash was $5.0 billion versus $6.1 billion excluding working capital on a non-GAAP basis. Inventory and receivable requirements absorbed funding capacity.
items: Align inventory holdings with operational reliability and committed product flows.
Tighten receivable collection practices where terms create avoidable cash delays.
Monitor cash available after working capital for debt reduction and investment.

headline: Pinnacle West should meet faster Arizona load growth with affordable, reliable capacity.
summary: Customer growth and weather-normalized electricity demand indicate underlying expansion beyond temperature effects. Faster peak demand creates a capacity challenge, while customer assistance highlights affordability needs. The priority is sequencing grid and supply investment around credible load commitments without letting rising service requirements create excessive bill pressure.
focusTitle: Match new load with dependable capacity and recovery.
focusText: Coordinate customer connections, generation availability and network investment using realistic demand scenarios. Prioritize reliable service at reasonable cost, and pair rate recovery planning with effective affordability support so customer growth produces sustainable utility economics rather than unmanaged infrastructure obligations.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Plan infrastructure around sustained underlying load
cards.text: Weather-normalized retail electricity sales increased 5.0%. That suggests demand growth beyond weather, while large-customer concentration and tariff recovery still determine the investment economics.
items: Validate major load additions against customer commitments and operating schedules.
Align network investment with the locations and timing of confirmed demand.
Monitor load concentration and cost recovery as new consumption develops.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect reliability as peak requirements rise
cards.text: Peak electricity demand increased more than 5%. Capacity must cover the demanding operating periods, which may require different resources than annual energy growth alone.
items: Coordinate generation maintenance with expected peak periods and reserve requirements.
Prioritize capacity and demand-management options that address specific peak constraints.
Monitor reserve margins and generation availability under stressed demand conditions.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make customer connections operationally manageable
cards.text: APS customer count increased 2.4%. Expanding service requires connection capacity and network readiness as well as adding accounts to the customer base.
items: Coordinate connection work with local feeder and substation investment plans.
Allocate field resources to areas with confirmed customer growth.
Monitor connection delays and infrastructure delivery as the customer base expands.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Preserve affordability alongside investment recovery
cards.text: APS connected customers to approximately $70 million in annual support. Assistance helps address affordability, but rising infrastructure needs make reach and payment outcomes important.
items: Improve assistance access for eligible customers experiencing payment difficulties.
Consider bill effects when sequencing infrastructure recovery and customer programs.
Monitor assistance participation and arrears alongside required investment spending.

headline: PNC should preserve broad earnings gains through disciplined funding and credit decisions.
summary: Net interest income and noninterest income both increased, while charge-offs declined and efficiency improved. The evidence supports a positive operating assessment. The priority is sustaining that combination through rate changes, credit conditions and continued investment, rather than treating favorable losses and operating leverage as permanent.
focusTitle: Reinvest in profitable relationships while preserving credit resilience.
focusText: Use better efficiency to support customer capabilities and diversified recurring fees. Price lending and deposits under changing rate conditions, and retain underwriting discipline so improved current losses do not encourage growth that weakens future risk-adjusted returns.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect interest earnings across rate scenarios
cards.text: Net interest income rose to $14.410 billion from $13.499 billion. Sustaining that contribution requires funding costs and asset yields to remain aligned as rates change.
items: Price deposit retention using relationship value and alternative funding costs.
Allocate loan growth toward relationships with attractive risk-adjusted spreads.
Monitor deposit costs and asset repricing under alternative rate paths.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen recurring fee relationships
cards.text: Noninterest income increased to $8.689 billion from $8.056 billion. Fees diversify the earnings base when growth reflects durable customer service rather than volatile investment items.
items: Expand relevant transaction and advisory services within existing client relationships.
Allocate sales resources toward products with recurring client demand.
Monitor recurring service fees separately from investment-sensitive income changes.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep better charge-offs from weakening credit standards
cards.text: Net loan charge-offs declined to $744 million from $1.041 billion. Lower realized losses support earnings, while early warning indicators remain important for new lending decisions.
items: Maintain underwriting standards where competitive lending terms become less attractive.
Prioritize borrower review where commercial property or cash conditions weaken.
Monitor delinquencies and credit migration alongside realized charge-offs.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Reinvest operating leverage where customers benefit
cards.text: The efficiency ratio improved to 60% from 63%. Expenses grew more slowly than revenue, creating room for selective investment without abandoning operating discipline.
items: Prioritize technology and service improvements with identifiable customer or productivity benefits.
Remove duplicated operating work before reducing essential relationship support.
Monitor efficiency together with client retention and sustainable revenue growth.

headline: PPG should turn modest continuing-business growth and savings into durable cash returns.
summary: Volume and pricing both supported organic growth, while divestitures masked that progress in reported sales. Structural savings and stronger operating cash add flexibility. The priority is reinforcing attractive continuing end markets and preserving cash conversion without interpreting portfolio shrinkage or working-capital releases as the underlying demand trend.
focusTitle: Allocate capital around continuing product and customer economics.
focusText: Protect price realization where products offer value, and use structural efficiencies to support customer execution in weaker industrial markets. Compare continuing operations on a consistent basis and prioritize reinvestment using sustainable cash after maintenance rather than reported sales alone.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support the volume behind organic growth
cards.text: Organic sales increased 2%, with one point each from volume and price. Modest demand improvement gives a base to strengthen, while end-market differences need targeted choices.
items: Concentrate sales and technical support on end markets showing repeat demand.
Preserve pricing where product performance supports customer value.
Monitor volume retention and contribution after customer price negotiations.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Use portfolio changes to improve continuing returns
cards.text: Divestitures reduced annual net sales by 3%. A smaller reported business can still improve economically, but the remaining portfolio should earn attractive returns on retained capital.
items: Redirect resources from divested activities toward stronger continuing customer opportunities.
Compare continuing-business margins and asset needs on a like-for-like basis.
Monitor the returns achieved from redeployed capital and retained operations.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make structural savings sustainable in operations
cards.text: Structural cost reductions produced $75 million of benefits. Recurring efficiency can help offset weaker industrial demand if implementation does not damage service or product capabilities.
items: Embed successful operating changes into procurement and manufacturing routines.
Protect product quality and technical support when removing duplicated costs.
Monitor recurring benefits after implementation spending and service effects.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve cash strength after temporary releases
cards.text: Operating cash reached $1.9 billion, improving more than $500 million. Working-capital releases and sustaining investment requirements affect how much of that improvement can recur.
items: Keep inventory aligned with continuing product demand and service needs.
Prioritize maintenance and high-return customer projects before discretionary distributions.
Monitor operating cash after working-capital movements and necessary capital spending.

headline: PPL should fund grid investment while preserving affordability and per-share returns.
summary: Completed capital investment and ongoing EPS growth show progress, while O&M savings can support affordability. Future equity requirements make financing part of the operating strategy. The priority is matching project delivery and recovery to funding needs so infrastructure growth produces durable service and shareholder value after dilution.
focusTitle: Coordinate capital delivery, recovery and equity funding.
focusText: Prioritize grid projects with clear reliability benefits and credible recovery mechanisms. Preserve sustainable operating savings to limit bill pressure, and sequence equity funding around actual project needs so capital is available without assuming that larger investment automatically improves per-share economics.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make grid investment earn its funding cost
cards.text: PPL completed $4.4 billion of capital investment. Modernization creates service opportunities while requiring timely recovery and effective project execution to support utility returns.
items: Prioritize projects using reliability benefits and approved recovery arrangements.
Coordinate construction spending with regulatory milestones and financing availability.
Monitor project costs and service improvements as assets enter operation.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Sequence equity with the actual capital program
cards.text: Management projected $3 billion of equity needs for 2026–2029; $1 billion was executed through 2025 forward agreements. Settlement and remaining funding still affect shareholders.
items: Align forward settlement and new issuance with project cash requirements.
Compare financing alternatives using dilution and allowed utility returns.
Monitor per-share earnings capacity after equity funding and investment recovery.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve O&M savings without deferring maintenance
cards.text: Annual run-rate O&M savings reached $170 million relative to 2021. Savings can help offset investment-related bill pressure when they reflect durable productivity improvements.
items: Extend work planning and procurement practices that reduce recurring operating waste.
Protect maintenance tasks required for safe and dependable grid service.
Monitor savings durability alongside asset condition and outage outcomes.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use ongoing earnings to guide reinvestment capacity
cards.text: Non-GAAP ongoing EPS increased to $1.81 from $1.69. Recurring utility contributions should determine how much investment and shareholder distribution the business can support.
items: Allocate reinvestment toward utilities with clear service and recovery opportunities.
Base distribution capacity on recurring earnings and capital funding demands.
Monitor utility contributions and cash support after special-item effects.

headline: Principal should improve asset retention so strong sales become net client growth.
summary: Retirement deposits and investment management gross sales improved, yet total AUM net outflows widened. That makes retention and product fit more urgent than generating additional gross sales alone. Better Specialty Benefits loss performance supports the earnings base while the asset businesses work to convert demand into lasting balances.
focusTitle: Prioritize retained assets and recurring relationship value.
focusText: Identify the strategies and channels losing assets, then coordinate sales, service and product responses around the reasons clients withdraw. Preserve retirement momentum and insurance pricing discipline, using net flows and contribution rather than gross activity to allocate commercial investment.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Address the sources of widening net outflows
cards.text: Total AUM net cash outflow was $8.8 billion versus $5.0 billion. Market appreciation can obscure withdrawals, making retention a central business improvement priority.
items: Identify strategies and distribution channels responsible for recurring redemptions.
Direct relationship and product support toward recoverable client retention issues.
Monitor net flows separately from market-driven changes in asset balances.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make stronger gross sales stick
cards.text: Investment management gross sales increased 16% to $127 billion. New sales provide opportunity, but withdrawals and fee rates determine the resulting retained economics.
items: Align sales incentives with retained assets and sustainable fee contribution.
Improve onboarding for new mandates to strengthen early client engagement.
Monitor redemptions and fee yields within newly acquired customer cohorts.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen the recurring retirement relationship
cards.text: Retirement transfer deposits rose 9% to $35 billion and recurring workplace deposits increased 5%. Recurring contributions can support durable client value when plans and participants stay.
items: Prioritize plan service and participant engagement for existing workplace clients.
Coordinate transfer onboarding with ongoing contribution and retention support.
Monitor plan retention and organic deposits after transfer activity normalizes.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve benefits profitability through pricing discipline
cards.text: Specialty Benefits incurred loss ratio improved to 58.7% from 60.5%. Better claims performance supports returns, while future pricing must still reflect changing claim conditions.
items: Price renewals using current claims experience and appropriate risk selection.
Preserve service quality that supports retention of profitable employer relationships.
Monitor claim trends and premium adequacy before accelerating benefits growth.

headline: Procter & Gamble should turn modest volume gains into durable household demand.
summary: Organic growth reflected both volume and pricing, while reported sales and total volume were unchanged. That supports a measured rather than aggressive growth assessment. Strong operating cash provides reinvestment capacity, and the priority is preserving consumer value and repeat purchasing without relying on price increases to carry expansion.
focusTitle: Invest in demand where value and contribution reinforce each other.
focusText: Prioritize product improvements, availability and pack choices that support household adoption. Use category-level elasticity to guide pricing, and maintain cash discipline so consumer investment and distributions remain supported after working capital and essential capital spending.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build on organic growth category by category
cards.text: Non-GAAP organic sales increased 2% while reported sales were unchanged. Currency and portfolio changes complicate the headline, making underlying category demand more useful for resource decisions.
items: Allocate brand investment toward categories with sustained consumer demand.
Improve availability in channels where product value supports retained purchasing.
Monitor geographic and category contribution separately from currency effects.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make underlying volume growth broader and repeatable
cards.text: Organic volume contributed one percentage point to sales growth, while total volume was unchanged. The volume improvement is modest and should be supported with effective consumer execution.
items: Target product and pack changes at barriers to household adoption.
Improve shelf availability for products generating repeat customer demand.
Monitor household penetration and repeat purchasing after promotional activity.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect pricing without weakening consumer value
cards.text: Higher prices contributed one percentage point to sales growth. Pricing supports revenue, but elasticity and private-label alternatives can influence whether households continue buying.
items: Test pricing and pack architecture using category-specific consumer response.
Use targeted offers where affordability changes can preserve profitable demand.
Monitor retained volume and contribution after price increases or promotions.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep cash conversion available for productive reinvestment
cards.text: Operating cash was $17.8 billion and non-GAAP adjusted free cash flow productivity was 87%. Cash supports brand investment and distributions after other business requirements.
items: Prioritize product and capacity investments with credible household demand.
Keep inventory and supplier planning aligned with category sales patterns.
Monitor cash conversion after working capital and necessary capital spending.

headline: Progressive should preserve underwriting discipline as direct-channel growth accelerates.
summary: Premium growth and a profitable combined ratio indicate a strong operating picture. Direct growth exceeded agency growth, while favorable prior-year loss development also supported results. The priority is keeping new business properly priced and economically retained, without letting reserve releases overstate the durability of current underwriting performance.
focusTitle: Grow policies where current underwriting and acquisition economics hold.
focusText: Allocate distribution spending using retained policy contribution and realistic loss assumptions. Maintain pricing and reserve discipline as the book expands, and judge profitability through current accident-year experience as well as calendar-year results that benefit from prior-year development.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Separate policy expansion from rate-driven premium growth
cards.text: Net premiums written increased 12% to $83.174 billion. Written premium combines pricing and policy growth, which call for different acquisition and underwriting decisions.
items: Allocate new-business capacity to risks priced adequately for expected claims.
Preserve service capacity where policy growth adds customer workload.
Monitor policy counts and retention separately from average premium changes.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the underwriting advantage as losses change
cards.text: The annual GAAP combined ratio was 87.4%, indicating underwriting profit before investment income. Sustaining that advantage requires attention to severity, reserve adequacy and pricing.
items: Update pricing decisions using emerging claim frequency and severity patterns.
Maintain underwriting selection where competitors pursue less attractive growth.
Monitor current loss trends and reserve adequacy alongside combined ratio.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Scale direct acquisition using retained customer returns
cards.text: Direct vehicle premiums grew 19% versus 11% through agencies. Different channel economics mean faster direct growth should not alone dictate marketing and service allocation.
items: Compare acquisition spending with retained policy contribution by distribution channel.
Coordinate direct marketing with onboarding and claims service capacity.
Monitor retention and acquisition payback before accelerating channel spending.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Avoid treating reserve releases as recurring new-business profit
cards.text: Favorable prior-accident-year loss development totaled $1.394 billion. Those releases supported the calendar-year result but do not establish the profitability of newly written risks.
items: Base growth budgets on current accident-year underwriting economics.
Keep reserving judgments separate from commercial pressure to expand premiums.
Monitor accident-year losses alongside reported results and prior-year development.

headline: Prologis should convert leasing momentum into occupied cash flow before stretching development.
summary: Record leasing and high occupancy support the logistics portfolio, while a long debt maturity profile provides flexibility. The data-center power pipeline adds an opportunity with different procurement and development requirements. The priority is turning signed leases into rental cash while staging new development around secured capacity and credible tenant demand.
focusTitle: Fund development from dependable leasing and executable power access.
focusText: Prioritize lease commencements, tenant retention and project returns across the existing portfolio. Preserve the funding advantage of long-term debt, and release data-center capital only as power procurement and tenant commitments become sufficiently concrete to justify construction exposure.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn leasing volume into dependable rental income
cards.text: Prologis signed 228 million square feet of leases. Record activity supports demand, while commencement dates, incentives and lease terms determine the resulting cash contribution.
items: Coordinate tenant fit-out and building readiness around lease commencement dates.
Prioritize leasing terms that preserve attractive contribution after incentives.
Monitor signed-to-occupied conversion and rental cash as leases begin.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect occupancy with selective local leasing decisions
cards.text: Owned and managed period-end occupancy was 95.8%. Vacancy remains relevant to cash flow even with high portfolio occupancy and strong annual leasing activity.
items: Prioritize tenant renewals in markets with greater competing supply.
Target leasing incentives to space where contribution justifies the concession.
Monitor local vacancy and tenant retention before adding speculative capacity.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Stage data-center spending around secured power
cards.text: The power pipeline was 5.7 GW, secured or in advanced procurement. Part remains unfinalized, and access to power differs from delivered revenue-producing capacity.
items: Sequence development commitments around confirmed power availability and tenant requirements.
Rank projects using procurement certainty and expected development returns.
Monitor power delivery milestones before releasing additional construction capital.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve financing flexibility through the development cycle
cards.text: Weighted debt interest was 3.3% with an 8.2-year average term. Longer maturity reduces immediate refinancing exposure while development commitments still consume funding capacity.
items: Align new debt maturities with projected lease and development cash flows.
Preserve liquidity for committed construction and tenant improvements.
Monitor future refinancing needs alongside optional development spending.

headline: Prudential should balance retirement growth with capital discipline and steadier asset retention.
summary: Institutional retirement and group insurance provided meaningful sales activity, while individual retirement declined and PGIM net flows were modest. The priority is choosing business that earns attractive risk-adjusted returns rather than relying on large retirement transactions or gross distribution activity to demonstrate sustained franchise growth.
focusTitle: Allocate capital toward retained and appropriately priced relationships.
focusText: Coordinate retirement pricing, insurance underwriting and asset management distribution around long-term contribution. Preserve the ability to write large institutional transactions when terms are attractive, while improving retail retention and annuity product fit so growth is less dependent on uneven individual deals.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Price large retirement transactions for capital and risk
cards.text: Institutional retirement sales were $25.9 billion, including over $12 billion of longevity risk transfer. Large transactions support activity but can make annual sales uneven.
items: Prioritize transactions with attractive risk transfer and capital-adjusted returns.
Align asset and liability resources with the obligations accepted.
Monitor capital usage and retained risk before expanding institutional commitments.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Strengthen flows beyond isolated mandate wins
cards.text: PGIM recorded $0.5 billion in total net inflows, including $2.1 billion from third parties. Modest overall flows make channel retention and mandate durability important.
items: Identify institutional wins and retail redemptions separately by investment strategy.
Target client support toward recurring reasons for withdrawals or lost mandates.
Monitor retained fee contribution and net flows after market movements.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve individual retirement product fit
cards.text: Individual retirement sales declined 3% to $13.6 billion. Demand and product mix within annuity offerings should guide distribution and pricing rather than a uniform sales response.
items: Align indexed and fixed annuity offerings with demonstrated customer needs.
Support distributors where product complexity prevents appropriate customer adoption.
Monitor product-level sales and contribution after guarantees and capital costs.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve insurance underwriting as sales expand
cards.text: Group insurance sales rose 11% to $611 million. Growth in life and disability supports the franchise when underwriting and servicing expenses remain appropriate.
items: Price new employer relationships using risk selection and expected claims costs.
Scale service capacity around onboarding and ongoing employer requirements.
Monitor retained premium contribution alongside underwriting and servicing expenses.

headline: PTC should turn commercial realignment into faster recurring growth and durable collections.
summary: Constant-currency revenue grew much faster than ARR because recognition effects influenced the comparison. Cash growth is encouraging, but go-to-market realignment required spending. The priority is improving customer acquisition, retention and activation rather than using accounting-driven revenue acceleration as the main measure of commercial progress.
focusTitle: Judge the sales model through recurring customer value.
focusText: Direct realignment resources toward productive coverage, activation of contracted deployments and retained subscriptions. Preserve collection discipline, and use ARR and sales productivity alongside cash to determine whether the commercial changes improve the underlying business enough to justify their cost.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make recurring growth visible in active deployments
cards.text: ARR increased 8.5% in constant currency. Annualized contracts indicate scale, but retained customers and activation of ramp contracts determine the durability of that growth.
items: Prioritize onboarding for contracted customers approaching deployment and usage milestones.
Address renewal risks through product adoption and customer success support.
Monitor churn and activated contract value within the recurring base.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require better sales productivity from realignment spending
cards.text: Cash flow absorbed approximately $20 million of go-to-market realignment outflows. Commercial changes should improve coverage and conversion rather than simply alter the cost structure.
items: Allocate sales coverage around qualified customer opportunities and renewal requirements.
Equip reassigned teams with clear account ownership and implementation support.
Monitor sales conversion and acquisition productivity after the realignment costs.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Plan from contract economics rather than revenue timing
cards.text: Revenue increased 18% in constant currency, with management highlighting ASC 606 effects. That outpaced ARR growth and should not alone drive permanent operating commitments.
items: Base hiring and capacity decisions on recurring contract and renewal demand.
Align delivery resources with committed deployments and deferred contract obligations.
Monitor recognized revenue against ARR progression before extrapolating growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve collection strength while funding commercial execution
cards.text: Operating and non-GAAP free cash flow both increased 16%. Cash supports investment, although billing seasonality and customer retention affect its repeatability.
items: Coordinate billing and collections with contract milestones and customer deployment.
Prioritize growth spending that supports recurring adoption and retention.
Monitor cash conversion after billing seasonality and realignment outflows.

headline: PSEG should sustain nuclear availability while earning affordable returns on utility investment.
summary: Nuclear availability and output support the generation business, while the regulated utility supplied most group earnings and increased income. A larger rate base extends the opportunity but also raises financing and customer recovery requirements. The priority is reliable operations and disciplined investment rather than pursuing asset growth independently of returns.
focusTitle: Protect operating reliability and the economics of regulated growth.
focusText: Coordinate nuclear maintenance with output and sales commitments, while prioritizing utility projects that deliver service value with credible recovery. Use recurring utility cash and financing costs to set the investment pace, preserving customer affordability as the asset base expands.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make rate-base growth deliver useful service returns
cards.text: Utility rate base reached approximately $36 billion, up about 7%. The investment supports earnings when assets provide customer benefits and obtain appropriate recovery.
items: Prioritize network projects by reliability value and approved recovery mechanisms.
Coordinate construction schedules with rate implementation and financing availability.
Monitor customer bill impact and realized returns as assets enter service.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the utility’s recurring earnings contribution
cards.text: PSE&G net income rose to $1.745 billion from $1.547 billion. Its contribution makes rate execution and funding costs central to the group’s investment capacity.
items: Align utility operating plans with approved rates and service obligations.
Direct retained resources toward projects with credible recovery and execution readiness.
Monitor utility cash support after financing costs and capital requirements.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect nuclear availability through maintenance discipline
cards.text: PSEG Nuclear achieved a 91.2% capacity factor. Reliable availability supports generation and cash potential, while outages and operating costs require continued attention.
items: Sequence planned outages around equipment condition and operating requirements.
Protect maintenance resources that reduce avoidable forced outages.
Monitor availability and outage costs before increasing production commitments.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Translate nuclear output into dependable cash economics
cards.text: Nuclear output reached 30.9 TWh. Production creates value through realized electricity prices and hedging, while maintenance spending remains necessary to preserve future output.
items: Align sales and hedging commitments with realistic plant availability.
Balance production objectives with required maintenance and operational reliability.
Monitor realized generation contribution after operating and maintenance requirements.

headline: Public Storage should improve existing-property growth while leasing up new capacity.
summary: Same-store revenue was essentially flat, so acquisitions and completed developments expand a business whose existing properties show limited growth. Financing terms provide breathing room. The priority is better occupancy and pricing economics across current facilities, while requiring new space and acquired properties to earn returns above their funding costs.
focusTitle: Prioritize property contribution over adding space alone.
focusText: Use local demand and retention to guide move-in pricing, promotions and development pacing. Integrate acquisitions with clear operating improvements, and protect financing flexibility until new facilities generate sustainable cash yields rather than treating completed square footage as realized earnings.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Restore growth within the existing property base
cards.text: Same-store annual revenue was $3.765 billion, essentially flat. Property-level occupancy, move-in pricing and tenant retention need coordinated attention before expansion can carry durable returns.
items: Adjust local move-in offers using occupancy and customer acquisition economics.
Improve retention practices where tenant turnover creates avoidable vacancy costs.
Monitor property contribution after discounts and marketing rather than occupancy alone.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Integrate acquisitions around cash yield improvement
cards.text: Public Storage acquired 87 facilities for $945.6 million. Scale adds opportunity, while acquired cash returns must justify financing and integration requirements.
items: Prioritize operational integration that improves local pricing and customer service.
Compare acquired property contribution with purchase and funding costs.
Monitor occupancy and cash yield before committing to further acquisitions.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make completed developments earn their capital cost
cards.text: Developments and expansions added 2.1 million rentable square feet at $408.9 million cost. Completed space still needs customer lease-up to generate acceptable returns.
items: Focus marketing and staffing on developments with the clearest lease-up demand.
Adjust new project pacing to local absorption and competing supply.
Monitor lease-up contribution and cash yield after promotional spending.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use financing time to preserve development flexibility
cards.text: Debt carried a 3.2% weighted interest rate and 6.3-year average maturity. Existing financing provides time, but refinancing and outstanding development commitments still matter.
items: Align funding decisions with facility lease-up and committed development spending.
Preserve liquidity for essential property upkeep and near-term maturities.
Monitor refinancing costs alongside cash from newly stabilized facilities.

headline: PulteGroup should align land and construction commitments with executable buyer demand.
summary: Deliveries demonstrate substantial operating scale, and backlog provides visibility into future closings. Land investment commits capital ahead of those outcomes, while cash and low debt-to-capital provide flexibility. The priority is protecting home-level returns and liquidity by matching starts and land decisions to order quality and buyer financing readiness.
focusTitle: Use financial flexibility to maintain production and land discipline.
focusText: Prioritize sold-home completion and local community absorption before expanding speculative exposure. Stage land development around demand, and evaluate incentives and cancellations together so backlog becomes cash without consuming the balance-sheet cushion through commitments that outpace buyer demand.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Stage land investment around community absorption
