cards.text: Land acquisition and development investment totaled $5.2 billion. Spending creates future selling opportunities while exposing capital before customer demand and home margins are certain.
items: Sequence land development using local orders and achievable community sales pace.
Reassess option commitments where expected absorption no longer supports returns.
Monitor land exposure and impairment risk before adding new community commitments.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Convert backlog without overlooking buyer readiness
cards.text: Year-end backlog was 8,495 homes valued at $5.3 billion. Contracted demand supports visibility but can change through cancellations or financing difficulties.
items: Coordinate construction and closing schedules with buyer financing milestones.
Target retention support where a viable buyer faces closing obstacles.
Monitor cancellations and net closing contribution within backlog cohorts.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve efficient delivery of sold homes
cards.text: PulteGroup delivered 29,572 homes. Closing execution converts earlier sales into cash and should remain aligned with replacement demand rather than a standalone volume objective.
items: Prioritize trade scheduling and materials for homes with confirmed closing readiness.
Balance construction starts against net orders and community inventory.
Monitor cycle times and completed unsold homes alongside delivery volume.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the housing-cycle liquidity cushion
cards.text: Year-end cash was $2.0 billion and debt-to-capital was 11.2%. Financial flexibility supports disciplined choices when sales or land economics become less attractive.
items: Reserve liquidity for committed land development and sold-home construction.
Compare discretionary capital returns with exposure under slower absorption scenarios.
Monitor cash after construction and land obligations before accelerating spending.

headline: Qnity should protect realization and establish standalone discipline as electronics volumes grow.
summary: Both principal segments expanded organically, with Interconnect growing faster, while total growth relied on units rather than better price and mix. The recent separation adds an execution priority. Qnity should support customer qualification and delivery while ensuring standalone operating and financing costs do not absorb the benefit of stronger demand.
focusTitle: Turn volume momentum into sustainable standalone contribution.
focusText: Allocate capacity and technical resources around qualified demand in both segments. Maintain pricing discipline as product mix changes, and establish the cost and funding structure required after separation, using actual standalone economics rather than assuming pro forma history already reflects a full operating year.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Keep unit growth from masking weaker realization
cards.text: Total volume increased 11%, while local price and product mix declined 1%. Stronger shipments should produce acceptable contribution rather than justify indiscriminate capacity expansion.
items: Prioritize product and customer orders using contribution after manufacturing costs.
Address pricing concessions where product differentiation supports better realization.
Monitor unit contribution and mix as production volumes expand.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support qualified semiconductor materials demand
cards.text: Semiconductor Technologies sales were $2.642 billion, with non-GAAP organic growth of 8%. Sustained growth requires customer qualification and production programs to support shipments.
items: Align technical support with customer material qualification and production milestones.
Allocate capacity to qualified products with credible customer requirements.
Monitor customer production and repeat orders before increasing supply commitments.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale Interconnect around durable electronics orders
cards.text: Interconnect Solutions sales reached $2.112 billion with 12% non-GAAP organic growth. Faster growth warrants support while separating AI-related demand from broader customer activity.
items: Coordinate production resources with confirmed interconnect customer launch schedules.
Balance commercial effort across AI-related and broader electronics opportunities.
Monitor order breadth and customer concentration as segment capacity expands.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Establish the full cost of operating independently
cards.text: The DuPont spin-off completed in November 2025; adjusted pro forma results assume earlier separation. A full standalone cost and funding structure still needs operational proof.
items: Assign ownership for standalone systems and functions previously supplied centrally.
Remove stranded costs while preserving customer delivery and technical support.
Monitor actual operating and financing costs against pro forma assumptions.

headline: Qualcomm should sustain mobile strength while converting automotive and IoT diversification.
summary: Handset revenue remained the largest chip stream and grew, while automotive and IoT expanded faster. The operating picture is stronger than the tax-depressed earnings headline suggests. The priority is preserving mobile customer economics and turning diversification programs into durable production revenue without misreading a noncash tax charge as demand weakness.
focusTitle: Fund diversification using customer production and product returns.
focusText: Protect the handset franchise while staging automotive and IoT development around executable programs. Evaluate operating contribution and cash capacity separately from the valuation-allowance charge, and require customer adoption and design conversion to justify investment beyond the established mobile business.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the economics of the handset franchise
cards.text: QCT handset revenue increased 12% to $27.793 billion. Mobile remains the largest chip revenue stream, making premium-device demand and customer design positions important.
items: Prioritize handset engineering that strengthens valuable customer design positions.
Align shipment and inventory planning with customer product launch requirements.
Monitor premium-device demand and customer concentration before expanding commitments.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Convert automotive design activity into production returns
cards.text: QCT automotive revenue increased 36% to $3.957 billion. Diversification is progressing, while long vehicle production cycles make program execution important beyond initial design wins.
items: Coordinate automotive development resources with customer vehicle production milestones.
Protect program support needed for qualification and production reliability.
Monitor design-to-production conversion and contribution across vehicle programs.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale IoT selectively across different customer markets
cards.text: QCT IoT revenue increased 22% to $6.617 billion. Connected-device growth diversifies demand, but industrial and consumer programs can have different cycles and economics.
items: Allocate application engineering to IoT products with repeatable customer demand.
Balance inventory commitments against industrial and consumer order patterns.
Monitor order breadth and product contribution as IoT shipments grow.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep the tax charge separate from operating allocation
cards.text: A $5.7 billion noncash tax valuation-allowance charge depressed GAAP earnings without an equivalent immediate cash outflow. Investment decisions should remain grounded in operating economics.
items: Base product funding on recurring operating returns and available cash.
Consider future tax capacity when evaluating longer-term capital allocation.
Monitor cash obligations without treating the charge as current operating deterioration.

headline: Quanta should convert contracted infrastructure work into cash without overstretching execution.
summary: Contracted obligations and broader backlog provide significant demand visibility, while cash generation supports equipment and growth. Eight acquisitions add operating complexity and affect comparisons. The priority is funded project delivery with disciplined labor, billing and integration, distinguishing committed work from estimated future activity before allocating capacity.
focusTitle: Stage capacity and acquisition integration around executable projects.
focusText: Prioritize projects with clear schedules, permitting paths and customer obligations. Preserve working-capital discipline as activity scales, and evaluate acquired businesses on organic execution and cash contribution rather than allowing a broader backlog measure to justify every equipment or staffing commitment.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build delivery plans around contracted obligations
cards.text: Remaining performance obligations totaled $23.76 billion. Contracted work gives visibility, while permitting, skilled labor and customer schedules determine the pace of conversion.
items: Coordinate labor and equipment deployment with permitted project start dates.
Escalate supplier and customer dependencies that threaten contracted milestones.
Monitor project contribution and schedule performance as obligations become revenue.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Separate estimated work from committed capacity needs
cards.text: Non-GAAP backlog was $43.98 billion, including estimates beyond contracted obligations. Broader visibility is useful, but estimated MSA activity does not carry identical delivery certainty.
items: Base permanent capacity additions on committed work and credible utilization.
Use flexible resource plans for estimated master service agreement demand.
Monitor estimate conversion and customer work releases before accelerating equipment purchases.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep project growth from absorbing the cash benefit
cards.text: Operating cash was $2.23 billion and non-GAAP free cash flow $1.67 billion. Receivables, billing and equipment needs determine how much growth can be self-funded.
items: Coordinate milestone billing with project progress and customer acceptance.
Address aging receivables before they constrain equipment and labor funding.
Monitor project working capital and cash after necessary equipment investment.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Integrate acquisitions around operating and cash standards
cards.text: Quanta completed eight acquisitions, with results entering from their closing dates. Acquired growth needs consistent project controls and disciplined integration to support returns.
items: Apply common project cost and billing controls across acquired operations.
Preserve skilled teams and customer relationships during integration changes.
Monitor organic performance and acquisition cash contribution after integration costs.

headline: Quest should turn higher testing volume into reliable service and better requisition economics.
summary: Organic volume increased, but acquisitions and relationships contributed much more to total requisition growth. Nearly flat revenue per requisition makes service efficiency and reimbursement important. Stronger cash supports investment, and the priority is integrating large testing relationships while retaining appropriate contribution and dependable patient service.
focusTitle: Scale testing capacity around quality and retained contribution.
focusText: Allocate laboratory and collection resources to actual channel demand, preserving turnaround and service as partnerships expand. Improve payer and collections execution so additional requisitions generate cash after delivery costs, rather than assuming total volume growth alone establishes stronger underlying economics.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Distinguish organic demand from added testing relationships
cards.text: Organic requisition volume rose 3.4% versus 12.3% total volume growth. Different growth sources require distinct commercial and integration decisions across testing channels.
items: Prioritize physician and hospital relationships with sustained organic testing demand.
Integrate acquired volumes into laboratory routing and collection capacity plans.
Monitor channel-level requisition retention separately from acquired volume additions.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Protect contribution when revenue per request is flat
cards.text: Revenue per requisition increased only 0.1%. Volume-led growth raises the importance of reimbursement, payer mix and efficient testing operations for profitability.
items: Improve payer contract and coding execution where reimbursement limits contribution.
Optimize testing workflows and routing without compromising analytical quality.
Monitor contribution per requisition after labor, supplies and collection costs.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make dialysis partnership scale dependable for patients
cards.text: Quest scaled services for over 200,000 patients at Fresenius dialysis centers. A large relationship needs consistent implementation, capacity and service quality to support its economics.
items: Coordinate collection schedules and laboratory capacity with dialysis center needs.
Resolve implementation issues through joint operating reviews with center teams.
Monitor turnaround, service quality and relationship contribution as volumes stabilize.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve collection gains while funding testing capacity
cards.text: Operating cash increased to $1.886 billion from $1.334 billion. Stronger cash provides flexibility, while collections and investment requirements affect how much can recur.
items: Extend collections practices that reduce avoidable reimbursement and payment delays.
Prioritize capital required for dependable testing and integration capacity.
Monitor operating cash after working-capital movements and laboratory investment.

headline: Ralph Lauren should turn new DTC customers into repeat full-price demand.
summary: Strong comparable DTC growth, customer recruitment and Asia expansion support the brand’s momentum. Gross margin also improved on an adjusted basis. The priority is preserving the quality of that growth: newly acquired customers should repeat, regional expansion should remain balanced, and pricing gains should survive promotions and cost pressure.
focusTitle: Deepen customer relationships while protecting full-price economics.
focusText: Allocate marketing and merchandising around repeat purchasing and retained contribution. Preserve brand value through disciplined assortment and inventory, and scale Asia using local customer demand rather than assuming strong regional growth alone justifies every additional store or acquisition expense.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the demand behind DTC comparable growth
cards.text: Global DTC comparable sales increased 13% in FY2026. Existing channels delivered momentum, making the balance between customer traffic and selling-price effects important for growth decisions.
items: Prioritize assortment and service practices associated with retained customer demand.
Improve digital and store conversion where customer traffic creates identifiable opportunity.
Monitor transaction growth and contribution separately from average selling prices.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make new customers worth retaining
cards.text: Ralph Lauren recruited 6.5 million new DTC customers. Recruitment creates value when customers return without requiring persistently high acquisition or promotional spending.
items: Build post-purchase engagement around relevant products and demonstrated customer interests.
Allocate acquisition spending using repeat-purchase contribution rather than registrations alone.
Monitor retained activity and acquisition payback across new customer cohorts.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Scale Asia around local customer economics
cards.text: Asia revenue increased 22% in constant currency. The region provides strong growth, while local demand and geographic concentration should guide expansion choices.
items: Adapt assortments and customer service to demonstrated local demand patterns.
Stage additional channel investment around existing location and customer productivity.
Monitor regional contribution and concentration as Asia becomes more important.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect margin through full-price inventory discipline
cards.text: Annual gross margin was 69.9%, with a 130-basis-point increase on an adjusted basis. Mix and full-price selling need to withstand discounting and tariff pressures.
items: Align inventory purchases with product-level demand and full-price selling potential.
Address sourcing costs while preserving product quality and brand consistency.
Monitor full-price sell-through and contribution after promotions and tariff costs.

headline: Raymond James should restore asset-gathering momentum while managing weaker cash earnings.
summary: Client and fee-based assets expanded, supporting recurring revenue potential, but domestic net new assets slowed. Cash-related earnings also declined despite the larger asset base. The priority is stronger relationship acquisition and retention, with advisor productivity and fee contribution offsetting rather than obscuring pressure on client cash economics.
focusTitle: Turn larger client balances into retained relationship growth.
focusText: Invest in advisor capabilities and service where they improve net new assets and recurring fees. Manage client cash choices around customer needs and relationship value, while sizing spending to sustainable fee and cash contribution rather than market-driven asset appreciation.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Improve organic asset gathering through advisors
cards.text: Domestic Private Client Group net new assets were $52.431 billion versus $60.709 billion. The franchise still gathered assets, but momentum slowed and deserves targeted attention.
items: Identify advisor teams where recruitment, transfers or retention weakened.
Direct onboarding and relationship support toward recoverable asset-gathering bottlenecks.
Monitor net new assets and retained relationships by advisor channel.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Separate market gains from deeper client relationships
cards.text: Client assets under administration increased 10% to $1.731 trillion. Larger balances create opportunity, while market appreciation alone does not establish stronger customer acquisition.
items: Prioritize relationship development with clients whose service needs are expanding.
Allocate advisor capacity using client complexity and retained contribution.
Monitor asset growth from new relationships separately from market movements.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make fee-based scale improve advisor productivity
cards.text: Private Client Group fee-based assets reached $1.008 trillion, up 15%. The recurring fee opportunity depends on pricing, client retention and efficient advice delivery.
items: Support advisors with tools that improve ongoing portfolio and client service.
Align fee arrangements with the complexity and value of advice provided.
Monitor fee yields and retained contribution per advisor as balances expand.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Manage cash migration through relationship economics
cards.text: Net interest income plus third-party deposit-program fees declined 4% to $2.633 billion. Client cash allocation and yields can weaken earnings even as invested assets rise.
items: Offer cash solutions aligned with client liquidity and return needs.
Budget operating commitments using realistic cash balance and yield assumptions.
Monitor cash migration and relationship contribution before increasing fixed spending.

headline: Realty Income should preserve rent durability while requiring acquisitions to beat funding costs.
summary: Occupancy and rent recapture support a stable property base, while same-store rent growth remained modest. Investment adds a larger growth engine but also financing and tenant exposure. The priority is protecting recurring tenant cash flow and disciplined acquisition spreads rather than using high occupancy to justify expansion at any price.
focusTitle: Allocate capital around durable tenant contribution and funding spreads.
focusText: Prioritize renewals and tenant quality across existing properties. Add investments only where expected cash yield compensates for financing, concentration and property risks, and evaluate portfolio growth separately from the slower rental progress of assets already owned.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect rental stability through tenant quality
cards.text: Occupancy increased to 98.9% across 15,511 properties from 98.7%. High utilization supports rental stability but does not eliminate tenant credit or vacancy exposure.
items: Prioritize renewals and operating engagement with significant tenant relationships.
Address vacant properties using local demand and realistic re-leasing economics.
Monitor tenant credit concentration alongside portfolio occupancy and collected rent.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve rent recapture after renewal costs
cards.text: Re-leasing achieved 103.9% rent recapture on $301.99 million of new annualized base rent. Higher renewed rents should remain attractive after incentives and leasing costs.
items: Prioritize early renewal discussions where tenant operations remain economically sound.
Compare proposed increases with alternatives after vacancy and improvement costs.
Monitor renewal contribution and tenant retention across upcoming lease expirations.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Improve existing-property economics without overreaching
cards.text: Company-defined same-store rental revenue increased 1.3% in constant currency. Modest internal growth makes stable tenant economics important rather than aggressive rent increases alone.
items: Pursue contractual rent opportunities that preserve dependable tenant payment capacity.
Improve property-level execution where avoidable costs reduce retained contribution.
Monitor existing-property cash growth separately from acquisition-driven portfolio expansion.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep investment yields ahead of full funding costs
cards.text: Pro-rata investment volume was $6.2 billion at a 7.3% initial weighted average cash yield, a company-defined measure. Returns depend on tenant performance and financing.
items: Compare new property yields with financing and ongoing ownership requirements.
Limit incremental tenant and sector concentration when selecting acquisitions.
Monitor realized cash returns before committing further acquisition capital.

headline: Reddit should sustain advertising growth while building durable advertiser and regional economics.
summary: Advertising drove strong annual growth, international revenue expanded faster than the U.S., and gross margin improved. Those results provide investment capacity but do not establish operating profitability by themselves. The priority is retained advertiser value and efficient regional scaling, with other revenue serving as a smaller diversification opportunity.
focusTitle: Invest behind durable monetization rather than growth alone.
focusText: Allocate product, sales and infrastructure spending around advertiser retention and sustainable contribution. Scale international operations where local monetization can support delivery costs, and develop non-advertising contracts without assuming the smaller stream removes dependence on advertising budgets.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make advertiser growth persist beyond initial campaigns
cards.text: Advertising revenue increased 74% to approximately $2.1 billion. Its weight in annual revenue makes advertiser retention and repeat campaign value central to durable growth.
items: Improve advertiser tools where campaign setup and measurement limit repeat spending.
Prioritize sales support for customers demonstrating sustained platform value.
Monitor advertiser retention and monetization alongside advertising revenue growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale international monetization with local cost discipline
cards.text: International revenue rose 76% to $417 million versus 68% U.S. growth. Geographic expansion broadens the opportunity while requiring locally effective commercial and operating resources.
items: Prioritize markets where advertiser demand supports additional local sales capacity.
Adapt monetization support to regional advertiser and operating requirements.
Monitor regional contribution after localization and infrastructure spending.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Develop other revenue with contractual discipline
cards.text: Other revenue increased 22% to $140 million. It adds diversification but remains secondary, making contract durability and customer concentration important to its investment case.
items: Prioritize non-advertising agreements with clear usage obligations and renewal economics.
Allocate delivery resources according to contracted customer requirements.
Monitor renewal concentration and retained contribution before expanding related commitments.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect gross-margin capacity as operating investment expands
cards.text: GAAP gross margin increased 70 basis points to 91.2%. High gross profitability leaves room for investment while infrastructure and operating expenses still determine overall returns.
items: Prioritize product and sales initiatives with identifiable monetization or retention benefits.
Improve infrastructure efficiency as platform demand and commercial activity expand.
Monitor operating expense growth and contribution rather than gross margin alone.

headline: Regency Centers should turn signed leases and rent spreads into commenced rental cash.
summary: Same-property NOI and comparable cash rent spreads show strength in the existing portfolio. Leasing activity supports future cash, but leased space exceeded commenced space at year end. The priority is timely store openings and economically sustainable renewals, preserving tenant affordability as higher rents convert from agreements into collected income.
focusTitle: Prioritize lease commencement and durable tenant contribution.
focusText: Coordinate landlord work and tenant build-outs around credible opening schedules. Preserve strong leasing economics after improvement costs and incentives, and use tenant sales health and retention to keep rent growth compatible with dependable long-term occupancy.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Close the gap between signed and operating space
cards.text: Same-property space was 96.5% leased but 94.1% commenced. Some committed space was not yet producing rent, making build-outs and store openings operational priorities.
items: Coordinate landlord improvements with tenant construction and planned store openings.
Escalate permitting or handover delays that prevent rent commencement.
Monitor signed-to-commenced conversion and delayed rental cash by property.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve leasing gains without straining tenant economics
cards.text: Comparable new and renewal leases achieved a 10.8% blended cash rent spread. Higher rents create value when tenant operations can sustain the new obligation.
items: Assess renewal terms using tenant trading health and competing local options.
Use selective incentives where retained contribution exceeds vacancy alternatives.
Monitor tenant retention and payment performance after rent increases commence.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make leasing activity efficient after improvement costs
cards.text: Regency executed approximately 6.8 million square feet of comparable leases. The volume supports future occupancy, while timing and capital requirements determine its cash return.
items: Prioritize lease packages with attractive rent after improvement and leasing costs.
Coordinate construction resources across properties with overlapping commencement deadlines.
Monitor net leasing contribution and time to commencement across signed deals.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep existing-property income growth operationally durable
cards.text: Non-GAAP same-property NOI excluding termination fees increased 5.3%. Existing assets contributed, making recurring rent and property expense execution important to sustaining the improvement.
items: Extend property operating practices that control costs without weakening tenant service.
Prioritize renewals and space activation where they improve recurring income.
Monitor base rent growth against controllable property expense changes.

headline: Regeneron should offset EYLEA franchise pressure through disciplined diversification and pipeline conversion.
summary: EYLEA HD growth did not prevent a sharp decline in combined U.S. EYLEA sales. Libtayo and Sanofi-recorded Dupixent sales provide stronger growth signals, while R&D spending increased. The priority is protecting retinal franchise economics and selecting diversification investments that can become sustainable Regeneron contribution.
focusTitle: Protect current product value while funding credible new contribution.
focusText: Coordinate retinal conversion efforts with pricing and competitive realities, and support oncology and research opportunities using evidence of adoption and clinical differentiation. Evaluate Dupixent through Regeneron’s collaboration economics, preserving the distinction between partner sales and the revenue available to fund its business.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Manage the retinal franchise beyond EYLEA HD growth
cards.text: Combined U.S. EYLEA and EYLEA HD sales fell 27% to $4.385 billion, despite EYLEA HD growing 36%. Conversion alone has not offset broader franchise pressure.
items: Identify prescribing and access barriers affecting retained retinal franchise demand.
Allocate commercial support using net franchise contribution and competitive positioning.
Monitor combined net pricing and share alongside EYLEA HD conversion.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Translate Dupixent momentum through collaboration economics
cards.text: Global Dupixent sales recorded by Sanofi rose 26% to $17.8 billion. Strong partner sales support the collaboration, but are not Regeneron consolidated revenue.
items: Coordinate collaboration support around indications and markets with sustained adoption.
Allocate resources using Regeneron’s expected collaboration contribution and obligations.
Monitor profit-share conversion rather than treating partner sales as company revenue.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Grow Libtayo with disciplined oncology investment
cards.text: Global Libtayo net sales increased 19% to $1.453 billion. Oncology can broaden the portfolio when regional adoption and development support produce attractive retained contribution.
items: Prioritize launch support where patient access and prescribing adoption are progressing.
Coordinate commercial investment with evidence from relevant clinical milestones.
Monitor regional contribution after launch and ongoing product support costs.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make larger research spending advance differentiated programs
cards.text: GAAP R&D expense increased 14% to $5.850 billion. Pipeline investment can support diversification while increasing the current cost of selecting unsuccessful programs.
items: Prioritize late-stage resources using clinical evidence and patient differentiation.
Stop or reshape programs whose evidence no longer supports their investment case.
Monitor study progression and spending commitments before expanding development capacity.

headline: Republic Services should preserve pricing and cash gains while improving volume and recycling economics.
summary: Yield supported revenue despite a volume drag, while lower recycled commodity prices challenged another earnings stream. Operational renewable gas projects add diversification and operating cash improved. The priority is retaining profitable collection demand and making recycling and gas assets earn attractive returns without relying on pricing alone.
focusTitle: Use strong cash to reinforce recurring service economics.
focusText: Preserve collection pricing where service value supports it, but address customer and route-level volume weakness. Align recycling costs and contracts with commodity exposure, and scale renewable gas from measured operating contribution rather than counting completed projects as realized cash returns.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve yield without sacrificing attractive collection volume
cards.text: Average yield added 4.1% to revenue while volume reduced it by 0.6%. Pricing supported growth, but retained customer and route contribution should guide further increases.
items: Target retention efforts where valuable collection customers face competitive alternatives.
Optimize routes and service frequency using actual customer demand.
Monitor volume and contribution separately across collection and disposal activities.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Adapt recycling economics to weaker commodity realization
cards.text: Average recycled commodity pricing fell to $135 per ton from $164. Lower sale prices make processing efficiency and contractual sharing of commodity exposure more important.
items: Align recycling contract terms with processing costs and commodity risk sharing.
Improve sorting and processing practices where they protect material value.
Monitor recycling contribution after commodity revenue sharing and operating costs.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make renewable gas projects deliver dependable returns
cards.text: Nine renewable natural gas projects were completed and operational. They add diversification opportunities, while utilization and realized offtake economics determine the cash benefit.
items: Prioritize stable operating output and commissioning follow-through at completed projects.
Align offtake arrangements with expected production and operating requirements.
Monitor realized gas contribution before expanding additional project commitments.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect cash capacity while funding essential service assets
cards.text: Operating cash flow increased 9.2% to $4.30 billion. Stronger cash supports investment and debt service after capital and acquisition commitments are considered.
items: Prioritize fleet and facility investment that sustains dependable collection service.
Stage discretionary acquisitions against available cash after operating requirements.
Monitor cash after capital spending and committed acquisition payments.

headline: ResMed should connect device growth to recurring patient engagement while preserving margin gains.
summary: Devices, masks and software all grew, while gross margin improved materially. That supports a constructive assessment across the platform. The priority is sustaining therapy adoption and recurring supplies, with software scaled on its own retention and implementation economics rather than assuming every revenue stream shares the same operating model.
focusTitle: Build durable patient and customer relationships across the platform.
focusText: Preserve device availability and supply continuity while improving resupply engagement. Invest in software where adoption and retention justify delivery costs, and use manufacturing productivity and product mix to protect gross margin without weakening therapy quality or customer support.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Translate device demand into sustained therapy adoption
cards.text: Device revenue increased 9% to $2.6652 billion. Growth supports the therapy platform when regional adoption and replacement activity lead to ongoing patient use.
items: Align device availability with regional clinical and customer demand.
Support onboarding and service practices that help patients remain engaged.
Monitor adoption and replacement demand separately before expanding production capacity.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen recurring supply demand around the installed base
cards.text: Masks and other revenue increased 11% to $1.8397 billion. Faster supply growth can reinforce recurring relationships when patient resupply needs and product fit are served.
items: Improve resupply availability and ordering around ongoing patient requirements.
Prioritize mask fit and product support that sustain therapy use.
Monitor resupply activity and retained contribution alongside device installations.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale care software through retained customer value
cards.text: Residential Care Software revenue increased 10% to $641.4 million. The software business adds a distinct opportunity with implementation and support requirements beyond physical therapy products.
items: Prioritize implementations that address customer workflow and adoption obstacles.
Allocate support resources to renewals and successful ongoing customer use.
Monitor retention and contribution after implementation and service costs.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect manufacturing gains without compromising quality
cards.text: GAAP gross margin increased to 59.4% from 56.7%. Better gross profitability supports investment when product mix and manufacturing efficiencies remain durable.
items: Extend manufacturing improvements that reduce waste while preserving product quality.
Align production and inventory with device and resupply demand.
Monitor gross contribution after mix changes and manufacturing cost movements.

headline: Revvity should restore segment profitability while preserving modest organic growth.
summary: Both Life Sciences and Diagnostics expanded organically, with Diagnostics growing faster, yet adjusted operating margins declined in both segments. The priority is not simply generating more revenue. Pricing, product mix and operating spending need to convert underlying demand into better contribution without undermining customer support or future product opportunities.
focusTitle: Link commercial growth to segment-level operating economics.
focusText: Target the cost and mix issues within each segment rather than imposing identical cuts across the portfolio. Protect recurring reagent and testing relationships, and allocate instrument, manufacturing and commercial investment where customer demand can support sustainable margins after the required delivery resources.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make Life Sciences growth improve profitability
cards.text: Non-GAAP adjusted Life Sciences operating margin fell to 32.0% from 33.4%. Modest revenue growth did not prevent a deterioration in segment economics.
items: Identify instrument and reagent lines with the greatest contribution pressure.
Target avoidable operating costs while preserving application and customer support.
Monitor product mix and recurring segment contribution after cost actions.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve the return on Diagnostics expansion
cards.text: Non-GAAP adjusted Diagnostics operating margin fell to 24.2% from 26.1%. Faster organic demand has not yet offset pricing, mix or spending pressure.
items: Prioritize diagnostic customer growth with attractive reimbursement and supply economics.
Align manufacturing and commercial spending with the recurring testing opportunity.
Monitor segment contribution after product mix and operating cost changes.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Develop Life Sciences demand with selective commercial support
cards.text: Life Sciences revenue was $1.431 billion with 2% non-GAAP organic growth. Limited underlying expansion calls for targeted instrument and reagent execution rather than broad capacity additions.
items: Support instrument opportunities with credible customer funding and purchase schedules.
Deepen reagent relationships where installed instruments create recurring usage.
Monitor organic orders separately from acquisition and currency effects.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve recurring Diagnostics demand across regions
cards.text: Diagnostics revenue reached $1.425 billion with 4% non-GAAP organic growth. Stronger underlying demand supports the segment if regional growth translates into retained testing relationships.
items: Prioritize supply and service continuity for recurring diagnostic customers.
Allocate technical resources to regions with demonstrated testing adoption.
Monitor regional volume retention alongside the profitability of new demand.

headline: Robinhood should turn customer funding and Gold adoption into durable returns on higher spending.
summary: Preliminary results show strong net deposits and Gold subscriber growth alongside a broader funded customer base. Operating expenses also rose materially. The priority is retaining customer assets and subscription value after acquisition and benefits costs, so growth investment earns returns beyond market-sensitive activity or initial customer recruitment.
focusTitle: Allocate spending around retained funded relationships.
focusText: Prioritize product and service investments that keep customers funded and economically active. Use Gold retention and contribution to govern benefits spending, and evaluate customer acquisition using sustained engagement while keeping expense commitments consistent with recurring rather than temporarily elevated activity.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the funding behind platform growth
cards.text: Net deposits were $68.1 billion, or 35% of prior-year platform assets. Customer funding provides a growth source distinct from asset price appreciation.
items: Improve transfer and account service experiences that support retained customer funding.
Prioritize products aligned with customers’ ongoing funded account needs.
Monitor retained deposits and customer contribution after introductory incentives.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make Gold growth economically durable
cards.text: Gold subscribers rose 58% to approximately 4.2 million. Subscription adoption can expand recurring revenue when retention and benefits costs support attractive contribution.
items: Prioritize Gold benefits associated with sustained customer subscription value.
Align benefit spending with subscription and broader retained relationship economics.
Monitor subscriber retention and contribution after promotional offers end.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn funded customer additions into ongoing activity
cards.text: Funded customers reached 27.0 million, up 7%. A larger base creates opportunity, but acquisition value depends on customers remaining funded and engaged.
items: Direct acquisition spending toward channels producing sustained funded customer relationships.
Improve onboarding where customers struggle to activate useful account features.
Monitor retained activity and acquisition payback across newly funded cohorts.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require higher operating costs to earn recurring returns
cards.text: GAAP operating expenses increased 25% to $2.38 billion. Product and acquisition investment should improve durable economics rather than permanently raising costs against volatile revenue.
items: Rank spending initiatives by customer retention or recurring contribution benefits.
Separate acquisition-related integration needs from ongoing operating commitments.
Monitor expense growth against retained customer revenue and service requirements.

headline: Rockwell should convert software momentum into broader customer adoption and service demand.
summary: Software & Control grew while Intelligent Devices and Lifecycle Services declined. Recurring contract value improved, but includes acquisitions and differs from recognized revenue. The priority is using software relationships to deepen sustainable automation demand while diagnosing whether weaker devices and services reflect deferred projects or lasting customer constraints.
focusTitle: Coordinate software, devices and services around executable customer projects.
focusText: Allocate technical sales and delivery capacity to funded automation opportunities and retained subscriptions. Preserve software adoption momentum, while aligning device inventory and service resources with project timing rather than assuming recurring contract growth confirms broad recovery across the whole portfolio.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use software growth to deepen customer value
cards.text: Software & Control sales increased 9% to $2.383 billion. Stronger segment demand creates an opportunity to expand adoption and connect customers with appropriate automation capabilities.
items: Prioritize implementation support for customers adopting software and control products.
Coordinate account plans around demonstrated customer automation needs.
Monitor software adoption and segment order conversion after initial purchases.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Align device resources with actual capital spending
cards.text: Intelligent Devices sales declined 1% to $3.756 billion. Softer equipment demand calls for regional and product-level resource decisions rather than a uniform recovery assumption.
items: Adjust device inventory and production to confirmed customer orders.
Focus application engineering on funded projects approaching purchasing decisions.
Monitor regional order breadth and customer capital plans before expanding capacity.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Recover service demand through project execution support
cards.text: Lifecycle Services sales declined 3% to $2.203 billion. Project timing and underlying service demand need distinct responses before permanent capacity changes are made.
items: Reengage customers whose automation projects stalled before service deployment.
Align service staffing with executable project and installed-base requirements.
Monitor delayed project conversion and retained service contribution by customer.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make recurring contracts become renewed, active customer use
cards.text: ARR grew 8% on the company’s constant-currency definition, including acquisitions. Contract value supports visibility but does not establish equivalent recognized revenue or organic growth.
items: Prioritize activation and renewal support for existing recurring contracts.
Allocate permanent support resources using retained customer obligations and utilization.
Monitor organic recurring growth separately from acquired contract value.

headline: Rollins should preserve service retention while scaling faster termite and commercial demand.
summary: All three main service categories grew organically, with termite and ancillary work expanding fastest. Acquisitions added another growth source. The priority is preserving customer service and technician productivity across that expansion, while ensuring acquired routes and faster-growing treatments earn attractive returns without weakening recurring residential relationships.
focusTitle: Scale service capacity around retained route contribution.
focusText: Allocate technicians and sales effort using service-line demand and repeat customer value. Integrate acquired operations into dependable scheduling and customer support, while preserving residential retention so the larger network produces sustainable economics rather than simply higher reported revenue.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support termite growth with dependable treatment capacity
cards.text: Company-defined non-GAAP organic termite and ancillary revenue grew 9.9%. Faster expansion deserves operating support when treatment demand, pricing and technician capacity remain aligned.
items: Allocate trained technicians to areas with confirmed treatment demand.
Protect treatment quality and follow-up service as customer volumes increase.
Monitor contribution and technician workload across termite and ancillary services.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve commercial account economics as contracts expand
cards.text: Non-GAAP organic commercial revenue grew 7.6%. Commercial demand supports underlying expansion when contract pricing and service delivery requirements produce attractive retained contribution.
items: Prioritize new commercial contracts with appropriate pricing for service intensity.
Coordinate route scheduling around customer access and contractual service requirements.
Monitor account retention and service costs after new contracts begin.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep residential relationships from losing attention
cards.text: Non-GAAP organic residential revenue grew 5.0%, slower than the other main services. Residential retention remains important even as faster categories attract expansion resources.
items: Improve renewal and scheduling experiences for recurring residential customers.
Align pricing and service frequency with local customer requirements.
Monitor retention and route contribution separately from residential price increases.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make acquired routes earn their purchase cost
cards.text: Rollins invested $310 million in acquisitions, with acquisition-related revenue contributing 4.1% to annual growth. Retained customers and integration efficiency determine the economic return.
items: Integrate acquired scheduling and service practices without disrupting customer relationships.
Combine routes where density improves productivity and dependable coverage.
Monitor acquired customer retention and cash contribution after integration spending.

headline: Roper should make software acquisitions earn cash returns while strengthening organic growth.
summary: Acquisitions contributed more revenue growth than existing businesses, reinforcing the importance of capital allocation. Application Software expanded, while Network Software gross margin slipped. The priority is integrating acquired vertical software at attractive returns and preserving the product and service economics needed for continuing organic customer expansion.
focusTitle: Balance acquisition deployment with retained product economics.
focusText: Allocate capital using acquired cash generation and financing costs, while giving existing businesses the product investment needed to retain customers. Investigate Network Software margin changes through mix and delivery costs so portfolio expansion does not hide deterioration within individual software franchises.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make existing-business growth a separate operating objective
cards.text: Company-defined organic revenue grew 5%, while acquisitions contributed 7% to reported growth. The acquisition engine is important, but the existing customer base must remain productive.
items: Prioritize product improvements that support retention and expansion within current accounts.
Allocate commercial resources using organic demand rather than total acquired scale.
Monitor organic pricing and customer growth separately from acquisition contribution.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require acquisition spending to generate durable cash returns
cards.text: Roper deployed $3.3 billion toward vertical software acquisitions. Purchase prices and financing create a return requirement beyond adding revenue to the portfolio.
items: Integrate acquired businesses around retained customers and dependable product delivery.
Compare acquisition cash contribution with purchase costs and financing requirements.
Monitor realized returns before committing additional capital to similar deals.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen the largest software franchise through customer adoption
cards.text: Application Software revenue reached $4.483 billion versus $3.8683 billion. Its scale makes retained adoption and the balance between organic and acquired growth important.
items: Prioritize implementation support and product investment for recurring application customers.
Preserve domain capabilities that support valuable vertical software relationships.
Monitor organic contribution within the segment after acquired revenue additions.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore Network Software gross-margin discipline
cards.text: Network Software gross margin declined to 84.1% from 85.0%. Product mix and delivery economics need attention even while portfolio revenue grows.
items: Identify products and customer requirements driving higher service or delivery costs.
Improve platform and support efficiency without reducing necessary customer capability.
Monitor gross contribution by product as software revenue mix changes.

headline: Ross should protect value-led sales growth while managing inventory and tariff costs.
summary: Comparable-store sales improved and the network expanded, providing a positive demand picture. Higher inventory and management-estimated tariff costs create execution requirements rather than evidence of a demand collapse. The priority is preserving compelling merchandise value and new-store economics without allowing stock or sourcing costs to absorb the sales gains.
focusTitle: Balance merchandise opportunity with disciplined stock and store returns.
focusText: Allocate buying and new-store resources around customer transactions and contribution. Maintain flexible sourcing and inventory decisions as tariffs affect costs, while preserving the assortment value that supports off-price demand rather than passing every cost increase directly into customer prices.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the merchandise value behind comparable growth
cards.text: Fiscal 2025 comparable sales increased 5% after 3% growth. Existing stores showed stronger demand, making transaction growth and markdown discipline useful guides to buying.
items: Prioritize categories generating customer transactions and attractive retained merchandise margin.
Apply successful assortment practices to stores with comparable local demand.
Monitor basket changes and markdown activity alongside comparable sales.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep inventory aligned with selling opportunity
cards.text: Year-end merchandise inventory was $2.631 billion versus $2.445 billion. More merchandise supports selection, but should remain consistent with sales and packaway economics.
items: Allocate stock using store-level sales patterns and category demand.
Address slow-moving merchandise before deeper markdowns become necessary.
Monitor inventory aging and packaway commitments relative to selling trends.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make added stores earn attractive local returns
cards.text: The network grew to 2,267 stores from 2,186. More locations extend reach, while occupancy, staffing and merchandise productivity determine whether expansion creates value.
items: Sequence openings around distribution readiness and attractive local customer demand.
Use early store performance to refine assortment and staffing plans.
Monitor new-store contribution after occupancy and operating costs.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Adapt buying economics to tariff-related cost pressure
cards.text: Management estimated an approximately $0.16 per-share tariff cost impact. Sourcing and mix decisions should preserve customer value while limiting the pressure on merchandise contribution.
items: Expand vendor alternatives where comparable merchandise quality and value are available.
Adjust buying mix using landed costs and customer price sensitivity.
Monitor contribution after tariff costs without losing the value proposition.

headline: Royal Caribbean should convert stronger cruise economics into cash for debt and ship commitments.
summary: Net yields increased while the disclosed non-fuel unit cost measure was broadly stable, supporting operating progress. Digital pre-cruise purchases improve spending visibility, while debt maturities and ship investment still require funding. The priority is protecting passenger contribution and allocating liquidity to obligations before assuming operating gains eliminate balance-sheet demands.
focusTitle: Preserve guest economics and sequence cash commitments.
focusText: Build on digital spending engagement and disciplined itinerary pricing, while keeping fuel and excluded expenses visible in cash planning. Match debt and fleet spending to dependable cash generation, treating undrawn facilities as financial flexibility rather than cash already earned.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the quality of passenger yield growth
cards.text: Non-GAAP net yields rose 3.8% as reported and 3.7% in constant currency. Pricing and onboard contribution should guide deployment rather than capacity expansion alone.
items: Prioritize itineraries with strong ticket and onboard contribution after variable costs.
Test promotions against retained passenger economics and booking quality.
Monitor pricing and onboard spending separately across comparable sailings.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep broad cost control behind the unit measure
cards.text: Non-GAAP net cruise costs excluding fuel per available passenger cruise day rose 0.1% as reported. Stability helps, while fuel and excluded expenses still consume resources.
items: Coordinate staffing and provisioning with sailing requirements and guest service needs.
Preserve maintenance planning that avoids disruption and expensive corrective work.
Monitor total cruise cash costs alongside the narrower adjusted unit measure.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn advance digital purchases into sustained guest value
cards.text: Nearly 50% of onboard revenue was booked before cruises, with 90% of those purchases digital. Advance engagement can support spending visibility when purchases are retained.
items: Improve digital offers around relevant guest plans before each sailing.
Coordinate pre-cruise purchases with onboard delivery capacity and service readiness.
Monitor conversion and refunds alongside total onboard contribution per guest.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Reserve liquidity for maturities and committed ship spending
cards.text: Liquidity was $7.2 billion including undrawn facilities, against $3.2 billion of scheduled 2026 debt maturities. Refinancing and new-ship commitments remain material cash considerations.
items: Align refinancing plans with ship payment and operating cash schedules.
Preserve available liquidity before approving discretionary fleet or shareholder spending.
Monitor cash and facility availability after debt and capital commitments.

headline: RTX should turn broad aerospace and defense demand into reliable, profitable deliveries.
summary: Collins, Pratt & Whitney and Raytheon all grew organically, while backlog provides substantial commercial and defense visibility. The priority is execution rather than order acquisition alone. Production capacity, engine service obligations and program costs must support delivery so strong demand becomes recurring operating contribution instead of larger unfulfilled commitments.
focusTitle: Allocate capacity around delivery constraints and program economics.
focusText: Coordinate supplier readiness, skilled labor and aftermarket support across the portfolio. Preserve profitable customer service while increasing production, and use backlog conversion and cost performance to govern investment rather than assuming commercial and defense demand carry identical operating requirements.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Translate backlog visibility into executable delivery plans
cards.text: Backlog was $268 billion, comprising $161 billion commercial and $107 billion defense. Contracted demand provides opportunity while schedules, cancellations and production readiness determine conversion.
items: Prioritize supplier and capacity constraints affecting committed customer delivery milestones.
Align long-lead procurement with contract schedules and funding certainty.
Monitor backlog conversion and program contribution across commercial and defense work.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Collins growth across equipment and aftermarket
cards.text: Collins Aerospace organic sales grew 9% on a non-GAAP basis. Original equipment and aftermarket demand can require different inventory and service resource decisions.
items: Allocate production and service capacity using customer equipment and repair requirements.
Protect aftermarket responsiveness while supporting scheduled original-equipment deliveries.
Monitor contribution and delivery reliability across the two demand streams.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Balance engine growth with fleet-support execution
cards.text: Pratt & Whitney non-GAAP organic sales increased 17%. Strong propulsion demand increases the importance of engine deliveries, shop capacity and ongoing customer service obligations.
items: Coordinate engine production with repair shop capacity and fleet-support requirements.
Prioritize bottlenecks that delay customer engines or create avoidable service costs.
Monitor delivery output and fleet-support spending as demand scales.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make defense growth earn its contract returns
cards.text: Raytheon non-GAAP organic sales grew 6%. Demand supports expansion, while throughput and fixed-price program economics remain important to the value of that growth.
items: Align production resources with funded defense delivery schedules.
Revalidate supplier and labor costs on fixed-price program commitments.
Monitor throughput and program cost changes before expanding capacity.

headline: S&P Global should deepen recurring data demand while managing issuance and market sensitivity.
summary: Subscriptions and Market Intelligence grew, supporting recurring customer relationships. Ratings benefited from issuance activity, while index-linked fees rose with much faster average ETF asset growth. The priority is sustainable workflow adoption and monetization, preserving the recurring base without assuming market-driven assets or financing activity will keep expanding at the same pace.
focusTitle: Allocate investment toward retained subscription and workflow value.
focusText: Preserve product quality and renewals while aligning Ratings capacity with issuance demand. Evaluate index economics using fee yield and flows as well as market appreciation, and keep portfolio comparisons consistent with the disclosed annual business perimeter.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Strengthen subscription value that supports renewals
cards.text: Subscription revenue increased 7% to $7.865 billion. Recurring relationships provide a foundation when customers continue finding value in the data and analytics they purchase.
items: Prioritize product improvements that deepen usage within existing subscriber workflows.
Allocate account support to adoption gaps and renewal requirements.
Monitor retention and contract economics alongside subscription revenue growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make Market Intelligence growth organic and retained
cards.text: Market Intelligence revenue rose 6%, with data, analytics and workflow demand alongside portfolio effects. Continuing product economics should determine where additional resources can earn returns.
items: Focus sales investment on workflows with demonstrated ongoing customer demand.
Integrate acquired capabilities where they improve existing customer utility.
Monitor organic adoption separately from acquisition and disposal effects.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep Ratings capacity flexible across issuance conditions
cards.text: Ratings revenue grew 8%, supported by corporate bonds and structured finance but offset partly by lower bank loan ratings. Financing activity can change the revenue mix.
items: Align analyst capacity with issuance demand while preserving analytical quality.
Protect surveillance resources required for ongoing rated obligations.
Monitor billed issuance and recurring surveillance contribution before expanding fixed costs.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Evaluate index growth through fees as well as assets
cards.text: Indices asset-linked fees rose 15% to $1.206 billion while annual average ETF assets rose 24%. Market levels and flows can influence assets differently from fees.
items: Prioritize index partnerships with sustainable fee economics and investor adoption.
Assess product mix when allocating development resources across index offerings.
Monitor net flows and fee yield separately from market appreciation.

headline: Salesforce should turn Agentforce and acquired contracts into retained, profitable customer usage.
summary: Subscription growth, GAAP margin and operating cash provide a strong base. Contracted obligations and Agentforce ARR indicate opportunity, but include acquisition effects or differ from recognized revenue. The priority is proving production adoption and renewals while keeping acquisition integration and new-product spending productive.
focusTitle: Connect contract growth to customer adoption and cash returns.
focusText: Prioritize deployment and renewal execution across the subscription base, with Agentforce resources directed toward durable production use. Integrate Informatica around customer value, and evaluate growth spending after acquisition costs and stock-based compensation rather than treating ARR or RPO as current revenue.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the subscription relationships funding expansion
cards.text: Subscription and support revenue increased to $39.388 billion from $35.679 billion. The dominant stream provides resources when renewals and product adoption remain durable.
items: Prioritize customer success support where purchased products remain underused.
Coordinate renewal plans around demonstrated workflow value and service needs.
Monitor retained subscription contribution and customer adoption across major products.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make Agentforce adoption tangible beyond annualized contracts
cards.text: Management reported Agentforce ARR of $800 million, up 169%. Contract scale supports opportunity but is different from recognized annual revenue or sustained production use.
items: Direct implementation resources toward customers moving Agentforce into production workflows.
Improve onboarding where customer usage fails to follow contracted adoption.
Monitor production activity and renewals alongside Agentforce contract value.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Convert obligations while separating acquired scale
cards.text: RPO was $72.4 billion, including approximately $2.2 billion from Informatica. The pipeline provides visibility, with recognition schedules and organic bookings guiding delivery capacity.
items: Align deployment staffing with committed recognition and customer implementation schedules.
Integrate Informatica capabilities where they support existing customer requirements.
Monitor organic obligation conversion separately from acquired contract additions.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep operating gains available for productive allocation
cards.text: GAAP operating margin reached 20.1% and operating cash was $15.0 billion. Both support investment while compensation and acquisition spending affect the economic return.
items: Rank incremental product spending by retained customer contribution and adoption.
Balance equity compensation and acquisition commitments with long-term shareholder economics.
Monitor cash after acquisition spending and the cost of scaling products.

headline: SBA should prioritize profitable tower leasing and funding flexibility over site count alone.
summary: Domestic leasing provides the larger revenue stream, while the international site base broadens operating reach. A large number of sites does not establish tenancy or attractive returns. The priority is extracting durable leasing contribution from existing assets while managing carrier, currency and refinancing exposure against substantial secured debt.
focusTitle: Allocate tower capital around tenant demand and debt capacity.
focusText: Prioritize amendments, retention and selective site investment supported by carrier requirements. Evaluate international operations using local leasing economics, and preserve refinancing flexibility so site expansion does not consume cash needed to service obligations or maintain covenant headroom.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen domestic leasing with disciplined carrier economics
cards.text: The annual revenue bridge identifies $1.866 billion of domestic site leasing revenue. Its weight makes carrier concentration, lease amendments and churn significant to recurring cash.
items: Prioritize amendments and renewals where carrier demand supports attractive contribution.
Coordinate site service and access around existing tenant requirements.
Monitor domestic churn and carrier concentration alongside leasing revenue.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make international diversification earn local returns
cards.text: International site leasing revenue was $705 million. Geographic exposure broadens the business while currency and local operating costs can change the cash contribution.
items: Allocate regional investment using local-currency tenant demand and operating returns.
Coordinate local costs and funding where possible with leasing cash receipts.
Monitor currency effects separately from underlying international leasing activity.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Use existing sites before adding marginal capacity
cards.text: SBA owned or operated 46,328 sites: 17,394 domestic and 28,934 international. The infrastructure offers leasing capacity, but tenant utilization determines its economic value.
items: Prioritize additional tenancy on sites with available profitable capacity.
Rank acquisitions and new builds using committed carrier demand.
Monitor tenancy and realized returns before expanding the site portfolio.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve tower cash for secured debt obligations
cards.text: Total debt was approximately $13.0 billion, including $10.0 billion secured. Refinancing and debt service are significant claims on recurring tower cash generation.
items: Sequence maturities and refinancing with expected leasing cash and capital needs.
Limit discretionary expansion where it reduces needed covenant or liquidity flexibility.
Monitor debt-service capacity and fixed-rate exposure under higher funding costs.

headline: SLB should align drilling resources with weaker demand while proving acquisition and digital returns.
summary: Well Construction declined, while reported Production Systems growth was entirely acquisition-influenced. Digital offered genuine ex-acquisition growth, and Data Center Solutions expanded rapidly from a smaller base. The priority is reallocating resources toward profitable customer demand without mistaking acquired scale or emerging businesses for a broad oilfield recovery.
focusTitle: Protect returns in the core and scale diversification selectively.
focusText: Adjust drilling capacity to regional customer activity, integrate ChampionX around recurring benefits, and prioritize digital adoption where operating value supports customer spending. Grow data-center exposure with concentration and capacity discipline so diversification improves returns rather than simply offsetting reported revenue weakness.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Reset Well Construction resources to customer spending
cards.text: Well Construction revenue declined 11% to $11.856 billion. Lower drilling-related demand calls for regional pricing and resource decisions rather than maintaining capacity for uncertain activity.
items: Align crews and equipment with funded drilling programs and regional utilization.
Prioritize contracts that preserve acceptable returns after operating costs.
Monitor customer capital plans and pricing before restoring incremental capacity.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make ChampionX integration deliver more than reported growth
cards.text: Production Systems revenue rose 12% to $13.325 billion but was flat excluding ChampionX. Organic demand and acquisition returns require separate operating assessments.
items: Integrate acquired operations around recurring cost and customer service benefits.
Preserve customer relationships while coordinating production equipment capabilities.
Monitor organic orders and acquired cash contribution after integration spending.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale digital where adoption produces repeat customer value
cards.text: Digital revenue increased 9% to $2.660 billion, or 7% excluding ChampionX. Underlying growth supports selective investment in software and digital operations.
items: Prioritize implementations with clear customer operating value and adoption readiness.
Use repeatable delivery methods to improve digital service economics.
Monitor retained usage and contribution separately from acquired digital revenue.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Grow data-center exposure without overcommitting capacity
cards.text: Data Center Solutions revenue rose 121% to $460 million. Rapid expansion adds diversification but remains smaller than traditional operations and needs disciplined scaling.
items: Allocate capacity around committed customer requirements and achievable delivery schedules.
Balance new customer development with exposure to concentrated large projects.
Monitor contribution and utilization before expanding related capital commitments.

headline: Sempra should align infrastructure spending with California recovery and committed funding.
summary: Texas earnings improved, while California earnings declined despite significant infrastructure investment. A proposed infrastructure stake sale could support funding but had not closed at the release date. The priority is disciplined project recovery and financing, preserving investment returns without treating prospective transaction proceeds as already available cash.
focusTitle: Coordinate investment, regulatory outcomes and transaction-dependent funding.
focusText: Prioritize projects with clear service benefits and recovery paths in Texas and California. Preserve alternatives for the capital program while the stake sale remains pending, and evaluate the cash benefit against reduced future infrastructure earnings participation before making further funding commitments.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Address the gap between California investment and earnings
cards.text: California earnings attributable to common shares fell to $1.428 billion from $1.846 billion. Regulatory disallowances and other comparability items matter before assuming underlying utility demand weakened.
items: Prioritize projects with well-supported recovery and effective regulatory execution.
Address operating or project practices associated with disallowed costs.
Monitor recurring California contribution after regulatory and other discrete effects.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make infrastructure spending deliver recoverable service value
cards.text: Sempra invested approximately $13 billion in infrastructure, primarily in Texas and California. The scale requires coordinated completion, financing and rate recovery.
items: Stage project spending around approved recovery and construction readiness.
Prioritize investments that address demonstrable capacity or reliability needs.
Monitor completed asset returns and financing costs as spending progresses.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Texas capital efficiency as earnings expand
cards.text: Texas Utilities earnings attributable to common shares increased to $861 million from $781 million. Growth supports the portfolio when Oncor investment earns appropriate regulated returns.
items: Extend project delivery practices that support efficient Texas infrastructure investment.
Coordinate capital schedules with applicable regulated recovery mechanisms.
Monitor Texas earnings contribution against incremental financing and capital requirements.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep the funding plan viable before the stake sale closes
cards.text: The agreed sale of a 45% infrastructure stake to KKR affiliates was for $10 billion. It remained pending, with proceeds and retained economics still consequential.
items: Maintain alternative funding capacity for committed projects until closing conditions resolve.
Allocate prospective net proceeds against existing funding needs before optional spending.
Monitor retained earnings participation alongside transaction funding benefits.

headline: ServiceNow should make large-account and contract growth produce durable subscription usage.
summary: Subscription revenue and current contracted obligations expanded, while the number of large customers increased. Strong operating cash supports investment. The priority is preserving renewal and deployment quality as relationships become larger, separating acquired obligations from organic demand and ensuring growth spending deepens customer value rather than contract scale alone.
focusTitle: Scale deployment and account support around retained contribution.
focusText: Prioritize adoption across major customers and coordinate implementation capacity with near-term contracted work. Use cash generation to support productive product and integration investment, while monitoring compensation and capital requirements so recurring growth remains economically attractive as the customer base deepens.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve subscription growth through successful customer use
cards.text: GAAP subscription revenue increased 21% to $12.883 billion. Recurring demand provides a strong base when new customers and existing accounts continue adopting the products they purchase.
items: Prioritize onboarding and workflow support where adoption is incomplete.
Coordinate renewal discussions around demonstrated customer value and expansion needs.
Monitor new customer retention separately from expansion within existing accounts.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Convert near-term obligations with clear delivery readiness
cards.text: Current remaining performance obligations reached $12.85 billion, up 25% as reported. Currency and acquisitions, including Moveworks, influence the snapshot and require separate capacity judgments.
items: Align implementation resources with expected subscription recognition and deployment schedules.
Integrate Moveworks capabilities where they improve existing customer workflows.
Monitor organic contract conversion separately from acquired obligations and currency effects.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Deepen large accounts without neglecting relationship risk
cards.text: Customers above $5 million in annual contract value reached 603, approximately 20% higher. Larger relationships increase the importance of enterprise deployment and renewal execution.
items: Assign coordinated account support to major customers with complex deployments.
