Prioritize adoption gaps before proposing additional enterprise contract expansion.
Monitor major-account renewals and concentration as contract values increase.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use cash capacity to fund productive scaling
cards.text: GAAP operating cash was $5.444 billion. That supports investment and acquisitions, while stock-based compensation and capital spending affect the broader economics of growth.
items: Rank product and integration spending by retained customer contribution.
Balance employee incentives with long-term dilution and operational requirements.
Monitor cash after capital needs alongside the cost of scaling.

headline: Sherwin-Williams should restore Consumer Brands and coatings profitability while protecting Paint Stores.
summary: Paint Stores increased segment profit on modest underlying store sales growth, providing a useful foundation. Consumer Brands and Performance Coatings earned less, showing that the broader portfolio needs attention. The priority is improving product and operating economics outside stores without mistaking acquisition-supported sales or flat industrial revenue for healthy contribution.
focusTitle: Allocate resources around segment demand and recurring contribution.
focusText: Preserve professional paint service and store productivity, while targeting Consumer Brands integration and weaker DIY economics. In industrial coatings, align costs and mix with end-market demand. Judge these decisions using the company’s segment profit measures rather than consolidated accounting gains.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make Consumer Brands growth profitable after integration
cards.text: Consumer Brands sales were $3.1664 billion, but segment profit fell to $509.6 million from $589.9 million. Acquisition-supported revenue did not preserve segment earnings.
items: Integrate Suvinil around identifiable operating benefits and customer continuity.
Adjust North American DIY assortments and spending to actual demand.
Monitor continuing contribution separately from acquired sales and integration costs.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore industrial coatings contribution on stable sales
cards.text: Performance Coatings sales were $6.7952 billion versus $6.7973 billion, while segment profit declined to $942.7 million from $1.0279 billion. Profitability needs targeted attention.
items: Prioritize industrial products and accounts with sustainable pricing and contribution.
Align manufacturing and commercial costs with end-market demand patterns.
Monitor mix and unit contribution before committing incremental coatings capacity.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Strengthen the volume behind modest store growth
cards.text: Paint Stores open more than twelve months increased sales 1.7%. Existing-location growth is positive but limited, making professional demand and pricing effects important.
items: Focus account support on professional repaint and commercial project opportunities.
Improve local availability and service where they increase customer conversion.
Monitor paint volumes separately from pricing within established stores.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Paint Stores operating leverage and service
cards.text: Paint Stores segment profit increased to $3.0615 billion from $2.9026 billion. The largest segment provides support when store costs and professional service remain disciplined.
items: Extend store operating practices that improve labor and inventory productivity.
Protect delivery and technical support required by repeat professional customers.
Monitor segment contribution alongside residential repaint and commercial demand.

headline: Simon should convert stronger retailer sales and redevelopment into durable leasing returns.
summary: Retailer productivity and base rents increased, while occupancy remained high with a slight decline. Extensive leasing and completed redevelopment support portfolio renewal. The priority is matching rent growth and capital spending to tenant health, ensuring signed activity becomes collected rental income rather than relying on noncash accounting gains as operating progress.
focusTitle: Prioritize tenant productivity and cash returns from refreshed space.
focusText: Use category-level retailer health to guide renewals, merchandising and redevelopment choices across U.S. malls and Premium Outlets. Preserve high occupancy while obtaining sustainable rents, and evaluate completed projects through lease commencements and contribution after capital costs.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use retailer productivity to strengthen the tenant mix
cards.text: Reported retailer sales reached $799 per square foot, up 8.1%, for the trailing twelve months. Stronger average productivity supports opportunity but varies across retail categories.
items: Prioritize leasing prospects that improve category balance and customer draw.
Use tenant sales trends to identify emerging renewal or merchandising needs.
Monitor category productivity and rent affordability rather than portfolio averages alone.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep higher rents compatible with retailer economics
cards.text: Base minimum rent increased 4.7% to $60.97 per square foot. Higher contractual rent supports income when tenants can sustain occupancy costs and remain viable.
items: Negotiate renewals using tenant productivity and local leasing alternatives.
Balance contractual rent increases with incentives needed for attractive retention.
Monitor occupancy costs and tenant payment performance after new rents begin.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect high occupancy by reducing avoidable downtime
cards.text: Occupancy was 96.4% versus 96.5%. The small decline is proportionate, while individual closures and renewal gaps can still affect rental cash and property attractiveness.
items: Begin renewal and replacement leasing before important tenant expirations.
Coordinate vacant-space preparation with incoming tenant build-out requirements.
Monitor closure exposure and leasing downtime by center.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make redevelopment and leasing activity earn capital returns
cards.text: Simon executed over 17 million square feet of leases and completed 23 significant redevelopment projects. Activity creates value when space opens and tenant demand supports investment.
items: Prioritize lease commencements and tenant opening readiness at completed redevelopments.
Allocate further project spending using expected contribution and tenant commitments.
Monitor project cash returns and tenant concentration as refreshed space stabilizes.

headline: Skyworks should turn higher R&D into design diversification while preserving cash and manufacturing returns.
summary: Apple-related revenue remained highly concentrated despite a small reduction in its share. R&D increased sharply, creating a greater need for commercial conversion, while gross margin was unchanged and operating cash provided flexibility. The priority is protecting valuable design positions and winning durable business beyond the largest customer.
focusTitle: Allocate development and cash around diversified product returns.
focusText: Prioritize engineering programs with credible qualification and customer demand, while maintaining the manufacturing capability required for existing business. Coordinate consolidation and investment with design schedules, and preserve funding flexibility so development commitments are supported even when concentrated product cycles shift.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Reduce design-cycle dependence through real customer wins
cards.text: Apple-related sales through multiple channels were 67% of revenue versus 69%. Concentration remains substantial, linking business results to one end customer’s designs and product cycles.
items: Protect content positions through reliable engineering and customer execution.
Prioritize diversification programs with credible qualification and production opportunities.
Monitor revenue and design progress outside the largest end customer.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make the R&D increase produce commercial milestones
cards.text: R&D expense rose 24.3% to $785.5 million. Higher spending needs product progress and design wins that justify the larger continuing development commitment.
items: Allocate engineering resources by technical milestones and customer qualification probability.
Reassess programs that consume resources without a credible production path.
Monitor customer wins and product contribution alongside development spending.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Preserve manufacturing economics through consolidation and mix changes
cards.text: GAAP gross margin held at 41.2%, while management cited mix, pricing and consolidation costs affecting gross profit. Stable margin can conceal offsetting operating pressures.
items: Coordinate facility consolidation with customer qualification and delivery requirements.
Align factory loading with confirmed product demand and inventory needs.
Monitor utilization and pricing contribution as consolidation costs evolve.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep operating cash available for essential product investment
cards.text: Operating cash was approximately $1.30 billion. That supports development and balance-sheet needs, provided capital spending and shareholder payouts do not consume necessary flexibility.
items: Prioritize capital required for committed customer programs and manufacturing reliability.
Size discretionary distributions after development and funding obligations.
Monitor cash available after capital investment under weaker design-cycle demand.

headline: Smurfit Westrock should make integration savings and capacity closures deliver durable cash returns.
summary: Management-reported synergies and stronger LATAM margin suggest integration progress. Capacity closures increase the need for dependable service from remaining assets, while operating cash comparisons reflect a changed business perimeter. The priority is preserving realized savings and customer contribution after closure, integration and investment costs rather than extrapolating headline annual cash growth.
focusTitle: Optimize the combined network around service and sustainable cash.
focusText: Embed integration benefits into operating routines while matching remaining capacity to customer requirements. Use comparable asset and cash economics to prioritize investment, and preserve successful regional practices without assuming the partial-year 2024 combination provides a like-for-like growth baseline.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Lock integration synergies into recurring operations
cards.text: Management reported exceeding its $400 million committed synergy target. Benefits support profitability when they remain after implementation costs and do not impair customer delivery.
items: Embed successful purchasing and operating changes across the combined network.
Assign remaining integration work clear cost and customer service outcomes.
Monitor recurring savings after integration expenses and retained operating requirements.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Preserve flexibility after removing high-cost capacity
cards.text: Approximately 600,000 tons of high-cost or inefficient capacity closed. Network optimization can improve returns while concentrating demand and delivery obligations on remaining facilities.
items: Rebalance customer orders across remaining mills using capacity and logistics economics.
Preserve contingency plans for outages at more heavily utilized facilities.
Monitor service reliability and closure costs alongside remaining plant utilization.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve LATAM’s stronger profitability through operating discipline
cards.text: LATAM non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA margin increased to 23.0% from 22.1%. Regional performance offers a strength to preserve through pricing, mix and input-cost management.
items: Protect customer pricing and product mix that support regional contribution.
Apply successful regional practices where other markets have comparable operating conditions.
Monitor volume and input costs alongside the adjusted margin improvement.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Allocate cash using the combined business’s recurring needs
cards.text: Operating cash was $3.392 billion versus $1.483 billion, but 2024 included the combined business only after July 5. The increase is not like-for-like.
items: Prioritize maintenance and integration commitments before discretionary capital returns.
Compare cash generation using a consistent operating perimeter where available.
Monitor cash after capital spending and integration payments before expanding commitments.

headline: Snap-on should rebuild tool demand while scaling repair systems without weakening credit quality.
summary: Commercial & Industrial and franchise tool sales were modestly lower, while Repair Systems & Information expanded. Financial Services adds substantial earnings but also credit exposure. The priority is product and channel execution tailored to those different demand patterns, with financing supporting viable purchases rather than substituting for healthy technician demand.
focusTitle: Balance tool recovery, repair-system adoption and disciplined financing.
focusText: Use account-level demand to adjust industrial and franchise inventory, while allocating product support to diagnostics and repair workflows showing adoption. Preserve appropriate underwriting so customer financing earns sustainable returns, and judge sales initiatives through retained contribution rather than financed volume alone.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve franchise tool conversion without overloading inventory
cards.text: Snap-on Tools sales were $1.9649 billion versus $1.9892 billion. Modest pressure calls for better technician demand and franchise execution rather than broad inventory loading.
items: Align franchisee inventory with technician purchase patterns and product interest.
Support demonstrations and offers that improve economically viable tool purchases.
Monitor sell-through and franchisee stock before increasing channel shipments.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Target industrial resources toward recoverable customer demand
cards.text: Commercial & Industrial sales were $1.4575 billion versus $1.4768 billion. Product, regional and critical-industry patterns should guide the response to softer reported demand.
items: Prioritize industrial accounts with funded maintenance and tool requirements.
Adapt product support to regional customer needs and application opportunities.
Monitor account conversion and product contribution across weaker industrial markets.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen repair-system adoption around customer workflows
cards.text: Repair Systems & Information sales increased to $1.8771 billion from $1.7979 billion. Diagnostics, software and equipment can support different demand from traditional tool purchases.
items: Coordinate diagnostics and software support with repair-shop workflow requirements.
Prioritize equipment opportunities that improve customer repair capability and productivity.
Monitor adoption and retained contribution across diagnostics, software and equipment.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep financing growth consistent with borrower quality
cards.text: Financial Services revenue was $412.9 million and operating earnings $281.8 million. Financing contributes meaningfully while exposing the business to customer payment and credit risk.
items: Price originations using borrower capacity and sustainable purchase economics.
Coordinate early collections support where customers show payment stress.
Monitor delinquencies and loss provisions alongside financing contribution.

headline: Solventum should turn continuing-business growth into stronger margins after transition costs.
summary: MedSurg, Dental and Health Information Systems all expanded organically, indicating a constructive demand base. Adjusted operating margin nevertheless declined, and divestiture effects complicate reported earnings. The priority is protecting customer adoption while improving the continuing cost structure rather than using the sale gain as evidence that operating profitability improved.
focusTitle: Preserve underlying demand while improving continuing operating contribution.
focusText: Allocate commercial and implementation support to the growing medical, dental and software businesses. Target transition and tariff pressure with specific operating improvements, and assess progress on a continuing basis so portfolio changes and historical carve-out accounting do not obscure the economics management can improve.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make growth cover the continuing operating cost base
cards.text: Non-GAAP adjusted operating margin declined to 20.5% from 22.0%. Transition expenses, tariffs and savings need operational attention even though the principal continuing segments grew.
items: Target transition work with identifiable recurring cost and service outcomes.
Address sourcing and tariff pressure while preserving product quality.
Monitor continuing contribution after transition costs rather than divestiture gains.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve medical demand through product and service reliability
cards.text: MedSurg non-GAAP organic sales increased 3.5%, with reported sales of $4.817 billion. The largest continuing segment provides a useful demand foundation.
items: Prioritize supply continuity for wound care and infection prevention customers.
Align clinical and commercial support with procedure-related product demand.
Monitor customer adoption and contribution alongside procedure activity.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Grow Dental through retained adoption and appropriate mix
cards.text: Dental Solutions non-GAAP organic sales increased 3.3%, with reported sales of $1.349 billion. Growth should be supported where product adoption and procedure demand justify resources.
items: Allocate technical sales support to products with demonstrated clinician adoption.
Align inventory and channel resources with regional dental procedure activity.
Monitor geographic mix and retained contribution as dental demand expands.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale health information software with disciplined delivery
cards.text: Health Information Systems non-GAAP organic sales increased 4.0%, with reported sales of $1.360 billion. Faster software growth needs successful implementation and retained customer use.
items: Prioritize implementation support where customers face adoption or workflow obstacles.
Coordinate renewal plans around demonstrated customer value and delivery requirements.
Monitor retention and contribution after implementation and support costs.

headline: Southern should keep operating cost growth from absorbing stronger electricity demand.
summary: Retail and wholesale electricity sales increased, and the regulated customer base expanded. Higher non-fuel O&M creates a separate profitability challenge, however. The priority is coordinating service capacity and cost recovery so demand growth improves utility economics without letting expense pressure or poorly sequenced infrastructure investment raise unnecessary customer costs.
focusTitle: Match service investment and recurring costs to recoverable demand.
focusText: Prioritize network and generation needs using customer growth and actual load requirements. Improve operating productivity while protecting reliability, and evaluate retail and wholesale economics separately because volume gains do not establish the same pricing, fuel or recovery outcomes in both channels.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Address O&M growth while protecting reliable service
cards.text: Non-fuel O&M increased to $7.066 billion from $6.518 billion. Higher recurring costs can offset demand benefits unless productivity and appropriate recovery keep pace.
items: Target avoidable operating work and procurement costs before reducing essential maintenance.
Align recurring expense plans with approved utility recovery mechanisms.
Monitor service outcomes and recovered costs after operating efficiency actions.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Translate retail demand into appropriate network decisions
cards.text: Retail electricity sales increased 1.6% to 151,336 million kWh. As-reported demand supports opportunity, but weather and customer-class mix affect what investment is justified.
items: Allocate network capacity using customer-class demand and localized load constraints.
Separate weather-related consumption from durable load when planning infrastructure.
Monitor retail contribution under regulated pricing rather than volume alone.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make wholesale growth earn its generation costs
cards.text: Wholesale electricity sales rose 4.7% to 52,504 million kWh. Faster volume growth is useful when contract pricing and generation costs support attractive contribution.
items: Coordinate generation dispatch with wholesale contract economics and reliability requirements.
Prioritize agreements that compensate for capacity and variable production costs.
Monitor realized wholesale contribution alongside fuel and generation cost changes.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Connect more customers without creating avoidable cost pressure
cards.text: Regulated utility customers reached 9.005 million, up 0.8%. Expanding service creates infrastructure needs that should be sequenced with connections and existing network capacity.
items: Coordinate connection schedules with feeder capacity and planned network work.
Prioritize upgrades where confirmed customer demand requires additional service capability.
Monitor connection delays and investment recovery as the customer base expands.

headline: Southwest should improve seat utilization and unit costs before expanding capacity further.
summary: Available seat miles increased while load factor declined, indicating weaker utilization of offered capacity. Non-fuel unit costs also rose, making route and operating productivity central. Fleet renewal provides an efficiency opportunity, but the priority is converting existing aircraft and schedules into better passenger economics rather than crediting later seating changes to 2025.
focusTitle: Align schedules with passenger demand and dependable aircraft productivity.
focusText: Use route contribution, fares and traffic to redeploy capacity where it can earn a return. Preserve operational reliability as fleet renewal changes maintenance requirements, and judge revenue initiatives against load factor and underlying unit costs rather than assuming additional capacity will resolve weaker utilization.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Recover load factor through route and schedule choices
cards.text: Load factor fell to 77.4% from 80.4%, a 3.0-point decline. Fewer offered seats were filled, increasing the need to balance traffic, fares and capacity.
items: Redeploy frequencies from weak demand periods toward stronger passenger opportunities.
Test fares and offers using total route contribution rather than bookings alone.
Monitor traffic and load factor after each schedule adjustment.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require capacity additions to earn adequate contribution
cards.text: Available seat miles rose 1.6% to 180,046 million. Capacity expanded despite lower load factor, so additional flying needs a clear passenger demand and return case.
items: Prioritize flying with credible demand after labor and airport costs.
Adjust seasonal schedules before committing resources to persistently weak routes.
Monitor route contribution and seat utilization before adding incremental capacity.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make productivity offset underlying unit cost pressure
cards.text: Non-GAAP CASM excluding fuel, profit sharing and special items increased 3.1%. Improving revenue economics also requires labor and airport resources to become more productive.
items: Coordinate crew and ground schedules with actual flight and passenger requirements.
Reduce avoidable turnaround work while preserving operational reliability.
Monitor labor and airport productivity alongside the disclosed non-fuel unit measure.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Convert fleet renewal into practical operating efficiency
cards.text: Southwest received 55 Boeing 737-8 aircraft and retired 55, ending with 803 aircraft. Renewal changes fleet economics without increasing the overall aircraft count.
items: Align maintenance and crew readiness with the changing aircraft mix.
Allocate renewed aircraft where utilization and operating economics support deployment.
Monitor maintenance costs and aircraft availability after deliveries and retirements.

headline: Stanley Black & Decker needs tool demand to catch up with its margin recovery.
summary: Better gross margin and Tools & Outdoor profitability show progress despite weaker organic sales. Cash also supported debt reduction. The next priority is turning those improvements into profitable tool demand while preserving the cash available for further deleveraging.
focusTitle: Make the improved cost base support profitable sell-through.
focusText: Direct commercial resources toward tool categories and channels that can grow without heavy discounting. Judge the recovery through organic demand, segment profit and cash together, so stronger reported margins do not mask continued customer weakness.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Rebuild demand without buying unprofitable volume
cards.text: FY2025 organic sales fell 1%, making customer demand the clearest unfinished part of the recovery. Higher margins alone cannot establish that the tools business has regained momentum.
items: Prioritize tool categories with stronger retailer sell-through and repeat orders.
Test channel promotions against incremental unit profit before expanding them.
Monitor orders and inventory together to avoid pushing excess stock downstream.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the economics behind gross margin gains
cards.text: Gross margin improved 90 basis points to 30.3% despite softer organic sales. That creates room to support demand, provided commercial spending does not give back the improvement.
items: Carry cost and sourcing improvements into product-level pricing decisions.
Allocate savings to launches with clear customer demand and attractive margins.
Watch realized pricing and product mix as sales volumes change.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep cash available for further debt reduction
cards.text: Operating cash flow of $971 million and non-GAAP free cash flow of $688 million supported approximately $240 million of debt reduction, giving cash discipline a practical strategic role.
items: Link inventory purchases to tool orders and channel replenishment needs.
Prioritize required capital spending before allocating discretionary cash.
Compare recurring cash generation with working capital releases when sizing debt repayments.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Extend Tools & Outdoor profitability into growth
cards.text: Tools & Outdoor segment margin rose from 9.0% to 10.1%. Protecting that improvement while rebuilding sales is more useful than treating margin and volume as separate goals.
items: Set channel plans using contribution profit alongside unit sales.
Protect product availability in profitable Tools & Outdoor categories.
Monitor segment margin as promotions and production volumes respond to demand.

headline: Starbucks needs more North American visits to justify turnaround spending.
summary: Higher tickets have not offset fewer global visits, and North America is weaker still. China offers a different challenge: transactions increased while ticket fell. With adjusted margin sharply lower, spending should improve repeat visits and store economics together.
focusTitle: Use store execution to rebuild profitable visit frequency.
focusText: Concentrate turnaround resources on the customer experience and operating routines that can restore North American traffic. Keep China promotion economics separate, and require better visit retention before broadening spending that further burdens margins.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn customer activity into repeat visits
cards.text: FY2025 global comparable sales fell 1%, combining a 2% transaction decline with a 1% ticket increase. Pricing and mix have not compensated for fewer customer occasions.
items: Test service and menu changes against repeat visits at participating stores.
Target offers toward incremental occasions rather than routine discount redemption.
Monitor transaction recovery separately from ticket changes and promotional mix.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Put North American store execution first
cards.text: North American comparable transactions fell 4% while ticket rose 2%. The core region therefore needs a visit recovery stronger than the global picture implies.
items: Prioritize stores with persistent traffic losses for operational support.
Align staffing and order handling with observed peak-period demand.
Compare repeat visits and service speed across store formats before scaling changes.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep China volume growth economically useful
cards.text: China transactions increased 4%, but average ticket declined 5%. More activity may be helpful, yet the spending tradeoff means customer counts alone cannot prove stronger unit economics.
items: Evaluate promotions using incremental contribution after discounts and store labor.
Tailor product bundles to preserve customer value without automatic price cuts.
Track whether acquired visits return when promotional offers end.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make turnaround investment earn a store-level return
cards.text: GAAP operating margin was 7.9%; non-GAAP margin was 9.9%, down 510 basis points. Both the ongoing economics and excluded costs matter when allocating recovery spending.
items: Tie additional store investment to measurable service and traffic improvements.
Separate temporary restructuring cash needs from continuing staffing commitments.
Monitor store contribution alongside transactions before expanding successful-looking pilots.

headline: State Street should convert won servicing mandates into durable fee growth.
summary: Custody and managed assets expanded substantially, but asset balances can benefit from markets as well as client activity. The uninstalled servicing pipeline provides a more concrete execution priority, while a large product launch program needs disciplined commercial follow-through.
focusTitle: Put implementation capacity behind fee-bearing client growth.
focusText: Prioritize mandate installation and product adoption where expected fees justify the service cost. Use net client flows, realized fee rates and implementation progress to distinguish a larger asset base from more durable earning capacity.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn custody scale into profitable relationships
cards.text: Year-end assets under custody and administration reached $53.8 trillion, up 16%. Larger balances can support fees, but their business value depends on client retention, pricing and servicing requirements.
items: Allocate servicing capacity to relationships with sustainable fee economics.
Use client reviews to deepen mandates where additional services meet clear needs.
Monitor net new assets separately from market appreciation and fee concessions.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect fee quality as managed assets expand
cards.text: Assets under management increased 20% to $5.665 trillion at year end. The increase creates commercial capacity, although asset growth and revenue growth need not move together.
items: Direct distribution resources toward strategies showing repeatable client demand.
Evaluate mandate growth using net flows and effective fee rates together.
Watch product mix for asset gains that dilute management fee economics.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Move uninstalled wins into live servicing
cards.text: Uninstalled servicing wins represented $320 million of fee revenue and $2.5 trillion of assets at year end. Winning mandates creates opportunity; installations determine when that opportunity becomes operating business.
items: Assign implementation resources according to client readiness and fee potential.
Resolve onboarding dependencies with clients before they delay asset transfers.
Track installation milestones, realized fees and implementation cost by mandate.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make product breadth earn its complexity
cards.text: Investment Management launched 134 products in 2025. A broader offering needs sufficient client adoption to justify distribution, administration and ongoing support across the expanded range.
items: Prioritize distribution for launches addressing demonstrated client demand.
Consolidate support where similar products fragment flows and operating effort.
Assess net flows and contribution economics by launch cohort before adding variants.

headline: Steel Dynamics needs better realized spreads while funding the aluminum ramp.
summary: Record steel shipments did not prevent lower steel and fabrication income. Selling-price pressure makes profitability per ton more important than volume alone, while aluminum growth working capital adds a separate cash requirement that should be paced against execution.
focusTitle: Manage for cash-producing production rather than shipment records.
focusText: Coordinate steel order pricing, fabrication commitments and aluminum funding around realized contribution and cash collection. Maintain volume where it earns adequate returns, while keeping new-platform spending tied to commissioning and customer delivery progress.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep shipment strength economically productive
cards.text: FY2025 steel shipments reached 13.7 million tons. That volume demonstrates operating activity, but the accompanying profit declines mean shipment records should not determine production or commercial incentives by themselves.
items: Prioritize mill schedules using product contribution and customer delivery commitments.
Coordinate output with firm orders to limit finished inventory accumulation.
Monitor realized spread and cash collection alongside tons shipped.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Defend price realization as contracts reset
cards.text: Average external steel selling price fell $15 to $1,089 per ton. Price pressure can absorb the benefit of higher shipments, making order mix and contract terms central to recovery.
items: Review contract repricing against current input costs before accepting volume.
Shift available capacity toward products with stronger realized contribution.
Track discounts and realized prices by product rather than aggregate sales alone.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Restore fabrication economics as well as steelmaking
cards.text: Fabrication operating income declined $260 million and steel operations income declined $155 million. The weakness spans two activities, so a steel shipment recovery alone would leave part of the problem unresolved.
items: Price new fabrication orders against steel inputs and execution requirements.
Match fabrication capacity commitments to profitable booked work.
Monitor order margins and delivery costs separately for fabrication and steel operations.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Tie aluminum cash commitments to operating progress
cards.text: Operating cash flow was $1.4 billion after $450 million of growth working capital for the aluminum platform. The ramp therefore competes meaningfully for cash even before judging its eventual returns.
items: Stage aluminum inventory purchases around commissioning and customer acceptance milestones.
Coordinate supplier payments and customer collections to contain funding peaks.
Monitor working capital release as aluminum shipments become cash receipts.

headline: STERIS should turn procedure-linked growth into sustained cash-funded capacity.
summary: Continuing operations delivered organic constant-currency growth and stronger operating and free cash flow. The opportunity is to maintain service capacity and cash conversion as demand grows. The gap between reported and adjusted earnings also matters when sizing sustainable investment commitments.
focusTitle: Expand where procedure demand supports dependable cash returns.
focusText: Use the stronger cash position to maintain service reliability and selectively add capacity. Assess investments against recurring collections, required capital spending and reported costs, preserving the distinction between adjusted earnings and resources actually available.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support underlying demand with reliable service capacity
cards.text: FY2026 non-GAAP organic constant-currency revenue from continuing operations increased 7%. Growth beyond acquisitions and currency supports investment in the operations serving procedure-related demand.
items: Prioritize service capacity where procedure-related orders indicate persistent demand.
Coordinate staffing and equipment availability to protect customer turnaround times.
Monitor service-line growth and capacity utilization before approving further expansion.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve collection discipline as activity rises
cards.text: Operating cash flow increased to $1.34 billion from $1.15 billion. Stronger cash provides flexibility, provided collections and working capital remain aligned with the expanding continuing business.
items: Align billing and collections with completed service and equipment delivery milestones.
Match consumable and equipment inventories to customer activity.
Monitor receivables and cash conversion alongside procedure-related revenue growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Allocate free cash after protecting essential capacity
cards.text: Non-GAAP free cash flow increased to $982.9 million from $787.2 million. The improvement supports investment choices, but required maintenance and expansion commitments still determine deployable cash.
items: Protect maintenance spending that sustains service reliability and customer availability.
Rank expansion proposals by expected utilization and cash payback.
Compare recurring capital requirements with cash remaining before other allocations.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Base recurring commitments on full business economics
cards.text: Continuing-operations diluted EPS was $7.93 versus adjusted diluted EPS of $10.17. The difference affects how much recurring investment the business can comfortably support, even with stronger cash generation.
items: Distinguish recurring operating costs from excluded items when budgeting service expansion.
Include associated cash costs in capital allocation decisions.
Monitor reported profitability and operating cash together when judging investment capacity.

headline: Stryker should protect execution capacity and margin as procedure volumes expand.
summary: Growth was predominantly volume-led, with both MedSurg and Neurotechnology and Orthopaedics contributing. Adjusted margin also improved. The priority is sustaining reliable delivery and clinical adoption while preventing capacity costs or implant pricing pressure from eroding those favorable economics.
focusTitle: Scale delivery and support around profitable procedure demand.
focusText: Preserve the operating practices behind margin expansion while allocating capacity to the categories gaining volume. Evaluate commercial investment through adoption, service reliability and contribution, with particular attention to Orthopaedics pricing as procedure activity grows.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Keep delivery capacity ahead of volume requirements
cards.text: FY2025 organic sales increased 10.3%, comprising 9.9% volume and 0.4% pricing. The balance makes product availability and execution more important to continued growth than broad price increases.
items: Align manufacturing and field support resources with procedure-related orders.
Resolve installation and replenishment bottlenecks in high-volume categories.
Monitor delivery reliability and inventory availability alongside unit growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen MedSurg adoption without overextending support
cards.text: MedSurg and Neurotechnology organic sales increased 10.7%. Continued expansion should be matched by hospital onboarding and support capacity so commercial wins translate into productive customer use.
items: Prioritize hospital deployments where staffing and workflow readiness support adoption.
Coordinate sales and service teams around customer implementation needs.
Track category demand and utilization when allocating additional commercial resources.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect implant economics as Orthopaedics volumes rise
cards.text: Orthopaedics organic sales grew 9.5% despite a 0.1% pricing decline. Volume provides momentum, but discounting and product mix deserve attention as the business pursues further procedure growth.
items: Evaluate implant bids using price realization and service cost together.
Align implant inventory and field coverage with regional procedure demand.
Monitor volume, price and product mix separately across Orthopaedics markets.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Reinvest margin gains selectively
cards.text: Adjusted operating margin expanded 100 basis points to 26.3%. Better profitability alongside growth offers room to support demand, provided expansion spending preserves the operating leverage already achieved.
items: Fund capacity additions where customer demand and utilization support returns.
Carry productivity improvements into production and service planning.
Monitor incremental profit alongside growth and costs excluded from adjusted results.

headline: Supermicro needs profitable AI deployments that do not outrun funding capacity.
summary: Management linked rapid sales growth to AI demand, but narrow adjusted gross margin leaves limited room for deployment errors. Large customer projects and substantial financing obligations make acceptance timing, inventory funding and contribution per system more important than sales growth alone.
focusTitle: Connect each major AI deployment to margin and cash milestones.
focusText: Coordinate procurement, customer acceptance and financing around contracted deployment needs. Broaden profitable demand where practical, and use the unaudited annual results as a baseline for checking whether sales momentum produces durable gross profit and cash.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make AI demand translate into repeatable deployment economics
cards.text: Management attributed 47% FY2025 sales growth to AI solution demand across several customer types. That supports commercial momentum, while leaving execution quality as the determinant of the growth’s financial value.
items: Prioritize AI configurations with clear customer readiness and contribution economics.
Coordinate system integration and delivery capacity before committing deployment dates.
Monitor accepted shipments and gross profit per deployment alongside order growth.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Protect the limited gross margin cushion
cards.text: FY2025 non-GAAP gross margin was 11.2%. At that level, component costs, configuration changes and execution overruns can materially affect the profit generated by large hardware programs.
items: Include component availability and integration effort in customer pricing decisions.
Control configuration changes after procurement commitments are made.
Track product-level gross profit and rework costs before expanding lower-margin programs.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Reduce dependence on individual deployment schedules
cards.text: Management described four large-scale datacenter customers, rather than the total customer base. Large deployments can produce uneven activity, making customer acceptance milestones important for production and collection planning.
items: Agree acceptance requirements with large deployment customers before shipment.
Stage production against confirmed site readiness and delivery windows.
Monitor customer exposure and delayed acceptances when allocating additional capacity.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Match inventory funding to financing obligations
cards.text: Year-end cash was $5.2 billion against $4.8 billion of bank debt and convertible notes. Cash balances therefore need to be considered alongside procurement needs and financing commitments.
items: Build deployment cash plans covering component payments and customer collections.
Reserve liquidity for contractual debt and note obligations.
Monitor inventory aging and funding needs before accepting additional large orders.

headline: Synopsys should stabilize Design IP while converting its expanded portfolio into revenue.
summary: Design Automation grew and management reported substantial backlog, while Design IP revenue declined. Ansys also contributed meaningfully to annual revenue. The business priority is therefore balanced execution: repair the weaker offering, integrate acquired demand and convert contracts without confusing acquisition scale with underlying momentum.
focusTitle: Use the expanded portfolio to deliver contracted customer value.
focusText: Align integration and engineering resources with backlog conversion and Design IP customer needs. Judge progress using implementation, renewals and business-level revenue, keeping Ansys contributions distinct when evaluating the growth of the existing portfolio.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make Ansys integration commercially productive
cards.text: Ansys contributed $756.6 million of FY2025 revenue. The contribution expands the reported business, while creating a need to retain acquired customer relationships and coordinate the broader offering.
items: Prioritize customer continuity during product and commercial integration.
Test combined offerings against clear engineering workflow needs.
Track acquired customer retention and integration costs separately from existing-business growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Convert backlog with disciplined delivery capacity
cards.text: Management reported $11.4 billion of year-end backlog. It provides contracted visibility, but the business benefit depends on delivery schedules, customer readiness and conversion into recognized revenue.
items: Allocate engineering and deployment resources to contracted delivery milestones.
Resolve customer dependencies that could delay backlog conversion.
Monitor recognized revenue, cancellations and implementation effort by contract cohort.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Address the specific sources of Design IP weakness
cards.text: Design IP revenue declined to $1.752 billion from $1.906 billion. The weaker business needs targeted product and customer execution, rather than assuming broader portfolio growth will resolve its decline.
items: Prioritize customer programs where IP availability affects design decisions.
Match development resources to demonstrated licensing and support demand.
Monitor design commitments, renewals and revenue conversion across IP categories.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect Design Automation momentum during integration
cards.text: Design Automation revenue increased to $5.302 billion from $4.221 billion. That strength supports the broader portfolio, but resources should preserve customer delivery while management integrates Ansys and addresses IP performance.
items: Protect engineering capacity serving active Design Automation customer programs.
Evaluate cross-selling through customer adoption and incremental contribution.
Separate acquired revenue from existing product performance in resource allocation.

headline: Sysco needs distribution productivity to catch up with sales growth.
summary: Case volumes and cash generation improved, and gross margin edged higher despite product inflation. Operating expenses, however, rose faster than sales. The priority is preserving service-led demand while improving the cost of handling and delivering each case.
focusTitle: Translate case growth into stronger delivery economics.
focusText: Focus operating improvements on route density, warehouse handling and local account profitability. Preserve customer service while using cash generation to fund productivity investments whose returns can be tested against case volumes and recurring operating costs.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build local growth through productive customer service
cards.text: FY2026 U.S. Foodservice case volume rose 1.4%, with local case volume up 1.7%. Growth in physical activity is useful evidence of demand beyond product cost inflation.
items: Prioritize local accounts that improve route density and repeat ordering.
Coordinate assortment and delivery frequency with customer usage patterns.
Monitor case retention and contribution after delivery costs by account.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve gross profit while managing food inflation
cards.text: Gross margin increased 10 basis points to 18.5%, alongside 3.0% product cost inflation. The improvement should be defended without letting price increases weaken customer relationships or case demand.
items: Align customer pricing updates with product costs and contract terms.
Offer assortment choices that preserve customer value and gross profit.
Monitor realized margin and case volumes together after pricing changes.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Bring operating expense growth below the activity it supports
cards.text: Operating expenses rose 5.6%, exceeding sales growth of 3.9%. With only modest case growth, operating productivity is the clearest opportunity to improve the earnings value of demand.
items: Rebalance routes and warehouse workflows around actual case throughput.
Target avoidable handling and delivery effort without weakening order accuracy.
Track cost per case and service reliability when judging efficiency changes.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use stronger cash to fund measurable productivity
cards.text: Operating cash flow rose 5.1% to $2.6 billion and non-GAAP free cash flow increased 16.3%. Cash provides flexibility to support service and efficiency if investments improve recurring economics.
items: Rank distribution investments by handling savings and customer-service benefits.
Keep inventory purchasing aligned with case demand and product shelf life.
Monitor cash conversion and realized operating savings after capital deployment.

headline: T-Mobile should preserve retention while scaling phone and broadband growth.
summary: Postpaid phone additions, broadband additions and service revenue all point to expansion. The next priority is maintaining customer quality and network economics as the base grows, using churn and the profitability of new connections to guide acquisition spending.
focusTitle: Make customer expansion reinforce retention and network returns.
focusText: Coordinate phone acquisition and broadband availability with service capacity and durable account economics. Judge commercial offers by retained service revenue and contribution after support costs, preserving the benefits of growth as the installed customer base expands.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep phone acquisition focused on durable accounts
cards.text: FY2025 postpaid phone net additions totaled 3.3 million. The growth supports scale, while the value of each addition depends on retention, service contribution and the cost of winning the account.
items: Allocate acquisition offers using expected retained service contribution.
Improve onboarding so new phone customers reach reliable service quickly.
Track new-customer retention and acquisition cost by offer and channel.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect retention as the customer base expands
cards.text: Postpaid phone churn was 0.93%. This annual measure deserves attention alongside additions because losing existing customers can offset the value of successful acquisition programs.
items: Prioritize service fixes where customer complaints signal avoidable departures.
Test retention offers against sustained account contribution after incentives.
Monitor churn by customer tenure and service experience before scaling offers.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Scale broadband where network capacity supports the economics
cards.text: Broadband net additions reached 2.0 million, including 1.9 million 5G additions. That creates an additional use of network capacity whose service quality and contribution should be assessed locally.
items: Match broadband availability to location-level capacity and customer experience.
Coordinate installation and support resources with new broadband demand.
Monitor broadband retention and network performance alongside connection growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Convert service revenue growth into recurring contribution
cards.text: Postpaid service revenue grew 11% to $57.9 billion. The stronger recurring base creates room to invest, provided promotions and support requirements do not absorb the economic benefit.
items: Evaluate bundles using account contribution across phone and broadband services.
Prioritize network investment where retention and usage support returns.
Monitor service revenue per account and promotional costs alongside total growth.

headline: T. Rowe Price needs to stem outflows and realign costs with fee economics.
summary: Higher asset balances supported the business, but substantial client outflows and a lower advisory fee rate weakened the quality of that growth. Expenses also outpaced advisory fees. Retention, product mix and operating discipline should take precedence over relying on favorable asset markets.
focusTitle: Rebuild client retention while protecting investment capability.
focusText: Focus distribution and product resources on strategies that can retain assets at sustainable fee rates. Align support costs with realized advisory revenue, preserving the investment and client-service capabilities needed to improve flows rather than cutting uniformly.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Address the client decisions behind asset losses
cards.text: FY2025 net client outflows totaled $56.9 billion. This is the clearest signal that a larger year-end asset base does not by itself demonstrate stronger customer demand.
items: Prioritize retention conversations in strategies with persistent redemption activity.
Use client feedback to refine product positioning and distribution support.
Monitor gross sales and redemptions separately to judge whether interventions work.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn asset scale into durable relationships
cards.text: Year-end assets under management rose 10.5% to $1.776 trillion, while average assets grew 7.4%. That scale supports the fee base, but market gains should be distinguished from client wins.
items: Use existing client relationships to identify suitable additional mandates.
Allocate service resources according to relationship value and retention opportunity.
Separate market appreciation from net flows when assessing commercial performance.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect fee realization through product and channel choices
cards.text: The advisory fee rate excluding performance fees declined to 39.4 basis points from 41.0. Lower yield on assets reduces how much revenue asset growth can generate.
items: Evaluate new mandates using expected fees after servicing and distribution costs.
Prioritize products where investment capability supports durable client value.
Monitor fee concessions and strategy mix alongside assets won or retained.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Reset expense growth around earned fee revenue
cards.text: Operating expenses increased 7.7%, versus 3.2% growth in investment advisory fees. The mismatch requires selective productivity action even while the firm works to improve flows.
items: Reallocate support spending from low-demand offerings to priority client strategies.
Simplify duplicated servicing and distribution workflows where practical.
Monitor expense growth against recurring advisory fees and retention outcomes.

headline: Take-Two should convert recurring player spending into stronger reported economics.
summary: Bookings grew strongly and recurrent consumer spending supplied most of the activity. Major franchises support the opportunity, but a GAAP loss shows that commercial momentum has not yet established reported profitability. Development and live-service spending should be disciplined around durable player value.
focusTitle: Make franchise investment earn returns beyond bookings growth.
focusText: Preserve the engagement supporting recurrent spending while directing development and marketing toward projects with credible lifetime economics. Assess franchise health, cash commitments and reported results together instead of treating higher bookings as a completed profitability recovery.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Translate booking momentum into economic returns
cards.text: FY2026 net bookings increased 19% to $6.72 billion. The stronger customer spending supports investment, while delivery, recognition and operating costs determine the profit eventually realized.
items: Prioritize content investment using expected lifetime contribution and player demand.
Align marketing commitments with release readiness and measurable acquisition quality.
Monitor bookings conversion into revenue and cash by release cohort.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve engagement behind recurrent spending
cards.text: Recurrent consumer spending bookings rose 17% and represented 78% of total bookings. That makes sustained engagement and player retention especially important to the economics of the portfolio.
items: Fund live-service updates that improve sustained player participation.
Test monetization changes against retention as well as spending per user.
Monitor repeat spending and engagement after major content updates.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Manage franchise dependence through selective development
cards.text: NBA 2K, Grand Theft Auto Online, Toon Blast and Borderlands 4 were major bookings contributors. Their importance argues for focused execution while testing additional content without indiscriminate expansion.
items: Protect development and service resources for the major contributing franchises.
Stage additional project spending around playable milestones and customer evidence.
Compare contribution and player retention across franchises before reallocating budgets.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Close the gap between commercial growth and reported profit
cards.text: The company recorded a $298.2 million GAAP net loss despite bookings growth. That outcome calls for scrutiny of project economics and recurring spending rather than assuming all growth has equal value.
items: Tie development approvals to full project costs and expected commercial returns.
Identify operating commitments that scale faster than profitable player activity.
Monitor reported profitability and cash requirements alongside bookings performance.

headline: Tapestry should repair Kate Spade while preserving Coach-led customer growth.
summary: Coach and direct-to-consumer growth show considerable strength, supported by a large intake of new consumers. Kate Spade moved in the opposite direction. The priority is brand-specific execution that rebuilds weaker demand without compromising the customer relationships and channel economics already working.
focusTitle: Allocate growth resources by brand economics and customer retention.
focusText: Protect Coach product momentum and the direct customer experience, while making Kate Spade investment conditional on stronger product response. Use new-customer repeat purchases and full-price selling to judge whether acquisition translates into durable brand value.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect Coach momentum with disciplined product availability
cards.text: Coach FY2026 revenue increased 24%, or 23% in constant currency. The strength supports continued investment where product demand and customer experience can sustain attractive selling economics.
items: Prioritize inventory availability in Coach products with demonstrated customer demand.
Use customer feedback to guide assortment depth and new product investment.
Monitor full-price sell-through and repeat purchasing alongside brand revenue.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Give Kate Spade a distinct recovery plan
cards.text: Kate Spade revenue fell 10%, or 11% in constant currency. Stronger group brands cannot resolve this demand weakness without focused work on the offering and customer response.
items: Test product and assortment changes with Kate Spade customers before scaling.
Align inventory commitments with observed sell-through to contain markdown exposure.
Monitor conversion and full-price sales after changes to product or promotion.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn new consumers into durable brand relationships
cards.text: Tapestry welcomed approximately 11 million new consumers, with about 35% from Gen Z. Acquisition creates opportunity, but retention determines how much future value those relationships produce.
items: Tailor post-purchase engagement to the product and brand customers selected.
Allocate acquisition spending using repeat contribution after marketing costs.
Track repeat purchases and retention across newly acquired consumer cohorts.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Preserve direct-channel economics as sales expand
cards.text: Direct-to-consumer revenue grew 16% on a pro forma constant-currency basis, excluding Stuart Weitzman. Scaling the channel should maintain customer service and contribution after fulfillment and acquisition costs.
items: Improve store and digital availability around demonstrated brand demand.
Evaluate promotions using incremental contribution after fulfillment and marketing.
Monitor direct-channel conversion and returns while keeping the pro forma scope consistent.

headline: Targa should match Permian growth and shareholder returns to cash-generating capacity.
summary: Permian gas volumes and NGL production grew, accompanied by stronger adjusted EBITDA. That supports the operating model, while continued growth and repurchases compete for capital. The priority is preserving reliable throughput economics before committing cash that may be needed by the network.
focusTitle: Allocate capital around integrated volume economics and funding resilience.
focusText: Coordinate gas handling and NGL capacity so physical growth supports dependable cash generation. Size discretionary returns after operating and growth requirements, using adjusted EBITDA as an operating indicator while checking the cash that remains available.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep gathering capacity aligned with producer activity
cards.text: Permian natural gas inlet volume averaged 6,391.4 MMcf/d, up 11%. The increase supports network utilization, provided capacity and service reliability keep pace with the specific locations generating demand.
items: Prioritize operating resources where confirmed producer activity supports throughput.
Coordinate maintenance with customer production schedules to protect availability.
Monitor inlet volumes and capacity utilization by operating area.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Coordinate NGL growth with the rest of the network
cards.text: Permian NGL production averaged 880.6 MBbl/d, up 12%. Growing output makes coordination between processing and downstream handling important to realizing the value of the additional activity.
items: Match NGL handling commitments to expected processing output and customer needs.
Stage capacity additions around demonstrated bottlenecks and contracted activity.
Monitor throughput, operating reliability and contribution across linked assets.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the profitability behind higher activity
cards.text: Adjusted EBITDA rose 20% to $4.96 billion. Stronger earnings alongside physical growth provide a useful signal, while sustaining the improvement requires operating discipline and economically sound expansion.
items: Rank growth projects using expected incremental cash contribution.
Protect maintenance and operating reliability as network utilization expands.
Monitor unit economics and cash conversion alongside adjusted EBITDA growth.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep repurchases subordinate to network and funding needs
cards.text: Common share repurchases totaled $642 million. Discretionary capital returns should be assessed alongside the cash required to maintain and expand operations as Permian activity grows.
items: Reserve funding for committed projects and essential operating requirements.
Evaluate buybacks against available cash after capital and financing obligations.
Monitor liquidity headroom as throughput growth changes working capital needs.

headline: Target needs demand and inventory discipline to restore store economics.
summary: Lower comparable sales coincided with weaker gross margin and a high adjusted expense rate. Markdown, cancellation and mix pressure make inventory decisions central to recovery. Higher interest expense further reduces flexibility, so rebuilding profitable sales matters more than expense cuts alone.
focusTitle: Rebuild profitable demand with tighter inventory and cost commitments.
focusText: Align assortment, purchases and store labor with customer response, then reinvest selectively where conversion and full-price selling improve. Preserve cash for financing needs while evaluating recovery through comparable sales, gross profit and expense productivity together.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore customer demand at profitable prices
cards.text: FY2025 comparable sales declined 2.6%. The decline makes existing-store relevance and conversion the immediate commercial priority, rather than relying solely on reduced expense dollars.
items: Test assortment and value changes in categories with persistent sales weakness.
Target promotions toward incremental trips and profitable basket additions.
Monitor traffic, conversion and repeat visits separately from ticket changes.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Reduce inventory decisions that become margin losses
cards.text: Gross margin fell to 27.9% from 28.2%; management cited markdowns, cancellation costs and category mix. Better purchasing and assortment choices could address pressures that cost reduction alone cannot fix.
items: Tie replenishment and seasonal commitments to current sell-through evidence.
Adjust category purchases earlier where cancellation or markdown exposure builds.
Monitor full-price sales and inventory aging before expanding promotional activity.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve expense productivity without weakening the visit
cards.text: The adjusted SG&A expense rate was 20.9% despite lower adjusted expense dollars. Reduced spending has not by itself restored operating leverage against the weaker sales base.
items: Align staffing and fulfillment workflows with actual store and digital demand.
Simplify low-value operating tasks to protect customer-facing service capacity.
Monitor labor productivity and customer conversion together after expense changes.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Preserve cash flexibility while interest costs rise
cards.text: Net interest expense increased to $445 million from $411 million, reflecting higher average debt. That raises the importance of inventory cash discipline and selective capital allocation during the recovery.
items: Prioritize capital projects with clear store productivity or demand benefits.
Use inventory reductions to release cash where stock exceeds customer demand.
Monitor debt service needs against recurring operating cash before discretionary spending.

headline: TE Connectivity should use Industrial strength to fund selective growth and address Transportation weakness.
summary: Organic growth and strong cash generation show a healthy operating base, but the segments are uneven. Industrial Solutions expanded strongly while Transportation declined. Resource allocation should preserve Industrial execution and target Transportation opportunities with credible customer demand rather than treating both markets alike.
focusTitle: Allocate capacity and development around segment-specific customer demand.
focusText: Support Industrial programs that can sustain growth and cash returns, while keeping Transportation commitments responsive to customer schedules. Use cash strength to maintain product capability and reliability without adding capacity ahead of demonstrated demand.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the underlying growth in the existing portfolio
cards.text: FY2025 organic sales increased 6%. The result supports continued commercial investment, while the divergence between Industrial and Transportation means aggregate growth is not a sufficient capacity-planning guide.
items: Allocate commercial resources using customer programs and product-level contribution.
Coordinate manufacturing commitments with firm orders across end markets.
Monitor organic growth and order conversion separately by segment.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Keep Industrial expansion reliable and profitable
cards.text: Industrial Solutions organic sales grew 17.6%. The business merits support where capacity, delivery reliability and product development can convert demand into recurring customer relationships.
items: Prioritize production and engineering capacity for confirmed Industrial customer programs.
Resolve delivery bottlenecks before adding broader fixed capacity.
Monitor program margins and customer delivery performance as volumes expand.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Target Transportation recovery without overcommitting capacity
cards.text: Transportation Solutions organic sales fell 1.0%. The softer activity calls for customer-program discipline, even while other parts of the portfolio support overall growth.
items: Match Transportation production and inventory to customer release schedules.
Focus development on programs with demonstrated demand and attractive contribution.
Monitor new program wins and existing program volumes before expanding commitments.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use cash strength to sustain product and operating capability
cards.text: Operating cash flow reached $4.1 billion and non-GAAP free cash flow was $3.2 billion. Cash provides flexibility to support growth while maintaining discipline over capital intensity.
items: Rank capacity projects by customer commitments and expected cash returns.
Protect maintenance and product development supporting priority customer relationships.
Monitor working capital and recurring capital requirements before allocating discretionary cash.

headline: Teledyne should make acquisition growth pay through cash and integration discipline.
summary: Reported and adjusted operating margins improved, while acquisitions added sales and capital spending increased. Higher net debt makes it important to preserve those operating gains and convert the expanded business into cash, rather than judging the strategy through acquired revenue alone.
focusTitle: Protect margin gains while earning returns on the expanded asset base.
focusText: Integrate acquired operations around customer continuity and operating productivity. Tie additional capital commitments to utilization and cash returns, leaving sufficient cash for financing needs as the business absorbs its larger portfolio and investment program.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make acquired sales become durable customer value
cards.text: Acquisitions contributed $270.1 million to FY2025 sales. They broaden the revenue base, but integration quality and customer retention determine whether that added scale produces worthwhile returns.
items: Prioritize continuity for acquired customers and critical product delivery.
Integrate duplicated operating processes where service quality can be preserved.
Monitor acquired-business retention and contribution separately from existing operations.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve margin improvement across the larger portfolio
cards.text: GAAP operating margin rose to 18.8% from 17.4%, while non-GAAP margin reached 22.6%. Improvement in both measures is supportive, while the gap still matters for full business economics.
items: Carry productivity improvements into acquired and existing operating plans.
Price new work for full delivery and support costs.
Monitor reported and adjusted margins as integration spending progresses.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make increased capital spending earn cash returns
cards.text: Operating cash flow was $1.191 billion, while capital spending rose to $117.3 million from $83.7 million. The investment should support identifiable operating needs rather than capacity growth without demand.
items: Rank capital projects by utilization, customer needs and expected cash benefit.
Stage discretionary expansion until operating milestones justify further spending.
Monitor collections and cash remaining after required capital spending.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep acquisition and investment choices within funding capacity
cards.text: Year-end non-GAAP net debt increased to $2.123 billion from $1.999 billion. The increase makes financing headroom a relevant constraint on further expansion despite stronger margins.
items: Reserve cash for debt service and essential operating investment.
Compare additional acquisitions with integration demands and financing capacity.
Monitor debt obligations against recurring cash generation before discretionary allocations.

headline: Teradyne should protect sales momentum while rebuilding robotics execution.
summary: Sales growth provides a stronger commercial base, but robotics restructuring and planned ERP implementation add execution demands. The priority is keeping customer delivery and critical technical capability intact while ensuring organizational changes improve sustainable economics rather than merely adjusted earnings.
focusTitle: Use restructuring to improve operating delivery and recurring returns.
focusText: Concentrate robotics changes on the capabilities required by customer demand, and manage ERP investment around reliable operating processes. Evaluate the result through customer service, full costs and reported profitability alongside revenue growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn stronger sales into reliable customer execution
cards.text: FY2025 sales increased 13% to $3.19 billion. Continued growth needs operating capacity matched to customer requirements, particularly while other parts of the organization undergo change.
items: Prioritize production and technical support for committed customer programs.
Coordinate capacity planning with confirmed orders rather than annual growth alone.
Monitor delivery reliability and product contribution as sales expand.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make robotics restructuring preserve critical capability
cards.text: Employee severance primarily involved robotics restructuring affecting approximately 400 employees. The operational objective should be a more sustainable business without losing the product and service capabilities customers need.
items: Protect robotics expertise tied to active customer deployments and support.
Align the revised cost base with demonstrated robotics demand.
Monitor service continuity, development delivery and realized recurring cost savings.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Judge the recovery using full operating costs
cards.text: GAAP EPS was $3.47 versus non-GAAP EPS of $3.96. The difference means adjusted performance alone does not capture all the economics of the operating changes.
items: Include restructuring-related cash commitments when sizing discretionary investment.
Distinguish temporary charges from continuing costs in robotics resource plans.
Monitor reported profitability and cash generation as restructuring progresses.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep ERP implementation tied to operating benefits
cards.text: Selling and administrative expense included $4.8 million related to planned ERP implementation. The spending should support dependable processes while avoiding disruption to sales, production and customer service.
items: Prioritize ERP workflows with clear order, inventory or billing benefits.
Stage implementation around operating readiness and tested process ownership.
Monitor implementation spending, order accuracy and disruption costs before broader rollout.

headline: Tesla needs vehicle demand and expense discipline alongside energy growth.
summary: Vehicle deliveries declined while operating expenses grew and margin weakened. Storage deployments and services revenue provide meaningful offsetting strength, but they do not establish that the vehicle business has recovered. Resources should follow profitable demand across the portfolio rather than growth narratives alone.
focusTitle: Restore operating leverage while supporting demonstrable energy demand.
focusText: Align vehicle production, commercial spending and operating commitments with customer demand. Preserve storage and services opportunities where delivery economics support investment, judging the unaudited annual results through contribution, cash needs and reported operating margin together.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Rebuild vehicle demand with controlled inventory commitments
cards.text: FY2025 deliveries declined 9% to 1,636,129 vehicles. The decline makes production alignment and customer conversion central to improving the economics of the vehicle business.
items: Align vehicle production and inventory with order conversion by market.
Test product and commercial offers against contribution after incentives.
Monitor deliveries, cancellations and inventory aging alongside new orders.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale storage around installation and contribution capacity
cards.text: Storage deployments rose 49% to 46.7 GWh. The growth warrants support, while customer readiness and execution determine whether additional deployments produce attractive business returns.
items: Coordinate storage production with contracted installation and acceptance schedules.
Prioritize deployments using contribution and cash requirements per project.
Monitor delivery performance and collections as storage volumes expand.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make services growth reinforce customer economics
