cards.text: Services and other revenue increased 19% to $12.530 billion. The activity provides another growth source, but revenue should be assessed alongside the resources required to serve it.
items: Allocate service capacity according to customer usage and support needs.
Improve workflows that reduce repair delays and repeat service effort.
Monitor service contribution and customer retention alongside revenue growth.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Bring operating commitments into line with earned growth
cards.text: Operating expenses increased 23% while operating margin fell to 4.6%. The mismatch calls for more selective spending, especially as vehicle deliveries move in the opposite direction.
items: Rank operating programs by demonstrated customer demand and expected returns.
Stage discretionary spending around product and commercial milestones.
Monitor incremental operating profit as vehicle, storage and services volumes change.

headline: Texas Instruments should align capacity investment and cash returns with internally generated cash.
summary: Operating cash flow improved, supporting substantial manufacturing and product investment. Yet shareholder cash returns exceeded the company-defined free cash flow measure, which includes CHIPS Act proceeds. The key priority is pacing commitments so long-term capability does not reduce funding flexibility.
focusTitle: Sequence investment and capital returns around sustainable cash capacity.
focusText: Protect strategically useful manufacturing and development work while staging discretionary spending against utilization and demand. Evaluate shareholder distributions after required investment and financing needs, separating government-related proceeds from recurring operating cash when assessing capacity.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the operating cash improvement
cards.text: FY2025 operating cash flow rose 13% to $7.153 billion. That creates investment capacity, provided inventory, customer collections and operating requirements remain controlled through changes in demand.
items: Align inventory and production planning with customer ordering patterns.
Protect collections discipline as product shipments change.
Monitor recurring operating cash and working capital separately from other funding.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make manufacturing spending follow useful capacity demand
cards.text: Capital expenditure was approximately $4.6 billion. The scale makes project sequencing and future utilization important to the cash return on manufacturing investment.
items: Prioritize capital milestones required for committed manufacturing capability.
Stage discretionary capacity additions against customer demand and utilization.
Monitor project cash requirements and readiness before releasing further spending.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect development value while controlling overhead commitments
cards.text: Research, development and SG&A spending totaled approximately $3.9 billion. These commitments should sustain customer-relevant products and commercial support without adding costs disconnected from future revenue opportunities.
items: Prioritize development programs with clear customer application needs.
Reallocate support spending toward product adoption and design-win execution.
Monitor project milestones and customer uptake when renewing resource commitments.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Size shareholder returns after funding the investment cycle
cards.text: Cash returned totaled $6.476 billion versus non-GAAP free cash flow of $2.938 billion. Because that free cash flow includes CHIPS Act proceeds, distributions need a broader funding assessment.
items: Reserve cash for committed capital projects and financing obligations.
Evaluate discretionary returns against cash remaining after required investment.
Monitor recurring free cash generation separately from CHIPS Act proceeds.

headline: Texas Pacific Land should preserve volume economics as realized royalty prices weaken.
summary: Royalty production rose substantially and water operations supplied another revenue stream, but realized prices declined. Higher depletion also lifted operating expenses. The priority is distinguishing cash-generating operating growth from commodity and accounting effects when directing water investment and other commitments.
focusTitle: Invest around durable water demand and royalty cash resilience.
focusText: Assess royalty volumes and realized prices together, then allocate operating resources to water services with credible utilization and collection economics. Separate depletion from cash operating costs so spending decisions respond to actual funding requirements rather than headline expense growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the value of rising royalty production
cards.text: Royalty production averaged 34.6 thousand Boe per day, versus 26.8 thousand. Higher physical activity supports earnings capacity, but the resulting cash remains sensitive to the price realized per unit.
items: Coordinate production reporting and royalty collection around operator activity.
Use activity changes to assess associated land and water service opportunities.
Monitor royalty volumes and cash receipts together by producing area.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep commitments resilient to lower commodity realization
cards.text: Average realized price fell to $34.18 per Boe from $39.87. The decline can offset production growth and makes commodity-sensitive cash assumptions important in capital allocation.
items: Evaluate discretionary commitments using a range of royalty price outcomes.
Prioritize spending that remains supportable under weaker realized prices.
Monitor realized prices and royalty cash per unit alongside production growth.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make water expansion earn its operating footprint
cards.text: Water Services and Operations revenue reached $307.5 million. The business provides an operating opportunity distinct from royalty pricing, with investment value dependent on customer activity and asset use.
items: Align water service capacity with confirmed customer requirements.
Prioritize projects using utilization, collection terms and expected cash contribution.
Monitor water revenue and operating cash returns by service activity.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Manage cash costs separately from depletion
cards.text: Operating expenses increased to $206.0 million from $166.7 million, mainly because of higher depletion. The distinction matters because the expense increase does not identify an equivalent increase in cash spending.
items: Set operating budgets around controllable water and land service cash costs.
Include maintenance requirements when evaluating the cash benefit of expansion.
Monitor cash cost trends and depletion separately against production and water activity.

headline: Textron should convert Aviation and Bell backlogs while preserving manufacturing cash flexibility.
summary: Bell military growth and substantial backlogs support demand visibility across two major businesses. That shifts the priority toward delivery execution and funding: engineering, production and customer milestones must turn orders into cash, while repurchases should remain consistent with manufacturing needs.
focusTitle: Put program delivery and cash conversion ahead of discretionary commitments.
focusText: Allocate manufacturing and engineering resources to executable customer milestones across Aviation and Bell. Protect schedule reliability and required investment, then evaluate shareholder returns against the cash remaining after delivery, working capital and financing requirements.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support Bell military growth with program discipline
cards.text: Management reported a second consecutive year of 20% military revenue growth at Bell. Continued growth should be supported by the engineering and production capabilities needed to meet customer requirements.
items: Prioritize technical resources around contracted military program milestones.
Coordinate supplier readiness with Bell production and delivery schedules.
Monitor program costs and milestone completion alongside military revenue growth.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn Aviation backlog into accepted aircraft and collections
cards.text: Textron Aviation ended the year with $7.7 billion of backlog. The balance supports visibility, while execution and customer readiness determine delivery timing and the associated cash conversion.
items: Sequence aircraft production around firm customer delivery requirements.
Resolve supplier constraints before they delay completion and acceptance.
Monitor backlog conversion, delivery costs and customer collections together.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make Bell backlog executable without stretching resources
cards.text: Bell backlog reached $7.8 billion at year end. The contracted opportunity creates resource requirements that should be coordinated with its growing military activity and program obligations.
items: Match Bell staffing and supplier commitments to program-specific delivery needs.
Stage spending around customer milestones and contractual funding arrangements.
Monitor backlog aging and execution cost before accepting additional production commitments.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep repurchases within manufacturing cash capacity
cards.text: Manufacturing operating cash flow was $1.3 billion, while share repurchases totaled $822 million. The comparison makes remaining investment and working capital requirements relevant to discretionary cash allocation.
items: Reserve cash for essential manufacturing investment and committed program costs.
Evaluate repurchases after capital spending and financing obligations.
Monitor delivery-related working capital against recurring manufacturing cash generation.

headline: Thermo Fisher should restore Analytical Instruments profitability while strengthening cash conversion.
summary: Underlying revenue growth was modest, and acquisitions and currency also supported reported growth. Laboratory Products and Biopharma Services improved its margin, but Analytical Instruments weakened and operating cash declined. Targeted segment execution is therefore more useful than a uniform growth or cost response.
focusTitle: Prioritize instrument economics and cash without weakening stronger services.
focusText: Focus commercial and operational changes on the Analytical Instruments margin decline, while preserving improvements in Laboratory Products and Biopharma Services. Require growth investment to demonstrate customer demand, sustainable contribution and cash collection across the portfolio.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Grow the existing business on clearer customer demand
cards.text: FY2025 organic revenue grew 2%; acquisitions and currency each contributed one percentage point to reported growth. The mix makes underlying customer activity important when allocating additional growth resources.
items: Prioritize customer programs with demonstrated recurring laboratory or service demand.
Keep acquisition integration resources distinct from existing-business commercial investment.
Monitor organic orders and customer retention alongside reported revenue.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Repair instrument margins with product-level action
cards.text: Analytical Instruments segment margin fell to 23.0% from 26.2%. The decline identifies a specific economic weakness, though the disclosed figures do not establish a single cause.
items: Evaluate instrument pricing, mix and delivery costs at product level.
Align production and service capacity with actual instrument demand.
Monitor contribution on new orders before expanding discounts or commercial spending.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the stronger economics in laboratory and biopharma services
cards.text: Laboratory Products and Biopharma Services margin increased to 14.0% from 13.3%. That improvement should inform resource allocation without assuming the same operating response fits instrument businesses.
items: Protect service reliability and workflows supporting the margin improvement.
Allocate incremental resources to contracts with attractive full-service economics.
Monitor contract retention and contribution as activity and customer requirements change.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Rebuild the cash available for investment
cards.text: Operating cash flow declined to $7.818 billion from $8.667 billion. Lower cash generation increases the importance of collections and working capital discipline when funding the expanded business.
items: Coordinate billing and collections with instrument deliveries and service milestones.
Align inventory commitments with customer orders and project schedules.
Monitor cash conversion and required capital spending before discretionary allocations.

headline: TJX should protect merchandise execution and underlying margin as comparable sales grow.
summary: Comparable sales growth was broad, with Canada particularly strong and positive results across the major banners. Adjusted pretax margin also improved modestly. The priority is preserving the buying and inventory discipline behind that performance, while separating the settlement benefit from recurring profitability.
focusTitle: Reinvest in merchandise availability where demand supports profitable turnover.
focusText: Use banner-specific demand to guide buying, replenishment and store resources. Preserve the value proposition and inventory flexibility that support repeat visits, judging investment returns against adjusted economics rather than a reported margin benefit from the settlement.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep comparable growth tied to merchandise productivity
cards.text: FY2026 consolidated comparable sales increased 5%. Growth at existing stores supports the offering, while continued buying discipline is needed to turn customer demand into attractive inventory returns.
items: Prioritize purchases using observed category sell-through and customer response.
Keep replenishment flexible so stores can respond to changing demand.
Monitor inventory turnover and merchandise contribution alongside comparable sales.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Support Canada without assuming identical demand elsewhere
cards.text: TJX Canada comparable sales increased 7%, the strongest disclosed banner result. The opportunity is to support its demand while preserving local buying judgment and store execution.
items: Allocate merchandise depth to Canadian categories showing sustained demand.
Maintain local assortment decisions when extending successful buying practices.
Monitor full-price sell-through and inventory productivity as Canadian sales expand.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Tailor operating support across the growing banners
cards.text: Marmaxx and TJX International comparable sales rose 4%, while HomeGoods grew 5%. Positive results across formats support investment, but assortment and operating needs should remain banner-specific.
items: Align store staffing and replenishment with each banner’s demand patterns.
Share useful buying practices while preserving distinct merchandise requirements.
Monitor category contribution and inventory aging separately across the banners.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect recurring profitability when judging investment capacity
cards.text: Adjusted pretax margin rose 0.2 percentage points to 11.7%, while reported margin benefited from a settlement. Recurring operating economics are the better basis for additional fixed commitments.
items: Base store and operating investment on margins excluding the settlement benefit.
Prioritize productivity changes that preserve the customer shopping experience.
Monitor buying gains, operating costs and adjusted margin as sales grow.

headline: TKO should turn rights and event growth into profit after central costs.
summary: UFC partnerships, WWE media and WWE live events all delivered revenue growth. Corporate and Other nevertheless remained a substantial adjusted EBITDA loss. The priority is preserving valuable commercial relationships while making event commitments and central resources support the economics of the combined portfolio.
focusTitle: Allocate resources to commercial growth that improves full-portfolio returns.
focusText: Protect sponsor, distribution and fan relationships, and evaluate each growth initiative after production, event and central support requirements. Use the retrospectively comparable acquisition scope consistently, so portfolio growth is not mistaken for an improvement in underlying operating efficiency.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build durable UFC partnership value
cards.text: UFC partnerships and marketing revenue increased $62.9 million. The growth supports the sponsorship offering, while renewal quality and activation requirements determine how durable the contribution becomes.
items: Prioritize partner renewals around demonstrable audience and activation value.
Coordinate commercial inventory to avoid commitments that impair fan experience.
Monitor renewal rates and contribution after partnership delivery costs.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve WWE media economics as content commitments grow
cards.text: WWE media rights, production and content revenue increased $135.1 million. The opportunity carries delivery obligations, making content reliability and production economics central to sustaining commercial value.
items: Align production resources with contracted content and distribution requirements.
Evaluate additional content using incremental rights value and delivery cost.
Monitor rights revenue and production contribution across commercial agreements.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make live-event demand translate into attractive event returns
cards.text: WWE live events and hospitality revenue increased $74.3 million. Higher activity is useful, but scheduling, venue terms and service costs determine the profit generated by the event calendar.
items: Prioritize event locations and formats with attractive expected contribution.
Coordinate hospitality capacity with ticket demand and service requirements.
Monitor event-level profit and repeat attendance alongside ticket and hospitality revenue.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make central spending earn its portfolio role
cards.text: Corporate and Other adjusted EBITDA remained a $322.2 million loss. The loss should be assessed against the support and capabilities it provides, rather than assuming revenue growth resolves central cost intensity.
items: Assign central resources to identifiable commercial or operating priorities.
Consolidate overlapping support workflows where business delivery can be preserved.
Monitor central costs and full-portfolio contribution using the consistent comparative scope.

headline: Tractor Supply should improve existing-store productivity before scaling overhead further.
summary: Store openings helped total sales grow faster than comparable sales, while SG&A rose faster still. A small gross margin improvement provides support but does not resolve the expense-rate pressure. The priority is making existing stores and new locations produce stronger contribution per operating dollar.
focusTitle: Connect expansion decisions to store productivity and operating returns.
focusText: Improve assortment, staffing and service in existing stores while holding new locations accountable for customer adoption and contribution. Preserve merchandise margin, and pace further operating commitments around evidence that the larger footprint can support its cost base.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Improve demand inside the existing footprint
cards.text: Comparable sales increased 1.2%, below total sales growth of 4.3%. The difference makes existing-store customer activity a more useful recovery lever than relying solely on additional locations.
items: Refine local assortments around repeat customer needs and category sell-through.
Test traffic and basket initiatives using incremental store contribution.
Monitor customer visits, conversion and repeat purchases separately from new-store sales.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make new stores earn their operating commitments
cards.text: Tractor Supply opened 99 stores; Petsense opened five and closed four. Expansion adds opportunity, while openings alone do not establish attractive economics or the net strength of each format.
items: Prioritize store support around local customer adoption and inventory availability.
Use new-store contribution and cash requirements to guide further expansion.
Monitor opening cohorts and Petsense closures separately when evaluating footprint returns.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Bring overhead growth into line with store productivity
cards.text: SG&A increased 6.6% to $4.19 billion, reaching 27.0% of sales from 26.4%. The expense burden requires operating improvements beyond modest comparable sales gains.
items: Align staffing and store tasks with observed customer activity.
Simplify support workflows that add cost without improving customer service.
Monitor expense per store and contribution as new locations mature.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect merchandise economics while rebuilding sales leverage
cards.text: Gross margin edged up to 36.4% from 36.3%. The small improvement is useful, but broad promotional spending could erase it before store expense productivity improves.
items: Tie replenishment to local category demand to limit aged stock.
Evaluate promotions after markdowns and incremental handling costs.
Monitor inventory turnover and gross profit dollars alongside the margin rate.

headline: Trane should convert strong commercial HVAC orders without weakening cash discipline.
summary: Bookings outpaced organic revenue growth, led by Americas Commercial HVAC, and backlog increased. Strong non-GAAP cash conversion supports investment. The main priority is therefore execution capacity: deliver the growing order book reliably while keeping working capital and project costs under control.
focusTitle: Put capacity behind executable backlog and protect cash conversion.
focusText: Coordinate suppliers, installation support and production around confirmed commercial HVAC delivery needs. Use the cash strength to address genuine bottlenecks, while staging broader expansion against customer readiness and the contribution expected from backlog conversion.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Support commercial HVAC demand with targeted capacity
cards.text: Organic bookings increased 11%, led by 22% growth in Americas Commercial HVAC. The concentration of order strength makes targeted execution resources more useful than uniform capacity expansion.
items: Prioritize engineering and production resources for confirmed commercial HVAC orders.
Coordinate customer site readiness with equipment delivery requirements.
Monitor order contribution and delivery lead times across the strongest categories.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make the larger backlog deliverable and profitable
cards.text: Year-end backlog reached $7.8 billion, up 15%. The contracted work provides visibility while placing demands on suppliers, production schedules and customer implementation capacity.
items: Sequence backlog around contractual dates and actual customer readiness.
Resolve supplier constraints before committing further delivery capacity.
Monitor backlog aging, cancellations and expected project margins.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect current revenue execution during the order ramp
cards.text: Organic revenue grew 6%, below the pace of bookings. The difference supports future opportunity but makes execution on existing work important while new orders enter the system.
items: Maintain service and installation support for current customer commitments.
Align production releases with executable demand rather than headline bookings.
Monitor shipped revenue and acceptance milestones against scheduled backlog conversion.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep growth investments consistent with strong cash conversion
cards.text: Non-GAAP free cash flow was $2.9 billion, equal to 98% of adjusted net earnings. That supports selective investment while setting a useful discipline for working capital and capital intensity.
items: Fund capacity projects that remove demonstrated order-execution bottlenecks.
Align inventory and supplier payments with delivery and collection schedules.
Monitor cash conversion after growth spending as the larger backlog is fulfilled.

headline: TransDigm should preserve operating strength while containing debt-funded distribution risk.
summary: Organic sales and EBITDA As Defined margin improved, indicating favorable operating performance. Large special distributions were partly funded by new debt, and repurchases added another cash use. The priority is keeping operating and financing resilience commensurate with those capital returns.
focusTitle: Protect operating cash capacity before adding discretionary distributions.
focusText: Maintain the product delivery and pricing discipline supporting margins, then evaluate shareholder returns against debt service, required investment and available cash. Strong adjusted profitability should support funding decisions without replacing an assessment of financing obligations.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve profitable demand in the existing portfolio
cards.text: Organic sales increased 7.7%. The growth supports the operating base, while customer delivery and product economics determine whether expansion continues to produce useful cash.
items: Prioritize production and service resources for committed customer requirements.
Evaluate new volume using contribution after full support and delivery costs.
Monitor customer demand, order conversion and cash collections alongside organic growth.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Maintain margin discipline without weakening execution
cards.text: Non-GAAP EBITDA As Defined margin rose to 53.9% from 52.6%. The improvement is supportive, provided product quality, customer availability and necessary investment remain protected.
items: Carry productivity improvements into operating plans across the portfolio.
Preserve maintenance and product capability required for customer commitments.
Monitor reported costs and cash conversion alongside EBITDA As Defined margin.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep debt-funded distributions within financing capacity
cards.text: A $5.0 billion debt issuance helped fund approximately $5.2 billion of special dividend and equivalent payments. The cash return creates financing obligations that persist beyond the distribution itself.
items: Reserve liquidity for debt service and essential operating investment.
Evaluate further distributions against cash generation under weaker operating conditions.
Monitor financing maturities and cash interest requirements alongside available cash.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Assess repurchases alongside the full capital-return program
cards.text: Share repurchases totaled approximately $0.5 billion. Their funding should be considered together with the special distributions and new borrowing, rather than as an isolated use of surplus cash.
items: Prioritize committed investment and financing needs before discretionary buybacks.
Compare repurchases with alternative uses that strengthen operating or funding capacity.
Monitor cash remaining after all distributions and required capital spending.

headline: Travelers should preserve underwriting discipline as premium growth moderates.
summary: Both the reported and underlying combined ratios improved, while investment income also increased. With written premium growth more modest, the priority is protecting risk selection and pricing quality rather than chasing volume that could undermine favorable underwriting economics.
focusTitle: Grow where underwriting returns justify the risk and capital required.
focusText: Use improved results to reinforce disciplined pricing, claims execution and portfolio balance. Treat investment income as a complementary source of earnings, preserving underwriting standards even when stronger asset income makes aggregate profitability look comfortable.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the underwriting practices behind stronger results
cards.text: The combined ratio improved 2.6 percentage points to 89.9%. The favorable result supports the underwriting model, while continued risk and claims discipline is required to sustain it.
items: Prioritize renewals and new business using expected risk-adjusted underwriting returns.
Protect claims capabilities that improve resolution quality and cost control.
Monitor loss experience and expense performance separately within the combined ratio.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Build on improvement in underlying insurance economics
cards.text: The underlying combined ratio improved 2.3 points to 83.9%. That provides a favorable view of ongoing underwriting, while business-line detail should guide where growth is most attractive.
items: Allocate underwriting capacity toward lines with sustainable pricing and loss economics.
Refine account selection using emerging claims and exposure information.
Monitor underlying performance by line before broadening risk appetite.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Avoid buying premium growth through weaker terms
cards.text: Net written premiums increased 2% to $44.387 billion. Modest growth can be compatible with attractive economics, so increasing volume should not require surrendering appropriate pricing or coverage discipline.
items: Evaluate new business against expected losses and required capital.
Target retention where pricing remains adequate for the insured exposure.
Monitor rate, exposure and retention contributions to premium growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep investment income supportive of the insurance model
cards.text: After-tax investment income rose 10% to $3.254 billion. The benefit strengthens earnings, but investment decisions should continue to fit claims liquidity and balance-sheet requirements.
items: Align investment liquidity and duration with expected insurance payments.
Preserve credit discipline when reinvesting available portfolio cash.
Monitor investment income separately from underwriting returns when allocating capital.

headline: Trimble should convert recurring contract growth into cash before extending buybacks.
summary: Recurring contract growth and positive organic revenue suggest a stronger existing business than the reported sales decline implies. A substantial gap between reported and adjusted operating margins and meaningful repurchases make conversion into full-cost earnings and cash the central allocation priority.
focusTitle: Build durable recurring economics around adoption, renewal and cash.
focusText: Prioritize customer implementation and retention so annualized recurring revenue becomes recognized revenue and collections. Base investment and buyback decisions on the cash and reported economics of the business, keeping portfolio effects and adjusted margins distinct.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn recurring contracts into sustained customer use
cards.text: Year-end annualized recurring revenue was $2.39 billion, up 14% organically. This is an annualized contract measure, so the opportunity depends on retention, implementation and conversion rather than immediate full-year revenue.
items: Prioritize onboarding and product adoption for newly contracted customers.
Coordinate renewal outreach around customer usage and demonstrated value.
Monitor recurring contract retention and conversion into recognized revenue and collections.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Allocate resources using underlying customer demand
cards.text: Reported revenue fell 3%, while organic revenue increased 6%. The different views make portfolio comparability important when deciding which products and customer workflows deserve additional resources.
items: Prioritize existing offerings with sustained organic customer demand.
Separate portfolio-related changes from sales execution in commercial planning.
Monitor organic growth and customer retention by product rather than aggregate sales alone.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep full operating costs visible in growth decisions
cards.text: GAAP operating margin was 16.5% versus non-GAAP margin of 27.5%. The gap matters when determining how much recurring investment the business can support profitably.
items: Include relevant excluded cash costs in project and resource decisions.
Distinguish temporary transition spending from continuing operating requirements.
Monitor reported profitability and cash contribution as recurring revenue grows.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Size repurchases after funding the recurring business
cards.text: Trimble repurchased $875.4 million of shares during FY2025. Discretionary returns should be judged alongside product investment, customer implementation costs and the cash conversion of recurring contracts.
items: Reserve cash for product reliability and committed customer delivery needs.
Evaluate buybacks against available cash after capital and financing commitments.
Monitor collections and operating cash before extending discretionary repurchases.

headline: Twilio should deepen customer adoption while preserving its operating profit turnaround.
summary: Customer expansion, organic growth and positive GAAP operating income support the business. The priority is making the larger customer base more productive through sustained usage, without allowing acquisition and service costs to erode profitability.
focusTitle: Grow retained customer contribution rather than account counts alone.
focusText: Prioritize adoption and reliable delivery for customers with durable usage needs. Evaluate commercial spending through retained revenue and full operating contribution as the customer base expands.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Build on improving existing-customer expansion
cards.text: Dollar-based net expansion improved to 108% from 104%. Existing customers are contributing more, making adoption and usage durability important commercial priorities.
items: Target adoption support to customers with relevant additional use cases.
Address service friction before it constrains customer usage.
Monitor expansion and contraction separately within customer cohorts.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make new accounts become active relationships
cards.text: Active customer accounts exceeded 402,000, versus over 325,000. The larger base creates opportunity, provided accounts develop sustained usage and worthwhile contribution.
items: Streamline onboarding around successful first production use.
Allocate acquisition resources using expected retained customer contribution.
Track activation, retention and support cost by acquisition cohort.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve underlying revenue momentum with reliable service
cards.text: Organic revenue grew 13%. Sustaining that growth requires dependable customer delivery and commercially useful products, rather than simply adding more account relationships.
items: Prioritize reliability and capacity for customer-critical communication workloads.
Focus product investment on demonstrated recurring customer needs.
Monitor organic growth and product contribution alongside service performance.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep growth spending consistent with reported profitability
cards.text: GAAP operating income reached $157.8 million, reversing a $53.7 million loss. The improvement should guide disciplined reinvestment as customer activity grows.
items: Stage commercial spending against incremental retained revenue.
Protect operational improvements supporting the return to profit.
Monitor incremental operating income after acquisition and support costs.

headline: Tyler should improve cash conversion as SaaS and transaction activity expand.
summary: SaaS growth and a larger recurring mix support revenue durability, while transaction activity adds another growth source. Cash increased more slowly, making implementation, collections and the cost of supporting growth the next operating priorities.
focusTitle: Convert recurring and transaction growth into dependable cash.
focusText: Coordinate public-sector customer implementation, billing and support around completed milestones. Preserve service reliability while assessing new growth through contribution and collections rather than revenue mix alone.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Turn SaaS demand into successful customer deployments
cards.text: SaaS revenue increased 20.6% to $777.8 million. Continued growth depends on customers implementing and using the service reliably, not simply signing contracts.
items: Prioritize implementation resources around customer readiness and contracted milestones.
Improve onboarding for workflows that delay productive customer use.
Monitor deployment completion, adoption and implementation cost by cohort.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect the quality of the recurring base
cards.text: Recurring revenue represented 87.1% of sales, versus 84.5%. The larger mix supports durability when renewals and customer service economics remain healthy.
items: Focus customer success resources on adoption and renewal needs.
Address recurring support issues before contract renewal decisions.
Monitor retention and contribution after ongoing hosting and service costs.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Scale transaction services without losing delivery economics
cards.text: Transaction-based revenue grew 15.8% to $808.4 million. Higher activity increases the importance of reliable processing and the cost of supporting each transaction.
items: Match processing capacity to observed customer transaction demand.
Prioritize workflow improvements reducing errors and manual intervention.
Monitor contribution per transaction and service reliability as activity grows.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Bring cash generation closer to commercial growth
cards.text: Operating cash flow rose 4.6% to $653.5 million, slower than revenue. Collections and delivery commitments deserve attention as the recurring business expands.
items: Align billing and collections with contract and implementation milestones.
Reduce unresolved delivery issues that postpone customer payment.
Monitor receivables and cash conversion by revenue stream.

headline: Tyson should contain Beef losses while preserving Chicken’s operating recovery.
summary: Chicken improved on both volume and margin, while Beef recorded a substantial loss. Prepared Foods also faces a volume-price tradeoff. Legal accruals complicate sales interpretation, so segment economics and cash exposure should guide the response.
focusTitle: Allocate resources by segment economics and controllable cash requirements.
focusText: Protect Chicken execution, match Beef commitments to economic throughput, and test Prepared Foods demand without assuming legal accruals represent customer weakness. Keep legal funding needs visible in allocation decisions.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Chicken’s stronger volume economics
cards.text: Chicken volume increased 2.6% and GAAP segment margin rose to 8.5% from 6.0%. The improvement supports disciplined investment in productive capacity and delivery.
items: Maintain operating practices supporting Chicken yield and service reliability.
Align production with customer demand to protect inventory quality.
Monitor volume contribution and segment margin together.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Constrain Beef exposure to uneconomic throughput
cards.text: Beef volume fell 1.9% and its GAAP operating loss reached $1.135 billion. The segment needs targeted cost, procurement and capacity decisions.
items: Evaluate Beef production schedules against full input and processing economics.
Match procurement and capacity commitments to profitable customer demand.
Monitor loss per unit and cash requirements before expanding throughput.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Test Prepared Foods pricing against retained demand
cards.text: Prepared Foods volume declined 2.5% while average price rose 3.3%. Higher realization should be judged alongside customer retention and contribution.
items: Evaluate pricing and pack choices using category-level customer response.
Target promotions toward incremental contribution rather than volume alone.
Monitor repeat orders, volume and realized price by product.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Separate legal exposure from ordinary sales execution
cards.text: Sales grew 2.1%, while increased legal contingency accruals reduced sales by $653 million. That accounting effect requires a different response from weaker product demand.
items: Plan liquidity around potential legal payments and operating commitments.
Use demand measures excluding accrual effects for commercial decisions.
Monitor legal cash exposure separately from segment sales and margins.

headline: U.S. Bancorp should preserve fee momentum while maintaining credit and capital discipline.
summary: Noninterest income grew and capital strengthened, while net interest margin and charge-offs changed only modestly. The priority is growing durable customer revenue without weakening funding economics, credit standards or the balance-sheet flexibility supporting that growth.
focusTitle: Deepen profitable relationships within funding and capital capacity.
focusText: Allocate commercial resources to customer needs that support fee and lending returns. Preserve underwriting discipline and capital headroom, evaluating growth through full relationship economics rather than individual revenue streams.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make fee growth durable at relationship level
cards.text: Noninterest income increased 7.6% to $11.891 billion. The strength creates opportunity to deepen relationships where service costs and customer retention support attractive economics.
items: Prioritize additional services that meet existing customers’ needs.
Improve onboarding and servicing for recurring fee relationships.
Monitor fee retention and contribution after delivery costs.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect lending returns through funding choices
cards.text: Taxable-equivalent net interest margin edged up to 2.72% from 2.70%. The modest improvement makes deposit pricing and asset returns important ongoing disciplines.
items: Evaluate loan pricing against funding costs and expected credit losses.
Target deposit retention using full customer relationship value.
Monitor deposit mix and repricing effects on taxable-equivalent margin.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep stable credit outcomes from encouraging weaker selection
cards.text: Net charge-offs were 0.57% of average loans, versus 0.58%. The broadly stable outcome supports continued discipline rather than relaxed standards.
items: Prioritize lending where borrower cash flows support repayment.
Address emerging borrower stress through early relationship intervention.
Monitor delinquencies and losses by loan category and vintage.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use stronger capital to support selective growth
cards.text: The year-end common equity tier 1 ratio increased to 10.8% from 10.6%. Greater capital supports flexibility when growth and distributions reflect risk requirements.
items: Allocate capital to relationships with attractive risk-adjusted returns.
Preserve headroom for credit deterioration and funding needs.
Monitor capital generation after lending growth and shareholder distributions.

headline: Uber should preserve trip-led operating leverage rather than rely on the tax benefit.
summary: Trips and gross bookings grew strongly, alongside substantially higher GAAP operating income. A large tax valuation release also benefited net income. The priority is sustaining marketplace contribution and service quality so operating progress remains distinct from that tax effect.
focusTitle: Scale marketplace activity with disciplined incentives and operating costs.
focusText: Direct investment toward markets and customer use cases that retain profitable activity. Judge reinvestment capacity using operating results and cash generation, separating the tax valuation release from recurring earnings.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep trip growth supported by marketplace reliability
cards.text: Trips increased 20% to 13.567 billion. Continued activity requires dependable availability and customer experience as the marketplace processes more journeys and orders.
items: Allocate marketplace support to locations with persistent service friction.
Improve repeat usage through reliable matching and issue resolution.
Monitor completed activity and retention alongside customer acquisition.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect contribution as marketplace spending expands
cards.text: Gross bookings rose 19% to $193.454 billion. Marketplace transaction value supports scale, but it is not equivalent to recognized revenue or profit.
items: Evaluate incentives using incremental retained marketplace contribution.
Prioritize growth initiatives with sustainable customer and partner economics.
Monitor contribution after incentives alongside gross bookings by business.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the operating leverage already achieved
cards.text: GAAP operating income increased 99% to $5.565 billion. The improvement supports reinvestment where additional activity can retain attractive economics.
items: Carry operating productivity gains into expanding marketplace workflows.
Stage new commercial spending against demonstrated incremental contribution.
Monitor operating income growth relative to activity and support costs.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Base recurring commitments on operating earnings capacity
cards.text: Net income included a $5.0 billion tax valuation release benefit. That strengthens the reported result without representing an equivalent recurring operating improvement.
items: Use operating contribution and cash for recurring spending decisions.
Evaluate discretionary allocations after operating and financing requirements.
Monitor recurring tax payments separately from the valuation release benefit.

headline: UDR should protect occupancy while addressing weaker Southwest property economics.
summary: Occupancy improved and same-store NOI grew, but expenses increased slightly faster than revenue. Regional results also diverged. The priority is targeted leasing and property cost execution rather than broad rent or spending changes across the entire portfolio.
focusTitle: Manage leasing and property resources around local contribution.
focusText: Preserve high occupancy without unnecessary concessions, address Southwest demand and expense pressures locally, and carry productive practices into other properties only where market conditions support them.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Keep property costs aligned with collected revenue
cards.text: Same-store revenue increased 2.4%, while expenses grew 2.6%. The narrow gap makes controllable property costs relevant even while overall operating performance remains positive.
items: Prioritize maintenance workflows that reduce repeat work and resident disruption.
Evaluate service contracts against property needs and operating value.
Monitor expense growth and collected rent by property.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve occupancy through retention and reliable service
cards.text: Full-year weighted-average same-store physical occupancy increased 0.2 percentage points to 96.9%. Strong occupancy supports revenue when retention costs and concessions remain disciplined.
items: Address recurring resident service issues before renewal decisions.
Coordinate unit turns with leasing demand to reduce vacancy time.
Monitor renewals and concessions alongside physical occupancy.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Treat Southwest weakness separately from Northeast strength
cards.text: Northeast same-store non-GAAP NOI grew 4.0%, while Southwest NOI declined 1.1%. Different local economics call for distinct leasing and spending plans.
items: Review Southwest rent offers against local leasing conversion and costs.
Prioritize property improvements with measurable retention or operating benefits.
Monitor regional revenue and expenses separately before reallocating capital.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make positive NOI growth support selective reinvestment
cards.text: Same-store non-GAAP NOI increased 2.3%. The improvement provides support, while maintenance, financing and other cash requirements still matter for investment capacity.
items: Rank property projects using expected incremental cash contribution.
Protect essential maintenance that sustains resident experience and retention.
Monitor cash remaining after recurring property capital requirements.

headline: Ulta should bring overhead growth under control while preserving stronger customer demand.
summary: Comparable sales and gross margin improved, with both transactions and ticket contributing. SG&A grew much faster, and inventory increased with acquisitions and brand support. The priority is turning customer momentum into operating leverage without losing merchandising effectiveness.
focusTitle: Match operating resources and inventory to profitable customer growth.
focusText: Preserve shrink and merchandise margin improvements while tightening overhead productivity. Separate Space NK inventory from existing-business requirements, and require new-brand investment to demonstrate sell-through and repeat customer value.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep comparable growth balanced across visits and spending
cards.text: Comparable sales grew 5.4%, with 3.3% ticket growth and 2.0% transaction growth. The combination supports demand beyond price or basket changes alone.
items: Prioritize customer experiences that improve conversion and repeat visits.
Evaluate offers using incremental basket contribution after discounts.
Monitor transactions and ticket separately by store and digital channel.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve merchandise and shrink improvements
cards.text: Gross margin rose to 39.1% from 38.8%, aided by lower shrink and merchandise margin. These gains should remain part of operating execution as sales expand.
items: Maintain shrink controls while protecting product availability and service.
Allocate assortment depth using category sell-through and margin contribution.
Monitor shrink and realized merchandise margin alongside promotional activity.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make overhead growth earn its contribution
cards.text: SG&A increased 17.4% and reached 26.6% of sales from 24.9%. The higher expense burden limits the earnings benefit of stronger sales and gross margin.
items: Align store and support workflows with actual customer activity.
Prioritize spending that improves conversion, retention or operating productivity.
Monitor incremental profit after added labor and commercial costs.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep acquisition and new-brand inventory productive
cards.text: Inventory increased 10.8% to $2.2 billion, including Space NK and new-brand support. Those commitments should be evaluated against their distinct selling requirements.
items: Separate acquired inventory from existing-store replenishment decisions.
Stage new-brand purchases around observed customer adoption and sell-through.
Monitor inventory aging and markdown exposure by brand cohort.

headline: Union Pacific should convert faster network performance into durable customer demand.
summary: Carloads grew modestly while freight revenue excluding fuel surcharge grew faster. Network speed, terminal dwell and workforce productivity all improved. The priority is preserving service reliability and using those gains to win profitable traffic rather than simply removing operating capacity.
focusTitle: Make operational gains improve customer service and contribution.
focusText: Coordinate commercial growth with network capacity and staffing. Preserve the reliability behind faster movement, and judge productivity through customer delivery, cost per shipment and profitable traffic retention together.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build profitable traffic beyond modest volume growth
cards.text: Revenue carloads increased 1%, while freight revenue excluding fuel surcharge grew 3%. The result supports commercial discipline, with additional demand needing attractive handling economics.
items: Target customer traffic that fits network capacity and service capabilities.
Price new business for handling requirements and contribution.
Monitor carload retention and revenue mix separately from fuel surcharges.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Use faster car movement to improve customer value
cards.text: Freight car velocity increased 8% to 225 daily miles per car. Faster movement creates opportunity to improve equipment availability and service for customers.
items: Coordinate train plans with customer delivery and equipment requirements.
Preserve maintenance capacity supporting dependable network movement.
Monitor on-time customer delivery alongside freight car velocity.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect terminal flow as traffic patterns change
cards.text: Average terminal dwell improved 8% to 20.9 hours. The improvement should be sustained as additional traffic and changing routes alter local operating demands.
items: Align terminal staffing and switching plans with expected arrivals.
Resolve recurring handoff constraints before adding concentrated traffic.
Monitor dwell variation and missed connections at individual terminals.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep productivity compatible with service resilience
cards.text: Workforce productivity rose 7% to 1,132 car miles per employee. The gain is valuable if staffing and training still support reliable operations through demand changes.
items: Match crew deployment to traffic requirements and service commitments.
Reinvest targeted savings in operating bottlenecks and training needs.
Monitor service failures and labor availability alongside workforce productivity.

headline: United should make premium growth and fleet investment produce durable cash returns.
summary: Premium and loyalty revenue grew, supporting differentiated demand. Aircraft additions and cabin refreshes expand the offering but also require capital and execution capacity. The priority is maintaining the economics of that investment while preserving flexibility against substantial financial obligations.
focusTitle: Allocate fleet and customer investment around cash-producing demand.
focusText: Match premium capacity, loyalty investment and aircraft deployment to demonstrated customer contribution. Evaluate discretionary commitments after required fleet spending and financing needs, using operating cash flow rather than revenue growth alone.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deploy premium capacity where customers support returns
cards.text: Premium revenue increased 11%. The opportunity depends on route-level demand and the operating cost of providing the enhanced experience.
items: Align premium capacity with observed booking demand by route.
Protect service consistency that supports repeat premium purchasing.
Monitor premium contribution and cabin utilization alongside revenue growth.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve loyalty value without uneconomic customer acquisition
cards.text: Loyalty revenue rose 9%. Sustained growth depends on customer engagement and the economics of providing benefits, rather than revenue expansion alone.
items: Target loyalty benefits toward durable engagement and repeat travel.
Evaluate acquisition offers after associated reward and servicing costs.
Monitor member retention and contribution across loyalty cohorts.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make aircraft and interior investment earn utilization
cards.text: United added 82 aircraft and refreshed 119 interiors. The expanded offering needs dependable deployment and operating readiness to justify its investment and support requirements.
items: Coordinate aircraft deployment with crew, maintenance and route readiness.
Prioritize cabin investment where customer demand supports incremental contribution.
Monitor aircraft utilization and operational disruption as additions enter service.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect funding flexibility through the fleet cycle
cards.text: Operating cash flow was $8.4 billion, while year-end debt and other financial liabilities totaled $25 billion. Cash generation should be assessed alongside fleet and financing commitments.
items: Reserve funding for committed aircraft and required maintenance spending.
Evaluate discretionary allocations after financing and operating obligations.
Monitor cash remaining after fleet investment and scheduled liability payments.

headline: UPS should make its network reset restore cash-supported operating economics.
summary: Aircraft retirement and the Amazon volume reduction strategy are reshaping the network while transformation charges continue. Reported margin trails adjusted margin, and shareholder returns exceeded adjusted free cash flow. The priority is aligning capacity and cash commitments with the changing parcel business.
focusTitle: Resize the network around profitable service and available cash.
focusText: Coordinate aircraft modernization and customer-volume changes with operating capacity, preserving delivery reliability. Evaluate transformation benefits after their full cash costs before extending distributions beyond internally generated funds.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Match fleet modernization to actual network requirements
cards.text: UPS retired its MD-11 aircraft fleet during FY2025 as modernization accelerated. Capacity and replacement decisions should support the network’s changing shipment mix.
items: Align air schedules and remaining aircraft utilization with shipment demand.
Coordinate modernization with maintenance and operational readiness.
Monitor delivery reliability and cost per shipment during fleet changes.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make lower Amazon volume improve network contribution
cards.text: The year-end release identifies ongoing transformation charges and the Amazon volume reduction strategy. The operating challenge is removing or redeploying costs as the customer mix changes.
items: Adjust sort and transport capacity to retained profitable volume.
Target replacement business using contribution after network handling costs.
Monitor cost removal and service quality alongside customer-volume changes.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Evaluate transformation through full operating economics
cards.text: GAAP operating margin was 8.9%, versus non-GAAP adjusted margin of 9.8%. Excluded costs matter when determining whether network changes create durable returns.
items: Include transformation cash costs in network investment decisions.
Distinguish continuing operating savings from temporary spending reductions.
Monitor reported margin and realized savings as capacity changes progress.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Bring distributions within sustainable cash capacity
cards.text: Shareholder cash returns were $6.4 billion versus $5.5 billion of non-GAAP adjusted free cash flow. Network investment and financing needs also compete for funds.
items: Reserve cash for required fleet and network commitments.
Size discretionary returns after operating and financing requirements.
Monitor recurring cash generation after transformation spending before additional distributions.
