headline: Vistra should execute contracted power growth while managing acquisition and hedge cash exposure.
summary: Long-term AWS agreements and a solar project entering service support contracted demand. The Lotus acquisition adds generation capacity, while unrealized hedge losses complicate reported earnings. The priority is reliable asset execution and funding matched to contractual obligations, rather than reacting to mark-to-market results alone.
focusTitle: Coordinate asset operations and liquidity with contracted delivery.
focusText: Protect generation reliability, integrate acquired capacity and assess hedge settlement requirements alongside physical cash generation. Treat agreement capacity as a contractual maximum, keeping it distinct from delivered electricity and realized revenue.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make long-term power commitments operationally dependable
cards.text: Vistra announced a 20-year AWS agreement for up to 1,200 MW from Comanche Peak. The capacity commitment creates long-term opportunity and delivery requirements.
items: Align maintenance planning with contractual availability and delivery obligations.
Evaluate supporting investment using expected contracted cash returns.
Monitor asset reliability and contract performance separately from maximum capacity.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Integrate Lotus around reliable generation economics
cards.text: The 2,600 MW Lotus gas generation acquisition closed in November 2025. Its late-year addition requires operating and commercial integration before judging full-period returns.
items: Prioritize plant maintenance and operating continuity during integration.
Align acquired-asset commercial commitments with actual generation capability.
Monitor integration spending and asset contribution after closing.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Protect the economics of the solar asset now operating
cards.text: The 200 MW Oak Hill Solar project entered service with an AWS power agreement. Operating execution now determines the return on the completed investment.
items: Coordinate operating resources with contracted solar delivery requirements.
Address availability issues that impair expected output.
Monitor realized generation, collections and operating costs against project assumptions.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Manage hedge funding without confusing valuation and operations
cards.text: Net income included an $808 million unrealized pretax loss on hedges expected to settle in future years. The charge does not establish equivalent current-period operating deterioration.
items: Plan liquidity around contractual hedge and collateral obligations.
Evaluate hedges together with the physical exposures they cover.
Monitor future settlement requirements separately from unrealized earnings movements.

headline: Vulcan should protect aggregates unit economics while rebuilding same-store shipment momentum.
summary: Acquisitions lifted shipments despite slightly lower same-store activity. Pricing exceeded unit cash-cost growth and cash gross profit per ton improved. The priority is preserving those economics while distinguishing acquired scale from demand recovery in existing operations.
focusTitle: Allocate capacity around profitable local demand and cash contribution.
focusText: Maintain pricing and operating discipline, integrate acquired volumes and target existing-market opportunities selectively. Judge additional shipments by contribution after production and delivery requirements rather than tons alone.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Rebuild demand in the existing footprint
cards.text: Annual aggregates shipments reached 226.8 million tons versus 219.9 million, with acquisitions offsetting slightly lower same-store shipments. Reported growth therefore overstates existing-site volume momentum.
items: Target local customer projects that fit available quarry and delivery capacity.
Align same-store production and inventory with committed demand.
Monitor acquired and same-store shipment trends separately.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve price realization as customer mix changes
cards.text: Mix-adjusted aggregates pricing increased 6%, while reported freight-adjusted pricing rose 4%. The difference makes customer and product mix relevant to commercial decisions.
items: Price new work for product, location and handling requirements.
Evaluate discounts using incremental contribution rather than shipment targets.
Monitor realized pricing and mix separately by local market.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep operating cost growth below earned realization
cards.text: Freight-adjusted unit cash cost of sales rose 2%. The cost discipline supports profitability if reliability and required operating maintenance remain protected.
items: Prioritize production workflows that improve equipment and labor utilization.
Protect maintenance that prevents costly unplanned quarry downtime.
Monitor unit cash costs alongside throughput and operating reliability.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make incremental volume preserve cash profit per ton
cards.text: Non-GAAP aggregates cash gross profit reached $11.33 per ton, up 7%. The improvement provides a useful hurdle for acquired operations and new commercial opportunities.
items: Allocate capacity using expected incremental cash contribution per ton.
Apply productive practices to acquired operations where conditions fit.
Monitor cash profit and required capital spending as volumes change.

headline: W. R. Berkley should preserve underwriting quality while deploying premium and investment growth.
summary: The combined ratio supports favorable underwriting economics, and disclosed rate increases and investment income provide support. The priority is selecting risks where terms remain adequate, rather than assuming premium scale or asset income can substitute for disciplined insurance pricing.
focusTitle: Allocate underwriting capacity using risk-adjusted returns and claims evidence.
focusText: Maintain account-level pricing discipline and claims execution, with investment assets aligned to insurance liquidity. Evaluate premium expansion through expected losses, operating costs and capital requirements together.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect the underwriting economics already achieved
cards.text: The full-year GAAP combined ratio was 90.7%. The result supports disciplined risk selection and claims management as the portfolio evolves.
items: Prioritize accounts with attractive expected underwriting returns.
Preserve claims resources that improve resolution quality and cost control.
Monitor loss and expense performance separately by business line.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Keep rate increases adequate for the insured exposure
cards.text: Rate increases excluding workers compensation were approximately 7.6%. The disclosure supports pricing execution but does not establish identical conditions across every line.
items: Match renewal pricing to changing exposure and expected claims costs.
Maintain coverage discipline when competing for desirable accounts.
Monitor retention and loss trends with workers compensation assessed separately.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make premium scale earn the capital it uses
cards.text: Net premiums written reached $12.7 billion. The scale creates capacity for earnings while requiring disciplined exposure management and sufficient resources for future claims.
items: Allocate underwriting capacity toward well-priced risks and diversified exposures.
Assess new business using expected losses and servicing requirements.
Monitor premium mix and capital needs as the portfolio grows.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve investment income without weakening balance-sheet fit
cards.text: Net investment income reached $1.4 billion, up 7.2%. Asset income supports results, while portfolio decisions should continue to reflect claims-payment requirements.
items: Align investment liquidity and duration with expected insurance liabilities.
Preserve credit standards when reinvesting portfolio cash.
Monitor investment contribution separately from underwriting performance.

headline: Grainger should protect gross profit while making investment and portfolio simplification pay.
summary: Underlying daily sales grew, but gross margin declined slightly. Portfolio exits and substantial capital expenditure add execution priorities. The focus should be profitable customer service and productivity, using the simplified business and new investment to strengthen contribution rather than sales alone.
focusTitle: Link distribution and commercial investment to customer contribution.
focusText: Preserve availability and service for valuable customer needs while targeting margin and operating productivity. Complete portfolio transitions cleanly, and evaluate capital projects using cash returns after the cost of serving growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep underlying demand supported by useful customer service
cards.text: Annual sales grew 4.5%; non-GAAP daily organic constant-currency sales increased 4.9%. Continued growth depends on product availability and dependable fulfillment.
items: Prioritize inventory availability for recurring customer maintenance needs.
Target commercial support toward retained, profitable customer relationships.
Monitor organic demand and customer contribution after fulfillment costs.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Address gross-margin pressure at product and account level
cards.text: Gross margin was 39.1%, down 30 basis points. The modest decline warrants targeted pricing and sourcing action without undermining customer service.
items: Evaluate product realization against supplier costs and customer requirements.
Adjust discounts using full account contribution rather than revenue alone.
Monitor mix and realized gross profit after pricing changes.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make portfolio exits simplify operating commitments
cards.text: Grainger sold Cromwell and closed Zoro UK during 2025. The changes reshape the business and require customer and operating transitions to be completed effectively.
items: Resolve remaining transition obligations and support requirements.
Reallocate retained resources to businesses with demonstrated customer demand.
Monitor continuing-business economics separately from exit-related costs.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Require capital spending to improve operating returns
cards.text: Capital expenditures totaled $684 million. Investment should produce useful capacity or productivity rather than adding fixed costs ahead of customer demand.
items: Prioritize projects improving fulfillment reliability or cost per order.
Stage expansion against actual throughput and capacity constraints.
Monitor realized project benefits and cash after capital spending.

headline: Wabtec should convert backlog visibility into reliable delivery and cash.
summary: Both multi-year and near-term backlogs grew, supported by substantial operating cash. The opportunity is execution rather than order acquisition alone. A significant reported-adjusted EPS gap also makes full project economics important when committing additional resources.
focusTitle: Match engineering and production to executable customer milestones.
focusText: Prioritize near-term delivery while protecting longer-term program readiness. Evaluate backlog conversion through contribution and cash collection, keeping overlapping backlog measures and adjusted earnings distinct in investment decisions.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make long-term backlog support disciplined capacity planning
cards.text: Year-end multi-year backlog reached $27.407 billion, up 23.1%. The balance provides visibility while requiring careful sequencing of engineering, production and customer requirements.
items: Stage capacity decisions around contracted program milestones.
Coordinate supplier readiness for long-lead customer requirements.
Monitor backlog changes and expected contribution by program.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Prioritize the work scheduled for near-term conversion
cards.text: The 12-month backlog was $8.234 billion, up 7.2%. It overlaps with multi-year backlog, so the measures should guide scheduling without being added together.
items: Allocate production resources to executable near-term customer deliveries.
Resolve customer acceptance dependencies before scheduled completion.
Monitor near-term backlog conversion and delivery reliability.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve cash generation as program commitments grow
cards.text: Cash from operations totaled $1.76 billion. Strong cash supports delivery and investment when inventories, billing and collections remain aligned with program progress.
items: Match procurement and inventory releases to production milestones.
Coordinate billing and collection with contractual acceptance terms.
Monitor program cash conversion and capital needs before discretionary allocation.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Use full project costs when assessing returns
cards.text: Diluted EPS was $6.83 versus adjusted diluted EPS of $8.97. The difference matters when determining sustainable earnings and the cost of fulfilling additional work.
items: Include relevant excluded cash costs in project investment decisions.
Distinguish temporary charges from recurring operating requirements.
Monitor reported profitability alongside backlog contribution and operating cash.

headline: Walmart should sustain retail demand while making advertising and inventory growth productive.
summary: Comparable sales grew at both Walmart U.S. and Sam’s Club, while advertising expanded rapidly including VIZIO. Inventory also increased. The priority is keeping merchandise availability and advertising value tied to customer demand, with acquisitions and accounting presentation distinguished from underlying growth.
focusTitle: Link inventory and advertising resources to profitable customer activity.
focusText: Preserve retail execution while allocating inventory to demonstrated demand. Evaluate advertiser returns and repeat engagement, separating VIZIO contributions and presentation effects when judging advertising’s incremental economic value.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make advertising growth valuable to merchants and shoppers
cards.text: Global advertising grew 46% to nearly $6.4 billion, including VIZIO. Advertising can be recorded as sales or reduced cost of sales, requiring consistent economic evaluation.
items: Prioritize advertiser tools demonstrating useful customer reach and conversion.
Coordinate advertising placement with relevant merchandise availability.
Monitor advertiser retention and contribution separately from VIZIO growth effects.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Walmart U.S. customer-demand execution
cards.text: Walmart U.S. annual comparable sales excluding fuel increased 4.6%. The strength supports continued focus on availability, value and dependable fulfillment.
items: Allocate replenishment to categories with sustained customer sell-through.
Improve fulfillment workflows where service friction limits repeat purchases.
Monitor transactions and contribution alongside comparable sales excluding fuel.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep Sam’s Club growth valuable to members
cards.text: Sam’s Club U.S. annual comparable sales excluding fuel grew 5.1%. Continued growth should reinforce member value and efficient operations rather than promotional activity alone.
items: Prioritize assortment and service improvements supporting repeat member visits.
Align club inventory and staffing with local shopping patterns.
Monitor member retention and basket contribution alongside comparable sales.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep inventory growth aligned with selling requirements
cards.text: Global inventory rose 4.3%, or 2.6% in constant currency, at fiscal year-end. Product and geographic allocation determine whether that stock supports sales or ties up cash.
items: Match inventory commitments to category demand and fulfillment requirements.
Address aged stock before it creates broader markdown exposure.
Monitor inventory turnover using consistent currency and portfolio scope.

headline: Disney should make content and Experiences growth justify rising capital investment.
summary: Entertainment and Experiences operating income improved, supporting both sides of the portfolio. The subscription base offers commercial opportunity, but capital spending rose substantially. The priority is allocating content and physical investment to durable customer economics and cash returns.
focusTitle: Invest where engagement and operating contribution support cash returns.
focusText: Preserve the profit momentum in Entertainment and Experiences while staging new commitments around demand. Assess subscriptions through retention and contribution, and require physical expansion to demonstrate returns after capital and operating costs.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn subscription scale into retained contribution
cards.text: Disney+ and Hulu ended the year with 196 million combined subscriptions. These are subscriptions, not unique people, making retention and account economics more useful than reach claims.
items: Prioritize content and product improvements that support sustained subscriber engagement.
Evaluate acquisition offers after content and servicing costs.
Monitor churn and contribution across subscription cohorts.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve the earnings value of Entertainment’s recovery
cards.text: Entertainment operating income rose 19% to $4.7 billion. Growth supports selective reinvestment where content and distribution decisions sustain attractive returns.
items: Allocate content budgets using expected audience demand and full project economics.
Coordinate distribution strategies to maximize retained contribution.
Monitor operating returns by content and distribution activity.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make Experiences demand earn expansion returns
cards.text: Experiences operating income reached $10.0 billion, up $723 million. The performance provides support for investment while making capacity and guest experience important operating disciplines.
items: Align operating resources with attendance and guest-service requirements.
Prioritize enhancements with measurable demand and contribution benefits.
Monitor guest spending and operating costs alongside segment income.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Stage capital commitments around demonstrated demand
cards.text: Capital expenditure increased to $8.024 billion from $5.412 billion. The higher investment raises the cash and execution hurdle for additional projects.
items: Prioritize committed projects using expected cash returns and readiness.
Sequence discretionary spending to preserve funding flexibility.
Monitor project costs and cash after capital investment.

headline: Waste Management should defend pricing economics while rebuilding underlying volume quality.
summary: Core pricing and Healthcare Solutions margins provide support, while collection volume was nearly flat even with wildfire cleanup activity. Lower recycled commodity prices add pressure. The priority is preserving service contribution without relying on temporary volumes or stronger commodity realization.
focusTitle: Build recurring service economics around price, route efficiency and mix.
focusText: Focus commercial growth on durable collection relationships and productive routes. Preserve Healthcare Solutions improvements, and manage recycling operations against the cash contribution available at current commodity prices.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Protect pricing through dependable customer service
cards.text: Legacy collection and disposal core price increased 6.3%. Maintaining that realization depends on service quality and customer retention rather than price action in isolation.
items: Target renewals using full account contribution after service costs.
Resolve reliability issues that weaken customer retention.
Monitor churn and realized pricing alongside route profitability.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Strengthen recurring volume beyond cleanup activity
cards.text: Collection and disposal volume grew 0.1%, including a 50-basis-point wildfire-cleanup contribution. Temporary activity supported a modest overall volume result.
items: Target recurring accounts that improve existing route density.
Match temporary cleanup resources to confirmed project requirements.
Monitor recurring volume and cleanup-related activity separately.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Carry Healthcare Solutions improvements into durable returns
cards.text: Healthcare Solutions adjusted operating EBITDA margin increased 180 basis points to 16.9%. The improvement supports further operational focus without assuming all integration work is complete.
items: Preserve operating practices improving collection and treatment productivity.
Prioritize customer continuity and service reliability during operational changes.
Monitor full costs and customer retention alongside adjusted margin.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep recycling decisions resilient to lower commodity prices
cards.text: Average single-stream recycled commodity prices fell to $75 per ton from $92. Operating choices should reflect weaker realization rather than assuming a price recovery.
items: Align processing and transport decisions with current material contribution.
Prioritize quality improvements that reduce contamination and handling costs.
Monitor realized commodity proceeds and cash costs per processed ton.

headline: Waters should deepen recurring customer value while supporting broad instrument demand.
summary: Pharmaceutical and industrial sales grew, alongside instrument systems and recurring service and chemistry revenue. The priority is sustaining reliable customer use of the installed base and allocating development and commercial resources to applications with attractive contribution.
focusTitle: Connect instrument adoption with dependable recurring customer support.
focusText: Use market-specific demand to guide system investment, then support customer uptime and recurring consumable needs. Evaluate growth on a consistent annual basis without including the later BD transaction as an operating result.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support pharmaceutical demand with application-specific execution
cards.text: Pharmaceutical market sales increased 9% as reported. The strength warrants targeted customer and application support where instrument performance and workflows sustain demand.
items: Prioritize technical support for active pharmaceutical customer applications.
Align development resources with demonstrated laboratory workflow requirements.
Monitor customer retention and product contribution within pharmaceutical sales.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve industrial growth through focused customer support
cards.text: Industrial market sales grew 6% as reported. The opportunity should be developed around specific applications rather than assuming pharmaceutical commercial priorities fit every customer.
items: Target industrial applications with recurring measurement and testing needs.
Coordinate installation support with customer operating readiness.
Monitor repeat demand and contribution by industrial application.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make instrument growth create a productive installed base
cards.text: Instrument system sales increased 5% as reported. Each installation can support ongoing customer relationships when deployment and service execution establish dependable use.
items: Prioritize installation readiness and customer training around new systems.
Match system inventory and production with confirmed customer orders.
Monitor acceptance, utilization and system contribution after installation.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect recurring growth through reliability and availability
cards.text: Service and precision chemistry recurring revenue increased 8% as reported. Sustaining the growth depends on useful support and dependable product availability for customers already using systems.
items: Align service capacity and chemistry availability with installed-base requirements.
Improve maintenance workflows that reduce repeat service interruptions.
Monitor recurring retention and contribution after support and fulfillment costs.

headline: WEC should plan investment around normalized demand and resolve Illinois recovery exposure.
summary: Electricity demand grew on both reported and weather-normal measures, while Wisconsin gas growth was weather-sensitive. Residential usage adds operating needs, and proposed Illinois settlement terms created an earnings charge. The priority is reliable service and prudent investment without assuming regulatory recovery is settled.
focusTitle: Allocate infrastructure spending using normalized demand and recoverable economics.
focusText: Preserve customer reliability while distinguishing weather-driven activity from structural needs. Maintain funding flexibility for Illinois outcomes and tie discretionary commitments to demand evidence and the applicable regulatory framework.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use normalized electric growth for capacity decisions
cards.text: Electricity deliveries excluding the Michigan iron ore mine grew 2.2%, or 1.1% weather-normal. The normalized measure provides a more restrained basis for long-lived investment.
items: Prioritize network needs supported by sustained customer load.
Coordinate capacity planning with observed demand and reliability requirements.
Monitor reported and weather-normal deliveries using the same mine exclusion.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Avoid extrapolating weather-driven gas growth
cards.text: Wisconsin gas deliveries excluding power generation rose 11.5% but declined 0.5% weather-normal. Reported growth therefore does not establish stronger underlying demand.
items: Size discretionary gas investment using normalized customer requirements.
Maintain operating readiness for weather-related delivery variability.
Monitor weather-normal demand and infrastructure utilization separately.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Match residential service resources to usage needs
cards.text: Residential electricity consumption increased 3.5%. The activity makes service reliability important while requiring care before treating one year’s increase as permanent load growth.
items: Target maintenance where local usage stresses service reliability.
Coordinate customer support around observed consumption and billing needs.
Monitor residential load patterns before committing additional fixed capacity.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Keep Illinois commitments consistent with recovery uncertainty
cards.text: GAAP earnings included a $0.46-per-share charge tied to proposed Illinois QIP and UEA settlement terms. The proposal is not final regulatory approval.
items: Plan liquidity around potential settlement and recovery outcomes.
Prioritize essential Illinois work while evaluating discretionary commitments.
Monitor final regulatory terms and their investment-funding implications.

headline: Wells Fargo should turn fee growth and lower credit losses into stronger operating leverage.
summary: Noninterest income increased and net charge-offs declined, while net interest income slipped and expenses edged higher. The priority is retaining the stronger customer revenue and credit performance while improving cost productivity, rather than relying on one revenue stream to absorb every pressure.
focusTitle: Grow relationship contribution while aligning expenses with revenue capacity.
focusText: Protect useful customer and credit capabilities, and direct productivity work toward recurring operating costs. Use the preliminary annual results to judge fee durability, funding economics and full relationship returns together.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Defend net interest economics through disciplined funding
cards.text: Net interest income was $47.484 billion, versus $47.676 billion. The slight decline makes deposit and loan pricing relevant despite stronger fee revenue.
items: Evaluate loan returns after funding and expected credit costs.
Target deposit retention using full customer relationship economics.
Monitor funding mix and repricing effects on net interest income.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make fee growth durable and cost-effective
cards.text: Noninterest income rose to $36.215 billion from $34.620 billion. The growth supports commercial investment where customer retention and delivery costs preserve contribution.
items: Prioritize services that address existing customers’ recurring needs.
Improve onboarding and servicing for valuable fee relationships.
Monitor retained fee income and contribution by business activity.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve credit improvement through borrower discipline
cards.text: Net charge-offs declined to $3.990 billion from $4.759 billion. Better losses support earnings while making continued risk selection and early intervention important.
items: Maintain lending standards based on borrower repayment capacity.
Address emerging stress through proactive borrower engagement.
Monitor delinquencies and losses by loan category and vintage.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Convert revenue progress into expense productivity
cards.text: Noninterest expense was $54.842 billion, versus $54.598 billion. The modest increase still requires a clear return from added operating commitments.
items: Simplify recurring workflows that add cost without customer value.
Prioritize spending supporting revenue retention or operating reliability.
Monitor full operating contribution after new spending commitments.

headline: Welltower should make large senior-housing investments earn sustainable per-share returns.
summary: Normalized FFO per share grew strongly while substantial investment expanded the portfolio. Fund commitments and liquidity support further opportunity. The priority is disciplined deployment and property execution, ensuring capital access translates into shareholder returns rather than asset growth alone.
focusTitle: Sequence capital deployment around operating integration and returns.
focusText: Support acquired-property execution while preserving funding flexibility. Evaluate new investments after operating and financing requirements, keeping fund equity commitments distinct from deployed capital and realized earnings.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make the expanded portfolio operationally productive
cards.text: Welltower completed $11 billion of pro rata net investments, excluding development funding, centered on U.S. and U.K. seniors housing. The scale increases integration requirements.
items: Prioritize property staffing, leasing and operating continuity after investment.
Stage additional property spending around demonstrated local demand.
Monitor investment-cohort contribution and integration costs using pro rata scope.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve growth in shareholder-level operating economics
cards.text: Annual normalized FFO attributable to common stockholders was $5.29 per diluted share, up 22.5%. Per-share performance provides a useful hurdle for subsequent capital deployment.
items: Rank new investments using incremental contribution after funding costs.
Protect property operating practices supporting recurring cash generation.
Monitor normalized FFO per share alongside required property capital spending.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Turn fund commitments into disciplined investment capacity
cards.text: Seniors Housing Fund I closed with approximately $2.5 billion of equity commitments. The commitments support opportunity but are not equivalent to completed investments or earnings.
items: Align capital calls with approved investment and funding milestones.
Prioritize fund opportunities using expected property cash returns.
Monitor committed, called and deployed capital separately.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve financing flexibility through the investment cycle
cards.text: Year-end non-GAAP net debt to adjusted EBITDA was 3.03 times and available liquidity approximately $10.2 billion. Funding capacity should support disciplined execution rather than accelerate commitments automatically.
items: Reserve liquidity for committed investments and financing obligations.
Evaluate additional deployment against operating integration capacity.
Monitor leverage and available liquidity after planned capital requirements.

headline: West should support biologics and components growth while addressing delivery-device stagnation.
summary: High-Value Product Components and biologics grew organically, while High-Value Product Delivery Devices declined slightly on that basis. Cash generation improved. The priority is allocating capacity and development to real customer demand without allowing the weaker device business to absorb resources indiscriminately.
focusTitle: Match specialized capacity to customer programs and cash returns.
focusText: Protect the quality and delivery requirements of growing components and biologics applications. Target device investment to verified customer needs, using operating cash and required capital spending to maintain disciplined funding.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Support underlying components demand with dependable supply
cards.text: High-Value Product Components sales grew 11.2% reported and 8.9% organically. The growth warrants capacity support where customer programs justify additional operating commitments.
items: Prioritize component capacity for confirmed customer requirements.
Coordinate manufacturing and quality resources around delivery milestones.
Monitor organic demand and contribution alongside customer delivery performance.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Target device investment where adoption supports returns
cards.text: High-Value Product Delivery Devices sales rose 0.5% reported but declined 0.3% organically. The weaker underlying result calls for selective customer and product execution.
items: Review device programs against customer adoption and procurement requirements.
Stage development and capacity spending around demonstrated demand.
Monitor program wins, conversion and full delivery costs.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve biologics growth through quality and readiness
cards.text: Proprietary Products biologics sales rose 9.8% reported and 7.7% organically. Dependable customer supply and application readiness are central to sustaining that opportunity.
items: Align biologics-related production with confirmed customer schedules.
Protect technical support and quality capabilities for active customer programs.
Monitor recurring customer demand and manufacturing reliability.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deploy cash toward justified specialized capacity
cards.text: Operating cash flow increased 15.5% to $754.8 million, with capital expenditure of $285.9 million. Stronger cash supports investment after essential manufacturing requirements.
items: Prioritize capital projects with committed demand and expected utilization.
Maintain working capital discipline across components and devices.
Monitor cash remaining after capital spending before discretionary allocations.

headline: Weyerhaeuser should restore Wood Products economics without relying on special-item gains.
summary: Wood Products income fell sharply, while Climate Solutions provided another earnings source and management reported operating improvements. A net special-item benefit also supported GAAP earnings. The priority is improving recurring segment cash economics rather than judging recovery through the headline result.
focusTitle: Align Wood Products commitments with profitable demand and cash.
focusText: Target production, pricing and controllable costs in the weaker business while preserving productive Climate Solutions activity. Assess operating improvements through realized cash benefits, separating special-item gains and charges from recurring performance.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make Wood Products capacity fit current economics
cards.text: Wood Products operating income declined to $55 million from $457 million. The change requires targeted product, production and cost decisions without assuming a single disclosed cause.
items: Align production and inventory with customer orders and contribution.
Evaluate product pricing against conversion and delivery costs.
Monitor segment cash contribution and inventory aging before expanding output.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve Climate Solutions contribution through selective investment
cards.text: Climate Solutions generated $102 million of operating income. The business provides support, while further commitments should demonstrate dependable customer demand and economic returns.
items: Prioritize opportunities with clear contractual and operating requirements.
Stage investment around customer commitments and project readiness.
Monitor realized contribution and cash requirements by activity.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make disclosed efficiency gains show up in recurring economics
cards.text: Management reported $92 million of operational excellence improvements. Their value should be judged through operating reliability and sustainable cost performance, not the disclosed improvement measure alone.
items: Extend productive practices where site conditions support them.
Protect maintenance and service capabilities while removing avoidable costs.
Monitor recurring cash savings and operating performance after implementation.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Base recurring commitments on earnings without special items
cards.text: GAAP earnings included a net $181 million after-tax benefit from special items. The net combines gains and charges and does not represent a recurring operating improvement.
items: Use recurring segment economics to size ongoing spending.
Plan cash around the individual special items’ payment implications.
Monitor operating cash separately from net special-item earnings effects.

headline: Williams should turn pipeline expansion and acquisitions into sustained cash returns.
summary: Completed transmission projects and acquisitions expand the operating base, while capital investment increased substantially. Stronger operating cash supports that effort. The priority is reliable integration and utilization, keeping the full funding program visible rather than judging investment solely through the disclosed capital measure.
focusTitle: Sequence growth commitments around execution and cash-producing capacity.
focusText: Protect pipeline reliability, integrate acquired operations and stage further investment against contractual milestones. Assess funding after all capital and acquisition requirements, using operating cash growth as support rather than a substitute for project returns.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Make completed transmission capacity produce dependable value
cards.text: Williams completed 1.1 Bcf per day of pipeline transmission projects. Capacity completion creates opportunity, while utilization and contract performance determine its economic contribution.
items: Coordinate operations with customer delivery and availability requirements.
Protect maintenance and reliability across newly completed assets.
Monitor utilization and cash contribution after projects enter service.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Integrate acquired systems around customer continuity
cards.text: Williams closed the Rimrock and Saber Midstream acquisitions. The added operations require reliable service and coordination with the existing asset base.
items: Prioritize operating handoffs and customer service continuity.
Coordinate acquired capacity with the wider network’s commercial needs.
Monitor acquired-asset contribution and integration costs separately.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Keep capital growth tied to executable returns
cards.text: Published capital investments excluding acquisitions rose to $4.294 billion from $2.706 billion. The measure also excludes specified purchases, so it does not capture every funding requirement.
items: Prioritize projects using contracted demand and expected cash returns.
Stage discretionary spending around construction and customer readiness.
Monitor all funding commitments alongside the published capital measure.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve cash generation through the expansion cycle
cards.text: Operating cash flow reached $5.898 billion, up 19%. The stronger cash supports investment while making working capital and collection discipline important as new assets ramp.
items: Align collections and operating payments with customer contract terms.
Reserve cash for committed investment and financing obligations.
Monitor cash remaining after the complete capital and acquisition program.

headline: Williams-Sonoma should improve Pottery Barn demand while keeping inventory productive.
summary: Comparable brand revenue grew, but performance differed substantially across brands. Inventory increased and gross margin edged lower with an accounting comparability effect. The priority is brand-specific merchandising and purchasing that support demand without creating markdown exposure.
focusTitle: Match brand inventory commitments to profitable customer response.
focusText: Preserve Williams Sonoma momentum, target Pottery Barn’s slower growth, and assess West Elm separately. Use matched-week sales and underlying merchandise economics when judging recovery, rather than total growth distorted by fiscal-week differences.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Build on matched-week customer-demand growth
cards.text: Comparable brand revenue increased 3.5%. The measure uses matched weeks and includes business-to-business activity, making it more useful than unadjusted annual totals for demand assessment.
items: Allocate assortment investment using customer response by selling channel.
Prioritize service and availability supporting repeat customer purchases.
Monitor consumer and business-to-business contribution within comparable growth.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Give slower brands distinct merchandising priorities
cards.text: Comparable revenue grew 6.9% at Williams Sonoma, 2.9% at West Elm and 0.4% at Pottery Barn. The divergence calls for differentiated plans.
items: Test Pottery Barn assortment and presentation against conversion outcomes.
Preserve successful Williams Sonoma buying while respecting brand differences.
Monitor brand-level full-price sales and repeat purchases after changes.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Protect merchandise economics beyond accounting effects
cards.text: Gross margin was 46.2%, down 30 basis points; prior-year freight accounting affected comparability. The decline should not automatically be attributed to weaker pricing or demand.
items: Evaluate promotions using current merchandise and fulfillment contribution.
Target controllable freight and handling productivity improvements.
Monitor underlying price realization separately from freight accounting effects.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Keep inventory aligned with each brand’s selling pace
cards.text: Merchandise inventory rose to $1.463 billion from $1.332 billion. The commitment needs particular attention where brand demand is growing more slowly.
items: Stage purchases around brand-level sell-through and customer delivery needs.
Rebalance slow-moving assortment before broader markdowns become necessary.
Monitor inventory aging and turnover by brand and category.

headline: WTW should preserve organic growth and margin gains after the TRANZACT exit.
summary: The reported revenue decline reflects the sale, while organic revenue, adjusted margin and operating cash improved. Prior-year impairment also distorts earnings comparisons. The priority is sustaining the retained business’s client economics and productivity rather than reacting to misleading headline changes.
focusTitle: Reinvest in retained-client growth while preserving operating discipline.
focusText: Use organic demand and cash generation to guide client-service and capability investment. Keep disposal and impairment effects distinct, assessing the continuing portfolio through retained revenue, full operating costs and customer outcomes.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Grow the retained business through client value
cards.text: Revenue fell 2% following the TRANZACT sale, while non-GAAP organic revenue increased 5%. The existing business’s demand is stronger than the reported decline suggests.
items: Prioritize client services with demonstrated renewal and expansion demand.
Coordinate commercial resources around retained customer needs.
Monitor organic growth and client retention on consistent portfolio scope.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Preserve productivity without weakening client delivery
cards.text: Adjusted operating margin increased 130 basis points to 25.2%. The improvement supports selective investment while requiring full costs and service capacity to remain visible.
items: Carry productive workflows into client-service operating plans.
Protect specialist capabilities supporting valuable customer relationships.
Monitor full contribution and service quality alongside adjusted margin.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep stronger cash funding useful operating capability
cards.text: Operating cash flow reached $1.78 billion from $1.51 billion. The improvement provides flexibility to support client growth after required operating commitments.
items: Prioritize technology and service investment with measurable customer benefits.
Maintain billing and collection discipline across retained relationships.
Monitor cash after capital and financing requirements before discretionary allocation.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Base spending decisions on comparable operating economics
cards.text: WTW said net income and EPS comparisons were not meaningful because 2024 included TRANZACT impairment charges. The earnings change alone cannot establish recurring performance improvement.
items: Use retained-business contribution to size recurring resource commitments.
Separate exit-related cash costs from continuing operating requirements.
Monitor comparable profitability and cash rather than impairment-driven earnings changes.

headline: Workday should convert subscription backlog while making restructuring improve delivery economics.
summary: Subscriptions and operating cash grew, supported by a larger near-term backlog that includes acquisitions. Restructuring expense also increased sharply. The priority is preserving implementation and customer retention while demonstrating that organizational changes improve the full economics of growth.
focusTitle: Protect customer execution while earning returns from restructuring.
focusText: Allocate people and integration resources to backlog conversion and renewal quality. Separate acquired contracts from existing demand, and use cash generation to fund change without weakening the implementation capability supporting recurring revenue.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve subscription growth through customer adoption
cards.text: Fiscal 2026 subscription revenue grew 14.5% to $8.833 billion. Sustaining that momentum depends on reliable customer implementation and renewals, not contract signing alone.
items: Prioritize adoption support where customer workflows constrain product value.
Protect implementation resources for active customer commitments.
Monitor subscription retention and contribution after support costs.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Turn near-term backlog into recognized recurring revenue
cards.text: The 12-month subscription backlog was $8.833 billion, up 15.8%, including Paradox and Sana acquisitions. The contract measure provides visibility but is not recognized revenue.
items: Sequence deployments around customer readiness and contractual start dates.
Integrate acquired customer support without disrupting implementation schedules.
Monitor acquired and existing backlog conversion separately.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Make organizational changes improve recurring economics
cards.text: Restructuring expense increased to $303 million from $84 million. The cost needs to yield durable operating benefits while protecting customer and product execution.
items: Preserve specialist roles critical to deployments and customer retention.
Tie changed workflows to identifiable recurring productivity improvements.
Monitor restructuring cash payments, service continuity and realized savings.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use cash strength without overcommitting transition spending
cards.text: Operating cash flow increased 19.4% to $2.939 billion. The stronger cash supports investment, while collection timing and continuing operating needs still affect deployment capacity.
items: Align billing and collections with subscription contract requirements.
Reserve cash for committed integration and restructuring payments.
Monitor recurring cash conversion and stock compensation alongside growth.

headline: Wynn should restore domestic property contribution while controlling development funding.
summary: Wynn Palace grew while Wynn Macau declined, and domestic performance was softer. Las Vegas profit weakened despite nearly flat revenue. The priority is property-specific operating execution, with development funding kept consistent with the cash generated by the existing portfolio.
focusTitle: Improve existing-property economics before expanding discretionary commitments.
focusText: Target Las Vegas cost and revenue mix, distinguish Macau properties’ demand, and support Boston selectively. Track remaining joint-venture funding against construction progress and operating cash rather than treating future development as an established earnings source.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Manage Macau properties as distinct demand opportunities
cards.text: Wynn Palace revenue increased $89.7 million, while Wynn Macau declined $54.0 million. The divergence calls for property-level commercial decisions rather than a single regional response.
items: Tailor gaming and hotel offers to each property’s demand patterns.
Allocate marketing using incremental property contribution after incentives.
Monitor gaming activity, win rates and hotel performance separately.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore Las Vegas contribution on the existing revenue base
cards.text: Las Vegas revenue rose $1.1 million while non-GAAP adjusted Property EBITDAR fell $44.4 million. Nearly flat sales did not preserve property profitability.
items: Align labor and operating schedules with actual property demand.
Evaluate marketing and service spending against incremental customer contribution.
Monitor revenue mix and operating costs behind Property EBITDAR.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Target Boston demand without broad promotional dilution
cards.text: Encore Boston Harbor revenue declined $10.3 million. The property needs local customer and operating action rather than assuming stronger Wynn Palace trends apply.
items: Test local offers using repeat visits and incremental contribution.
Coordinate staffing and amenities with observed customer activity.
Monitor promotional cost and retained demand after campaigns.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Keep development funding tied to milestones and liquidity
cards.text: Cumulative contributions to the 40%-owned Wynn Al Marjan Island joint venture totaled $914.2 million at year-end. This is lifetime funding, not annual investment.
items: Stage further contributions around contractual and construction milestones.
Reserve liquidity for remaining committed development and financing needs.
Monitor joint-venture exposure and funding against existing-property cash generation.

headline: Xylem should broaden order growth while protecting measurement and service momentum.
summary: Measurement and Control Solutions grew strongly, with Water Solutions and Services adding support. Applied Water advanced more modestly, and orders remained slightly below sales. The priority is replenishing executable demand across the portfolio rather than relying on one segment’s growth.
focusTitle: Allocate commercial resources around order replenishment and customer execution.
focusText: Support measurement deployments and service retention while targeting Applied Water demand selectively. Use segment order intake and backlog conversion to guide capacity, keeping equipment projects distinct from recurring service requirements.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Keep order intake aligned with the revenue base
cards.text: Orders rose to $8.904 billion from $8.730 billion, with reported book-to-bill of 99%. Intake was slightly below recognized sales despite growth.
items: Prioritize commercial opportunities with executable customer project schedules.
Coordinate backlog delivery with new-order replenishment needs.
Monitor orders, cancellations and backlog by segment.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve measurement growth through deployment readiness
cards.text: Measurement and Control Solutions revenue grew 11% reported and 9% organically on a non-GAAP basis. Customer implementation capacity is important to sustaining that momentum.
items: Coordinate product delivery with customer deployment and installation schedules.
Prioritize technical support for active measurement programs.
Monitor order conversion and contribution alongside organic growth.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Deepen water-service relationships with dependable delivery
cards.text: Water Solutions and Services revenue increased 5% reported and organically. Service growth supports another demand source when renewals and operating contribution remain healthy.
items: Prioritize service reliability for recurring customer water needs.
Align local staffing and equipment with contracted service requirements.
Monitor retention and contribution by service contract.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Target Applied Water opportunities without broad capacity additions
cards.text: Applied Water revenue increased 3% reported and 2% organically. The more modest growth warrants selective customer and application support.
items: Separate industrial and building customer demand in commercial planning.
Match inventory and production to confirmed application-level orders.
Monitor order quality and product contribution before increasing fixed capacity.

headline: Yum should repair Pizza Hut while preserving stronger brand and digital economics.
summary: Taco Bell comparable sales were strong and KFC expanded its footprint, while Pizza Hut sales and profit declined. Digital ordering is now substantial across the system. The priority is brand-specific franchise economics, especially turning Pizza Hut investment into healthier restaurant contribution.
focusTitle: Allocate brand and technology support around sustainable franchise returns.
focusText: Preserve Taco Bell demand, require KFC openings to earn attractive returns, and target Pizza Hut execution separately. Evaluate digital growth after delivery and service costs, recognizing system sales as restaurant activity rather than consolidated revenue.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep Taco Bell growth valuable to franchisees
cards.text: Taco Bell full-year same-store sales increased 7%. The demand supports investment where traffic, ticket and operating costs sustain attractive restaurant economics.
items: Protect menu and service execution supporting repeat customer visits.
Evaluate promotions using incremental restaurant contribution.
Monitor traffic, ticket and franchisee unit economics together.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Make KFC expansion earn returns after closures
cards.text: KFC opened 2,986 gross new restaurants across 105 countries. Gross openings show development activity but do not measure net footprint growth or investment success.
items: Prioritize new markets using local demand and operator readiness.
Support new restaurants through supply and service execution.
Monitor opening-cohort returns and closures alongside gross development.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Give Pizza Hut a focused demand-and-profit plan
cards.text: Pizza Hut same-store sales declined 1% and GAAP divisional operating profit fell 9%. The weaker brand needs targeted commercial and operating action.
items: Test menu and value changes against retained customer demand.
Coordinate franchise support around service reliability and viable restaurant costs.
Monitor unit contribution and closures after recovery initiatives.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make digital convenience improve restaurant contribution
cards.text: Digital system sales approached $40 billion, nearly 60% of system sales. The channel’s value depends on customer retention and restaurant economics after ordering and delivery costs.
items: Improve ordering workflows that reduce errors and abandoned purchases.
Evaluate delivery offers after fees and restaurant fulfillment costs.
Monitor repeat digital use and franchisee contribution by ordering channel.

headline: Zebra should make acquisition integration and organic growth restore stronger cash conversion.
summary: Both segments grew organically, while acquisitions added scale and portfolio breadth. Operating cash declined despite reported sales growth. The priority is integrating acquired businesses without losing existing-customer execution, while improving the cash produced by the larger portfolio.
focusTitle: Connect portfolio expansion to retained customer value and cash.
focusText: Protect frontline and automation demand, integrate Elo Touch and Photoneo selectively, and tighten working capital. Judge acquisition progress through customer retention, full contribution and cash returns rather than reported revenue growth alone.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve existing frontline demand within acquired growth
cards.text: Connected Frontline sales grew 9.1% reported and 5.6% organically on a non-GAAP basis. The distinction matters when allocating commercial and integration resources.
items: Support existing mobile-computing and printing customer programs.
Coordinate acquired offerings around demonstrated customer workflow needs.
Monitor existing-business retention and contribution separately from acquired revenue.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Build automation growth through useful deployments
cards.text: Asset Visibility and Automation sales rose 7.5% reported and 7.0% organically. Underlying demand supports focused investment in customer applications.
items: Target scanning, RFID and machine-vision applications with demonstrated demand.
Align implementation support with customer deployment readiness.
Monitor adoption and contribution by application and customer market.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make acquired capabilities earn the purchase commitment
cards.text: Elo Touch and Photoneo cost $1.365 billion net of cash acquired. Integration should retain customers and produce worthwhile economics across the expanded portfolio.
items: Prioritize acquired-customer continuity and critical product delivery.
Stage cross-selling around validated customer needs and support readiness.
Monitor integration costs and acquired-business cash contribution separately.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Restore cash conversion across the larger business
cards.text: Operating cash flow declined to $917 million from $1.013 billion. Working capital and spending discipline are important as the acquisition program absorbs additional resources.
items: Align component purchases and inventory with executable customer orders.
Resolve billing and collection delays after delivery.
Monitor cash remaining after capital spending and integration requirements.

headline: Zimmer Biomet should preserve implant growth while making Paragon 28 integration earn returns.
summary: Knees and hips delivered underlying growth, while acquisition effects lifted reported S.E.T. growth much more. Operating cash supports investment. The priority is maintaining procedure-linked execution and separating acquired scale from progress in existing products as integration resources are allocated.
focusTitle: Match product and integration spending to demand and cash contribution.
focusText: Protect implant availability and customer support, target Paragon 28 integration around continuity, and evaluate expansion through organic adoption and full costs. Preserve cash for required manufacturing and product investment.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Keep knee growth supported by reliable procedure supply
cards.text: Knee sales increased 4.7% reported and 4.0% on a non-GAAP organic constant-currency basis. Continued growth depends on implant availability and customer execution.
items: Align knee inventory and field support with procedure schedules.
Prioritize product availability where customer demand is sustained.
Monitor procedure volumes, pricing and contribution by geography.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Develop hip demand using distinct regional economics
cards.text: Hip sales increased 4.7% reported and 3.8% organically in constant currency. Its growth should be assessed separately from knee performance.
items: Allocate hip commercial support using local procedure and implant demand.
Coordinate product mix with customer clinical and operating requirements.
Monitor hip volumes and realized pricing by market.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make acquired S.E.T. scale produce durable economics
cards.text: S.E.T. sales grew 15.2% reported but 4.1% organically in constant currency, excluding Paragon 28. Acquisition contribution should remain distinct from existing-product momentum.
items: Prioritize Paragon 28 customer continuity and supply integration.
Test combined commercial offerings against demonstrated customer requirements.
Monitor acquired retention, integration costs and existing-product organic growth separately.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Use operating cash to support disciplined product investment
cards.text: Operating cash flow totaled $1.697 billion. The cash base supports product and integration needs after manufacturing, working capital and other committed requirements.
items: Prioritize capital projects using utilization and customer demand.
Align implant inventory with procedure schedules and collection terms.
Monitor cash after required capital and acquisition-related spending.

headline: Zoetis should address China weakness while converting product innovation into adoption.
summary: Companion animal growth and underlying livestock expansion provide support, while China declined. Portfolio changes distort reported livestock demand, and innovation milestones are not realized sales. The priority is market-specific commercial execution and product adoption rather than broad portfolio expansion alone.
focusTitle: Allocate commercial resources to retained demand and validated adoption.
focusText: Protect productive pet and livestock products, investigate China by category, and stage innovation spending around customer uptake. Use consistent reporting scope when evaluating the annual international business and portfolio changes.

cards.label: What is working
cards.title: Preserve companion-animal momentum through clinic adoption
cards.text: Companion animal revenue increased 5% to $6.587 billion reported. Sustained growth depends on product uptake and repeat demand across animal-health categories.
items: Prioritize clinic support around demonstrated product and service needs.
Align product availability with veterinarian and customer demand.
Monitor adoption and repeat purchasing by pet-medicine category.

cards.label: What stands out
cards.title: Support retained livestock growth after portfolio changes
cards.text: Livestock revenue fell 5% reported but rose 8% on a non-GAAP organic operational basis. Currency and divestitures materially affect the interpretation.
items: Allocate supply and commercial resources to retained livestock products.
Separate divested-business effects from existing customer demand.
Monitor organic operational contribution by retained product and market.

cards.label: What could improve
cards.title: Give China a category-specific recovery plan
cards.text: China revenue declined 16% reported to $227 million. The result identifies a geographic weakness without establishing one common cause across animal-health categories.
items: Evaluate local companion-animal and livestock customer demand separately.
Target product and channel support using demonstrated local adoption barriers.
Monitor realized sales and product contribution after commercial changes.

cards.label: Risk to watch
cards.title: Make innovation milestones earn commercial returns
cards.text: Zoetis reported approximately 185 geographic expansions, lifecycle developments and new-product innovations. These milestones represent varied activities rather than 185 new revenue-producing launches.
items: Prioritize commercialization using customer need and product readiness.
Stage additional spending around approval and adoption milestones.
Monitor realized product revenue separately from innovation and expansion counts.
